beats.t: Nothing had been going Yeoni’s way lately. One unlucky day would have been easy enough to shrug off, but little things had been going wrong for days.
That morning was no different. There had definitely been three alarms: 7:10, 7:15, and 7:20. Yeoni had even given each one a proper name.
[ Get up ]   [ Seriously, get up ]   [ Keep this up and your life is over ]
Not one had rung. By the time Yeoni opened their eyes, the light slipping through the curtains had turned yellow. Exactly the color of being late.
The phone was at 1 percent. The charger sat neatly in the outlet. The problem was the other end: it wasn’t connected to the phone.
…You cutting me off too?
The charger said nothing. That day, it felt as though everything in the world had quietly turned its back on Yeoni alone.
The sock on the left was white; the one on the right, gray. Even the patterns were different. Yeoni stared down for about three seconds.
…They say mixing and matching is fashionable these days.
Yeoni decided to look on the bright side. Staying positive was the only way they knew to weather bad luck.
The real trouble was the bus. Yeoni tapped the card—beep. Please try again.
Another tap. Beep. Please try again. And another. Beep. Please try again. The people behind Yeoni watched without a word.
(That silence was the worst part.) …You worked fine yesterday.
The card finally registered on the fourth try. By then, the trust between them had already taken a small hit.
(Yeoni left a mental review.) Transit card… one star. Reason: took four tries. Would not buy again.

For lunch, Yeoni bought a tuna-mayo rice triangle. The moment the wrapper came off, it fell face-first onto the floor. Rice scattered everywhere; with half its seaweed peeled away, it looked utterly forlorn.
(It looked as though it couldn’t accept its own fate.) …I’m sorry. You were a good tuna mayo.
Yeoni bought another one. This time, it didn’t fall. But the first bite set their mouth on fire. Spicy pork. The wrapper had clearly said tuna mayo.
Seriously? Even the rice triangles are lying to me now?
The rice triangle said nothing. Naturally. It was a rice triangle.
Tuna mayo on the outside, spicy pork on the inside. Isn’t that false advertising? I’m filing a consumer complaint. I mean it.
Up to that point, it had been funny. The sort of thing a friend would laugh off with, “What is going on with you today?”
But a few days later—it stopped being funny.

A part-time job interview was canceled that very day. An assignment file became corrupted just before submission. A parcel went to the wrong building. A café coupon had expired yesterday, discovered only at the counter.
An important message came back as failed to send. Apologies always arrived a moment too late, and words meant to help somehow came out wrong.
Once, three dots flickered in a chat window. Something was about to arrive—then quietly vanished.
Yeoni stared for a long time at the space where those three dots had been, then turned the phone face down.

The room’s darkness settled softly over the overturned phone. Yeoni pulled the blanket up to their nose. It was one of those nights when no one was to blame, yet everything made you feel sorry. There had been more and more nights like that.
…Why does everything keep going wrong? Did I do something?

Small misfortunes gnawed a little more out of each day. At first, Yeoni had laughed them off as coincidences. But when coincidences pile up for days, the back of your neck grows cold, as if someone is standing behind you. Days begun with a joke had become days spent looking for excuses.
Still, Yeoni didn’t want to believe in fate. It was far too convenient a word.
If things fail, it’s fate. If you break up, it wasn’t meant to be. If you’re late, the time wasn’t right… Those sayings always leave me stuck in the same place.
They made everything easier to explain. They did nothing to make it easier to bear.
That night, Yeoni peeled off the wet socks, tossed them aside, and collapsed onto the bed. Enough thinking about today.
Today was… one for the history books.
Battery: 4 percent. Yeoni reached for the charger—and the screen lit up on its own.
…What?
In the middle of the home screen sat an unfamiliar app. A black night sky. A doorway traced in moonlight. One tiny star. And two words.
〈  Code Destiny  〉
Did I… install this?
No memory of it. Yeoni pressed and held the app to delete it. The screen answered.

[ This app cannot be deleted. ]
[ This app is connected to destiny. ]
Apps these days have some serious nerve.
I never paid for it, but apparently there are no refunds. No, forget refunds—I can’t even delete it. Five stars for sheer audacity.
Yeoni checked Settings. It wasn’t in the app list or the storage menu. But there it was on the home screen, utterly at ease. As though that spot had always belonged to it.
Then a notification appeared.

[ User fortune damage: 87% ]
[ Luck leak detected · Bond code partially corrupted · Abnormal wealth code outflow ]
[ User: Yeoni ]  [ Age: 23 ]  [ Day Master candidate: 乙 ]  [ Day Pillar code: 乙亥 ]
How… how do you know my name and age?
[ The universe has always known. ]
That makes it even creepier!
Enough. Where’s customer support? Put me through to a person. Right now.

[ Customer support: The universe ]
[ Agents: None · Your place in the queue: ∞ ]
Yeoni tossed the phone onto the pillow. It bounced a couple of times, then lit up again.
[ Begin destiny restoration? ]     [ YES ]     [ Later ]
Naturally, Yeoni tapped [Later]. The screen changed.
[ There is no later. ]
…Then why did you ask?
[ YES ]     [ YES ]
That isn’t a choice. That’s a kidnapping notice.

[ Terms of Service, Article 1 ]
[ By being born, the user has already agreed to all provisions. ]
A tarot card rose above the screen. Against black, a door made of moonlight. A small flower before it. At the bottom—[ THE DOOR ].
Is that… even a tarot card?
At that moment, the door in the card opened. Creeeeak—the sound came from the room, not the phone.
A real moonlit door stood in the air at the foot of the bed. Beyond its narrow opening, an unfamiliar night sky swirled.
This is… still my room, right?

Instead of an answer, cards poured through the doorway. The Star, the Moon, the Sun, the Wheel of Fortune. The assignment on the desk, the inside-out umbrella, even the half-eaten cup noodles began circling the room.
My assignment, my umbrella, my noodles—…Actually, forget the noodles!
[ Tarot gate open ]  [ Connecting to the fortune world ]  [ River of Saju coordinates confirmed ]
Close it. I said close it! A river? This is a studio apartment!
[ Converting initial avatar ]
Light burst from inside the doorway. Yeoni clung to the headboard until the very end. The headboard, unfortunately, was less loyal than expected. Snap.
Traitor!
And just like that—Yeoni was sucked through the tarot gate.
Beyond the door lay endless night. Night above, night below. Constellations flowed like a river, and countless tarot cards circled Yeoni, whispering. Choice. Descent. Beginning. Transformation.
[ Destiny code connection complete ]  [ Entering the damaged fortune world. ]
I never agreed to—

episodes.title: I Became a Flower Pig
episodes.tag: Episode 1 · I Became a Flower Pig

beats.t: At some point, the fall softened and light wrapped around Yeoni. Their arms shrank, their fingers grew blunt. When they opened their eyes, they were in the middle of an enormous lotus-leaf boat floating on a river.
I TURNED INTO A PIIIIIG!
The scream carried across the night-dark river, then cut off. This body did not even have enough lung capacity left to keep screaming.

The lotus leaf was impossibly large, wider than a bed in most studio apartments, with dewdrops gleaming like lamps along its edge. No oars, no sail, no engine. Just a giant leaf. Yet it floated. Steadily, at that.
Yeoni stared down at themself for a long time. Short forelegs. A round belly. A curly tail. A little flower blooming on their head. However they looked at it, this pink body was not human.
No. ...How am I supposed to do my assignments with these hands?
An odd sound slipped into the end of their next sentence.
This makes absolutely no sense, oink.
Yeoni froze.
...What was that?
Hello. I am a human being.
That came out normally. Yeoni felt the tiniest bit relieved.
Okay. I can talk. At least there's that.
But then they looked at their forelegs again.
...My fingers are gone.
This is clearly a downgrade. From a human with ten fingers to a pig with two front hooves.
A moment ago, Yeoni had been in their room. Wet socks, a strange app, a tarot doorway. Now they were a pig with a flower. A flower pig, to be exact.
Yeoni flopped onto the lotus leaf. Their soft body squished a little, then sprang back. The sensation was so vivid that it only made things worse.
Okay. Got it. ...This is a dream.
Obviously. However weird the world had become, turning into a flower pig because you tapped the wrong app was going too far.
Yeoni tapped the leaf with a front hoof. They could feel it.
If it's a dream, I should pinch myself awake. ...My hoof can't reach my face.
...Nice graphics, though.
Yeoni reached a very serious conclusion. Having stayed up until three grinding a limited-time event, they were clearly suffering gaming aftereffects.
Status window.
Nothing appeared.
Menu. ...Inventory.
Only the wind passed. Yeoni narrowed their eyes.
...Terrible UI. One star.
Then a low voice came from the edge of the leaf.
Still feels like a dream? Can't blame you.
Yeoni went rigid. Slowly, they turned their head. Something was sitting at the leaf's edge.
At first they thought it was just a white cat. Small, round, fluffy. But on its head sat a navy wizard's hat with a golden crescent moon. A cat. Wearing a hat.
...What are you?
I am Yeongnyangi.
A cat?
No.
Then what? You look exactly like a cat in a hat.
To be precise, I am not an ordinary cat.
Then why are you so tiny? You'd fit in my palm.
Yeongnyangi's whiskers twitched.
...Isn't that a bit much for someone you just met?
I just got dragged into another world and turned into a pig. Today, I think I've earned the right to be rude.
Yeongnyangi fell silent for a moment.
...Fair point.
Are you an NPC?
No.
That's what all NPCs say.
...Now that you mention it, that did sound like an NPC.
I am the guardian of the River of Four Pillars.
...An NPC with lore, then.
Yeoni pressed a hoof against the flower on their head. Its petals trembled. The sensation was far too distinct.
Wow. The detail is insane.
Does it hurt?
No. It just feels weird.
Then it is real.
That is a ridiculously sloppy test.
Instead of replying, Yeongnyangi looked over the side. Yeoni followed that gaze. Only then did they properly see their surroundings.

A river. But no ordinary river. Its water was as dark blue as the night sky, starlight breaking over every ripple. Strange Chinese characters swam beneath the surface like fish: Gapja, Eulchuk, Byeongin, Jeongmyo. The sort of characters that would make you give up if they appeared on an exam.

Mist lay in the distance, with vague pillars rising beyond it. A great moon hung overhead. Its light was strangely free of cold. It was beautiful. Impossibly so. ...Which made it even more frightening.
You could wake from a dream. You could switch off a game. But this place felt like a dream with no known way to wake or turn it off.
...Where is this?
The River of Four Pillars.
Four Pillars? Like saju?
The place where the codes of human destiny flow.
Right. I understood none of that.
That is normal. Most humans understand little on their first visit.
I'm not human anymore.
A flower pig, to be precise.
I hate that word more every time I hear it.
Better than just a pig, isn't it?
...Is that meant to comfort me?
An objective analysis.
Yeoni took a deep breath. A little snort escaped. Oink, oink. An unbearably cute sound. The fact that it had come from their own mouth made them suddenly furious.
Why a pig, of all things! ...And where am I? I want to go home.
That will not be easy.
Wasn't expecting an easy answer.
Yeongnyangi walked slowly across the leaf. It glowed faintly under each step. Star-shaped markings tipped those pink paw pads. Apparently this was more than a cat that said strange things.
Yeongnyangi. Are you in charge here?
Something like that.
Then I'd like to file a complaint. Turning someone into a pig for tapping an app seems a bit excessive.
You are rather cute.
Adding that to the complaint. ...And what I tapped was an app. Code Something-or-other.
Yeongnyangi's expression stiffened a little.
That was a door.
Looked like an app.
It merely took a form humans today would readily tap. You might not open a door, but you would tap an app.
Yeoni had no comeback. It was true, which made it more annoying.
Then the water beneath the boat heaved. Splash. Yeoni instinctively ducked.
What was that?
Yeongnyangi's eyes changed. A moment ago, this had seemed like an irritated cat. Now it was different. Violet irises flared gold, and the crescent on the hat began to burn faintly.
The residue of misfortune. ...Things that leaked out of your reality.
My... reality?
Yeongnyangi pointed to black ink spreading across the river. The dark water swallowed the passing characters one by one. Their shining strokes blackened and twisted out of shape.
Your luck has been going wrong lately.

The silent alarms. The card rejected three times. The rice triangle with the wrong filling. The corrupted assignment. The canceled plans. The app that would not go away. Yeoni suddenly had nothing to say.

They had laughed it all off, but it had kept nagging at a corner of their mind. Why did everything go this wrong? Why was their timing always off? Why did even the smallest things seem to slip past them, every single time?
Does that... have something to do with this place?
Your destiny code has been damaged. The characters of your Four Pillars have scattered.
Someone messed with my saju? Why? What could possibly be worth the trouble?
To learn that, you must first reclaim your characters.
Before Yeongnyangi could finish, a black hand surged from the river. Too long to be a hand, too solid to be a shadow. Made of black water, it reached for the edge of the leaf.
Yeoni froze. Their heart dropped. Every joke they had been forcing themself to hold on to vanished. That was no piece of dream scenery. Something was coming to catch them.
Is that... coming for me?
Yes.
Why?
Because you are its target.
How can you say that so calmly!
The black hand reached over the boat. Yeoni tried to retreat, but this body still felt borrowed. Their short legs scrambled uselessly on the leaf.
Why are this body's controls so awful!
You will get used to them.
Just as the hand reached for Yeoni, Yeongnyangi vanished. Or seemed to. A golden line slashed through the air. Shhk. The hand split in two, scattering drops of ink.
Yeongnyangi landed at the leaf's edge. A small body. But there had been nothing small about that movement.
Do not call me just a cat again. I am no ordinary cat.
Yeoni considered that for a moment.
...Combat cat?
The cat's eyes narrowed.
My real name... I cannot tell you. Call me whatever you like.
Then Yeongnyangi. A mystical kitty. I'll stake one star on my naming skills.
The black hands did not disappear. More shadows rose from the river. Severed hands melted back into the water and gathered again, thicker and longer.
Yeongnyangi tapped the leaf with a paw. Tap. Clear droplets rose around its rim, forming little shields. A black hand scraped across them. Screeech.
...Worst sound ever.
They will not hold for long.
Then what do we do?
...The flower on your head is alive.
Yeoni touched it with a hoof. A petal brushed the tip. At that moment the flower glowed, very faintly. It was warm. Barely, but unmistakably.
What is it?
A trace of your Day Master. The central character that represents you.
Yeoni immediately gave up trying to understand.
Fine. For now, let's just say my flower is a battery.
It is not.
I'm putting it in terms I understand.
A mistaken understanding is dangerous.
You explain things exactly like a professor teaching a required elective.
The black hands approached again. Yeongnyangi looked across the river. Four lights emerged in the mist.
One was a sharp blue. One flickered like a warm flame. One flashed gold. The last shone as softly as an old bookshelf.
The characters of your Four Pillars are scattered across four islands. The Island of Companions. The Island of Expression. The Island of Wealth. The Library of Resources.
Yeoni looked at the four lights. Too vivid to be a dream, too chilling to be a game. Yet strangely, they seemed to be calling. Something deep inside stirred quietly.
I have to visit all of them before I can go home. Is that it?
Yes.
Hold on. I never agreed to any terms and conditions.
There is no consent procedure.
Can I get a refund halfway through?
No.
A help forum?
No.
Customer support?
...There is me, more or less.
...That makes me incredibly nervous.
Complaints are not accepted.
Worst customer service ever.
Neither are star ratings.
Then one black hand broke through the shield.
OINK—AAH!
Yeoni immediately covered their mouth.
...That was only because I got startled.
I know.

Yeongnyangi sprang up again. Golden patterns appeared on those claws. Four Pillars Starlight. With a sweep of a paw, blades of starlight fanned across the river. The black hands were severed all at once.
The lotus-leaf boat surged forward. The river parted as though opening a road. As soon as Yeongnyangi landed, a low murmur followed.
This time... I will not lose you.
Before Yeoni could ask, Yeongnyangi was already looking beyond the mist, with the eyes of someone who knew a path they had never traveled.
Our first destination is the Island of Companions.
Companions?
An island of things that resemble you.
There are more things like me?
Many. Friends, rivals, pride, jealousy—and courage.
Silently, Yeoni watched the first light in the mist. It was less beautiful than sharp, like glass. Getting close seemed likely to draw blood.
...Why does the very first island already feel wrong?
Facing yourself was never going to be comfortable.
...There you go sounding like a quote again.
Because it is true.
The lotus-leaf boat gathered speed. Behind them, black hands tore up through the river again. Ahead, the fog thickened. Beyond it, an island's silhouette slowly emerged. The Island of Companions.
Countless tiny mirror shards floated around the island. In every one, something was reflected.

Before they reached the island, the lotus-leaf boat caught in a clump of reeds. Yeongnyangi pressed a paw against the current. Amid the clinking mirror shards came a faint grinding of teeth. Yeoni pricked up their pig ears. It almost sounded like someone holding back tears.
Over there. Something's under the reeds. Like a black ball of fluff. Wait, it has eyes. I'm not just looking at a doll that fell in the water, am I?

A little cloak edged with gold thread was tangled in the reeds. A striped tail wriggled beneath it. A black tiger. Even wet, its red eyes were bright, and the marking on its forehead glowed red as a wound. A black loop finer than thread encircled its right forepaw.
If you're done staring, leave. I can recognize pity even reflected in water. And I'm not a ball of fluff. Take that back first.
You can talk, too. Then you can ask to be rescued. Just say you need help. Your paw's shaking like that—pretending you're fine only makes it hurt more.
Wait. Don't touch it. That is no animal trap. It is a ring seeking an owner. Touch it and it will ask your name. Answer, and you will be bound to that one.

Yeoni stopped with a hoof outstretched. They were not even certain of the body or name they would return to. But the ring tightened every time the tiger drew breath. Turning the boat away and leaving that tiny paw behind felt more frightening.
So I just don't give it my name? Then let's not talk it open. I'll use this. Yeongnyangi, just keep the boat steady. I'm scared too, so save the complicated explanations for later.

Yeoni picked up a dry leaf stalk from the boat's edge in their mouth. Black water spurted as they pushed it between the ring and the fur. The tiger reflexively lashed at Yeoni's nose, then stopped. The stalk snapped. The ring was still tight.
Stop. You can't even control your own body. Who do you think you'll save with paws like that? If you get hurt, will you charge me for it?
If it hurts, say it hurts. Stop putting a price tag on everything. I didn't negotiate this long the day I dropped my rice triangle. You're the one who needs help right now.

Gold gathered at the tips of Yeongnyangi's claws. A direct cut at that angle would injure the tiger's paw too. Yeongnyangi withdrew the blade-like light and tilted the leaf. The current changed direction. For one brief instant, the taut ring loosened.
Now. Push, don't pull. Don't try to force the ring past it. Make room for the paw to slip free.

Yeoni pressed their forehead against the tiger's shoulder. They rolled together onto the wet leaf. The ring stayed behind in the river and contracted, clutching at empty air. It bit three times at the place the paw had been, then burst into black foam.
Why did you push with your own body? You could have been hurt. You could have ordered that cat in the hat to do it. That's what the power to give orders is for.
Why would asking a friend be an order? Besides, I only just found this out myself. A pig's forehead is surprisingly useful. Ow. My nose, on the other hand, is just uselessly sore.

The tiger looked at the scratch on Yeoni's nose. Red eyes narrowed while it tugged at the hem of its cloak. A child who did not retreat even after getting hurt. The tiger studied Yeoni's expression for a long time, measuring how close a single pained face might draw this child.
Tell me what you want. Directions, an object, anything. Debts grow if you leave them. Settling this now would be easier for us both.
As long as you're okay, that's enough. If I had to ask for one thing... your name? You seem like you'd get angry if I kept calling you Tiger.
A name isn't something you give away lightly. Once you hold it, you can call me wherever I am. A life spent answering anyone who calls isn't much of a life.
Then you don't have to give it. I'll just call you Tiger. I don't need to know someone's name to help them.

The tiger's tail went still. A droplet fell from the gold clasp and rolled across the leaf. Yeongnyangi saw it crawl toward the tiger instead of returning to the river. Without a word, a paw came down between Yeoni and the tiger.
We travel together as far as the landing. After that, we go our separate ways. I won't ask who sent you. Don't ask this child's name either.
Are all cats in hats this unfriendly? You free one little paw and start putting up fences. Afraid I'll bite your friend?
I thought he was a big cat at first, too. He really hates that, though. Do you hate being called a little tiger?
Leave out 'little.' Ranking people by size is a thoroughly outdated habit. Count the cloak, and I'm not even that small.

Yeoni laughed. Instead of joining in, the tiger lowered its ears. Yeoni's gaze held little wariness toward this small, soaked animal. When the tiger hid its reddened ears under the cloak, Yeoni only softened their voice further. The tiger remembered that difference.
Sit over there where it's dry. Your cloak must be heavy with all that water. All that gold trim looks cool, but washing it must be a nightmare.

The tiger held out the cloak's hem. A black thread hidden inside the gold edging slipped among the fabric's red fibers. When Yeongnyangi turned, it stopped. The tiger licked its wet paw as though nothing had happened.
Hold this against your nose. Drying the water should make it sting less. I'm not giving you the cloak, so don't start thinking it's yours.
Got it. Borrowing. Thank you. You sound scary, but your hands are kinder than I expected. Or paws, I guess.

The island's bell rang. The tiger pricked its ears at the first note and leaped from the boat before the second. Its injured paw never touched the water. The black surface briefly hardened, becoming a narrow path wherever it stepped.
Do not follow those tracks. A creature that makes roads across water did not get trapped because it lost its way.
You mean it got caught on purpose? Then was the pain an act too? I thought that face was real. I know a little about the face people make when they're holding pain in.
Real pain and a hidden motive can exist together. You must see both. That does not make your choice to help wrong.

Yeoni pulled a red strand from the cloak off their nose and laid it on a hoof. Somehow, they could not throw it away. Beyond the island mist, the black tiger looked back. Its smile was gone. Only two red points remained above the water.
So you stop when you see someone hurt. Wherever you go, now I know who to put in your path. Next time, come where that cat isn't.

The pain of the ring crossing the boundary had been real. But what the tiger had stolen was not a route. It was Yeoni's reaction. The broken end of a black thread from the cloak sank into the river. Beneath it, someone's name was silently erased.

episodes.title: A Cat in a Hat? Yeongnyangi
episodes.tag: Episode 2 · A Cat in a Hat? Yeongnyangi

beats.t: The lotus-leaf boat touched the landing on the Island of Companions. Tap. A smaller sound than Yeoni had expected.
The black hands pursuing them stopped abruptly at the island. They writhed outside the mist for a moment, then slipped beneath the river.
Clinging to the leaf's edge, Yeoni took a long time to catch their breath. Their short, fingerless forelegs were rigid with effort. Somehow, though, they were still holding on.
I'm alive...
A little snort slipped out after the words. Oink. Yeoni immediately clamped a hoof over their mouth.
No. That was just breathing. Not a pig noise.
Without answering, Yeongnyangi leaped lightly onto the landing. As his small body touched down, golden paw prints bloomed briefly on the black glass floor, then faded.
Wow. Add a few sound effects and this would be a whole game.
You still think this is a game?
Haven't given up hope. Give me one loading screen and I'll believe it immediately.
I understand that you're trying to find some other explanation.
I'll take that as a compliment. But seriously, what are you? A cat in a hat, or a cat doing cosplay?
...Not an ordinary cat.
Except you keep looking like a cat.
Say that once more and I'll leave those paw prints on your forehead.
Yes, yes, Lord Cat. Lord Cat of the Magnificent Hat.
Yeoni cautiously tried to climb off the leaf. Front hooves down first; then, as they shifted their hind legs—
Uh, whoa?
Their short legs refused to cooperate. Yeoni landed nose-first on the dock. Thud.
It did not hurt. Their pride hurt a little instead.
Your landing... could use some practice.
Stop analyzing me.
Isn't this the kind of thing that comes with a tutorial? No controls, no save function, not even a refund button.
A sharp snort punctuated the complaint. Oink. Its gravitas dropped by exactly half.
The Island of Companions was quiet. No grass, no houses, no people. Instead, the whole island seemed built from shards of mirrors.
The ground gleamed like black glass. Mirrors large and small floated in the air, some palm-sized, others as large as doors. Every one hung at a different angle.
Mirrors reflecting the sky. The river. The lotus-leaf boat. And mirrors reflecting Yeoni.
Yeoni peered into one nearby. A flower pig looked back. Pink body. Small flower perched on its head. Short forelegs.
It was far too cute. That was why Yeoni disliked it.
I still can't get used to this.
When did my cheeks get so chubby? Did someone secretly pump air into them?
Yeoni lifted a hoof; the flower pig in the mirror lifted one too, left and right reversed. Yeoni tilted their head; it tilted its head exactly the same way.
Hey. Stop copying me.
Naturally, the mirrored pig merely mouthed the words. No sound came out. Somehow that was even more irritating.
When Yeoni turned this way and that, their tail swayed along. That was cute too, which only made them more annoyed.
Come on, mess up just once. Give me a little lag and I'll admit you're fake.
Oh, seriously.
What's wrong?
My whole aesthetic was supposed to be cool and badass. Now someone's switched my genre to soothing animal cuteness.
...I can't tell whether you like it or hate it.
You wouldn't understand. Having your entire appearance change genres overnight.
I have been a finished masterpiece since birth.
Oh, yes. Of course you have.
Companion cat review: personality, two stars. But the hat's pretty, so... another half star. I'm being generous.
Yeoni let it go and walked farther inland. The mirror fragments grew denser as they went. But something was strange.
Some mirrors did not reflect Yeoni as a flower pig. At first, they thought they had imagined it. They stopped.
There was a person inside the mirror.
Wet hair. A loose hoodie. Sweatpants baggy at the knees. A charger cable tossed on the bed. A phone in one hand.
And a tired-looking, twenty-three-year-old college student staring down at the screen. Yeoni. The original Yeoni. So familiar it felt unfamiliar.
Yeoni approached the mirror slowly. Their hooves made little tapping sounds against the ground. Tap. Tap.

The Yeoni in the mirror sat on the bed, exactly as they had been in the real world moments before. Hair tied back carelessly, fatigue lingering on their face. Still, it was the face Yeoni knew as their own.
Human hands. Human legs. Human eyes. Everything Yeoni had lost was there, just one layer of glass away.
Yeoni looked down at their hooves, then back at the mirror. Something in their chest tightened strangely.
I... looked like that, didn't I?
The voice came out quieter than expected. Their throat kept closing.
Forgotten sensations returned all at once. Swiping across a screen with a finger. The hair tie resting around their wrist before they tied their hair.
The irritation of pulling off wet socks. The stunned emptiness of seeing their assignment disappear. All those tiny things had suddenly become impossibly distant.
Yeoni raised a hoof to the mirror. Cold. The reflected Yeoni raised a hand. Human palm and short hoof met with a single pane of glass between them.
An unexpected swell of emotion rose in Yeoni. They wanted to go back. They really did.
Until a moment ago, 'I want to go home' had been half a joke. Now it was different. The words had suddenly become real.
I want to go home. To my room. My bed. My fingers.
...Yeongnyangi.
I'm listening. Go on.
Is that... really me?
Yeongnyangi looked at the mirror. His expression grew a little more serious too.
Your original appearance.
Then if I go in there, can I go back?
No.
The answer was quick and firm. Unable to look away from the mirror, Yeoni asked again.
...Why?
The mirrors on the Island of Companions are not exits. They reflect the places you have lost.
Places?
The place you believed was yourself. The you others see. The you you wanted to become. And the places you feel you were pushed out of.
It sounded understandable, yet Yeoni did not want to understand. That made it worse.
Then the Yeoni in the mirror moved. Yeoni stopped breathing.
Until that moment, the mirror had clearly been copying them. Now it was the other way around.
The human Yeoni in the mirror wore a different expression. A little calmer. Standing a little straighter. A little more confident, in a way that did not feel like Yeoni at all.
You're late.
Yeoni froze.
...What?
You're always late.
Quiet words, sharp as fingernails. Without realizing it, Yeoni took a step back.
Late for your alarm. Late replying. Late apologizing. Late for every opportunity.
A thin crack appeared across the mirror.
And this time, too—you're late.
Yeoni bit their lip.
What are you?
Me? Yeoni.
That was the answer Yeoni hated most. They tapped their chest with a hoof.
I'm Yeoni.
Really? In that body?
For a moment, no words came. Yeoni was angry, but strangely unable to answer at once.
The Yeoni in the mirror was too natural. The appearance they had worn in their room. Their voice. Their face. Their expressions.
If someone had to choose the real Yeoni from the two of them, would they choose the pink flower pig? Or that person?
Be careful.
What is that thing?
A reflection created by the Island of Companions. A rival with your face. Another you, seeking your place.
So, a doppelgänger.
In simple terms, yes.
My life really is squeezing in every possible trope.
You are not here as a spectator.
There's no place for you here.
Those words echoed across the entire island. One by one, the surrounding mirrors began to shine. Each small mirror held a different scene.
The back row of a lecture hall. A seat someone else had already taken. Yeoni's message posted too late in the group-project chat. An unread reply.
A text canceling an interview. A contest entry that had failed to submit. And a single rice triangle lying on a convenience-store floor.
Hey, leave the rice triangle out of this. That's too pathetic.
Yeoni tossed it out like a joke, but their voice trembled at the end. Such little things. Individually, all of them could be laughed off.
But piled together, they made Yeoni feel constantly pushed aside. Nudged from their place, late, missing out—until eventually it felt as though they had ceased to exist.
Then the largest mirror slowly rose. It was different from the others. Dark blue light surrounded it, and its surface rippled like water.
A human Yeoni stood inside. This time, though, not in their room. Above a black river.
A tiny shoot had sprouted beneath that Yeoni's feet. Below the shoot, deep waters stirred.
[ 乙亥 ]
Yeoni stared quietly at the two characters appearing on the mirror's edge. Strangely, they could not look away.
Eulhae. They looked unfamiliar, like characters seen for the first time, yet felt like a name known long ago. Something rang softly inside Yeoni's chest. The flower on their head glowed faintly.
Found it.
Found what?
Your Day Pillar. The pillar of the day you were born. The characters closest to your center.
The Eulhae Day Pillar.
Eulhae...
As Yeoni said it, the flower shone a little brighter. The human Yeoni in the mirror saw the light too. For the first time, that face stiffened.
No.
The mirrored Yeoni reached out. The characters [乙亥] along the edge began sliding toward that outstretched hand.
Yeoni, stop it!
How!
Hold on to your name!
What does that mean! Explain it so I can understand!
Do not let your place be taken!
You hate yourself right now, don't you?
Yeoni hesitated.
You hate that body. You hate being here. You hate your real life and its rotten luck, too.
The reflected Yeoni stepped forward. The mirror's surface undulated like water.
So let me do it. I'm the real Yeoni.
Yeoni's heart plunged.
I'll go back in your place.
Yeoni could not breathe. That reflected self was all too convincing. Human form. Familiar face. Normal hands. Normal voice.
Everything the present Yeoni had lost, that other one possessed.
Even if you went home looking like that, nobody would believe you're you.
The words lodged in Yeoni's throat. They looked down at their hooves. Pink. Short and round. Cute, but nothing like themself.
Only for a moment. One very brief moment. What if that other one went back instead? What if that one was better?
The fact that they had thought it left Yeoni a little cold.
Do not listen too closely to those words.
But...
The mirror burrows into the gap where you dislike yourself.
Yeongnyangi stepped in front of Yeoni.
The Island of Companions is an island of conflict. But your opponent is not a stranger. It is another you, trying to take your place.
You talk too much.
The reflected Yeoni snapped their fingers. All the surrounding mirror fragments rose at once. Sharp glass rained toward Yeoni and Yeongnyangi.
Get back!
The golden tassel at the tip of Yeongnyangi's hat blazed. He leaped and spun in midair, golden claws striking away the glass. Clang. Clang. Clang.
Fragments scattered in every direction. The instant he landed, Yeongnyangi crouched again.
Keep your eyes on those characters!
Yeoni glared at the great mirror. Eulhae. The characters wavered between the human reflection and the flower pig, as though unable to choose their real owner.
You said they're mine.
Yes. They are the characters you must reclaim.
Then why are they trying to go over there?
Because you are denying yourself.
Yeoni held their breath. Denying reality. They had called it a dream. Insisted it was a game. Forced it into the shape of an otherworld adventure story.
They had kept rejecting the self that had become a flower pig. They could hardly help it. They did not want to admit it. They were frightened.
And little by little, the mirrored Yeoni had been occupying that gap.
Oh... Is that how it works?
The reflected Yeoni reached out again. The characters [乙亥] slid farther toward that hand. The flower on Yeoni's head wavered precariously.
Yeoni.
Yeoni closed their eyes. Just for a moment. A very brief moment. Then opened them again.
They were still afraid. Still wanted to go home. Still hated this body. Still wished this were a dream. But.
Hey.
The reflected Yeoni looked over. Yeoni tapped their chest with a hoof.
I don't like how I look right now either. Not one bit.
No fingers. Short legs. I oink when I get startled.
A tiny oink did indeed escape at the end.
...See? That annoys me too.
Exactly, so I can—
But.
Yeoni cut in. The flower shone again. Still weak, but clearer than before.
Even so, I'm Yeoni.
The reflected Yeoni's expression hardened.
Even looking like this.
Yeoni took a step forward. With such short legs, it was not a large step. But it was unmistakably forward.
Even if I was late.
Another step.
Even if things went wrong.
Another step.
Even if my luck has completely fallen apart.
At last, Yeoni stood before the great mirror.
I decide where I belong.
At that instant, the characters [乙亥] shuddered violently. The human Yeoni in the mirror clenched their teeth.
Not yet. You don't even know what you are.
The mirror cracked open. Dark blue water poured through the split. Deep, cold water. Within it, a tiny green shoot began to rise.
乙 — Eul.
Dark blue currents swirled beneath the shoot.
亥 — Hae.
Eul Wood. Hae Water. A small shoot and deep water. The mirrored characters finally revealed their full form.
[ 乙亥 ]
And then the human Yeoni took a step out of the mirror.
Yeoni froze. The human who had walked out smiled with a face exactly like their own.
Fine. Prove it, then.
Every mirror around them lit up at once.
Prove you're the real Yeoni.
Yeoni faced the opponent wearing their face. They had reclaimed nothing yet. But one thing was certain. Those characters, Eulhae, were the first pillar they had to take back.
Do not retreat.
Yeoni breathed in deeply. The small flower petals on their head stirred in the wind.
Right. But first, one thing.
The reflected Yeoni tilted their head. Yeoni narrowed their eyes.
Don't wear my face and smile like such a jerk.
The reflected Yeoni stopped smiling.
[ Island of Companions · The First Trial Begins ]
Even breathing echoed in the mirror corridor. Yeoni's short nasal breaths struck the glass walls and returned in overlapping layers.
Opposite them stood a being with Yeoni's real face. Damp bangs, an old hoodie, a person standing on two legs. It slowly smiled.
Prove it, then.
...Prove what?
That you're the real Yeoni.
The moment those words ended, the entire Island of Companions sank a beat beneath their feet with a heavy thud.
Whoa! Hey, this world has an earthquake option too? I never signed up for that!
Hundreds of floating mirrors flipped over together. Blue letters lit up across their backs, one after another.
[ Island of Companions · Main Trial Begins ]
[ Verifying original identity. ]   [ Time limit 10:00 ]
Yeoni blinked their round eyes. The petals above their head took on a chilly hue in the blue light.
What? Why the sudden identity check? I just logged in.
That's right. With the login rights to your life at stake.
Yeoni's hoof paused. The easy grin drained slowly from their face.
...Login rights?
This is the Island of Companions. It tests whether you can hold your place. Lose that place, and your route home becomes uncertain too.
Wait. Does that mean—
That thing could walk into the real world instead of me?
Yeongnyangi did not answer. Only the tip of the white cat's tail stopped, once. His silence was answer enough.
Quick on the uptake. My brain, after all.
The reflected Yeoni spread both hands. Ten fingers, every joint intact. Wet hair, a hoodie, two legs, the original face. Everything Yeoni had lost.
Yeoni, meanwhile, was a flower pig. Short hooves. Round belly. A single small flower on their head. Far too cute, and far too disadvantaged.
Wow. Is this starting stat gap for real?
If it feels unfair, win.
Hey, don't say obnoxious things with my face. It feels weird.
It's your way of talking too, you know.
...Do I really sound that annoying?
Yes. Very.
Okay. Forced self-awareness achieved. That kind of hurts.
A mirror slid down and stopped right before Yeoni's nose. A sentence appeared on the glass.
Eek, too close! Can you not shove yourself in my face? Personal space, hello?
[ Verification Item 1 · Name ]
An easy question. Yeoni answered at once.
Yeoni.
The mirror gave an unsympathetic double beep.
[ Insufficient ]
...Why? I'm telling you my own name. What's insufficient about that?
I know the name too.
The reflected Yeoni calmly repeated it in exactly the same voice.
Yeoni.
The mirror shone blue, much brighter this time.
[ Two candidates confirmed ]   [ Unable to identify original ]
Hey, Yeongnyangi. Isn't this system's security pathetic? If a name is all it takes, I could hack somebody's account too.
The Companion energies share your own element. Appearance alone cannot tell you whether someone is on your side. That is what makes this difficult.
Why are you only telling me something that important now?
Now is when you need to know.
If you ran customer support, I'd give you one star. Your service is terrible.
There isn't anywhere to leave a rating here. What a shame for you.
A second mirror descended silently. Night-colored darkness slowly spread from within the glass.
[ Verification Item 2 · Memories ]
Yeoni's real life appeared in the mirror. The morning the alarm did not ring. The moment their transit card failed three times at the gate.

The night their assignment corrupted just before submission, leaving them staring numbly at a blinking cursor. A message they deleted instead of sending. An unread reply they checked all day. And the face that smiled as though nothing was wrong.
Yeoni closed their mouth. Each scene was nothing much on its own. But when they arrived together, something inside their chest felt pressed hard beneath a hand.
I was always late.
[ Memory matched ]
When I wanted to speak, it was too late. When I wanted to hold on, I'd already missed my chance. I pretended I was fine, then fell apart alone in my room.
[ Memory matched ]
The flower above Yeoni's head trembled faintly, though there was no wind.
See? I know your whole life too. Beginning to end.
Yeoni pressed their back teeth together. It was true. Every scene belonged to their own memories. They could not deny it.
Yet something was strange. Something remained, like a fish bone lodged in their throat.
The reflected Yeoni was reciting those memories. But all the feelings that had hurt inside them were missing. Like a report on somebody else's life. Meticulous footnotes, not one line of emotion.
...You're right. I was late.
The mirror shivered.
Sometimes I kept my mouth shut when I should have spoken. Sometimes I switched my lock screen on a hundred times waiting for a reply. And plenty of times I smiled like nothing was wrong.
Yeoni laid a short hoof against their round chest.
But inside, I wasn't okay at all.
The reflected Yeoni's face tightened, ever so slightly. As though the flawless report had acquired its first typo.
I wasn't joking because I felt fine. It was because if I didn't laugh, I thought I'd start crying right there.
The mirror blazed.
[ Emotion matched ]   [ Original identity response detected ]
The flower above Yeoni's head brightened. A layer of warmth mingled with the chilly blue light.
...Not bad.
I do know a little about my own story.
Then get the next one right. This one will hurt a little.
A third mirror descended. Unlike the others, it pretended to reflect nothing before an image slowly formed.
[ Verification Item 3 · Present Body ]
A flower pig stood inside the mirror. Pink body. Little flower on its head. Round belly. Short legs. Yeoni themself.
Ah... Still can't get used to that.
Then give up. Make it easy on yourself.
No thanks.
You said you hate that body.
I do. Honestly, I do. No fingers, stumpy legs, oinks coming out of my nose whenever I get startled—
My life's visual balance is completely broken. Plot it on a graph and it's a cliff.
An involuntary little oink slipped out at the end. Yeoni squeezed their eyes shut.
Oh, come on. That one doesn't count.
The system keeps count. That isn't up to us.
See? You hate it too. Something like this can't be your true body.
I hate it.
Yeoni admitted it readily. Then slowly raised their head. Their eyes did not waver in the blue light.
But hating it doesn't mean it isn't me.
The reflected Yeoni's smile stopped abruptly. Yeoni looked straight into the eyes of the flower pig in the mirror.
I don't like how I look. But the one standing here in this corridor instead of running away is me.
The flower above their head lit itself. This time, the light did not come from a mirror.
I'm the one holding on even when I'm scared. The one arguing to the bitter end in this ridiculous situation. The one getting pissed off by what you say. All me.
The mirror shook violently. Hairline cracks raced over its surface.
[ Present self acknowledged ]   [ Original identity response increasing ]
A green shoot popped through the glass floor directly beneath Yeoni's hoof. Smaller than a fingernail. But unmistakable.
Take it. Now.
Their body moved before thought. Yeoni reached out a short hoof. The moment the shoot touched it, warmth seeped into their body.
What... is this?
Eul Wood. The first character of your Day Pillar, its Heavenly Stem.
The green shoot swayed gently on Yeoni's hoof, as though breathing.
Small grasses, flowers, vines. They may not look powerful, but they do not die easily. They bend instead of breaking, then grow again.
Yeoni looked down at their hoof. Still no fingers. Yet strangely, a sense of holding something tightly remained. One tiny root. Thin, but alive.
The reflected Yeoni's face hardened, cold as ice.
At the outstretched hand, the scattered mirror fragments gathered again like iron filings. This time they formed not curves, but honed, razor-sharp blades.
Be careful. Rob Wealth is moving now.
Rob Wealth? What's that supposed to be?
Energy like your own. Yet a force that takes what belongs to you. It wears a sibling's face and tries to claim a share of what is yours.
That's right. Even that little shoot you barely managed to get—I can take it.
Dozens of blades rose around the reflected Yeoni in a fan. Then all of them rained toward Yeoni.

Yeongnyangi sprang up. Golden claws slashed the air. Clang! Clang! Clang! The blades scattered, then instantly gathered again. Shatter them and they returned. Cut them and they flew again. There was no end.
Yeongnyangi!
I can open a path! But I cannot protect your characters in your place!
At that shout, the reflected Yeoni reached toward them. The energy of [乙] nestled in Yeoni's hoof began to shake, like a tiny shoot about to be pulled out, soil and all.
Hey, this... It's slipping out!
Rob Wealth! If you cannot call what is yours your own, it will be taken!
What's so special about one little blade of grass?
At those words, the light of [乙] visibly weakened. Yeoni looked down at the trembling shoot.
A tiny thing that seemed ready to snap underfoot or blow away in a single gust. And yet its leaves still trembled with life.
It may be small, but it's mine.
The fading light of [乙] revived. The reflected Yeoni's eyebrow twitched.
Even if it looks weak, it's mine. It doesn't need your stamp of approval to belong to me.
The flower on Yeoni's head bloomed brightly. Green vines shot out beneath their hooves.
The vines threaded among mirror fragments and coiled around each incoming blade. Clatter! The blades stopped dead in midair.
...Good.
Huh? What did I just do?
You used Eul.
Oh, did I get a skill? Have I awakened?
Something like that.
Can I name it? I was thinking 'Little Sprout, Please Hang In There.'
Not now. And not that name, ever.
Why so firm? Show some respect for my naming sense.
Then how about 'Weed'? Short, punchy, easy to remember.
No.
An oink escaped Yeoni's nostrils in protest. Nobody took their side.
The reflected Yeoni clenched their teeth. For the first time, unease crossed the formerly relaxed face.
...It isn't over yet.
The other Yeoni lowered a hand, and the final mirror drifted forward. It was different from the rest.
Black water filled it. This time, even Yeoni could not bluff.
The water lay perfectly quiet, without a single ripple. That stillness only made it more chilling.
Eul alone does not complete Eulhae.
...Is that Hae?
Yes. Hae is deep water. Midwinter water. On the surface, still as though frozen, but holding a great deal within.
The black water in the mirror slowly stirred. From its depths came a muffled voice.
[ ...Come down. ]

Yeoni stiffened. This was unlike the black hands that had chased them across the river. Not an enemy attacking from outside, but something quietly calling from within. Deep, cold feelings they kept wanting to avoid.
You can't go in there.
...Why?
You hate going deep.
Yeoni had no immediate comeback. No wisecrack, no meme, nothing.
When your thoughts get heavy, you deliberately change the subject. You act funny because you're afraid you'll fall apart alone. And you only admit what really hurts long after it happens.
That water has been inside you from the beginning.

Scenes rose in the black water. A night waiting for a reply. A long message finished but never sent. A chat closed and muted while pretending not to care. A face staring at the ceiling, alone in bed in a dark room.
Yeoni's breath caught. It hurt more than anything the reflection had said. Because all of it was real. Not one detail embellished.
You found Eul. But if you turn away from Hae, your Eulhae Day Pillar will remain incomplete.
...What happens then?
You reclaim only half of your center. You return to reality incomplete.
Yeoni stared at the last mirror. Black water. Deep water. Somewhere at its bottom, the second character waited quietly.
Yeoni tightened their hooves. Still no fingers. But now they thought they understood a little. Fingers were not the only way to hold on to something.
You can't go.
Why do you keep telling me what I can't do?
Because you're afraid.
Does being afraid mean I can't do it?
You... always let it.
I told you not to say things like that with my face.
Why? Because it's true?
No. It being true makes it even more annoying.
The reflected Yeoni thrust out a hand. Black water spilled over the final mirror's frame. A roaring rush covered the corridor floor in an instant.
Yeoni tried to dodge, too late. Cold water wrapped around their short hooves and climbed above their ankles.
Yeongnyangi!
Yeongnyangi leaped. His claws blazed gold and cleaved the black water vertically. It parted, then rejoined as though nothing had happened.
Cutting won't work on this!
Then what am I supposed to do!
Do not run!
If I don't run now, I'm going under!
Run, and it grows deeper!
The reflected Yeoni stood on top of the black water, shoes dry, not even a toe wet.
Exactly. Run, and it gets deeper. Just like you've always done.

The black water dragged Yeoni's round body downward. They dug their clawless hooves against the floor. But their body was small and their strength insufficient. They were afraid. Real fear, the kind no joke could cover.
[ Come down. Stop pretending you're fine. Look at the feelings you buried. ]
Yeoni squeezed their eyes shut. At that moment, warmth spread inside a hoof. The [乙] they had just reclaimed. The warmth of a tiny shoot.
Yeoni opened their eyes. A green vine grew beneath their hoof again. But it did not push back the black water. Instead, it rooted itself in the water.
Yes! That's it!
Are you sure? I'm putting roots into the water right now!
Eul does not grow by avoiding water. It takes water in and grows!
Why are you only giving me the instruction manual now!
Because you only just showed me!
The vine was thin. A flick of a fingertip looked enough to snap it. Yet even when black water crashed over it, it bent once, then stubbornly lifted its head again.
Yeoni caught their breath at the sight. Small. Apparently weak. Yet alive. Just like Yeoni right now.
Stop.
No.
Yeoni planted their hooves more firmly. From below, the vine's roots held the body the current kept pushing away.
I'm still scared. But you taking my name because I'm scared—I hate that more.
The black water surged. Inside the last mirror, a single character appeared faintly, like water mist.

Still far away. Too deep to reach with an outstretched hoof. But clearly visible. The flower above Yeoni's head trembled. The shoot of [乙] was carefully sinking its roots toward the black water of [亥].
Stop it!
The reflected Yeoni shouted for the first time. There was no ease left in that voice.
A huge wave rose inside the final mirror. Black water towered like a wall and yanked Yeoni forward.
Grab me!
Yeongnyangi rushed over and caught Yeoni's hoof in his mouth. It did not hurt. But the water was too strong. The white cat's small body was dragged along too.
Then go down there yourself.
The last mirror swung wide like a door. Black water poured like a waterfall. Yeoni gritted their teeth and held on. At last, their entire body was sucked forward.
OINK—AAAAH!
This time it was not an act. Not a comic snort, but a scream of genuine fright.
Don't let go of your name! Hold on to Eul!
Yeoni gripped the warmth inside their hoof with everything they had. There were no fingers. Still, they held tight in their heart.
Just before being pulled under, Yeoni caught one last glimpse of the human standing outside the mirror. The reflection was smiling. But there was no confidence left in that smile.
Let's see whether you can still say you're yourself, even in the deep water.
Yeoni fell endlessly through the black water. The flower on their head shone brightly one final time.
And in the deepest darkness, the second character, asleep until now, quietly opened its eyes.
[ The Abyss of Hae Water was opening. ]

episodes.title: The Abyss of Hae Water
episodes.tag: Episode 4 · The Abyss of Hae Water

beats.t: Splash. Their feet broke the surface. Then the world folded into blackness.
Cold, black, endless water. Strangely, Yeoni could breathe. That made it more frightening. Rather than falling, they were sinking very slowly, as though suspended in empty air.
My body's a feather, so why does my heart weigh a ton?
Only the small flower on their head shone like a living light beneath the water. Yeoni tried to clench a hoof. It still did not work well, but the warmth within it was distinct.
That little shoot. You're still here.
Yeongnyangi! Yeongnyangi, where are you!
No answer. Only black ripples moving slowly, without a word.
Above and below were equally dark. Distant lights drifted like old memories. Unread messages. Unsent sentences. Swallowed words. Moments when tears had risen, only to be laughed away.
They swam past Yeoni like little fish. Each brush of a fin chilled their skin.
Uh, that fish just swam past with something I'll cringe about in bed! Hey, that's my likeness! Get away!
What is this place... cloud storage for every embarrassing moment of my life?
Let me cancel the subscription. I only wanted the free trial.
A little bubble slipped out after the words. Blub. But there was writing inside it.
[ I'm fine. ]
The bubble did not rise. Instead, it sank heavily into the black water.
Hey, why is 'I'm fine' going down? Shouldn't it float if it's fine?
I'd like to file a bug report. Nothing in the terms said 'I'm fine will sink.' Did anyone QA this before release?
As though answering, more bubbles appeared in a string.
[ It's nothing. ]   [ I'm really fine. ]   [ I don't care. ]   [ Lol, I said I'm okay. ]
Yeoni's face stiffened. Every word was one they had said.
More precisely, words they used only on days when they were not fine at all.
One by one, the bubbles stuck to Yeoni's body. Then suddenly grew heavy as weights.
Wait, wait! What's happening!
Front legs! Back legs! Why are you all doing your own thing? A little teamwork!
All four short legs thrashed wildly underwater. Yet their body did not move forward an inch.
Pff—just inhaled a bucket through my nose. This pig snout has premium suction, I'll give it that.
This body is a complete package of defects. What kind of pig can't swim?
The flower overhead flickered. A green vine unfurled from inside a hoof. The power of Eul.
The vine pushed through the water. But the black water was too deep. Before long, it stopped.
Its tip wavered aimlessly, as though it did not know where to root.
I told you.
The reflected Yeoni emerged through the black ripples. Still human. Not wet, not a single hair out of place. So perfectly untouched it was chilling.
This is somewhere you can't enter.
How are you staying dry underwater? Waterproof coating?
Because I do not waver.
Wow, you are seriously obnoxious.
An involuntary snort bubbled from Yeoni's indignant nose. Oink. Half the menace vanished from the expression they had worked so hard to make.
That's your way of talking too.
...I've copyrighted that line. Stop using it.
The reflected Yeoni circled slowly, as though walking on level ground. Black water parted gently beneath each step.
This is the Abyss of Hae.
I know. Yeongnyangi told me.
Then you should understand. Eul is a shoot that needs water to live. But do you know what you're worst at in the world?
Yeoni could not answer. They opened their mouth, then closed it.
Going deep.
The reflected Yeoni flicked a finger, and a scene appeared in the black water like a strip of film.
Yeoni lying in bed with a phone. A chat with no reply. One sentence, written and erased, then written and erased again.
[ Actually... I was a little hurt. ]
The sentence never sent. It was erased, leaving only a cursor, then became a bubble and sank. Yeoni's throat tightened. It was that sentence, not the water, that made breathing hard.
Stop.
Why? It's your memory.
Another scene. Yeoni smiling brightly in front of friends.
“Oh, it's fine. I don't care about that sort of thing.”
Their face in profile as they turned away. The corners of their mouth were raised, but their eyes were not smiling at all.
The next scene. Dawn, after an entire assignment they had worked on all night vanished. Yeoni gave a small, lonely laugh at the empty screen.
“Wow. Legendary. My life really is a variety show.”
A few seconds later, the smile quietly disappeared. The sound of typing in the room stopped too.
The next scene. A text saying an interview was canceled. The message Yeoni sent a friend afterward.
“Lmao, my luck is wrecked again today lol.”
But below it, one sentence remained gray, its send button never pressed.
[ Honestly, I'm a little scared. What if things keep going this wrong? ]
Yeoni closed their eyes. They thought they had brushed it off. Thought laughter had carried them past it. But everything was here. Settled at the bottom of the black water, not one thing erased.
You always stop your sentences with laughter. You could say it hurts when it hurts, but you have to crack a joke first.
...Is that so bad?
Not bad. It's even funny.
But you never listen to your own feelings. Not once.
Yeoni had no answer. The black water grew heavy again. Bubbles clung all over their body.
[ I'm fine. ]   [ It's nothing. ]   [ I don't care. ]   [ That's just how I am. ]
Each bubble looked light as a feather. But the more that stuck, the heavier they became. Yeoni's body was dragged down and down.
Hey, dragging me to the deep sea for pretending I'm fine is a bit much, isn't it!
Pretending to be fine is the thing that sinks best.
Stop making quotable lines. I'm annoyed enough without you publishing a collection.
Then a very faint voice came from far away, as though descending from the surface.
Yeoni.

Far overhead, gold shimmered in the black water. Yeongnyangi. Unable to enter, he could only scrape the ripples with his claws from above. The Abyss of Hae Water was sealed water; outside power could not easily reach within.
Yeongnyangi! I'm completely submerged here! I don't even know which basement floor this is!
Don't push the water away! First, relax your body!
Then what? Introduce myself and tell the water I look forward to working together?
Introductions can wait.
Eul is Wood that grows by drinking water!
You already said that! Enough reruns!
Don't just think about it. Let your body feel the water!
The black water kept dragging Yeoni down. A vast pattern became faintly visible at the bottom. Curling waves. One character hidden at the center of their whirlpool.
Hae. But it was still on the bottom, beyond reach.
You can't go.
Is that seriously the only thing you can say?
I say you can't because you can't.
Ugh, brutal truths delivered with my own face are twice as infuriating.
My face, my voice, my way of talking. You have no idea how it feels to get beaten up by a whole matching set of facts.
Then prove it.
The reflected Yeoni reached out. The light of [乙] in Yeoni's hoof flickered like a candle.
However tightly you hold Eul, you cannot complete Eulhae without accepting Hae.
A flower cannot live without water. But you hate your own water.
My water?
Your deepest feelings. Those sentences you erase after watching the cursor blink.
Another scene appeared in the dark water. An unlit room. Yeoni sat alone, fiddling with a phone as though nothing was wrong. But the screen was off.
They were not looking at anything. Only staring blankly at their face reflected in the black screen. The Yeoni in that scene did not say one word. The silence hurt more than any scream.
Back then, I...
The words caught in their throat and never reached the end.
You were lonely.
The black water surged once.
And scared.
Another surge.
But you didn't tell anyone. Not a single person.
Bubbles rushed in all at once and enclosed Yeoni completely. The water rose to their neck.
[ I'm fine. ]   [ I can do it alone. ]   [ It doesn't bother me. ]   [ That's how it is for everyone. ]
Yeoni took a deep breath. Air came even underwater, but the center of their chest was blocked tight. That pressure was not the weight of water. It was the weight of everything endured for too long.
...Yes.
The bubbles stopped dead. The reflected Yeoni stopped circling too. Yeoni slowly raised their head and touched their chest with a wet hoof. Their heart was beating there.
I wasn't fine.
The words spread in rings through the water. One bubble burst. Pop.
[ I'm fine. ] ...Gone
I said it was nothing. But to me, it really was something.
Another burst. Pop.
[ It's nothing. ] ...Gone
I said I didn't care. Actually, it was all I thought about every night.
Pop. The black water grew a little lighter. A layer of weight lifted from their shoulders.
[ I don't care. ] ...Gone

Yeoni closed their eyes. This next sentence was the one they did not want to say. Speaking it felt as though it would make it real. But swallowing it felt as though they would remain on this bottom forever. Yeoni opened their eyes.
I was scared.
The entire black water heaved. For the first time, the reflected Yeoni's expression fell away.
I was scared things would keep going wrong. Scared I'd done something terribly wrong without knowing it.
I thought laughing it off would make me really okay. But I wasn't okay, and that scared me even more.
Bubbles began bursting everywhere. Pop. Pop. Pop. With each one, another small stretch of water cleared.
The character [亥] at the bottom sharpened, as though someone had wiped fog from glass.
Stop.
No.
Inside Yeoni's hoof, [乙] glowed warmly like a hand warmer. A green vine grew again.
This time it did not repel the water. It did not run. The vine slowly put down roots into the black depths, then trembled just a little, as though drinking water for the first time.

Yeoni felt it throughout their body. Not all the cold water was an enemy. It held loneliness, fear, words never sent. But it was not only water that meant to kill them. Because it existed, this tiny shoot could drink and grow.
Yes. ...That's it.
Hae is not water that exists to drown you. It holds a place where your roots can endure.
My roots...

The words landed strangely beneath Yeoni's ribs. They had always pretended to be bright, lighthearted, untroubled. Underneath, deep water had always gathered. Tiresome, heavy, cold water. Yet there were roots inside it.
Yeoni stretched out a hoof. The vine of [乙] reached straight toward [亥] at the bottom.
No! If you accept that—
I'll become more real than you?
The reflected Yeoni shut their mouth. Seeing that silence, Yeoni gave a little laugh.
Okay. No response means I got it right.
The vine's tip touched [亥]. A huge ripple spread in circles through the black water.
Cold water wrapped around Yeoni. But this time it did not drag them down. Instead, it lifted them as gently as two hands.
The character [亥] slowly rose. The black water turned the indigo of a deep sea at night. Within it, small stars lit one by one.
...Beautiful.

For the first time, Yeoni thought so. Water that had only frightened them began to look different. Cold, but clear. Dark, but not empty. It held memories, feelings, wounds, and a heart that had survived them all.
The flower above Yeoni's head opened fully. Two characters floated side by side before them, shining.
...The Eulhae Day Pillar.
As the words fell, the two characters joined in a single light. A green shoot rooted itself upon the deep water.
Then a small flower bloomed in the center of the black abyss. Absurdly small, but undeniably alive.
Yeoni held their breath at the flower. It looked just like them. Still weak, still small, still terribly frightened—yet alive.

Yeongnyangi's voice poured down from above. Golden claws parted the surface. Light rushed in like a waterfall. Yeoni rose. This time, instead of pulling them under, the water pushed their back upward.
You think finding Hae means it's over?
Probably not. Yeah, figured as much.
The Island of Companions isn't finished. Finding your roots and defending your place are entirely different things.
Then I'll go up and do that too. I'm starting to get the hang of this tutorial.
A tiny snort escaped at the end of the boast. Oink.
...Okay, I am still not used to that.
Light burst. Whoosh! Yeoni shot through the Abyss of Hae Water and rolled across the Island of Companions. Droplets flew everywhere.
Ow... Zero points for that landing.
...Still alive?
Yeoni slowly got up. The flower on their head shone incomparably more clearly than before. A blue wave pattern curled gently beneath it.
Eul and Hae have connected.
[ 乙亥 · Eulhae ]
They were no longer merely two characters. A small flower and deep water. A heart that wavered but did not die. The self that smiled brightly while carrying so much far beneath the surface.
Turns out I'm a more complicated type than I thought.
Only just realizing that?
Yep. But being complicated doesn't mean I'll give that fake my place. Not a chance.
All the island's mirrors shone together. The reflected Yeoni slowly walked out of the water.
The atmosphere was different this time. Black mirror fragments gathered beneath those feet. The eyes were colder, the voice lower.
Fine. ...Now let's begin the real test.
What? There's still another test?
Hey, when do the credits roll in this game? You keep inserting trials like paid DLC at every stage.
You have found Eulhae. But the Island of Companions insists on testing whether you can defend those characters too.

The reflected Yeoni raised a hand. Countless mirror shards floated behind like a folding screen. Each reflected a different Yeoni. Jealous Yeoni. Giving-up Yeoni. Yeoni comparing themself to others. Yeoni forcing a smile. Yeoni unable to trust even themself.
Come on, then. This time you must fight all those selves you believe you've already defeated.
Yeoni drew breath. A moment ago, fear would have come first. They were still afraid. But it was not quite the same fear. Eul's warmth rested in their hooves; Hae's water gathered deep in their chest.
Okay.
Yeoni looked their reflection straight in the eyes. The flower above their head shone brightly.
I just went all the way down to the abyss, you know. I've had a pretty major mental patch update.
The reflected Yeoni smiled without a sound.
[ Island of Companions · Final Trial Begins ]

episodes.title: The Selves on My Side
episodes.tag: Episode 5 · The Selves on My Side

beats.t: The air in the mirror corridor grew heavy. Yeoni had barely dried off after the Abyss of Hae Water. Yet the reflected Yeoni before them was already raising a hand.
Countless mirror shards rose behind the reflection. Each held a different face of Yeoni.
Angry Yeoni. Giving-up Yeoni. Yeoni comparing themself to others. Yeoni smiling as though everything was fine. Yeoni with a face that said they could do nothing.
And yet another Yeoni, looking thoroughly sick of watching all those selves.
Wow. I have more release versions than I thought. Someone should have tidied up the updates.
This is the final trial on the Island of Companions.
At least tell me the name of the test. Let me prepare myself before I die.
At that moment, words appeared in the center of the corridor.

[ Island of Companions · Final Trial ]
[ Distinguish those who share your face. ]
[ Make Friends your allies; sever Rob Wealth. ]
Hold on. Why this sudden difficulty spike with no tutorial?
When energy like yours supports you, it takes the face of Friend. When it covets your share, it takes the face of Rob Wealth. Here, you must see that difference yourself.
So they both have my face, but one's on my side and the other's a fraud trying to steal my place?
Yes. But both wear your face. Don't be fooled by appearances.
Wow, innovative game design. Enemies and allies use the same skin. Would it kill you to add friendly-fire protection?
Yeoni scanned the mirror shards. Every face was theirs. Every expression too. Their throat grew dry. What were they supposed to use to tell them apart?
It won't be easy.
The reflected Yeoni snapped their fingers lightly. Click.
The angry-faced Yeoni came forward first. Arms folded, foot tapping the ground, glaring.
“You always hold everything in, then explode too late over the wrong thing.”
Hey. Opening with a brutal truth is cheating.
“You could say you don't like something right there. Instead, you act fine, then go home and kick your blankets alone.”
Stop. I just came out of the abyss after swallowing all that water. My mental state is still soggy.
“So you're going to cover it with another joke?” Yeoni shut their mouth. A reply stuck in their throat.
In the gap left by Yeoni's silence, black mirror fragments grew like thorns beneath the angry self's feet.
Careful. Now it is trying to take your share too.
Wasn't that one on my side? Everything it just said was true.
It is cornering you with truths so it can take your place. That is Rob Wealth.
Angry Yeoni smiled sharply. “So I'll speak for you. You can't do it anyway.”
Red glass fragments shot from those fingertips like arrows. Yeongnyangi sprang up to block them. Clang!
Yeoni, pull yourself together!
I know, I know!
Yeoni planted their hooves firmly. The energy of [乙] warmed their chest. Green vines sprouted beneath their feet.
But Angry Yeoni did not stop. “You're always late. Late getting angry, late speaking up, late making every decision.”
Yeoni clenched their teeth. It hurt more because it was not wrong. A hot pressure tightened beneath their ribs.
But this time, they did not want to turn and run.
...You're right. I blow up too late a lot. I won't deny it.
Angry Yeoni's eyes wavered, as though that answer had been unexpected.
But I don't want you exploding for me.
Because then those aren't my words. There's a voice, but I'm not in it.
Yeoni stepped into the path of the flying red shards.
Being angry isn't bad. But stealing my mouth and shouting for me—that isn't being on my side.
The red glass fragments trembled in midair, losing speed.
You can be on my side. But not in a way that makes me disappear.
Angry Yeoni's face stiffened. The black shards underfoot melted away. The red light softened, as though folding away its thorns.
“Then... don't just keep holding it in,” Angry Yeoni murmured.
Okay. Next time I'll say it there and then, so I don't end up kicking my blankets. I'll practice.
Angry Yeoni dissolved into red light. The light became a small red mirror shard and quietly settled beside Yeoni.
It has turned toward Friend. You have gained an ally.
Oh. Did I just catch my first Pokémon? Felt like throwing a Poké Ball.
As Yeoni fluttered their hooves excitedly, their flat nostrils puffed out a snort all by themselves. Oink. A pale streak of breath fogged the corridor, then dispersed.
...Do not understand it that way.
They are not Pokémon. They neither run away nor evolve.
But thinking of it that way suddenly makes this feel manageable.
The next to come forward was Giving-up Yeoni. No, not come forward. Still slumped on the floor, that self merely raised its head. Its eyes were empty.
“You don't have to try. It's only going to fail again.”
Yeoni's heart dropped. That voice was too familiar. The exhaustion before even beginning. Nights spent folding hopes away early, afraid hope would only make it hurt more.
“You know it too. The more you hope, the more exhausting it gets.”
...Yeah. I know. Painfully well.
“Then just let it go.” Gray mirror fragments floated around that self. Each reflected a moment when Yeoni had given up.
An application closed just before clicking Submit. A message fully written, then erased. Fingers turning a screen facedown at dawn as though it meant nothing.
“No expectations, no disappointment.” The words were strangely sweet. A promise not to hurt. Yeoni's feet slipped back for a moment.
Then blue ripples curled beneath the flower on their head. The energy of [亥]. Deep water. A heart that might sink, but never quite disappear.
But I... I've given up early to avoid being disappointed so many times.
Giving-up Yeoni slowly raised its head.
It was easier then. For that one moment.
The gray shards trembled like ripples.
But trying and failing hurts for a few days, then ends. Not trying follows me for years. Every time I lie down at night, it comes back.
Giving-up Yeoni's face twisted. “...But it's still scary.”
Yes. I'm scared right now. My hooves are shaking.
But I don't want you folding away my choices just because I'm afraid. If I'm going to fold them away, I'll do it myself.
One by one, the gray shards lost their strength and fell. “Then... what about when it's really hard?”
Then let's rest.
“...Instead of giving up?”
Yes. Resting and giving up. Let's start telling those apart, you and me.
Giving-up Yeoni watched silently for a long time. Then nodded, slowly, very slowly. Gray changed to silver. A small silver shard flew over to join Yeoni.
Your second Friend.
Second... Is this a loyalty card? Collect ten and get a free gift?
Is this really a trial? It feels like paid therapy right now.
The Island of Companions is where you sort through the energies like yourself within you.
Then give the service a softer name. That was practically personal training at a mental gym. And I haven't even paid membership fees.
There are no fees. But neither can you leave halfway through.
Then the reflected Yeoni clapped. Clap. Clap. Clap. Three slow beats.
Touching. I nearly cried.
But tell me. Do you really think all of them can be on your side?
This time, dozens of mirror shards rushed forward at once. Comparing Yeoni. Jealous Yeoni. Forced-smile Yeoni. Yeoni belittling themself.

“They can do it. Why can't you?” “Pretend you're fine. Don't ruin the mood.” “You've always been unlucky.” “Don't get your hopes up.” “Step forward for nothing and you'll only embarrass yourself more.”
Voices poured in from everywhere at once. Yeoni wanted to cover both ears. But their blunt hooves let all the sound through.
Oh, come on! This is a group chat blowing up at three in the morning!
Can't mute it, can't leave. This is mandatory participation!
Of course. They're all you.
The voices swelled. “Compare yourself.” “Hide it.” “Give up.” “Just laugh it off.” “There was never a place for you to begin with.”
The flower on Yeoni's head shook precariously. The green light of [乙] dimmed. Even the ripples of [亥] roiled black.
Yeongnyangi stepped in front and sliced the fragments away. Clang, clang, clang. But they multiplied faster than he could cut them down.
Yeoni, don't fight them one at a time! You'll be buried!
Then what do I do! They all have my face. I don't know where to start!
Set a standard!
A standard? What standard!
The voice that protects you, and the voice that takes you away. Divide them by that alone!
Yeoni caught their breath. The protective voice and the taking voice. Those two phrases clicked together in their mind like a lock.
Suddenly, the mirror shards that had looked identical began to look a little different.
Angry Yeoni had really been shouting for them to speak. Giving-up Yeoni had really been whispering that it was all right to rest.
But Comparing Yeoni kept cutting them smaller. Forced-smile Yeoni erased them from the spot. Self-belittling Yeoni quietly left their chair empty.
Yeoni stamped a hoof firmly into the ground.
Okay. Time to sort this out.
The flower overhead brightened green again.
Those of you trying to protect me, come over here.
Green vines opened a path to Yeoni's right. The red and silver shards settled side by side along it.
And those of you who keep eating away at me—
Yeoni looked straight at the reflection.
Stay exactly where you are.
Hmm. You think you can tell the difference?
I'm starting to get the idea. Can't guarantee my accuracy, though.
What if you're wrong?
Then I'll learn again. Retaking classes is my specialty.
I'm not someone who always chooses perfectly. But now I won't mistake every voice I hear for my own.
With those words, the light of [乙亥] appeared before Yeoni. A green shoot rooted itself upon deep water. The water was dark but clear; the shoot small but firm.
Yeoni reached a hoof toward the light.
No!

The reflected Yeoni swung a hand. The shards of Comparing Yeoni, Forced-smile Yeoni, and Self-belittling Yeoni fused into one mass. A huge hand of black glass was born. It reached to seize all of [乙亥].
Yeoni.
I know. I see it!
Little Sprout, Hang In There! Just three seconds!
...Are you settling on that name?
Names later! This is urgent!
Green vines burst outward and wrapped tightly around the black glass hand. But the hand was too large. The vines stretched taut, creaking as though about to snap.
Yeoni slid backward. Their hooves scraped the floor.
Aagh, is this strength gap real? Somebody patch the balance!
See? You're weak in the end. You always were.
Being weak and losing are completely different things.
The water of [亥] moved. Deep water flowed into the base of the vines and supported their roots from below. The vines thickened, blue seeping into their green light.
Eulhae has connected! Now, Yeoni!
Yeoni slammed their outstretched hoof down with all their strength.
Get out of my place!
