The vines constricted the black glass hand. Crack. A hairline split appeared across its back. For the first time, the reflection's face hardened.
Yes, I waver! I admit it!
Crack. Fractures spread like a web.
But me wavering doesn't give you the right to live my life for me!
Crash! The black glass hand shattered. The mirrors of comparison, forced smiles, and self-belittlement broke with it. Their fragments scattered into black dust.
Only a few shards remained. The angry self's red shard. The silver one that said resting was allowed. And a small blue shard, newly born.
...Well done. I mean that.
I really did well, right? Confirm it for me.
Yes. You did well.
Okay. Save this moment. I don't get many scenes like this in life.
Overcome with delight, Yeoni threw up their hooves. Their short hind legs lost balance, and they toppled sideways. The cool pose had lasted exactly three sentences.
Yeongnyangi shook his head silently. Then another message appeared in the center of the corridor.

[ Friend classification complete ]
[ Rob Wealth purification in progress ]
[ Eulhae Day Pillar recovery: 87% ]
Wait. Why isn't it 100%? I just cleared it!
The reflected Yeoni smiled slowly. That self had not disappeared. It stood calmly on the broken mirror fragments, looking down at Yeoni.
Of course.
I'm the final Rob Wealth.
A chill ran down Yeoni's spine. Wings of black mirror spread wide behind the reflection. Every feather held a face.
Faces Yeoni had envied. People they had secretly compared themself to. Selves they wished to become. And the versions of their own face they hated most in the world.
To defeat me, you don't have to break me.
The reflection pointed a fingertip at the center of its chest.
You have to take me back inside you.
...What? What does that mean?
I'm the self you threw away. Destroy me, and part of you disappears too.
Yeoni searched for a rebuttal and found none. Beside them, Yeongnyangi's expression had hardened too.
Yeoni.
...Yes.
This is the true final trial.
Yeoni faced the self in the mirror. A human face. An apparently flawless expression. And curled inside the smile, a force that stole. Rob Wealth.
Okay. So, basically... this is the final boss fight.
Yes. You finally caught on.
The whole island shook again. One final sentence appeared over the corridor.

[ Final Rob Wealth Battle ]
[ Reclaim the self in the mirror. ]
Reclaim. You make it sound so easy.
If you run, it will take your entire place.
Then what if I just fight and smash it?
If all you do is destroy it, you lose part of yourself too.
Then what's the answer? Give me a hint.
...Make it yours. Do not push it away. Embrace it.

Yeoni looked at the reflection for a long time. The reflection looked back in the same way. One human, one flower pig. Completely different faces, yet their eyes resembled each other a little more than before.
I really do make being me difficult.
...You can say that again.
This reply held no mockery. For one brief moment, the blink of an eye, they looked like the same person sharing the same exhaustion.
Then the reflected Yeoni spread its black wings and lunged.
[ Island of Companions · Final Battle Begins ]

episodes.title: Beyond the Mirror, I Know Myself
episodes.tag: Episode 6 · Beyond the Mirror, I Know Myself

beats.t: The reflected Yeoni spread black wings. Not feathers, but layers of broken mirror shards fitted together.
Every shard reflected Yeoni's face. Comparing Yeoni, Jealous Yeoni, Giving-up Yeoni.
Yeoni smiling as though everything was fine. And Yeoni unable to believe in themself.
Wow... I really have a crowded inner staff.
And everyone's more expressive than me. It feels unfair that the original looks the most miserable.
Focus. All of those are Rob Wealth, shaking your place.
But they look like me.
That makes them more dangerous.
Unauthorized use of my face, and unauthorized duplication too. Where do I report a likeness violation?
The reflected Yeoni slowly rose. As the shards behind it rotated, the whole island trembled like a bell.
[ Island of Companions · Final Trial ]
[ Reclaim the self in the mirror. ]
[ On failure, return-to-reality rights will transfer to Mirror Yeoni. ]
Hold on. Transfer of rights?
Yes. Your life account, my login.
That's insane. This is straight-up account theft.
Something like that.
No two-factor authentication?
There was.
The reflected Yeoni pointed to the flower on Yeoni's head.
The Eulhae you just found.
Yeoni held on again to the warmth in their hooves. Eul, a small shoot. Hae, deep water. Both shone faintly, still not fully one.
But it isn't at 100% yet.
A number appeared in the air.
[ Eulhae Day Pillar recovery: 87% ]
Why 87%, specifically? Such an awkward number to make someone anxious.
Eighty-seven percent complete. Like that download bar that looks nearly done but never finishes. That's this.
The last 13% remains.
What is it?
That apparition.
Exactly. Reclaim me, and it's complete.
You?
I'm the you that you cut away because you didn't want to acknowledge it.
So I don't have to beat you...
You have to take me back. Can you do that?
The words were strangely chilling. Breaking it would have been easier. Call it a fake and smash it. But take it back? Let it into themself?
That face was infuriating, its words obnoxious. It picked out every part Yeoni wanted to flee and jabbed at it. Yet in the end, it too was Yeoni.
I really do make my own life difficult.
You do.
The wings spread wide, and black fragments rained down.
Get back!
Golden claws cut the air. Clang, clang, clang. Shards bounced away in every direction.
But broken fragments rejoined. Cut one and there were two; cut two and there were four.
Why are they multiplying?
The more they take, the more they grow. Cutting alone won't end this.
Why are you telling me that now!
Because I'm seeing it now!
Even rolling is hard with legs this short! I'll plant my nose in the ground trying to retreat!
The reflected Yeoni lowered a hand. This time the fragments converged on Yeoni, not Yeongnyangi.
You're late. You're weak. You're always pretending to smile.
There's no place for you. If you can't do it, I will.
The voices burrowed into their ears together. Words Yeoni thought had vanished in Hae's abyss returned. Pretending to be fine. Laughing it off. Running away.
See? You're still wavering.
Yeoni planted a hoof on the ground.
Am I not allowed to waver?
The reflection's eyebrow rose slightly.
You said I'm Eul Wood. A little plant. Isn't swaying normal, then?
...It is.
Wavering doesn't make me fake.
Eul's light strengthened. Green vines grew beneath Yeoni's hooves. Instead of breaking the shards, they bound them tightly and lowered them to the floor one by one. Clatter.
Why aren't you breaking them?
You said that only makes more of you. So I'll tie them up.
Using your brain, are you?
I do use my brain, you know.
Then why were you always late?
That one hurts. Let's discuss it in counseling later.
Talk after we get out. Move now.
I know.
Yeoni planted their hooves more firmly. Blue ripples of Hae spread beneath the floor, supporting the vines' roots. The green vines thickened.

Before, Yeoni would have covered their wavering heart with jokes and pretended to be fine. But that wavering heart and that deep water were both part of them. The flower could live only if they did not push the water away.
Then what about this?
A vast mirror rose behind the reflected Yeoni. Yeoni's reality appeared inside. Their room, a phone on the bed, the Code Destiny app open.
A human Yeoni sat before it, with the same face as the reflection. Yeoni stopped breathing.
What is that?
Synchronization.
[ Connecting to return-to-reality protocol ]
[ Candidate: Yeoni / Candidate: Mirror Yeoni ]
[ Original identity verification remaining: 13% ]
While you hesitate here, I can connect to the real world first.
So it really is account theft!
I told you. If you can't do it, I will.
The Yeoni in the mirrored reality picked up the phone. An [Approve Return] button appeared. Yeoni tried to rush forward, but black shards blocked the way.
No!
Why? You still hate that body.
The reflection pointed to Yeoni's flower-pig body.
Who would recognize you if you returned to reality?
The words were sharp. Pink body, short legs, a flower overhead. The present Yeoni was so unlike the Yeoni of the real world.
If I go back, nobody will think anything is wrong. I have your face.
The Yeoni in the mirrored room placed a finger over the button. Yeoni's flower shook. The light of Eulhae shook too.
Yeoni.
Yeoni closed their mouth. It was not wrong. Same face, voice, memories. A Yeoni who never wavered or ran late might be better. For one very brief moment, that thought occurred.
But then they remembered what they had seen in Hae's abyss. Nights pretending to be fine. Unsent words. Feelings endured alone. And the small flower that had bloomed in that deep water.
Yeoni slowly breathed in.
No.
No what?
You are my face.
The flower shone overhead. Vines extended beneath their hooves.
You know my voice and my memories. But you don't know why I laughed.
What?
Why I pretended I was fine. Why I couldn't speak. Why I was late. Why I fell apart alone.
Blue ripples flowed beneath the vines.
You only recite it like a correct answer. You don't feel the pain. That's why you aren't me.
The airborne mirrors shook. In the mirror of reality, the [Approve Return] button flickered.
Then what am I?
The question sounded angry, but also a little hurt. Yeoni caught that note and stepped forward.
You're the me I tried to throw away.
The me that pretends to be perfect. The me that pretends not to be hurt.
The me that tried to stand there looking okay in my place.
Then break me!
The black mirror wings spread wide.
You have to break me to win!
The fragments rushed in again. Yeongnyangi started forward, but Yeoni spoke first.
No.
Green vines grew like a wall. Instead of piercing the fragments, they enfolded them.
I won't break you.
What?
If I erase you, I'll just be pretending not to see the parts I wanted to throw away. Again.
The words echoed across the island. One by one, the mirrors stopped. For the first time, the reflected Yeoni had nothing to say.
Yeoni approached slowly. Honestly, they were afraid. The fake could attack at any moment. The return button still flashed; the wings were still sharp. Yet Yeoni did not stop.
The flower overhead shone. Eul was warm inside their hooves; Hae quietly supported them deep in their chest. Yeoni stopped before the reflection.
Human face and flower-pig face looked at one another.
If you accept me, you'll waver again.
I know.
You'll compare yourself again. Be jealous again. Pretend you're fine again.
Maybe I will.
Even so?
Even when that version of me appears, I won't pretend I don't know it anymore.
The reflection's eyes trembled. Yeoni held out a hoof.
So come on.
The reflected Yeoni looked down at it.
It's not even a hand.
Does that matter right now?
It is a little funny.
I know. Hurry up and take it. This is embarrassing.
The reflected Yeoni gave a tiny laugh. This time it was not mocking. A little irritating, a little tired, a little relieved. A laugh that truly sounded like Yeoni.
The reflection reached out. Its palm touched Yeoni's hoof.
The black wings scattered into fragments. Crash! But it did not hurt. It sounded like an old shell falling away.
The reflected Yeoni's body dissolved into light and slowly seeped into Yeoni.
Yeoni closed their eyes. The feelings of comparison, envy, wanting to do well, trying not to lose, pretending to be fine—all rushed in together.
They were strange and uncomfortable, yet all belonged to Yeoni. Instead of pushing them away, Yeoni simply breathed in. Like deep water. Then breathed out softly. The petals stirred.
[ Original identity verified: 100% · Return-to-reality rights: Yeoni ]
[ Island of Companions final trial complete ]
[ Rob Wealth purified · Friend fragments acquired ]
Congratulations, Yeoni.
Did you just say my name?
I knew it all along.
After treating me like a user this whole time?
Now there is no need to distinguish you.
Three of the broken shards flew before Yeoni. Red, silver, and blue.
These fragments will support you from within now. They have become Friends.
Items?
Closer to talismans.
Great. Into the inventory.
You won't find an inventory, however hard you look.
Ugh, seriously unfriendly UI.
Not unfriendly. Simply nonexistent.
The three shards circled the flower on Yeoni's head, then attached themselves like small petal ornaments. A red petal, a silver petal, a blue petal.
I feel kind of upgraded.
The power of Companions. Now, when you waver, you will be a little better at distinguishing the voices that support you from those that bring you down.
Oh. So I've got a mental filter now?
In very simple terms, yes.
Nice. Could've used that in everyday life too.
The whole island trembled. Mirrors rose into the sky; cracks opened in the black glass floor. Green and blue light rose together from beneath it.
Eulhae. Two characters floated before Yeoni, like a little shoot rooted in deep water. This time they did not feel strange. They felt like a name fitting exactly at the center of their heart.
The Eulhae Day Pillar.
The two characters seeped into their chest. Warmth and cold spread together. Strange, but not uncomfortable. The little flower bloomed more clearly.
[ Four Pillars characters recovered · Day Pillar: 乙亥 ]
[ Day Pillar imprinted · Eulhae no longer requires recovery ]
Did I really clear the first stage?
Yes. You passed the first gate.
What's the reward?
You just received it.
Anything more tangible? Coins, maybe?
No.
This world's economy needs work.
At least tell me where customer support is so I can request a refund. ...Oink.
Yeongnyangi sighed. But there was a very small smile at the corner of his mouth.
Then a sound came from far away. Boom. Boom. Boom. At first like a heartbeat, then a rhythm. A beat, music, cheering crowds.
Yeoni raised their head. Beyond the Island of Companions, now clear of mist, an entirely different island glittered. Colored lanterns, dancing shadows, delicious smells, songs rising into the sky.
Wait. What is that? It smells incredible over there.
My nose reacted first. My nostrils are flaring all by themselves. ...Oink.
The next island.
Does it have food?
Food, songs, and a stage.
Oh. Finally, the cozy part?
Yeongnyangi did not answer. His silence was a little ominous.
Why aren't you answering?
The Island of Expression.
Expression?
Expression, words, talent, the pleasure of eating, the power to create. An island of energy flowing from within you to the outside.
So an island for eating, talking, and singing?
Roughly.
Sounds good.
On the surface.
That tone again. You're making me nervous.
The lotus-leaf boat floated back onto the river. The Island of Companions slowly receded behind them.
At that moment, a black feather fell through the distant sky above the Island of Expression. As it landed on the highest stage, the music cut off abruptly.
...Not the cozy part, then?
Apparently not.
Yeoni felt Eulhae within their chest. A small shoot and deep water. Their center, just reclaimed. They lifted a short hoof.
Okay. Let's take the next road too.
Ready to go?
Yeoni looked at the Island of Expression. Still afraid, but less unsteady than before.
Yeah. But please tell me I won't have to go onstage in a pig's body this time.
Yeongnyangi did not answer.
Hey. Why aren't you answering?
You'll see when we arrive.
Now I'm really worried.
[ Entering Island Two · The Island of Eating God and Hurting Officer ]
The lotus-leaf boat glided toward song and light. And on the stage, the black feather still lay quietly.

The smell of fried sugar rushed at them as soon as they stepped off the lotus-leaf boat. Singing shops and plates tapping rhythms filled the alley. Yeoni found the food before their nose harder to believe than the mirror trial they had just finished. Hunger was the simplest proof of being alive.
Look at that. They're frying clouds. Actual clouds, and they don't disappear in the oil. Yeongnyangi, skip the explanation. Just tell me if I can eat them.
You can. But when you pay, watch what they take besides money. Especially if the first thing a shop says is that it's free.

A child was playing a small drum in the alley. People clapped, but their expressions vanished when the drumming stopped. Clear fragments piled up before the child instead of coins. In each, someone's smiling lips appeared briefly.
That isn't money. Are they giving away their smiles? The kid is entertaining, but shouldn't someone ask if they get those smiles back afterward?
No business would work if you got them back. The receiver feels good today; the giver gets a full stomach today. That's enough. Calculate tomorrow too, and you'll never buy anything.

The black tiger sat on a red rooftop awning. The ring mark on its forepaw was hidden under the cloak, but river sand still clung to the damp gold trim. Yeoni raised a hoof in greeting. Only after checking the surroundings did the tiger nod.
Is your paw okay? Won't you hurt it again climbing so high? Come down. I can't come rescue you all the way up there right now.
Do you always ask about wounds first when you meet someone again? More interested in what they hurt than what they gained? What an exhausting habit.

The tiger jumped down. An empty plate happened to be beneath it, but slid aside before its paw landed. Yeongnyangi noticed. Yeoni was watching only the child's drumsticks. The child gripped them so tightly that the handles dug into small palms.
Can't you rest? You've been playing the same song over and over. Your hands have been bleeding for a while. Getting applause doesn't have to hurt that much.

The child tried to stop, then resumed drumming. A tag hanging around their neck trembled. Small print on it said they had borrowed today's applause in advance. The line saying they could not leave the stage until it was repaid was on the back.
That child chose it. Rather than a song nobody heard, they wanted an audience even if it meant debt. Grant someone's wish and they always call you the villain afterward.
They wished for applause, not bleeding hands. Did you even give them time to read the back? Showing only the pretty front and calling it a choice is pretty underhanded, isn't it?

The tiger slowly flattened its ears. When Yeongnyangi moved in front of Yeoni, the tiger did not retreat. Instead, it pressed the red jewel at its throat with a paw. The child's drumming broke for a beat, then accelerated.
Don't touch that necklace, Yeoni. Break it by force here and you tear the child's voice, not the drum. Those who write these contracts always use the victim as a shield.
Then we can be the audience. Not borrowed applause—applause from people listening right now. Yeongnyangi, got any rhythm? If not, just match your paws to mine.

Yeoni tried to follow the quick drumbeat and fell twice. Onlookers laughed. They got up and tapped the ground again. Only after giving up on looking skilled could they properly hear the drum. The child always struggled most just before the chorus.
Rest here. I'll take that beat until you come back in. There's no line saying you have to do everything alone. If there is, show it to me now.

Two small hooves tapped the ground. A dull sound to call applause. Yet the child looked up for the first time. Someone was not waiting for the song to end, but stepping inside it to fill an empty space.
Count to three, then breathe. Keep hold of your own beat. If matching other people leaves you breathless, you can rest a moment.

Yeongnyangi's tail tapped the floor. Its slow, precise sound steadied the child's hands. One onlooker followed the same rhythm. Then two, three. The alley's sound gradually changed. Among purchased cheers, newly born applause began to mingle.
Why do they like such a mess? It's wrong. Missed beats, cracked voices. Worse than the arranged performance.
That kid just smiled at us. They know we're matching them. Being good at it can wait. Today, those hands need to rest first.

The tiger looked at the child's tag. The debt engraved on its front was fading stroke by stroke. Not because the borrowed applause had been repaid, but because borrowing was no longer necessary. That form of repayment did not appear in the ledger.

A black droplet sprang from the tiger's paw and struck the tag. The final line binding the child blurred. At the same moment, the tiny name on the tag's edge was sucked into the droplet. The child, catching their breath after setting down the drumsticks, did not see.
You just helped, didn't you? I saw it. Even if you tell me to pretend I didn't, I did. I'm saying thank you. Fold your ears if you don't want to hear it.
You saw what you wanted to see. You can take the child today. But leave the tag. I clear away the paperwork when accounts are settled.

The child broke a fried cloud in half. One half went to Yeoni; the other was placed before the tiger. The tiger looked first at the cut edges, as though measuring which portion was larger. The child smiled again without even looking at the sizes.
There's some for you too. No fine print on the back this time. Taste it. You can get angry if it's bad, though I didn't fry it, so I can't take responsibility.

The tiger took a bite. The child smiled and thanked it, unaware of what had been stolen. The tiger looked from that smile to Yeoni's. It did not take even a single ledger page to make them believe a debt had been erased.
Let's go, Yeoni. Leave someone who needs rest to rest. Keep demanding proof of what you've received, and even gratitude becomes a shackle.

Yeoni left the alley with the child. Yeongnyangi watched the tiger's paws to the last. When the droplet at its feet slipped behind the awning, his violet eyes narrowed. The tiger swallowed the remaining food without avoiding his gaze.
Free them once, and they never see the second line. When will you see it, Yeoni? Could you recognize it without that cat?

The tiger climbed onto the awning and looked down the alley. The shopkeeper who lent applause had vanished. Only the ledger remained. A red mark was stamped inside the cover—the same shape as the marking on the tiger's forehead.

The tiger erased the child's name from the original ledger. Not destroyed it: moved it into the lining of its own cloak. One golden thread turned black. The paw closing the back cover did not tremble. The tag it would show Yeoni tomorrow was clean now.

episodes.title: The Festival Where the Sun Stopped
episodes.tag: Episode 7 · The Festival Where the Sun Stopped

beats.t: At sunset, even the smells of the festival street were noisy. Browning sugar, charring skewers, laughter mingled with drumbeats.
Yeongnyangi. I've decided. I'm spending the rest of my life on this island.
We arrived less than an hour ago.
An hour is enough. They fry clouds here. If this isn't heaven, what is?
Half a fried cloud was wedged between Yeoni's hooves. The drumming child had split it for them. Steam still rose from it.
The first bite deserves reverence. Star rating after I swallow.
It's hot. Blow on it first.
Don't worry. Pigs handle hot food well. ...Probably.
Song packed the street. A noodle shop sang while tapping pots with ladles. A rice-cake shop improvised songs from customers' names.
Nobody sang well. Everybody sang loudly.
That man's completely off-key, and the customers love it even more.
On this island, that is the right rhythm.
Yeoni opened their mouth wide. At that moment, a bell rang from the highest stage at the street's far end. Dong.
The drums stopped midbeat. Songs, laughter, even the crackle of frying oil—all at once.
...What? Who pressed Mute?
The sun, half-submerged at the horizon, had stopped. Neither setting nor rising. A red semicircle pinned to the sky like a frozen screen.
The sun has stopped.
The sun isn't something that stops.
Look there.
One black feather stood embedded at the top of the highest stage. The very feather they had seen falling over the river.
Crows poured down beneath it. Hundreds settled on every rooftop. Not one cawed.
Hear this announcement.
A large crow in black judicial robes stood beside the feather. A white mask, neither smiling nor weeping, covered its face.
From this moment, singing is forbidden on this island. So are rhythm, whistling, and loud laughter.
Offending mouths will be stamped. That is all.
A singing ban in the middle of a festival? What's the festival supposed to run on? A minute of silence?
Lower your voice. Those crows are all ears.
If singing's banned, what about humming?
Singing.
Clapping?
Rhythm.
Then breathing? Breath has rhythm too.
Breathing is still allowed. For now.
One by one, people closed their mouths. They put down ladles and hid drumsticks in their sleeves. Nobody asked why.
Only the skewer seller could not hold back. A customer dropping a skewer apparently struck him as funny. Ha, ha, ha.
A crow dived. Its beak struck the back of his hand, leaving a gray stamp.
He was only laughing!
The seller opened his mouth to laugh again. Ha, ha. Instead of sound, only air came out. Less air than before.
Each stamp diminishes the voice. Expression is the energy that brings what is inside outward. Words, songs, flavors you create.
Block the mouth and all three are blocked together.
All three? Taste too?
Yeoni looked down at the fried cloud between their hooves. The sparkling sugar coating had turned ash-gray.
Yeoni bit into it. Chewed. Chewed again.
...There's no taste.
When the sun stops, fire cools. That sun cooks the flavors of this island.
This is a crime. You fry a cloud, then take away its flavor? That's fraud, a crime, an international incident.
This is not a nation.
Then it's a cosmic incident. I'm review-bombing this entire island.
Perhaps the injustice was too much. A sound burst from Yeoni's nose.
OIIIIIINK!
The entire street turned toward Yeoni. Hundreds of rooftop crows cocked their heads at the same moment.
That sound had pitch.
No, that wasn't singing! It was a pig noise!
The final note rose. Singing.
A black shadow brushed Yeoni's hoof. A sting. A coin-sized gray stamp marked the pink skin.
My hoof! My cute little hoof's been branded!
This child came from another island. You can't stamp them before even explaining the rules here.
The masked crow looked down at Yeongnyangi. No eyes were visible through the mask's holes.
Set foot on this island and its ears hear you. Make your excuses at trial. Starting with the next stamp.
Judicial robes fluttered. The crow vanished toward the feather. The other crows remained motionless on the rooftops.
...Yeongnyangi. Is my voice smaller now?
Your voice sounds fine. Nothing to worry about yet.
Knowing that's supposed to comfort me makes it sadder.
Behind the festival street lay a night market. Or what had once been one. The awnings remained, but their colors had drained away. Skewers, candy, people's faces—all gray.
It's even quieter here than on that street.
These people were stamped earlier. The feather had been eating away at this island long before the sun stopped.
Two or three gray stamps marked the backs of the merchants' hands. When customers came, they pointed at prices instead of speaking.
An old woman at a candy stall saw Yeoni's hoof and beckoned them closer.
Hello. I'm not a scary pig. It's my first time here.
The woman spoke with breath instead of voice. Like air escaping a balloon.
One takes laughter, two take song, three take speech. There were three stamps on her hand.
You... can't speak anymore.
She shook her head, then placed one candy in Yeoni's hoof. A gray candy.
Thank you. I'll enjoy it even if it has no taste. I mean, I'll enjoy it.
The woman's eyes crinkled in a smile. A silent smile. Yeoni could not believe anyone could put a stamp on that.
Yeoni put the candy in their mouth. It tasted of nothing. Still, they rolled it around until it was gone.
Yeongnyangi. What did this island used to be like?
It was midday all day. The festival began at noon, and the sun set only when the songs ended.
That sun is Byeong, the light of high noon. It must reach noon again before this island can have another day.
Then we just push the sun back up to noon, right?
Easy to say.
Talking's always easy. It's the talking island. ...Oh, right, currently the no-talking island.
A drum rolled out from the far side of the market. Someone had dropped it. Boom. The sound rang far too loudly.
The crows on the roofs spread their wings together. The drum's owner had already hidden behind an awning. Yeoni picked up the drum and froze.
...Oh. I didn't play it. Seriously.
Put it down. Slowly.
Yeoni lowered the drum gently. The crows tilted their heads, then folded their wings again.
This isn't an island. It's a library. With about a hundred librarians.
Hundreds.
Thanks for the correction. Not thankful at all.
Yeoni walked among gray awnings. Their hunger grew with every step. Food was everywhere, yet there was nothing they wanted to eat.
This is the scariest part. Being hungry but wanting none of the food.
That is how people wither. First they lose flavor, then laughter.
Then everyone on this island is withering right now.
That is why we must not stay long. You have a stamp too.
No way. I haven't tasted a single specialty yet. I'm not leaving before the flavor comes back.
Motivated by appetite.
Appetite is noble. Humanity discovered fire because it was hungry.
You are currently a pig.
Pigs are noble too!
Then another scent slipped among the gray smells. Simmering soy sauce, toasting sesame, and the faintest hint of something burned.
Wait. Yeongnyangi. Did you smell that?
What?
Something delicious! Actually delicious! A smell that isn't gray!
Yeoni's nose moved on its own. Their hooves followed it. Yeongnyangi had no chance to stop them.
Yeoni. Don't just follow it.
My nose went first. I'm only following my nose.
The scent led to a narrow alley at the market's end. Sunlight never reached it. Only lamps under the eaves were lit.
Deep inside came the crackle of frying oil. And a very small voice.
It was not a song. Too fast for a song, too rhythmic for ordinary speech.
Turn up the heat, oil the pot. Mute the mouth, but flavor won't stop. Gray sky overhead, my pan burns red.
...Is that rap? On this island? Right now?
If discovered, that won't end with just three stamps.
A brown otter crouched in a ramshackle food cart at the alley's end. Turning rice-cake skewers over a small pan, the otter muttered so softly that only the pan could hear.
The rice-cake skewers glowed orange. In the middle of the gray island, they alone had color.
...An ember.
That fire was not borrowed from the sun. It was kindled within.
Yeoni took a step without realizing it. A gray plate broke underfoot. Clink.
The otter jumped. The skewer in its paw flew into the air. Yeoni caught it in their mouth.
Hey. That's my skewer.
...Delicious.
Of course it is. I grilled it. But what are you? A pig?
Five stars. No, six.
Stars only go up to five, you flower-headed pig.
And why is a flower-headed pig sniffing around someone else's alley?
The smell spoke to me first. Said it was delicious.
So this is an island where otters rap.
Not rap. A recipe recital. Just happened to have a beat.
People call a recipe with a beat rap.
People are wrong.
Wingbeats poured overhead. The alley entrance darkened. Crows were descending toward the sound.
You saw it. All of it. Heard the rap too.
Ah, I heard nothing. My ears were folded.
If you heard it, you're an accomplice. Run, pig.
The otter ran, clutching the pot. Yeoni followed in something closer to a roll. Yeongnyangi brought up the rear, glaring toward the descending crows.
Left! No, not your left—my left!
Use the person running in front as your reference! I have four legs now. This is confusing!
The alley twisted like an anthill. At a dead end, the otter stopped and kicked open a wooden hatch in the ground.
Get in. Watch your head. Oh, your belly'll probably get stuck first.
We just met! No body commentary!
They dropped in one after another. As the hatch closed, wingbeats passed overhead. The sound circled for a long time, then receded.
Below was a cramped kitchen. Ladles and sieves covered the walls. A small clay jar stood in the center. Inside it, one ember flickered as though breathing.
Short introductions. Moka. Otter. Cook.
Yeoni. Human. Pig due to circumstances.
Yeongnyangi.
Cat?
Not just a cat.
Not just a cat, but that tiny? This island really is finished.
Right? That's what I thought at first.
You two really only met today, right?
Instead of replying, Moka set the pot over the ember jar. The same rice-cake skewers. Soy sauce simmered with a hiss.
That smell. That's it. The smell that brought me all the way here.
Do you spend your whole life getting dragged around by smells?
Smells don't lie.
Moka handed over a skewer. Yeoni glanced at the gray stamp on their hoof, wondering if there would be any taste.
One bite. Sweet and salty burst on their tongue, followed by smoky fire. Tears gathered in Yeoni's eyes.
I can taste it. Even with the stamp, I can taste it.
A-are you crying? Over one skewer?
It's not one skewer. It's a whole day's worth of unfairness.
Only after finishing did Yeoni look down at their hoof. One corner of the gray stamp had faded like singed paper.
Yeongnyangi, look. A bit of the stamp's gone.
Real flavor burned it away. Only a little, but still.
That's why I grill in secret every night. So even one person remembers what flavor is.
Jeong Fire. A little flame like a lamp. Even when the sun stops, it remains while someone tends it.
Don't know the fancy words. It's my grandmother's fire.
Moka cupped the ember jar in his paws. Several patches of singed fur marked his palms.
Grandma ran the loudest food cart on this island. Sing her a song, get a free skewer.
Exactly my kind of place.
Bad singers got two. Payment for courage, she said.
Your grandmother was the best. Five stars.
Grandma gets six. You said six was possible earlier.
Grandmother-only exception accepted.
Where is your grandmother now?
Moka's paws paused. Oil spat once.
She passed away before sunset. I've been keeping the fire alive since.
...Sorry. Shouldn't have asked.
You didn't ask. The cat did.
I'm sorry.
It's fine. Anyway, that's why I don't sing. I only cook.
Wasn't that singing earlier?
I told you, a recipe.
First recipe I've heard with such a good beat.
The tips of Moka's ears turned red. He stirred the pot with a ladle for no reason.
It won't come out in front of people. Only in front of the pot.
Why?
Don't know. People's eyes are scarier than pots.
Usually, yes.
Anyway. There's exactly one place left on this island where songs survive. Tonight might be its last.
Where?
An underground stage. Want to come? You'll understand there—what this island used to sound like.
Dangerous.
That's why we have to go. It's the last place with songs, you said.
Talking to you always gets stuck at this point.
The hatch overhead rattled. All three held their breath. Claws scraped slowly across the wood.
Every night. Now I can tell how many there are just by the footsteps.
How many was that?
One. But that one's the heaviest.
The judge has come.
Rumor says that crow used to perform too. Everyone laughed at the very first line, supposedly.
So it got rid of every song? For revenge?
Don't know. Nobody's remembered its name since that day.
The underground stage was inside an abandoned water tank. Lamps hung along the round walls. About thirty people sat knee to knee on the floor.
The musicians beat drums wrapped in cloth. Cotton filled the end of a flute. The singer whispered her song.
She was a woman with cropped silver hair. Her voice was thin as thread, but unbroken.
That's Yeoul. Best singer on the island. She was a regular at Grandma's cart.
You look incredibly proud right now.
No I don't. That's just my face.
But this is a whispering concert.
Sing loudly here and they'll hear above. So everyone sings softly. But they sing to the end.
Together, the whispers sounded strangely loud. Thirty people's breaths rose and fell to the same rhythm. Yeoni's hoof tapped the floor without permission.
They said breathing was allowed.
Yes. Breathing is allowed. They're all singing with their breath now.
The song ended. Instead of clapping, people pressed their palms to one another's. Silent applause.
I like this. These people really love singing.
They do. It's what they live for.
Then one lamp went out. Another. Darkness walked toward them from the stage.
Lovely performance. Now let's settle the account.
The black tiger sat at the stage's edge. Gold-thread cloak, red eyes, red forehead mark. A thick ledger lay open beneath its paw.
Tiger?
We meet again, Yeoni. And the cat in the hat is still beside you. Even changing islands can't separate you.
What are you doing here?
Working. Some of these people borrowed applause. Today is repayment day.
Lending luck and collecting interest, are you?
Business is good. Especially here. Everyone was starving for applause.
The singer onstage went pale. A small tag hung around her neck, just like the one the drumming child had worn in the alley.
Don't touch Yeoul. She borrowed it when she was about to give up singing. She wanted to hear great applause just once.
And she did. Great applause. Enough to bring this stage down that night.
What you receive must be returned. Applause cannot be repaid with applause. You pay with your voice.
The tiger pressed a paw against the ledger. One shining thread unwound from the singer's throat, crossed the air, and was drawn into the book.
Stop!
The singer opened her mouth. Not even a whisper came. People stood, but nobody could approach the stage.
You wanted her song, not to ruin her voice!
How do you know what I wanted?
Then tell me what you want. I'll repay it. Her share too.
Yeoni. Take that back.
The tiger's red eyes settled on Yeoni. The paw turning ledger pages stopped too. For one brief moment, the tiger looked as though it was calculating.
You'd take someone else's debt? Without even knowing the interest?
I don't know about interest. Just give her voice back.
...That habit of stopping when someone is hurt. Still the same.
I won't collect from you yet. Your value will rise far beyond this.
Stop bargaining over people's voices, you striped menace!
Stripes are markings too. Don't address someone else's markings carelessly, otter.
The ceiling boomed. Once, then again. A crack opened in the tank's rusted roof.
The roof tore open. Crows poured down like black rain. At their center, the robed crow slowly descended.
The den of song has been found.
Stamp them all.
They were all whispering! How is this noise!
Whispers are songs too. Applause without clapping is still applause.
The crows stamped down. Thump. Thump. Gray flowers bloomed on the backs of hands. One by one, the earlier rhythm of breathing went out.
People scattered, swallowing their screams. Lamps fell. Moka pushed people toward the back door.
This way! Heads down! Don't speak, just breathe!
Yeoul! Hurry, you too!
The voiceless singer stood frozen onstage, still holding a cotton-covered microphone. Yeoni jumped onto the stage.
Yeoni, above you!
A black net fell from overhead. Yeoni pushed the singer off the stage. The net covered Yeoni alone.
Aagh, it's sticky! What is this!
Let go!
Yeongnyangi leaped, golden claws aimed at the net. Dozens of crow feathers wrapped around his small white body. He was slammed into the floor.
Yeongnyangi!
When Yeoni looked behind the stage, the tiger was already gone. So were the ledger and the shining thread. Only one strand of gold lay on the floor.
Defendant: Flower Pig.
Charges: incitement to song, unauthorized fine dining, excessive exclamations.
What even are excessive exclamations!
The net lifted into the sky. The last thing Yeoni saw was Moka's clenched face through the gap in the back door.
To the courtroom tomorrow morning.
The courtroom was a giant birdcage. Curved iron bars rose into the sky. On every tier inside sat silent people bearing gray stamps.
Yeoni hung in the defendant's place, still in the net. It had not loosened at all through the night.
Do defendants have human rights here? Or at least pig rights?
The robed crow landed on the high dais. Its eyes remained hidden behind the mask. A feather gavel tapped the table once.
Court is in session.
Defendant: Flower Pig. Three charges. Incitement to song, unauthorized fine dining, excessive exclamations.
That third one's a crime I've genuinely never heard of.
Records show the defendant uttered forty-seven exclamations yesterday.
You were counting those?
Forty-eight.
Examples will be read aloud. Oink. Oiiink. Oink-aaah. Wow. Awesome. Insane.
Hearing them in the judge's voice is really embarrassing.
Oink-aaah is a word I haven't heard either.
You heard it too! On the first day!
A few shoulders on the tiers trembled with suppressed laughter. The crow's head whipped toward them. The shoulders froze.
Where is the defense counsel's place?
Yeongnyangi was bound beside the witness stand, tightly wrapped in feathers. His voice, at least, carried clearly through the court.
The defendant has not been granted counsel.
Under this island's law, a performer may have one applauder. I will fill that role.
There was a law like that?
Just thought of it.
Best lawyer. Five stars.
...Granted. On condition that the applauder does not applaud.
Clapping with cat paws is difficult anyway.
Exhibit One.
A crow brought a silver tray. On it lay a half-eaten rice-cake skewer. Yeoni's eyes lit up.
Oh, my skewer.
Yeoni. Drooling over the evidence makes defending you difficult.
It's not my fault my body reacts first.
Flavor was detected in this skewer. State its source.
Yeoni pressed their mouth shut. Moka's name rose to their tongue, then retreated.
Found it on the ground. Anyway, I found it.
False testimony added.
Objection. The person eating cannot be held responsible for the food being delicious.
Overruled.
Objection. An exclamation cannot automatically be classified as a song.
The defendant's oiiink had pitch. Falling from sol to mi.
You assigned solfège to my scream?
...Now that you mention it, it was sol to mi.
Yeongnyangi! Whose side are you on!
Your Honor, I challenge the storage conditions of the evidence. The skewer has gone cold.
Why is that a problem?
A cold skewer has no flavor. Without flavor, unauthorized fine dining cannot be established.
Oh, that sounded kind of lawyerly.
Overruled. The defendant drooled even at the cold skewer.
Call the witness.
The barred door opened. The old woman from the gray market entered, three stamps on her hand. Seeing Yeoni, she bowed her head a little.
Witness. Did this pig sing in the market?
The woman could not answer. The stamps had taken even her speech. Instead, she brought her hands together before her chest, then slowly opened them.
What does that mean?
A flower blooming. When you ate her candy and smiled at the market.
She nodded once. A few people on the tiers opened their hands too. Silent flowers bloomed throughout the courtroom.
Enough.
For the first time, the crow's voice cracked. The people hurriedly lowered their hands.
Um, Your Honor. Can I ask one thing?
The defendant may not ask questions.
Then I'll talk to myself. Why would someone hate singing this much? Did a song slap the judge in the face?
I've been laughed at plenty for singing badly too. My highest karaoke score was forty-seven.
Forty-seven. The same as today's exclamation count.
The courtroom went still. The claws gripping the feather gavel whitened.
Singing invites ridicule.
If nobody sings, nobody laughs at anyone.
...Who laughed at you?
The gavel slammed the table. It cracked. The crows on the bars spread their wings in unison.
Verdict.
Defendant Flower Pig: entire voice confiscated. Applauder Cat: hat confiscated for complicity.
His hat? Why Yeongnyangi's hat!
The loudest hat in the world.
I'll take that as a compliment.
Two crows approached Yeongnyangi with scissors. The blades touched the tassel at the hat's tip. One golden strand fell to the floor.
Yeongnyangi did not blink. Yeoni's breathing quickened instead. Their heartbeat drummed in their ears.
Don't touch him.
The defendant may not speak.
I said, don't touch him!
The words leaving Yeoni's mouth became fire. Letter-shaped flames leaped into the air. DON'T. TOUCH. HIM. NOW. Four masses of flame melted the scissors.
...Hurting Officer.
The fire did not stop. With every breath Yeoni took, the words grew hotter. The iron bars glowed red. People on the tiers edged away.
If you hate singing, just don't sing yourself! Why shut everyone else's mouths!
Yeoni, stop!
You like everyone living in silence? You like an island with nothing to laugh about that much?
One flame curved toward the tiers, toward the old woman's seat. Yeongnyangi tore through the feathers binding him and leaped.
White light collided with red fire. Yeongnyangi's paw knocked the flame aside. It skimmed over the woman's head, struck the bars, and scattered.
Y-Yeongnyangi?
I'm fine. Breathe first. Slowly.
Yeoni drew breath. The fire dwindled. A burned smell remained in their mouth. Yeongnyangi was hiding a paw behind his back.
I nearly hit her.
If you had, I would have scolded you. You didn't. That's enough.
Did you see? Words are fire. That is why they must be stopped.
At that moment, metal clattered in the roof vent. Rattle. Rattle. Something was rolling down.
Your fried food is ready!
Moka dropped from the vent and overturned a pot of oil. As lumps of batter touched the heat from the bars, white smoke erupted.
Clear the smoke!
Too late. Grandma's smokescreen fritters last ten minutes.
You can make a smokescreen out of fried food?
Double the flour in the batter. Tastes awful, though. Don't eat it.
That's the saddest part.
Moka's kitchen knife cut the net's edge. Yeoni tumbled from the defendant's stand. Yeongnyangi caught their scruff in his mouth and hauled them up.
The exit?
Sewer. Put up with the smell if you want to live.
These net marks already make me a patterned pig, and now a sewer too?
Mourn your pattern later. Run.
The sewer emerged below a seaside hill. The evening sea was silent. Waves broke without a splash.
Looks like the sea got stamped too.
Since the day the sun stopped. The waves shut their mouths.
Moka retrieved the small ember jar from behind a rock. He fried flat pancakes from the remaining batter. This time they smelled right.
Eat. These are the tasty ones.
One bite spread the rich flavor of oil. Yeoni's ears fluttered on their own.
Thanks. ...But why did you come? If they catch you, you get stamped too.
I told you, hearing it makes you an accomplice. What kind of accomplice abandons another accomplice?
You're surprisingly loyal.
Not surprisingly. Openly.
Halfway through the pancake, Yeoni stopped. Their hoof tips still stung where the fire had passed.
That was me earlier. My words turned into fire.
Hurting Officer. The sharpest of the forces flowing from within you to the outside.
Then what about Eating God?
The same fire, burning in a way that lets someone eat and smile.
Put simply, fire for grilling skewers versus fire that burns a house. Same fire, different use.
Oh. Teacher Moka explains it better.
I'm a cat. Not good at metaphors. Hmph.
Grandma said songs were what raised the sun. If everyone sang at noon, it climbed to its highest point.
Then singing at noon will make the sun move again?
An old story. A fairy tale. Don't actually believe it.
I'm very good at believing fairy tales.
Byeong is the midday sun. If this sun cannot pass noon, that story is not wrong.
...Really? Then Grandma was right?
The laughter settled. Yeoni hugged their knees and watched the silent waves.
That crow, when its voice cracked earlier... It looked like it really hurt.
Don't pity it. That thing tore down my grandmother's shop sign.
It's not pity. I just wonder who laughed.
Nobody answered. Soon, Yeoni's breathing slowed. The pig fell asleep with pancake still in their mouth.
Yeongnyangi walked alone to the water and dipped his forepaw into the silent waves.
Steam rose. Beneath the white fur, the skin was blackened. The burn resembled a character. 傷—wound.
...Faster than I expected.
Yeongnyangi withdrew the paw and brushed fur over it. When he looked back, Yeoni was still asleep.
At the same time, in the empty courtroom, the crow picked up the golden tassel strand from the floor.
Hurting Officer has awakened. At this rate, noon will come.
The crow tucked the strand inside its robes. A black feather trembled there all by itself. There was no wind.
Before then, I will devour that pig's voice.
A large sheet of paper went up on Moka's underground kitchen wall. Crooked letters at the top read: Operation Noon Concert.
Right, meeting starts now. Objective: raise the sun to noon.
First pig I've seen plan an operation from one line of a fairy tale.
You're the one who brought up that fairy tale.
We need three things. A high stage, people to sing together, and the courage to make the first sound.
The stage should be the highest place on the island. Where the black feather fell.
The Sundial Stage. Performances used to happen there every noon. Now it's a crow's nest.
I'll gather people. I'm good at promotion.
How do you promote a singing performance on an island where singing's banned?
Don't call it singing. Free skewers at noon. Everyone will come.
Who's grilling those skewers?
Now, which otter grills the best skewers on this island?
The pig whose voice turns into fire is handling promotion.
I'll control that. Probably.
Then the last part. Who makes the first sound?
Yeoni and Yeongnyangi looked at Moka together. Still holding his ladle, Moka backed away.
Why are you looking at me?
Now, which otter has the best rhythm on this island?
I told you, it's a recipe!
Read the recipe at noon. Loud enough to carry.
...So the cat makes jokes too.
Not a joke.
Yeoni headed to the gray market. Gathering people meant meeting people first.
The market remained quiet. But a small sound came from an alley entrance. Tap, tap-tap. Chopsticks tapping a wooden box.
A sound? Someone hasn't been stamped?
A boy of about ten sat before the box. The backs of his hands were clean. No stamps. He saw Yeoni and hid the chopsticks behind his back.
Don't hide them. I'm not an inspector. As you can see, I'm a pig.
The child watched Yeoni for a while, then gave a little smile. He tapped the box again. Tap, tap-tap, tap.
Nice rhythm. You've played drums before, haven't you?
He nodded. Then suddenly tilted his head, looking unable to remember when.
What's your name?
His mouth opened, then closed. Opened again. No name came out.
It's okay. If you can't remember, tell me later.
Child, what do your mother or friends call you?
He shrugged, looking puzzled that such an easy question had no answer.
He tried writing something on the box with a finger. Drew the first stroke and stopped. He did not know where the second should go.
Yeoni, look at his wrist.
A gold-thread mark encircled the child's wrist. A fine scar, as though a thread had been tied there and cut. A little gold still remained.
The mark of a debt-binding thread being cut. But his name was cut away with it.
I think I know who did that.
Yeoni remembered the strand of gold on the underground stage's floor. The same color.
Then I'll call you something for now. Captain Drum. How's that?
His eyes widened. Then he struck the box with his loudest beat. Tap, tap, boom.
That means you like it, right? Captain Drum, perform with us at noon.
On the seaside hill, Yeongnyangi sat on a rock and began the lesson. His students: one pig, one otter, one Captain Drum.
Two ways to use fire. Eating God and Hurting Officer.
Oh, finally unlocking the skill tree?
No tree. Only skewers.
Yeongnyangi signaled Moka. Moka placed six skewers on the grill.
Eating God first. Send fire to the skewers. Without anger. Think: become delicious.
Become delicious.
Yeoni extended a hoof toward the grill. Nothing. Tried again. One skewer warmed slightly.
Lukewarm. Serve that to a customer and it's one star.
You know you're setting my heart on fire right now?
All six skewers burst into flame at once. In an instant, they were charcoal.
My skewers!
That is Hurting Officer.
Uh, sorry. I got angry and it shot out.
The same fire. Only where your heart is looking differs. Again.
Six more skewers went on. Yeoni closed their eyes and imagined Grandmother's cart. The grandmother who gave two skewers to customers who could not sing.
Soy sauce hissed on the grill. The skewers browned evenly. Moka picked one up and tasted it.
...Four stars.
Four? Why not five?
Five belongs to Grandma. Don't get ambitious.
Now Hurting Officer. It is a blade. A blade must be used narrowly. Cut only that rope.
Yeongnyangi indicated a rope hanging from a rock's edge. An empty pot dangled from it.
Cut it with words, right? One phrase?
The shortest, most precise words.
Break free!
Two flaming words flew out. They chipped the rock beside the rope, knocked the pot away, and fell into the sea. The rope was untouched.
That was Grandma's pot!
Far too many family heirlooms are dying today.
Yeoni shouted ten more times. On the ninth, the rope broke. Captain Drum tapped his box. Boom, boom.
There. Remember that feeling.
Yeongnyangi staggered briefly as he stood, when he put weight on his right forepaw. He sat down again with an unconcerned face.
Yeongnyangi, is your leg asleep?
Cats' legs fall asleep after sitting too long too.
How old is this cat, anyway?
Do not ask.
A grandpa cat.
I said, do not ask.
My turn now. Practice.
Ooh, recipe-recital rehearsal!
Moka climbed onto the rock. Pig, cat, and child looked up at him. He opened his mouth.
Nothing came out. It was not a stamp. Moka's hands bore none.
...Close your eyes. All of you.
You can't even with just us three watching?
Three is the scariest. The pot doesn't look at me.
Captain Drum took a pot lid from his bag and held it before his face. Yeoni copied him. Yeongnyangi covered his eyes with a paw.
Two spoons of soy, one spoon of sweet. Keep the heart gentle and high the heat.
A small voice, but it had rhythm. Behind his lid, Captain Drum tapped his knees. Yeoni's tail swayed to the beat.
See? All it takes is one lid between us.
You going to tell the whole island to wear lids at noon?
Not a bad idea. A lid festival.
On an evening whose sunset never moved, Yeoni toured the alleys with flyers against their chest. Only pictures on the flyers: a sun, a skewer, a smiling face.
At one corner, a lamp went out. Yeoni stopped. They knew this sequence now.
Cute flyer. Two stars for drawing ability.
Don't rate other people's promotional materials.
The noon concert. Everyone's heard. The crows know too.
...Already?
Rumors travel faster than songs here. Songs are banned; rumors aren't.
The tiger opened its ledger. One line stood empty. Yeoni's name was written at the top.
So here's an offer. I'll lend you applause. At noon, a thousand people below the stage will clap for you.
A thousand?
Enough applause raises the sun too. Even if the singing's clumsy. Guaranteed.
Yeoni looked at the ledger. The empty line glittered. It looked easy. Far too easy.
What's the interest?
Now you ask that too.
Learned at the underground stage. Paid for with Yeoul's voice.
We'll decide later. I'll give you a good rate.
No.
The tiger's tail stopped.
A sun raised on borrowed applause will set when repayment comes. Then this island spends its whole life paying you interest.
Clumsy or not, we'll raise it with real applause. If it won't rise, we'll sing again tomorrow.
...There might not be a tomorrow.
Are you worrying about me?
Business. Lose a customer and the ledger goes empty.
Then I'll just sing well today.
The tiger shut the book, a little louder than usual.
Debts grow if left alone. Even debts you never took. Refusal has a price of its own.
And Yeoni. Don't go up on the roof tonight.
What's that supposed to mean? Warning or threat?
No answer. When the lamp came on again, the alley was empty.
That night, Yeoni could not sleep. They eased open the underground kitchen's hatch and climbed onto the roof. Things they were told not to do always made them curious.
Just one practice. Very quietly.
Looking toward the Sundial Stage, Yeoni hummed. Sol to mi. The notes that had earned ridicule in the courtroom net. Strangely, it felt good.
As the humming ended, one patch of moonless sky grew darker. Wings.
The voice that will raise the stage at noon.
Confiscated.
Wait, sentencing can only happen in court—right, there's no law like that, is there.
The crow opened its beak. A shining thread unwound from Yeoni's throat. Trembling in the shapes of sol and mi, it was drawn into the mask.
Yeoni tried to shout. Breath passed through their throat. Nothing came out.
The crow flew away. Only one pig and a black feather remained on the roof.
Below, the hatch opened. Yeongnyangi was climbing up. Yeoni called to him.
Yeongnyangi. Their mouth unmistakably formed the name. Not a sound came.
The three sat around the ember jar in the underground kitchen. Nobody spoke first. Only two of them could have made a sound even if they tried.
I shouldn't have left you alone. I'm sorry.
Not the cat's fault. It's the pig's fault for doing exactly what they were told not to.
(He's right, so why is it so annoying?)
Yeoni opened their mouth wide, then closed it. Not even escaping air made a sound. Their throat felt like an empty box.
The crow took more than your voice. The entire path through which words emerge. The path of Hurting Officer.
Then the noon concert's finished. The one meant to make the first sound can't talk.
(You're supposed to make the first sound!)
Yeoni pointed a hoof at Moka. He shook his head. Yeoni pointed again. He shook it harder.
Stop pointing. I'm not doing it.
Yeoni, try writing.
Moka took a small blackboard from the wall. With chalk in their mouth, Yeoni wrote: Moka, you do it.
The instant the final stroke ended, the letters faded gray and scattered like dust. Nothing remained on the board.
(Writing doesn't work either?)
Wow. That crow is thorough. Like a tax collector.
Writing carries words too. The crow blocked that path as well.
So this pig can't do anything now?
(Anything?)
Yeoni pulled the board back. This time, instead of letters, they drew a circle with short lines around it. A sun.
The picture did not fade. White chalk remained on the board.
Drawing still works.
A skewer below the sun. A smiling face beside the skewer. ...Free skewers again?
(Correct.)
The force poured out through words is called Hurting Officer; the force made through your hands, Eating God. The crow stopped words. The power to make things remains.
(Then I've still got half left!)
Yeoni added more pictures. The market. A grill. People in a line. Stamps on their hands fading little by little.
You want to grill skewers at the market? Without talking?
Yeoni nodded vigorously. Then drew an otter beside the pig in the picture. A slightly better-looking otter than the real one.
...Why'd you make me handsome?
Flattery.
(Not flattery. Your future appearance.)
Fine. Let's do it. One condition. I only grill. I'm not standing in front of customers.
The voiceless pig will face the customers. Fair enough.
(A perfect team.)
In the middle of the gray market, Moka dragged over an abandoned cart and set a grill on it. Yeoni placed the blackboard at the front. Sun, skewer, smiling face.
Nobody approached. People glanced at the board and passed. On this island, free food meant a trap.
See? Nobody's coming.
Yeoni took a skewer into the middle of the street and acted out eating it. Very dramatically.
(Mmm. That's the taste. That's it.)
One bite, eyes closed. Two bites, hooves cradling cheeks. Three bites, lying on the ground and flailing.
What is that supposed to be?
A review. A five-star one.
A passing child stopped. One stamp on their hand. A child whose laughter had been taken. They looked down at the flailing pig.
The corners of the child's mouth twitched. Laughter tried to emerge, caught on the stamp. Yeoni held out the skewer.
The child took a bite. A corner of the gray stamp faded like singed paper. The child smiled. Silently, but unmistakably.
...It's real. The stamp burned away.
People who had seen it approached the cart one by one. First three. Then ten. A line formed.
Not enough skewers! Cat, make some dough!
Look at the shape of my paws.
Never heard of being so busy you'd borrow a cat's paws?
Not just a cat.
Just or not, knead it a hundred times.
A cat in a hat's pride is being mixed into dough.
(Pride-filled dough ought to be chewy.)
Eventually Yeongnyangi pulled the bowl close. Flour dusted his hat brim and white fur. Watching children's shoulders shook.
Yeoni handed out skewers along the line. Gestures instead of words. Hot, so blow. Tasty, give a thumbs-up. Finished sticks go here.
(Everyone understands without words!)
Customers, one blow each, please. You're spitting on the grill.
Tap, tap-tap came from the market's far side. Captain Drum put his box beside the cart and began keeping time. Heads nodded to his rhythm.
One corner of the gray market regained a little color. Smoke from the skewers rose golden.
Then metal rang above the market roofs. Everyone in line froze. A wing's shadow covered the cart.
Unlicensed business. Unauthorized fine dining. Unauthorized rhythm.
And silent incitement.
How is it incitement when nobody even spoke!
(I really didn't! Not one syllable!)
Laughter is the beginning of song.
People backed away. Yeoni took a skewer and walked toward the crow. Their hoof shook, but the skewer stayed level.
(Have one too.)
The defendant may not speak.
Yeoni nodded, then held out the skewer again.
The crow's wing knocked it away. It rolled onto the ground. Yeoni did not pick it up. Instead, they brought over the blackboard.
Yeoni, step back.
Yeoni drew. A stage. A small person onstage. Laughing people below. They erased the laughing faces and drew them again. This time, applauding faces.
(I wish it had been like this. That day.)
The crow looked at the drawing. Its mask shook. Crack. A split opened down the middle.
Through it appeared a face. A boy. The shadow of someone about fifteen or sixteen, frozen with a microphone in hand.
...A person?
Don't look.
The crow covered its cracked mask with a wing. Its voice split low, the same crack heard in the courtroom.
Don't look. Don't laugh. Nobody.
The crow took flight. A few feathers fell. One landed on Yeoni's blackboard, covering the drawn stage.
The market people stayed beside the cart. Nobody fled. Someone picked up the fallen skewer, dusted it off, and placed it on the cart.
The old woman. One of her three stamps had faded. She gave Yeoni a thumbs-up.
(I got five stars.)
Don't cry. If you cry, I'll... no, I won't cry.
Today's business was a success. Without a single word.
Night. The three lay on a roof overlooking the Sundial Stage. Above the island's highest stage hung the stopped sun.
One side of it had been eaten black. The shadow, only fingernail-sized when they arrived, now covered half the sun.
Bigger than yesterday.
The more fire we light in the market, the more they hurry over there.
(What if it covers everything?)
If Byeong is devoured, this island will be trapped in night. Noon will never return.
(Then my skewer stall becomes a permanent night market.)
Your face shows exactly what you're thinking. Business, isn't it.
Then when? The noon concert.
When the next bell rings. The moment the sundial casts its final shadow.
Yeoni touched their throat. Empty. A pig unable to make the first sound had promised a noon concert.
(What if I really can't do anything?)
Don't make that face.
Moka pressed a paw onto Yeoni's head. An awkward touch.
You made a hundred people smile at the market today without saying a word. That's harder than being a good talker.
(...Moka complimented me.)
(Wish I could record this. Oh, right. No voice.)
Not a compliment. A statement of fact.
Yeoni began nodding off. Moka draped his apron over them. Then he noticed Yeongnyangi's forepaw.
Cat. What's with that paw?
Nothing.
Charred skin showed through white fur. 傷—wound. The character was clearer than yesterday.
You got hurt in court. By the pig's fire.
Don't tell. Not this child.
Why? They need to know to be careful.
If Yeoni knows, they won't make a sound at noon. For fear of hurting me.
Moka stared at Yeongnyangi for a long time. Then pulled the apron up to cover the sleeping pig's ears.
...Tell them after noon. Or I will.
An otter threatening a cat.
Cooks are good at threats. Have to be, to last in front of a fire.
On the high dais of the empty courtroom, the crow crouched without removing its cracked mask. Threads of sol and mi glittered inside its robes.
That pig knows nothing about singing. So why?
The crow traced the crack with a wingtip. Wind slipped through. It smelled like the wind that had struck its face onstage long ago.
Then the shadow below the dais stretched long. Five black fingers bloomed at its end.
You are wavering, child.
You have swallowed the pig's voice. Now it is time to swallow noon.
When the sun is fully devoured, I will gather all your feathers too. And every song that remains.
Just before the bell, at the Sundial Stage. The sun had been eaten down to a slender crescent. The sundial's pointer had almost lost its shadow.
The three climbed the rear steps. Yeoni's throat was still empty. Moka gripped his ladle so tightly that his paws had gone white.
(Will anyone come?)
How many flyers did you hand out?
(A thousand. All pictures.)
You drew this a thousand times? Your paws must hurt.
Both of you, quiet. Actually, one of you already is.
Cat. Be honest. Do you think this will work?
I don't know.
That's where you're supposed to say yes!
If I say something will work when I don't know, you won't believe me. We try because we don't know.
(Yeongnyangi was kind of cool just now.)
The bell rang. The first bell. The entire island trembled at its sound. Crows perched on every roof over the stage lifted their heads together.
This is a noon-prohibited zone.
All who ascend will be confiscated.
The mask remained cracked. The crow held its head slightly lowered so nothing could be seen through the gap.
C-cat. There's nobody here.
Moka was right. The square below the stage stood empty. Only wind passed through.
(They're too scared to come after all.)
Of course. Obviously. I wouldn't come either. Let's go back.
It's only the first bell. Don't rush.
Then it came. Tap, tap-tap. A box being beaten in an alley at the square's edge.
Captain Drum. Behind him, the old woman. Behind her, the market people. The underground audience too, and Yeoul. Everyone held a pot lid.
(The lid festival!)
...They actually brought lids.
They brought them so you wouldn't be afraid. They didn't come to watch you. They came to join you.
Disperse.
The flock descended over the square. People flinched, but nobody turned away. The old woman stood at the front, holding her lid like a shield.
Those who sing are ridiculed. Did you come not knowing that?
Moka, now!
N-now?
Before the second bell. The first sound.
Moka walked to the center of the stage. His legs felt like wooden sticks. More than a hundred eyes in the square turned to him at once.
He opened his mouth. Nothing came out. No stamp on him. Nothing the crow had eaten.
...I can't. It won't come out.
Yeoni approached from behind with a pot lid. They held it up in front of Moka's face.
(You said it comes out in front of a pot.)
Moka looked at the lid. At his reflected face. And behind it, the pig's smiling face.
Two spoons of soy.
A small voice. Perhaps only the old woman at the front could hear.
One spoon of sweet. Keep the heart gentle and high the heat.
Captain Drum struck the box. Boom, tap-tap. Moka's voice grew a little louder.
Turn the skewers, turn, turn before they burn. Grandma said that life's got turns to learn.
The rhythm tangled. On the final line, Moka's voice cracked with a squeak.
Laughter burst from somewhere in the square. One person. Two. It spread.
See? Ridicule.
(No. If Moka stops—)
Moka stopped. His face went bright red. Then he laughed too. His cracked voice was simply too funny not to.
Oh, ruined it! From the top! Two spoons of soy!
(Moka's laughing. Onstage.)
The square shouted along. Two spoons of soy! Laughing, offbeat, tapping lids.
They aren't laughing at him. They are laughing with him.
It was a song. A chaotic, tuneless song. A recipe followed by a hundred people, each a beat late.
...Why?
The crow's voice trembled. Another crack spread through the mask.
Why is nobody angry? It's wrong. Ridiculous.
(It's good because it's ridiculous.)
Yeoni moved their mouth without sound. The crow saw the shape of those words.
A shining thread unwound from inside the crow's robes. A thread trembling in the shapes of sol and mi. Drawn toward the square's laughter, it flew back into Yeoni's throat.
OIIIIIINK!
Sol to mi. The notes mocked in the courtroom rang through the center of the square.
Let's make that our chorus!
I didn't return it. The thread went by itself.
I know. Thank you anyway.
...Nobody has said thank you to me before.
The second bell rang. The sundial's pointer caught its final shadow. Almost all the sun had been devoured.
Yeoni. Push the sun upward. With song.
Song? My karaoke score is forty-seven.
Exactly. With a forty-seven-point song.
Hey, my voice cracked too. You're not the only one embarrassed.
Is that comfort?
Accounting between accomplices.
Yeoni drew breath. They remembered how their words had become fire in court. Then, they had been angry. Not now.
Become delicious.
Yeoni's voice became an ember. Instead of sharp letters, round lights spread above the square. People's voices took up the fire one by one.
Everyone together! Two spoons of soy!
A hundred embers rose into the sky and touched the edge of the devoured sun. The black shadow flinched as though burned.
The shadow tore. Light poured through. The sundial's pointer planted a short shadow precisely on the ground. Noon.
Then black hands poured from the torn darkness. Their fingers reached neither for people nor the sun, but for one thing alone. The crow.
You have failed, child. I am taking back the feathers.
Please wait. Not yet, I still—
Who are you? Show yourself.
The cat in the hat. Do not hurry. You are not yet my share.
Black hands enveloped the crow. The mask shattered. Behind it was the shadow of a boy holding a microphone.
No!
Yeoni lunged. Their hoof touched the boy's fingertips. Warm. An instant later, those fingertips slipped away like smoke.
I wanted...
I wanted to sing together too.
The black hands vanished into shadow. Only one gray feather remained in Yeoni's hoof.
The sun rose over the island's center. Roofs, alleys, and sea regained their colors. A wave crashed with a splash. A sound unheard for so long.
Gray stamps melted from the hands of people in the square. The old woman opened her mouth. A hoarse voice, but unmistakable words.
She spoke. Just now, she spoke.
What did she say?
That it was delicious. My skewer. Just like my grandmother's.
See? I told you five stars wasn't out of reach.
...Not five yet. Four and a half.
Moka. You're crying.
Oil splashed! In my eyes!
There isn't even a fire lit right now.
Two characters rose from the sundial's pointer. 丙午—Byeong-o. The midday sun and the midday Horse. They seeped into Yeoni's chest.
[ Four Pillars characters recovered · Month Pillar: 丙午 ]
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □□ ]  4/8
Half filled! Only half to go!
The remaining half is harder.
Can you say that later? This is celebration time.
Your Month Pillar. The energy of your season. Byeong is Hurting Officer; Jeong within O is Eating God. You used both today.
Yep. One burned skewers, one grilled them.
Precisely.
Yeoni opened their hoof. The gray feather rested there. Its tip trembled faintly.
I don't even know his name. He said he wanted to sing with us.
He tore down my grandmother's shop sign.
I know. But still.
...Still, we could have sung together. Like today.
A feather remains. That means it isn't over.
The sun began to descend. Properly setting at last. The lotus-leaf boat floated up beside the river, ready for the next island.
Moka. Come with us?
Why would I?
We're accomplices. What kind of accomplice abandons another accomplice?
Don't steal my lines.
Moka wrapped the ember jar in his apron and packed his grandmother's ladle too. Captain Drum followed them to the boat, beating his box. Boom, tap-tap, boom.
I'll guard the ember. You just stay out of trouble.
But trouble is my specialty.
Exactly why I'm saying don't.
The boat rocked. As Yeoni caught the railing, the gray feather slipped from their hoof and rode the wind.
Ah, the feather!
The wind has it. Feathers know their way back.
Where did you learn a line like that?
Just made it up.
Yeoni crouched before Captain Drum. The gold-thread scar still marked his wrist.
Captain Drum. I promise I'll find your name.
He nodded, then struck his box as loudly as he could.
Just before boarding, Yeongnyangi met Moka's eyes. Moka's gaze dropped to his right forepaw.
Noon is over.
I'll tell Yeoni on the next island.
Are cats animals that postpone promises?
Without answering, Yeongnyangi boarded. Beneath his white fur, the wound character had deepened a little.
On the hill, the black tiger sat against the setting sun. Wind carried a gray feather from the square. The one that had left Yeoni's hoof.
A black paw pinned it down. After staring at it a long while, the tiger slipped it inside its cloak.
Raising the sun with a song full of cracked notes. Five stars.
A song without ridicule. If such a thing existed, you could have told me from the beginning.

episodes.title: The Empty Line in the Ledger
episodes.tag: EP.12A · The Empty Line in the Ledger

beats.t: Evening came for the first time to the island whose sun had returned. The sun descended toward the horizon on schedule. Occasional pot-lid beats still drifted from the square.
The seaside hill was quiet. Each time the waves licked the sand and withdrew, the smell of wet salt rose.
The black tiger lay on a rock. A thick ledger was open between its forepaws.
The paper was old, but the writing gleamed as though new. Every loan and collection recorded, not one line out of place.
Let's settle things. Start with today's receipts.
A claw turned the first page. The rustle cut clearly between the sounds of waves.
Underground stage. Twelve bundles of applause lent. Collection complete.
Singer Yeoul. One strand of voice. Collection complete.
If you stood onstage with borrowed applause, you repay it when you leave. Nobody forced anyone to borrow.
A silver thread unwound by itself between the ledger pages. It trembled finely, though there was no wind.
A tiny sound came from its tip. Someone drawing breath and choosing a first note.
Shh. You're mine. The price was paid.
The tiger pinned the thread with a claw and tucked it between the pages. It took a long time for the trembling to stop.
Then the sun on the horizon flickered once.
Where the light went out, the waves rose backward. Black finger marks approached across the sand, one by one.
Several black hands rose above the water. They encircled the tiger and opened their palms upward.
The sun has returned.
...It has. Because of the song.
A song. That pig's song.
I lost a feather. That child was a useful vessel.
The crow wasn't my assignment. I was only responsible for applause.
Then did you collect the applause?
The tiger's whiskers moved slightly. Its paw pressed harder against the ledger.
...Most of it.
The gold ring on its right forepaw heated. It narrowed a notch, biting into fur.
Ghh...!
Most. I never entrusted you with most.
The tiger lowered its head. As it steadied its breathing, fine heat kept spreading beneath the ring.
Next time, I will leave nothing.
You are a beast that keeps promises. That is why I chose you. Do not forget why you are here.
I have never forgotten. To stop that child before they become a monster.
The next island trades in time. Collect the pig's time there.
Leave not one hour. Only what is empty can be filled.
Filled? With what—
Instead of answering, the hands sank. Sunset spread again. As though nothing had happened, waves licked the sand.
The ring's heat did not fade easily. The tiger dipped its paw in seawater and withdrew it only much later.
Empty to be filled. Filled with what?
Doesn't matter. Collect what I'm told and it's over. That's the contract.
The tiger turned pages again. The final page for the Island of Expression held a line for the flower pig.
Nothing received. A thousand refused claps. One refused deal. Red writing appeared beside them of its own accord.
[ Flower Pig · Uncollected ]
Uncollected...?
The tiger rubbed the letters with a paw. The red writing neither smeared nor vanished.
My ledger has no uncollected entries. Never has.
I said refusal had its own price. So collect it. Simple arithmetic.
Despite those words, the claw lingered over the line.
The daytime scene kept overlapping it. A pink pig standing voiceless onstage, holding up a pot lid.
Idiot. Borrowed applause would have been so much easier.
Stops at every injury. Gives freely. Refuses what's offered. Someone like that won't last.
...And someone like that becomes a monster? The numbers don't add up.
Then rain sounded from the sea. The tiger lifted its head. The sky was clear, only the sunset red.
The rain was sounding only inside its ears.
A brief scene flashed. Wet asphalt. A flickering bus-stop light. A yellow umbrella tilted overhead.
Someone smiled beneath the umbrella. No face visible. Only a half-soaked shoulder.
...What was that?
The rain cut off. Only waves remained. The tiger pressed a paw to its forehead.
I'm tired. I policed an entire island.
The tiger turned back several pages. The Island of Companions. One line still needed erasing there.
[ Drumming child · Name — Held in safekeeping ]
One name. Change safekeeping to collection complete, and it's done.
The tiger felt inside its cloak. In a small pocket stitched with gold thread, one name pulsed warmly.
One stroke of a claw would transfer the child's name into the ledger. The tiger looked down at the scar that would remain on the wrist. Once handed over, a name was not easily returned.
The claw did not fall. The tiger pushed the pocket deeper into the cloak.
Later. After the next island.
The child's drumming in the square still echoed in its ears. A beat that never faltered, played by someone who did not even know his own name.
Last, the tiger took the gray feather from its cloak. The feather the crow had left behind.
Its tip was still warm. Bringing an ear close, the tiger heard the faintest humming.
Wanted to sing together, did you.
Everyone says that at first. One bout of ridicule, and it's over.
It was for me too.
The tiger shut its mouth, startled by its own words. It could not remember what it meant.
It did not enter the feather in the ledger. Instead, it tucked it into the innermost part of the cloak, beside Captain Drum's name.
The gold ring tightened again. The tiger gritted its teeth and closed the book.
The next island. Where they sell time. Every last moment of that pig's time.
Debts grow when you leave them. So this time, nothing uncollected.
The tiger descended the hill. Footprints trailed across wet sand, then ended at the water.
Wind lifted one corner of the ledger. Inside the closed book, the two red characters still refused to go dark.
The tiger's body dissolved into black mist and scattered over the sea. Beyond the horizon, toward the island of ticking clocks.

episodes.title: The Island That Sells Time
episodes.tag: Episode 13 · The Island That Sells Time

beats.t: Sound crossed the water before the boat reached the harbor. Tick, tick. The entire island seemed to sit inside a giant clock.
What's that sound? The whole island's ticking.
Seasickness plus clocks. One star for this island.
One thing before we disembark. This is the Island of Wealth. It will keep asking what you earn, spend, and leave behind.
