Wealth means money, right? A money island sounds kind of exciting.
The instant Yeoni stepped onto the pier, a small chime sounded at their wrist. A round clock pattern appeared over pink fur.
[ Island of Wealth · Currency: Time ]  Time held 72:00:00
A clock appeared on my wrist! I mean, foreleg! Anyway, it's there!
Here, you pay in time. Spend it, and your day shrinks by that amount.
Wait. What about time spent cooking? Does that get deducted too?
If somebody buys what you make, it should increase.
Then I'll be the richest one here.
The market bustled. Merchants held out wrists instead of coins when naming prices. Touch wrists together, hear a tick, and the transaction was done.
A blue airship with rabbit ears floated overhead. Papers fluttered like snow from its belly. Short on time? Blue Rabbit Finance will lend you some.
The airship's smiling. Are those ads? It says they'll lend us time.
Borrowed time carries interest. Don't pick those up carelessly.
Small signs stood on every stall. One loaf: 3 minutes. One apple: 5 minutes. Asking directions: 30 seconds.
They charge money for directions? I mean, time?
Smiling must be free, then. Look, nobody's doing it. If it's free, they won't bother.
Before finishing the sentence, Moka claimed an empty stall. He took out his remaining skewer ingredients, lit a fire, and tapped the pot with his ladle.
Authentic Island of Expression skewers! Two minutes each! Not delicious? Three minutes back!
The first customer offered a wrist skeptically. Tick. One bite made the customer's eyes widen. Soon a second wrist extended.
See? Work and your time grows. I'll raise this island to two stars.
That is Direct Wealth. What accumulates from the work of your own hands. Slow, but steady.
Then I can earn some too. I'm good at writing reviews.
Who gives time for reviews? Help manage the line.
The strange thing was people's faces. Many had young voices but white hair. Others had outlines blurred like ink in water.
Yeongnyangi. That person's... face is fading.
They sold too much time. Sell a day, and fade by a day's worth.
Then a basket clattered in the middle of the market.
Thief! someone shouted. The crowd parted like a wave. At its center stood a little white rabbit, clutching a bread basket.
No! I didn't steal it! It's a delivery! My sister baked this bread!
A burly merchant thrust out his wrist. Six loaves, eighteen minutes. There was no transaction record, he said.
The crowd encircled the child. Heard that household went broke lately. Broke family's kid stealing—only natural. Murmurs narrowed the circle.
Wait! The child says it's a delivery! No record doesn't automatically mean theft!
Now the looks turned to the flower pig. A talking pig was apparently not a common sight here either.
Lend me the scales, please. I will weigh the six loaves.
Yeongnyangi placed the bread on one side and the order slip tucked under the basket on the other. The scales stopped perfectly level.
The order slip weighs exactly the same as the bread. I know of no thief who carries an order slip with stolen goods.
The crowd murmured, then dispersed. On this island, nobody disputed proof given by scales.
That was really cool. Five stars.
I said what I saw. Keep the stars.
Thank you! Really, thank you! I'm Luna. I live with my sister at the bakery on that hill!
A bakery? If one loaf sells for three minutes, how many seconds does it cost to make?
Don't know the cost. But my sister doesn't sleep lately. She kneads all night, and every morning her face is a little blurrier.
Yeoni and Yeongnyangi exchanged a look, remembering the faded faces in the market.
Luna. Is your sister selling her time?
I don't know. She says she's fine. She says it ten times a day.
A purple tent stood at the entrance to the bakery alley. A handwritten sign hung above it. Compatibility Readings. Free for Ladies.
You there, the pink lady. Excuse me, but may I have your birth date and time first?
Me? I'm a pig.
Pig or cat, everyone was born at some time. I'll read your compatibility for free.
The man inside looked about twenty-six or twenty-seven. His long hair was loosely tied back. He wore a black glove on his right hand only.
Keep away.
Oh, a guardian. Shall I read yours too, Mr. Cat? There is a charge for gentlemen, though.
Yeongnyangi, are you jealous? Your ears went flat.
Caution. He is suspicious.
Suspicious, yes. He's human but not fading on this island. He's the only sharp one.
Moka was right. Everyone in the market had blurred outlines, but this man was distinct as an ink drawing.
An observant otter. I'll read yours later too.
Don't give an otter a compatibility reading.
My name is Yundal. A fortune-teller here, a guide elsewhere. And you, my lady?
Actually, first—when were you born, Mr. Cat? It costs, but I'll give a first-customer discount.
I don't know.
A cat who doesn't know his own birthday. Apparently I'm not the most suspicious one here.
(Come to think of it, I don't know Yeongnyangi's birthday either.)
Um... July sixth, 2002. Around eight thirty in the morning, I'm told.
With his gloved hand, Yundal took a brush and drew eight boxes on paper. He filled some, then the brush stopped.
A vine born in summer's midday. Eulhae Day Pillar, Byeong-o Month Pillar. But...
Your Hour Pillar is empty. The entire space where your birth hour should be.
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □□ ]  4/8
How do you know that? Only we can see it.
I received the same app. Three years ago.
The tent fell quiet. Yeongnyangi's tail struck the floor once.
The same app? You came to mend your destiny too?
Came to mend it, ended up staying. Call me your senior user.
One piece of free advice. People with empty Hour Pillars sell for the highest price here. There is an empty slot in which to hold time.
Sell? Who would buy me?
There is always a buyer. The question is who sets the price first.
Yundal folded the paper and handed it to Yeoni. Beside the Hour Pillar, small letters read: Just like me.
(What does 'like me' mean?)
Compatibility booth review. Free, but somehow felt expensive. Three stars.
Three stars is this tent's all-time high. Usually it's one.
The bakery at the hilltop was small and old. Through the windows, a city above the clouds spread below. Opening the door released the smell of fresh bread. Moka's nose twitched.
That smell is... real. The first real smell I've found on this island.
You brought Luna home. Thank you. Have a loaf each. No charge.
Free? On this island?
If I charge time for bread, it starts tasting like a clock.
Luna's sister's face was half-faded. Only her flour-dusted fingertips were strangely clear.
Good dough texture. Honest hands. But when do you sleep?
The orders are backed up. I have to prepare tomorrow morning's too.
You're lying. You didn't sleep yesterday either.
I can't take free bread. Let me work instead. I'm good at folding dough.
With pig hooves?
Pig hooves are made for dough. They're soft.
Then... twelve minutes per hour. Starting tomorrow morning.
Luna's sister lightly touched her wrist to Yeoni's hoof. Tick. Small words appeared beside the numbers. Scheduled wages: 12 minutes.
My first salary... I mean, hourly wage.
A document stuck out beneath the counter. A contract stamped with a blue rabbit. Yeoni narrowed their eyes.
(Blue Rabbit Finance... a time-loan contract?)
Then the ticking in Yeoni's hoof accelerated. The numbers on the clock mark began draining away by themselves.
Yeongnyangi! My time's shrinking! I haven't bought anything!
Someone is collecting it. Look at the end of that thread.
A fine black thread extended from Yeoni's hoof through the window. It vanished downhill toward the clock tower rising at the island's center.
Something's on top of the tower.
A black silhouette sat on a clock hand at the top. A cloak hem blew in the wind.
That cloak... the tiger.
Yeongnyangi stepped in front of Yeoni. The black thread pulled taut. The numbers kept falling.
Then the bakery door opened. The man from the purple tent stood there, breathing hard, pulling off his right glove with his teeth.
Sooner than I expected. My lady, promise one thing before I cut that thread. Don't be hurt if tomorrow I forget what you see now.

episodes.title: The Hand of the Void
episodes.tag: Episode 14 · The Hand of the Void

beats.t: A black thread stretched taut beyond the bakery window. Whenever it pulled toward the clock tower, the numbers on Yeoni's front hoof lost another digit.
Who are you?! Actually, I don't care who you are! Please do something about this!
That's why I'm here. My lady, your hoof, this way.
I'm not putting Yeoni in the hands of a stranger.
Then try cutting it with your claws, Mr. Cat. Her hoof will come off before the thread does.
The man opened his bare palm. A coin-sized hole pierced its center. Inside, it was blacker than the night sky.
There's... a hole in your hand. An actual hole.
The wind blew backward. The black thread curved toward the hole, then vanished into it with the slurp of a noodle.
[ Time held: 71:41:09 — Frozen ]
It stopped. The numbers stopped!
Ugh... Today's a little salty.
The man clenched his hand. Between his fingers, the edge of the hole had widened by the width of a grain of rice.
Does that hole get bigger every time you use it?
Sharp eyes. Yes, it does. That's why I use it sparingly. Only for ladies like you.
The shadow atop the clock tower tilted its head. Its cloak fluttered once, and it vanished behind the hands.
(It saw us. It watched us cut the thread, and just left.)
The next morning, the first steam rose from the bakery chimney. Yeoni tied on an apron and stood before the dough.
Fold with your wrist, not your palm. Leave the dough some room to breathe.
Room to breathe! Yeongnyangi says that all the time, too. Breathe, breathe, breathe.
Yeoni's hooves suited the dough better than expected. Something soft folding something soft produced neat, even layers.
Good for a first try. Better than Luna.
Sis! You said that was a secret!
A long line stretched past the window. Outside, Moka tapped a pot with his ladle as he organized the queue.
Around lunchtime, Luna's sister touched her wrist to Yeoni's hoof. Tick. The pending numbers turned into real ones.
[ Time earned by my own hands: +00:12:00 ]
Twelve minutes. Twelve minutes I earned.
You're that happy over just twelve minutes?
Not just. I'm not spending these. I'm framing them. In a frame inside my heart.
For the first time, Luna's sister laughed aloud. Only the corners of her mouth stood clear in her fading face.
Luna, let's take a roll to that man from yesterday, too. The one who cut the thread.
Yesterday? What man?
The purple tent. The glove. The man with a hole in his hand.
Someone like that came here? Sis, did we have a visitor yesterday?
Well... I don't remember. We must have been busy.
The merchant at the skewer stall across the way shook their head, too. A purple tent? There isn't a tent like that in this market.
(It was yesterday. We all saw him.)
The bakery door opened. The man from the purple tent came in yawning. Luna greeted him like a customer she had never seen.
Welcome! Is this your first visit?
Yes, my first. Every day is my first.
Mister. Everyone forgot you. In just one night.
I know. That's how it works. After a day, my face fades. After three, my name.
How can you say that with a smile?
If I cried, you might give me free bread. That would be cheating.
I remember. Every single thing that happened yesterday.
Today you do.
That was all Yundal said before picking up a roll. He held out his wrist, but there was no tick. The register could not read it.
Sir, your wrist is... completely empty.
Yes. So I always buy on credit. This lady will pay for me.
Keep your hands off my twelve minutes. Those are for framing.
That expression deserves five stars.
You too, Yeongnyangi?! Star ratings are my specialty!
Just then, the shop window rattled. A blue airship descended directly above the bakery, casting a shadow over it.
A rope ladder dropped from the airship's belly. A white rabbit in a blue vest glided elegantly down it.
Hello there! Blue Rabbit Finance. I'm here for the customer whose payment comes due today.
It's still today. You said I had until evening.
You read the back of the contract, didn't you? Collateral: one tomorrow. Due: noon today. And it's one minute to noon, isn't it?
The clock tower bell rang. Once, twice. Before the twelfth chime had finished, the rabbit snapped its fingers.
Shining sand spilled from Luna's sister's chest. In midair, it gathered into a small hourglass that slipped neatly into the rabbit's paw.
Give it back! Give my sister's tomorrow back!
Don't worry! She'll be perfectly fine today. She just won't have a tomorrow.
Identify yourself. Whose hand are you?
Oh my, what a perceptive cat. I'm the weakest of the Chairman's hands!
If we were fingers, I'd be the little one. Still, I can run an island like this all by myself.
Who's the Chairman?!
I'm not allowed to tell you that. But I'll tell you something nice instead.
The rabbit hopped up to Yeoni. Its pink nose twitched, and its eyes curved into crescents.
Oh, goodness. Your chart has an empty hour slot, doesn't it? That's why your luck always arrives a beat late, isn't it?
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □□ ]  4/8
Blue Rabbit Luck Loans! We'll fill in the blanks for you. Just a tiny bit of interest. And a few of your tomorrows as collateral.
(They can fill the blanks? Then I'd be one step closer to home...)
Yeoni. Don't hold out your hoof.
Fill that blank with something borrowed, and you'll pay interest for life. I'm living proof.
The rabbit's ears pricked up. It studied Yundal for a while, then burst into peals of laughter.
Oh! Now I recognize you. Our Hour of the Rabbit customer! You're still on this island?
Hour of the Rabbit? What does that mean?
That's the hour he was born. Around five in the morning. I ate it instead of collecting interest. Delicious!
Yundal's gloved right hand trembled. His mouth still held its smile, but his eyes did not.
How did it taste? My dawn.
Like dew? A little salty. Someone must have been crying that morning!
My lady. Mr. Cat. Just knock that hourglass out of its paw. I'll eat the rest.
You dare pick on the weakest? Even the weakest has a fat wallet!
The rabbit swept a paw, and gold coins poured out, stacking into a layered shield. Someone's day was engraved on each one.
Metal, I can handle. I'll cut through the tangled grain first.
Yeongnyangi's claws slashed diagonally across the coin shield. It cracked but did not fall. The coins clung to one another and held.
Yundal thrust his bare hand into the gap. The hole swallowed one coin, two, dozens. The shield sank like a sandcastle drained of water.
Urgh... Quite a lot added to my tab today.
Hand it over! Give her tomorrow back!
Yeoni hurled themself forward. Their pig's head struck the rabbit square in the belly. The hourglass flew into the air.
But the rabbit's long ear whipped around and snatched it. The rabbit caught hold of the ladder.
The weakest is always quick at running away! I'll put her tomorrow safely in the vault. The deepest compartment beneath the clock tower!
The airship rose into the clouds. A drifting flyer stuck to Yeoni's nose. Short on time?
It got away... right in front of us.
Outside, Moka flung down his ladle. That rabbit and this island get minus five stars! His voice carried through the glass.
When night fell, the island's ticking slowed a little. Yeoni and Yundal sat side by side on the bakery roof.
Does your hand hurt?
Only when the hole grows. The rest of the time, it's just a little drafty.
What that rabbit said earlier. Is it true? That it ate your birth hour?
It's true. I downloaded that app three years ago, too. Customer Support: the Universe.
You too? So you're my senior?
I am. I just haven't managed to graduate.
Yundal looked up. In the sky above the island, constellations like clock hands turned slowly.
This was the first island I landed on. I didn't have enough time, so I borrowed from that rabbit. A day, two days, a week.
I couldn't pay it back. The interest grew faster than the principal.
So it took the collateral. The hour I was born. Around five in the morning, when my mother held me for the first time.
Yundal took off his glove and held his palm to the moonlight. Stars showed through the hole.
The gap where my hour used to be moved here. Empty time. The Void. It draws everything in, but nothing remains.
Seven of the eight characters won't open the door. The door home.
So you've been here for three years...
At least my compatibility readings have improved. Three years of asking people for their birth dates and times.
Is that something to brag about?
The tip of a navy hat rose over the roof's edge. Yeongnyangi approached silently and sat between them.
Is that hole why people forget you, too?
Mr. Cat has joined us. Yes. Without an hour, there's no hook for a memory to catch on. I slip out of people's minds.
Yundal is an alias, too. It means leap month. A month that's there, yet isn't. Suits me perfectly.
Then what's your real name?
In the vault with my birth hour. The deepest compartment beneath the clock tower. That rabbit helpfully told us earlier.
I've heard a beast guards the vault. A beast with a ledger.
Yes. Black cloak, stripes. It records every bit of time collected in its ledger. I think you already know it, my lady.
(The shadow on the clock tower. The tiger.)
Yeoni looked down at the numbers on their hoof. Beside the frozen 71:41:09, a small twelve minutes glimmered.
I earned my twelve minutes. Her tomorrow is something she earned. And your name belongs to you.
The one who takes someone else's things is the thief. The one who takes them back isn't.
Then let's rob it. The vault.
Rob it? The clock tower vault?
Yeoni. Did you just say we should rob the vault?
Moka poked his head out of the window below the roof. I heard rob. I'm good at luring guards with delicious smells.
Ha... First plan like that I've heard in three years. I like how reckless it is.
It's not reckless. It's planless. I'll make the plan.
See? Yeongnyangi wants to do it, too.
Then the bakery's attic hatch burst open. Barefoot and in pajamas, Luna scrambled onto the roof.
My sister... She won't wake up. No matter how much I call her or shake her, she won't wake up.
[ Luna's sister · Today remaining: 05:59:59 ]
The number dropped by one. The today of someone whose tomorrow had been stolen was silently running out.
Six hours. We open the vault before dawn.

episodes.title: How to Support a Breath
episodes.tag: EP.14A · How to Support a Breath

beats.t: In the bakery attic, Yundal unfolded a sheet of paper on a table made of stacked flour sacks. It showed a charcoal cross section of the clock tower.
The vault has seven levels beneath the clock tower. The deeper you go, the slower time moves.
By the last chamber, a single step takes about an hour. One breath could take a day.
So if you sneeze down there, you lose a week?
Hold in your sneezes. Especially you, Moka.
Why especially me?
Otters have sensitive noses. Oh, speaking of which, what time were you born, Moka?
You're asking an otter his birth time at a moment like this? One star.
That's a habit of yours, isn't it? Asking everyone you meet.
Occupational hazard. Once I know someone's birth hour, I can see where they're likely to stumble.
I keep stumbling at the seventh chamber. Time has almost stopped there.
Ordinary breathing won't sustain you there. Your breath freezes and catches in your chest.
Your breath freezes? Then how do we get in?
Support it. Hold it up from underneath so it doesn't fall.
Before that, let's assign our roles. Moka, you'll lure the guards at the entrance with food smells.
What are the guards? Rabbits?
People who couldn't repay their time. They stand guard outside the vault to pay their debts. They'll be hungry. They've been hungry a very long time.
Then I'm feeding them, not luring them. That I can do.
Moka's whiskers drooped, then rose again. He seemed to be remembering the faces of the people on the Island of Expression who had lost their sense of taste.
Mr. Cat opens the way, I eat the locked doors, and our lady goes to the deepest chamber.
Why do I have to go deepest?
The seventh chamber only opens with time you've earned yourself. You're the only one of us who has any.
(My twelve minutes.)
Yeoni covered the small writing on one hoof with the other. The twelve minutes they had meant to frame suddenly felt heavy.
Can I review this plan? Five stars for recklessness, three for detail. I can't give the survival rate a rating yet.
An honest review. The best I've had in three years.
On the roof, the island's ticking grew distant. Yeongnyangi sat facing Yeoni and held out a paw.
Rest your hoof on my paw. Press lightly as you breathe in, and don't lift it when you breathe out. Let's try it together.
Press, don't let go. Got it. Seems easy enough.
The first breath was easy. On the second, the center of Yeoni's chest began to ache. On the third, their hoof slipped.
Not easy at all. My breath keeps running upward.
Because you're pulling it up. Don't tug at it. Set it down on the ground.
(Don't tug at it. I've heard that somewhere before.)
Yeoni closed their eyes. They sent the breath down below their belly, instead of into their chest. Yeongnyangi's paw supported it from beneath.
A pale green shoot sprouted from the tip of Yeoni's hoof. It slowly wound its way up over Yeongnyangi's paw.
I did it! Did you see? A sprout!
At that moment, silver flashed from Yeongnyangi's paw. The climbing shoot was silently severed and fell to the roof.
Uh... why did it get cut?
My energy is Metal. A power that can cut Wood.
Remember that. Mine is an energy that hurts you. The closer you get, the more it does.
But you just supported my breath. Would an energy that hurts me hold me up like that?
That's...
You can't answer, can you? Then I'll go with my interpretation. Half cutting, half supporting.
Instead of answering, Yeongnyangi picked up the severed sprout and tucked it behind Yeoni's ear.
Is this... a decoration? Like a ribbon?
Keep it as evidence. So you can't change your story later about getting hurt in training.
First cat I've ever seen tuck evidence behind someone's ear. Four stars.
Why deduct one?
Your explanation was too short.
Beneath the attic window, Moka clicked his tongue as he turned a skewer. Are those two training or dating?
We can hear you! We're training! I've even got evidence!
After Yeoni went back down to the attic, Yeongnyangi stayed at the roof's edge. In the moonlight, he turned his left paw over.
The fur on its underside was burned in patches, scorched in the crow's courtroom. Green sap from the sprout had spread over the wound.
That paw still hasn't healed.
How long have you been watching?
Since we first met in the tent. Whenever you take a step, your left paw is always half a beat late.
Hurting Officer is strong in our lady's chart. The energy that makes words into fire. The stronger that fire grows, the more it hurts the Officer.
Don't say who that Officer is. Not to Yeoni, either.
If you don't say it, it'll all come out someday. Hiding a wound doesn't make it smaller.
I know. But not now. I don't want Yeoni to become afraid of their own fire.
Yundal watched Yeongnyangi's profile for a while. The cat's violet eyes spread into gold, fixed only on the light in the attic window.
Keeping a secret is expensive. Your birth hour should cover it, Mr. Cat.
I don't know it. My birthday.
You really don't know? I thought you were joking yesterday.
Yundal stopped smiling and patted Yeongnyangi's shoulder once with his gloved hand.
All right. I'll put it on your tab. My whole life's on credit, too. I know the feeling.
At two in the morning, the four gathered in the shadows of the square beneath the clock tower. Its hands turned sluggishly overhead.
Forty skewers for the scent diversion. Twenty spicy, twenty sweet.
Luna's sister has four hours left. We get out before sunrise.
[ Luna's sister · Today remaining: 03:58:12 ]
Don't forget how to support your breath.
How could I? I've got the evidence tucked behind my ear.
Yeoni looked up at the clock tower. Nobody stood on its hands. That was even more frightening.
The tiger is below. A vault keeper doesn't leave its vault.
Those stripes. That's the one that collected the applause on the Island of Expression. This time, it's my turn.
We're not going to fight. We're going to get things back.
Remember those words in the seventh chamber, too.
Yundal adjusted his glove. His fingertips trembled ever so slightly.
Let's find your name, too. Once we do, I'll be the first to call you by it.
Then you'll be the third person to say my name, my lady.
Why third?
First my mother, second me. Then you.
The tower bell rang twice. Following the shadows, the four slipped through the clock tower door.
The clock tower's back entrance was shabbier than expected. A rusty lift rope hung beside a narrow door barely wide enough for a bread basket.
My sister sends bread down here every morning before dawn. Breakfast for the vault guards.
Thanks to Miss Luna, we can skip seven layers of front doors. You're today's star contributor.
Then do I get five stars?
Five stars and a flower stamp. Let's tell your sister when she wakes up.
At the far end of the square, a lantern swayed. A rabbit patrol in a blue uniform passed by, yawning.
Get down. The patrol comes around on the hour. Four minutes until the next one.
(Four minutes. On this island, that's a roll and a half.)
Look at that patrol rabbit's ears. They're twitching at the smell of skewers. That one's hungry, too.
Once the patrol turned the corner, the four darted from shadow to shadow. Luna led the way and lifted the narrow door's bolt.
The lift basket creaked downward. One after another, the four and Luna clung to the rope and slid into darkness.
The first level was a factory. Hundreds of people worked machines in silence. Instead of coins, ticking grains of sand poured from them.
Are these all guards? They look more like workers.
This is the level where people work off the time they owe. Their days don't pass while they work here. But they can't go home, either.
Every worker's face was blurred. Some were children, others elderly. Among the indistinct faces, one large panda struggled to stay awake.
They all look hungry. Faces that have lost their taste.
Change of plan. I'm feeding them, not luring them. The scent diversion is a bonus.
Moka lit his portable brazier. Twenty spicy skewers sizzled at once, stirring the factory air.
One by one, the machines fell silent. The workers raised their heads. The sound of swallowing spread among the blurred faces.
Line up. No charge. But if it's good, tell me it's good. That's your payment.
The panda took the first skewer. With one bite, the blurred edges of its eyes briefly cleared. Delicious, it said in the smallest voice.
Did you hear? It's delicious!
Of course. This time, the flavor is real.
A small child stood at the end of the skewer line, a baby rabbit with folded ears. Even after receiving a skewer, the child only stared at their wrist without eating.
Not eating? It's good.
The child held out a wrist. Tiny numbers blinked on it. Debt remaining before home: 00:01:00.
One minute? You're here because of one minute?
The child nodded. Just one more minute of work, and they could go to their mother, they said softly through the smell of skewers.
(One minute. With the twelve I earned...)
Not now, my lady. That's the price of the seventh chamber's door. We'll see them again on the way back.
Wait for me. I'll make sure to stop here on our way back. Eat your skewer before it gets cold.
It smells like my sister's bread. A warm smell.
We go down while Moka keeps their attention. Time slows from the second level onward.
Miss Luna, stay beside Moka. The grown-ups will go below.
No. It's my sister's day. I'm going to find it.
Then come with us as far as the third level. Wait there, and I'll bring it back for you. I promise.
The second level. A golden corridor stretched on endlessly. Needles on the gauges set into the walls moved as slowly as honey.
After one step, Yeoni's feet grew heavy. At the second, their own heartbeat thundered in their ears.
My breath... it's rising.
Support it. Like yesterday. Set it down low.
Yeoni sent their breath below their belly. The severed sprout behind their ear stirred slightly. Their legs moved again.
Before the third-level door, the corridor jolted. Floor panels flipped, and metal arms shot upward. A silent trap, without even an alarm.
Yeongnyangi sprang forward. His golden claws cut three metal arms in one stroke. The severed arms fell slowly through the slowed time.
The way's clear. You need to open that door.
Yes, yes. I'll eat the locked parts.
Yundal pressed his palm to the door handle. The whole lock disappeared into the hole. His shoulders twitched once.
Locks on this island taste strongly of iron. Makes my teeth ache.
Mister, it got bigger again just now, didn't it? Let me see your hand.
It might hurt less if a lady held my hand.
Say things like that when your hand isn't hurting!
They parted with Luna on the third level. She crouched by the door and spread five fingers. Come back within five hours.
The fourth, fifth, and sixth levels. Time thickened as they descended. Falling drops of water hung suspended like pearls.
I think I'm going to sneeze.
Do it now, and that's a week.
I know. That's why I'm holding it in. This level gets one star.
Moka's nose twitched. Without a word, Yeongnyangi covered it with the hem of his cloak. The sneeze vanished quietly into the star-embroidered lining.
Your cloak has a sneeze filter, too, Yeongnyangi? One extra star.
Free of charge. Today only.
The seventh chamber. A vast circular vault stood open. Thousands of hourglasses lined the walls in tier upon tier.
Is every one of these someone's day?
A day, a month, ten years. Time sold and stolen on this island.
Each hourglass made a tiny sound. A child's laughter, rice cooking, someone calling a name. The sounds of days that had been sold.
All these sounds have flavor. Sounds like the smell of dinner in someone's home.
Don't listen too long. Follow someone else's day, and you could find yourself stuck in it.
[ Luna's sister · Today remaining: 01:12:40 ]
Yeoni searched the labels one by one. At the end of the third row, they found an hourglass bearing a drawing of flour-covered hands.
Found it! Hers! It has a picture of hands!
Yundal ran to the opposite wall. One drawer at the very bottom had a blank label instead of a name. The drawer was empty.
It's gone. The place where my birth hour should be.
Mister...
It's all right. That rabbit must carry it around. The type that gets attached to things it's eaten.
Then came the sound of a page turning in the center of the vault. Very slowly, very deliberately.
A black tiger sat on a round dais at the vault's center. A ledger lay open over its cloak, and a golden egg rested at its feet.
You're late, pig. Though I knew you'd take the bakery lift.
You knew, and you didn't stop us?
No vault keeper stops guests coming in. It stops them leaving.
The tiger turned a page. Yeoni saw it clearly. Among the densely filled lines, only one was empty.
[ Flower Pig · Uncollected ]
I was told to collect your time on the next island. But you've walked right into the vault yourself.
Who told you that? Is your boss in that ledger, too?
So many questions. Leave a debt alone, and it grows. That's why you collect on time.
Then what about you? What did you borrow, and from whom?
The tiger's tail stopped. Its page-turning paw hung in the air for the briefest moment.
Nothing a pig needs to know.
(Just now, it couldn't answer.)
Keep your paws off Yeoni.
Stay out of it, cat. You're already cracked, too. That left paw.
Yeongnyangi's left front paw twitched almost imperceptibly. Yeoni missed it. Their eyes were on the egg at the tiger's feet.
(That egg... why does it seem so familiar? It's like something inside me is calling.)
My lady, that egg. 辰, Chen. The character for your Hour Branch. Chen Earth is a storehouse. This entire vault was built on that egg.
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ? ]
Why is my character buried under a vault?
As though it recognized Yeoni, the egg trembled very slightly. Something stirred beneath its golden shell.
A chart with an empty hour is a house with its storehouse left open. Anyone can come in and stack things inside.
You're talking too much. Give me the egg. And give her day back.
The tiger swept its tail once. Black water spread along the clock hands on the floor. The moment it touched an ankle, it froze time.
Don't touch the water! Touch it, and you'll stop!
Yeongnyangi drew out a golden line and split the flow. Through the opening, Moka leaped and clutched Luna's sister's hourglass to his chest.
Got it! Hers! I've got it right here!
Take that one. It wasn't in my ledger to begin with. It belongs to the rabbit's share.
Then I'll take that egg, too.
That, you may not.
Yeoni leaped onto the dais. The instant their hoof touched the egg, the entire dais became a giant clock face.
A bell rang seven times. The clock hands spun around Yeoni, and transparent glass walls rose around their body.
I can't move! My breath... I can't get my breath down!
[ Time trap · Escape price: 72:00:00  Held: 71:53:09  Shortfall: 00:06:51 ]
Yeoni.
I won't say I'm sorry. There's no column for that in the ledger.
Beyond the glass, two blue ears dropped from a vent in the vault ceiling. Blue Rabbit hung upside down and waved.
Oh my! You're exactly six minutes and fifty-one seconds short. Shall Blue Rabbit Finance lend it to you? Just a teeny-tiny bit of interest!
(Borrow, and I get out. Refuse, and I stop here.)

episodes.title: The Weight of Direct Wealth
episodes.tag: Episode 16 · The Weight of Direct Wealth

beats.t: Time inside the glass walls was thick as honey. While Yeoni blinked once, Yeongnyangi called their name three times outside.
Don't think too long! Borrow just six minutes and fifty-one seconds, and you're out. Sign with a hoofprint!
The contract the rabbit held out slid through the glass and floated before Yeoni's nose. In the interest column, tiny writing went on without end.
(Six minutes and fifty-one seconds. A little more time than the price of two rolls.)
My lady, read all the way to the end. My contract started out that length, too.
Oh, do be quiet, Hour of the Rabbit customer! Advice from a failed predecessor doesn't qualify for a discount.
Yeoni read the bottom line. Late interest payments require additional collateral. Collateral: the customer's birth hour.
You said you'd fill my hour slot. So in the end, you're planning to take it away.
My, aren't you clever! But if you can't get out now, you'll simply stop here, won't you?
Yeoni. Support your breath. Think after that.
Yeoni lowered their breath beneath their belly. Even in the dense time, one breath settled into its proper place. Their head cleared a little.
(If the trap measures time, I don't have enough. But this island's been strange from the beginning.)
(Six rolls and one order slip weighed the same. This island measures weight, not length.)
Tiger. Does this trap measure time by how many hours it is? Or how much it weighs?
Holding its ledger below the dais, the tiger raised its head. This time, it looked straight at Yeoni.
Weight. The only thing in this vault that measures length is the rabbit's ledger.
Oh, Mr. Vault Keeper! You can't just go spilling trade secrets like that!
Then I'll use this. Nothing borrowed, nothing given.
Yeoni lifted a hoof. Beside the nearly seventy-two hours, the small twelve minutes shimmered. Yeoni separated out only those twelve minutes and placed them on the clock face's scale pan.
[ Time received: 71:41:09 — Weight: 0.3 ] [ Time earned by my own hands: 00:12:00 — Weighing ]
The scale's needle trembled. A little at first, then wildly. It made a full circle and stopped at seventy-two.
The glass wall cracked. The cracks spread like a web, then shattered with a chime, scattering into glittering sand.
I'm out! My twelve minutes weighed the same as seventy-two hours!
Direct Wealth. What you earn by your own hands is heavy. The heaviest thing on this island.
A pig kneading dough broke the vault. I'll bump this island up to three stars.
[ Time earned by my own hands: 00:01:00 remaining ]
Huh? One minute left. Guess it only cost eleven.
What kind of rule is that?! Weight? That's cheating!
The rabbit launched itself from the vent. Its paw aimed not at Yeoni but at the golden egg on the dais.
Yundal thrust out his bare hand. The hole swallowed the entire lump of coins in the rabbit's paw. The rabbit lost its balance in midair.
Urgh... Today's tab is going to be really hard to pay.
A cord swung from the stumbling rabbit's neck. From its end hung a tiny hourglass filled with dawn light.
This? Our Hour of the Rabbit customer's! Come and get it if you want it!
Yundal's hand reached halfway toward the hourglass. Just then, a chunk of stone fell from the cracked ceiling, straight toward Yeoni's head.
Yundal turned his hand. The hole swallowed the stone. In that instant, the rabbit bounded back into the vent.
The weakest is always quick at running away! I'll show you your birth hour again next time!
Mister! You could've grabbed it just now!
I could have. But then your head would have been flattened. Those numbers don't add up.
Enough. This is as far as you go.
The tiger climbed onto the dais. With the golden egg beneath its paw, black water began spreading across the floor again.
Take her day. That was the rabbit's share. But not the egg. That's in my ledger.
You said that egg was my character. Why is my character in your ledger?
Because I got into the empty house first.
Yeoni is not empty.
The whole vault shook. Something collapsed upstairs. The machines stopped, and the workers' screams traveled down the corridors.
Breaking the trap has brought the levels down! The people on the first level are getting trapped!
(The factory. That child.)
Yeoni looked once at the egg. Once at the tiger. Then they turned and ran toward the lift rope.
Pig! What about the egg?
Later! There are people upstairs!
The first-level factory tilted. Sand poured between the machines like waterfalls. Luna and Moka were pushing the workers toward the narrow door.
You're late, pig! But I kept her day safe. Nice and warm against my chest.
The panda braced a leaning machine with its broad back. Workers filed out beneath it, skewers still in their mouths.
Yeoni! That little kid won't come out! They say they still have a minute left!
The baby rabbit with folded ears sat in front of a stopped machine. The wrist numbers had not changed. Debt remaining before home: 00:01:00.
Hey, little one. Let's go. This place is collapsing.
The child shook their head. If they left a debt behind, their mother's door would not open. Instead of crying, they clung to the machine.
(My one minute. This time, truly the last minute.)
Yeoni looked down at their hoof. One small line of writing blinked. The last fragment of the twelve minutes they had wanted to frame.
Yeoni touched their hoof to the child's wrist. Tick. The tiniest sound.
[ Flower Pig → Baby Rabbit: 00:01:00 ]  [ Debt remaining before home: 00:00:00 ]
There. Go home now. Take your skewer with you.
For the first time, the child's blurred face became clear. Clutching the skewer, the child ran toward the light beyond the narrow door.
Pig, you just broke your frame. The one inside your heart.
That's okay. The frame's empty, but the nail's still there. I can earn more.
The black tiger stood in the shadow of a collapsed machine, the golden egg in its mouth. Its face said it had heard that tiny tick.
Stupid pig. That minute could have paid off a line or so in your ledger.
I write my own ledger. And I decide where my last minute goes.
The tiger said nothing for a long time. Then the egg in its mouth made a tiny but unmistakable cracking sound.
The egg broke. A palm-sized, ocher dragon crawled between the shell fragments, slipped from the tiger's mouth, and landed on Yeoni's hoof.
A dragon. A baby dragon!
It was my egg. Written in my ledger. Why is it going to you?
Chen Earth is a storehouse. A storehouse sides with the one who gives things out, not the one who piles them up. That's what my teacher said.
The baby dragon curled up on the clock pattern at Yeoni's wrist. The pattern melted away, and a single character engraved itself in its place.
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  5/8
辰. Chen. The fifth character.
The tiger closed its empty mouth. It opened the ledger, looked at one line, then shut it again without writing anything.
Uncollected today. Next time, I collect everything.
The black cloak disappeared into the shadow of the fallen machine. Only a piece of eggshell on the floor remained warm.
Dawn. The island's sun caught on the tip of a clock tower hand. In the bakery attic, Moka carefully took the hourglass from his chest.
When it touched Luna's sister's chest, the sand flowed backward into her. Color slowly returned to her faded face.
Luna...? Why are you crying? We need to make the morning dough.
You idiot, Sis! Never sell a day again! Promise me!
I promise. And for today, I think I'll ask customers to pay for their bread with stories instead of time.
I like that. Stories taste like dough before it's baked.
Murmurs rose from the square outside. The people from the factory studied their wrists and looked at one another's faces.
The blurred faces grew clearer little by little. With a skewer in its mouth, the panda bowed to the bakery window.
See? That's the effect of my skewers. Half pig effect, too.
I think this island can have four stars now.
Mister. We missed your birth hour, but come with us. We're bound to meet that rabbit again.
My lady, you just asked me to come with you, didn't you? I'll take that as a sign we're compatible.
Don't believe that's the whole story. Just use it as a guide when choosing your path.
There goes Mr. Cat's jealousy again. All right, I'll come as your guide. A guide who's wandered all four skies.
Then I'll stop calling you mister. I'll call you Yundal. Yundal.
For a moment, Yundal lost his words. Apparently, it had been three years since someone had spoken that alias with a smile.
Yes. Today, I'll go by that name.
Yeongnyangi discreetly hid his left paw behind his back. Yundal's eyes followed it, then returned to Yeoni without a word.
Just then, the baby dragon sneezed. Along with eggshell crumbs, an old sheet of paper shot from its nostrils. It was a library borrowing card.
[ Library of Resources · Borrowing record — Flower Pig: The First Spring · Not returned ]
The First Spring? I've never borrowed a book like that.
That's where memories become books. If a book you've never borrowed is checked out to you, it's a book you've forgotten, my lady.
Five in the morning. The bakery attic was still dark, and only the borrowing card beneath Yeoni's hoof was warm.
(The First Spring. Not returned. But I've never borrowed a book like that.)
The corner of the card smelled of water. Cold and a little lonely, like the ground at a bus stop after the rain.
Why aren't you asleep? Dawn's still a long way off.
Look. Apparently, there's a book checked out in my name. But I don't remember a thing.
Yeongnyangi looked down at the card. For a fleeting moment, his left paw lifted from the floor, then settled quietly again.
I've heard library overdue fines are terrifying. So go to sleep.
(That paw just now. Is it hurting again? If I ask, he'll just say no again.)
The baby dragon sleeping around Yeoni's wrist woke with a flick of its tail. It sniffed the card, then sneezed loudly onto it.
A bookshelf-sized opening appeared in the attic wall. The sound of turning pages swept through it like breathing.
What now, this early? Pig, what did you open this time? It's not a fridge, is it?
Ah, this door. It's been a while. The Library of Resources.
Mister, you've been here before?
There isn't a sky I haven't visited in three years. This place is quite friendly, as long as you keep quiet.
Quiet. The hardest word in the world for me. Followed by diet.
Beyond the opening, endless bookshelves stretched beneath a domed ceiling. All the books slowly swelled and sank.
The books... they're breathing. They really are.
Every book here is someone's memory. As long as its owner lives and remembers, it breathes like this.
Golden letters slowly rose over the marble floor. The rules of the library.
[ Library of Resources · One book per visitor · A book once read cannot be undone ]
(Exactly one book. Then I only need to find The First Spring. Simple.)
One book? Stingy, stingy. Even a market sample stand lets you come back three times.
Moka's voice echoed to the ceiling. Dozens of books on the nearest shelf snapped their covers shut at once.
Then a papery shhhh spread from all directions. Moka quietly put his ladle between his teeth.
The books are telling you off. Mr. Otter, please keep the rapping to a whisper.
Whispered rap isn't rap. It's prayer. You're asking me to change genres.
Yeongnyangi followed a step behind. Among all the breathing books, he alone seemed to walk holding his breath.
There was no librarian at the central desk. Instead, a large catalog lay open, turning its own pages.
Give it your name, and it'll tell you your shelf. Ladies first.
Yeoni. Oh, and just in case, could you look under Flower Pig, too?
The catalog's letters spread like ink, then gathered into a single line.
[ Flower Pig · Collection: 23 volumes · On loan: 1 volume, The First Spring · Borrower: ■■■ ]
The borrower's name... it's erased. Like someone deliberately blacked it out.
More importantly, twenty-three volumes? Your life's twenty-three books long, pig? Mostly about eating, I bet.
Half of them are reviews! Star ratings are perfectly legitimate memories.
While the others laughed, Yeongnyangi studied the catalog. A tiny bead of water had formed over the erased borrower's name.
Let's find the shelf. This isn't somewhere to linger.
On the way to Yeoni's shelves, Yundal stopped at another section. He pressed his gloved palm hard with his other hand.
Is your book here, too, mister?
It is. Want to see? You need to save your one book, so just the cover.
The book Yundal pulled out was thin. The place for a name on its cover was blank, and its breathing was very shallow.
Every time someone forgets me, it loses a page. Last year, it was twice this thick.
Unable to find an answer, Yeoni stared at the thin book. A fresh line of pencil writing appeared on its last page. The lady called me Yundal.
That was yesterday.
Yes. Thanks to you, I gained a page. It's the first time my book has grown thicker in three years.
Hey, con artist. Save that kind of story for mealtimes. You're giving your listeners indigestion.
Then dinner tonight is on Mr. Otter.
How did you get that from what I said?!
Yeoni's shelf was lower than expected. Every spine bore a tiny flower, and at the far end was a gap the width of one book.
Wow, my books. This is My Elementary School Lunch Ratings. And this is I Hate the Boss at My First Part-Time Job.
Your way of naming things hasn't changed since childhood.
That's a compliment, right? I'll take it as one. No objections accepted.
Yeoni slipped a hoof into the gap. The inside of the shelf was damp. Someone had taken the book with wet hands.
(This is where it was. The First Spring.)
Yeoni. What will you do if you find that book?
Read it. It's my book. Why?
Nothing. Just asking.
Yeongnyangi looked away from the gap. Yeoni was just turning to look at his face again.
Then glass shattered deep in the library. Every breathing book held its breath at once.
In the inner reading room, the most precious memories lay in glass cases. Several black hands crawled over the cases like spiders.
The protected shelves. They only keep memories there that the owner must never forget.
One black hand pierced the glass and picked up a thin book. Then it tore out and ate the pages one by one, savoring them.
[ Mother's Lullaby · Owner: Baby Otter · Pages remaining: 9 → 6 ]
Baby otter? Hey, that belongs to a kid from our island! Spit it out!
Yeongnyangi leaped first. His claws split the black hand, but the severed fingers scattered like ink, then joined again.
I can't cut it. This isn't a body.
A fine read. Other people's memories... always taste so sweet.
The voice came from no single place. It was as though all the darkness between the shelves had opened its mouth at once.
Put that down. It's someone else's lullaby!
Flames burst from Yeoni's hoof. The black hand flinched back, and at the same moment, a nearby bookshelf's corner caught fire.
My lady! This is a library! A library!
Moka beat the burning shelf with his ladle. The books huddled together, rustling like screams.
(No fire. Here, the stronger I get, the more other people's memories burn.)
Yeoni. Breathe first. Set it down on the ground.
Yeoni drew back the fire. Their hoof trembled. The black hand crawled toward the lullaby's remaining pages again.
Then the rules on the floor glowed faintly. Only now did Yeoni see the small writing beneath them.
[ Addendum · A memory read aloud with care returns to its owner ]
(Read it aloud, and it goes back. But that will use up my one book.)
My lady, if you use it now, you won't be able to open The First Spring. One book per person.
I know. But my spring can wait a little. This one's being eaten right now.
Yeoni jumped between the black hands and hugged the lullaby book. The six remaining pages trembled against their chest.
Yeoni read the first page aloud. Sleep well, my baby. The ripples hold you, and Mama holds the ripples.
When the moon rises, the river sleeps, and you sleep, too. Mama is here. When you open your eyes, I'll be here.
The voice was awkward, without a tune. Yet with each line, another black hand slipped from the book.
Care, is it? There's no flavor in that.
As the voice retreated, the black hands dissolved into the darkness. Only Yeoni's reading remained in the room.
At the last page, the book melted into golden light and flew through the ceiling. Toward a sleepless baby otter on some faraway island.
[ Mother's Lullaby · Returned · Reader: Flower Pig (1/1) ]
Pig... you just threw away your one book. You came here to find your twenty-three-volume life.
I didn't throw it away. I lent it. Though I won't ask for it back.
I've never seen a visitor spend their one book on someone else's. If there were a librarian, you'd get a prize.
I'll give the prize. Half my snack tonight.
Half? Only half? Mr. Cat's a little stingy today.
With the black hands gone, the library began breathing again. But something about its breathing sounded damp.
Strange. This sky doesn't even get rain, to protect the paper.
A splash sounded beneath Yeoni's hoof. Cold water seeped up through the cracks in the marble.
A large pawprint marked the puddle. It resembled a cat's, but was several times larger.
The wet tracks circled the reading room and led to the stairs descending below. They smelled like the drop of water on the erased borrower's name.
The tiger. It got here before us.
(The smell of rain. Exactly the same smell as the card.)
Water rose with a rushing sound below the stairs. Then a low, chilling voice floated over it.
I'm taking The First Spring. You can wash away right there, pig.
Water surged upward from the stairs. Every breathing book drew a deep breath at once.
In an instant, the water rose to their knees, then their waists. Holding their breath, books floated up and drifted away.
OIIINK! My feet! I can't touch the bottom!
Pigs float! Stay calm. You're a swim ring right now!
Yeoni flailed. Their body floated, but it would not move as they wished. The current kept pulling them between the shelves.
The middle of the water suddenly went still. A black spine slowly surfaced there.
The black tiger. Droplets clung to the tips of its fur, and the golden ring at its neck shone wetly.
It would have been better if it had ended upstairs. But you had to follow me down.
Give my book back! My name was on the borrowing card!
Cards blur when they get wet. Names, too.
The tiger struck the surface with a paw. Water rose like a wall and swallowed an entire bookshelf.
(Hold on. Wood has roots. I just need to put down roots.)
Green roots stretched from Yeoni's hooves, searching for the floor. But they lost their way in the water and floated upward.
They won't hold. My roots can't find the bottom!
There's too much water! When water overflows, it carries Wood away, roots and all. Excess Water Sets Wood Adrift—水多木漂!
Give me a life jacket, not a proverb!
The next wave swallowed Yeoni. Their small body was sucked between the shelves.
Yeoni.
Yeongnyangi plunged in without hesitation. But the moment his fluffy fur soaked up water, his small body began sinking like a stone.
Mr. Cat! Metal generates Water, so water drains your strength! Metal generates Water—金生水!
I know. I know, but does that matter right now?
Yeongnyangi gritted his teeth and paddled. For every handspan forward, he sank two.
Oh, honestly. Everyone move. Who here can actually swim?
Moka clamped his ladle between his teeth and slipped underwater. One sweep of his violet tail like an oar split the current.
You're coming at an otter with water? This is my front yard.
Moka grabbed a fistful of the sinking Yeongnyangi's cloak collar and pulled him up. Dangling from the otter's hand, the drenched cat broke the surface.
Let go of the cloak. Being dragged by the scruff is beneath a cat's dignity.
Find your dignity after the water drains. For now, just breathe, you heavy lump of iron.
Find Yeoni first. Not me.
I know, I know. But I've got to fish you out before I fish out the pig. If you both sink, that's two round trips for me.
Moka pushed Yeongnyangi onto a floating bookshelf, then threw himself back into the water. This time downward, toward where Yeoni had vanished.
Underwater, all was quiet. Soaked books drifted slowly like jellyfish, and someone's memories glimmered faintly between their pages.
(Breathe. Support the breath. Yeongnyangi said so. Don't pull it up. Set it down on the ground.)
Yeoni stopped flailing their hooves. As they relaxed, the current stopped shoving them and wrapped around them instead.
Right ahead, an old umbrella drifted upside down. It was exactly like the one Yeoni had left abandoned in the corner of their attic room.
A torn page clung beneath it. A bus stop in the rain. Two people under one umbrella. Their faces were blurred by water.
(Is that... me? It looks like me, but I don't remember this.)
A black paw snatched the page. The tiger stared at Yeoni from directly ahead. Even underwater, its voice rang clear.
Don't look. That isn't for you to see.
Why? It's a book borrowed in my name. Why do you get to decide?
Some debts are better left unknown. Especially ones you can never repay.
(This smell. The rain smell from the card. You were the one who erased the borrower's name.)
Do you know me? You've acted like you know me ever since we first met.
No. And I don't need to. I only collect what's written in the ledger.
Liar. If it was just something in your ledger, why did you hide that page so quickly?
The tiger's red eyes wavered for a moment. They alone seemed untouched by the water.
The tiger crumpled the page in its paw. Yet the movement was strangely careful. As though hiding it, not throwing it away.
Then the darkness at the bottom split. Five black fingers rose like seaweed and wrapped around the tiger's ring.
What are you hesitating for? Sink that pig.
You said I only needed to retrieve the book. As for the pig...
That is an order. The price for leaving an uncollected entry in your ledger.
The golden ring tightened. The tiger caught a short breath, then raised its paw and laid it on Yeoni's head.
(It's pressing me. Down, down.)
But the paw did not press immediately. For one beat, one very short beat, the tiger stayed still.
Get that paw off, Stripes!
Moka charged through the current. He lashed the tiger's side with his tail, then seized Yeoni's scruff in his teeth and pulled them up.
The baby dragon on Yeoni's wrist snapped its eyes open. It looked at the water once, then opened its mouth wide.
The dragon began drinking. A whirlpool streamed into its tiny mouth, and the water swallowing the shelves swiftly receded.
The drained library floor was sodden as mud. Soaked books lay scattered everywhere, catching their breath in thin gasps.
This little thing drank all that water?
Chen Earth is a storehouse for water. 辰 is the earth that holds water in. That dragon didn't come to you by chance, my lady.
Its belly's going to burst. Hey, dragon. How many liters did you drink?
With its belly bulging, the baby dragon curled around Yeoni's wrist again. Then it gave a small burp of water droplets.
Five stars. No, six. Even if it breaks the rating rules.
At the far end of the muddy floor, the tiger stood on the landing leading down. The ring at its neck still glowed red-hot.
I didn't know you traveled with a dragon, too. That won't work next time, either.
Why did you stop earlier? When it told you to push me down. You stopped for one beat.
You imagined it. Everything looks slow underwater.
The tiger turned away. Before descending, it drew its clenched paw once toward its chest, like someone protecting something from getting wet.
Its black tail vanished into the darkness below. Only wet pawprints continued down, one step at a time.
At the water's edge, Yeongnyangi shook himself. With his fur plastered to his body, he looked half his usual size. Water dripped from his hat's tassel. Coughing, he stood.
Mr. Cat! Are you okay? Did you swallow much water?
I'm fine. Moka saved my life. Don't make me say it twice.
Should've recorded that. I could've milked it for the rest of my life.
Yeoni looked at Yeongnyangi's left paw. A stain like red rust spread over the scorched patches. He quickly hid it beneath his cloak.
That paw. It's been strange for a while. Show me.
It's because it's wet. Iron rusts when it gets wet, too. It'll be better once it dries.
Yundal glanced at Yeongnyangi. He said nothing. Instead, he pushed his gloved hand deep into his pocket.
(They all know something. There's something only I don't know.)
The soaked books struggled to breathe on the floor. Some had pages stuck together, blocking their airways.
Leave them like this, and they'll all stiffen up. But we saw what happened with fire earlier.
That's because you used too much heat. Pig, do you bake bread with the heat turned all the way up?
No. Then the outside burns and the inside stays raw.
Exactly. Drying books is the same. Low and slow. About as warm as your palm.
Yeoni gently rested a hoof on a book. Instead of flames, they slowly let warmth flow through. Warm as a quilt laid in the sunshine.
The stuck pages separated one by one. The wet book gave a little cough, then began breathing again.
It worked! It's breathing. Moka, are you actually a genius?
Only noticing now? Cooking is the study of handling fire. Rap is the study of handling breath.
Expression helping Resources. Using fire to dry soaked memories—this may be a first in the library's history.
Yeoni looked down at what they held. A corner of the page the tiger had crumpled and taken had caught on their hoof and stayed behind.
A scrap the size of a fingernail. The edge of an upturned umbrella. And one tiny line of writing. Let's share the umbrella.
(Let's share. Who said that to whom?)
A staircase emerged beneath the wall as the water drained. Wet golden writing hung above its entrance.
[ Basement Level 3 · Things That Have Not Happened · Read with Caution ]
The shelves of things that haven't happened. Even I've never gone down here. They say those are memories no one has lived yet.
The tiger went down, too. There are wet pawprints on the stairs.
Yeoni folded the scrap and tucked it inside their hoof. A faint sound like rain came from below.
Let's go down. My spring is down there.
Let's go. But if there's water this time, I'm rescuing the pig before the cat. Changing the order.
The baby dragon on Yeoni's wrist hugged its swollen belly and gave a little cry. Somewhere below, someone folded an umbrella.
The stairs were longer than expected. With every step down, the rain sounded a little closer. It felt as though rain was falling even underground.
Rain in a basement. Who did this library's drainage? One star.
(Star ratings are my job. Moka's invading my territory.)
The door at the bottom opened by itself. The air inside was cold and clear, as though nobody had ever breathed it before.
Books as transparent as glass bottles hung in midair from red threads. Golden rules appeared on the floor.
[ Basement Level 3 · Things That Have Not Happened · Open a book, and it comes a little closer ]
Things that haven't happened are in books? Then is the whole future here?
Less the future than things that might happen. They might come to be, or never happen at all.
Wait. Hey, look. Moka's Solo Underground Show Sells Out. Can I open this?
It says opening it brings it a little closer. It doesn't say you can skip practice.
Then what's the point?! If a sold-out show gets closer but my skills stay the same, that's just humiliation getting closer.
Moka really doesn't practice his rap, huh.
I do! While you're asleep!
So that was the rhythm coming through the wall every night.
Beatboxing, not mice! Are those cat ears just decorations?
The baby dragon on Yeoni's wrist stretched its neck toward the rain. The water it had drunk earlier still sloshed inside its belly.
Want another drink? No. You'll burst. I'll really give you one star this time.
Smiling, Yundal moved toward the next shelf. His fingertips touched a thin book, then stopped.
[ Yundal Goes Home · 0 pages ]
Mister. Zero pages.
Con artist, did you really plan on never going back? Why isn't there even one line?
It has a cover. That's enough. Having a cover means it isn't over yet.
He withdrew his hand without touching the book again. Inside his glove, the hole made a tiny sound of wind.
Then I'll call your name every day. Yundal, Yundal. That'll make your book upstairs one page thicker every day, too.
A page a day means three thousand pages in ten years. That book will be too heavy to carry.
Don't worry. I'll carry it. Delivery fee charged separately.
Yundal smiled. This time, there wasn't a trace of teasing in it.
Meanwhile, Yeongnyangi walked ahead alone. Even at forks, he never hesitated. Like a route he'd taken many times.
Mr. Cat, do you know the way? Isn't this your first time here?
I'm following the smell. The wet pawprints go this way, too.
(The pawprints ended back on the stairs.)
Following Yeongnyangi, Yeoni noticed a book. Half the title on its pale pink cover was blurred.
[ Flower Pig · By the Cherry-Blossom River with the White □□ · 0 pages ]
White what? With a white what? Why is that the part that's blurred?!
White rice cake. For you, it's a white rice cake. A book about eating rice cakes by a cherry-blossom river.
Don't make me a glutton even in a book with zero pages!
Ahead, Yeongnyangi's tail stopped for the briefest instant, then swayed again. He did not turn.
In the deepest part stood a small pedestal with one book on it. Unlike the others, it was not transparent. Black cloth covered it, and black chains bound it.
White letters marked the cover. Flower Pig · The First Spring.
Found it. It was here.
One moment. Why is a book that's supposedly on loan here? And these are the shelves of things that haven't happened.
What does that mean?
It means a spring that happened somewhere has now become something that never happened. Someone hid this book here.
A padlock hung at the center of the chains. Two characters were engraved on it. 壬午.
Yeoni's heart thudded. The empty Year space on their chart seemed to pull toward those two characters.
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  5/8 — Response: 壬午
My Year Pillar. My characters are inside this book.
Yeoni touched the lock with a hoof. Instantly, the golden writing on the floor turned red.
[ Access denied · Flower Pig has already read one book (1/1) ]
Oh. The lullaby.
Then I'll open it. Move over.
When Moka grabbed the lock, the chains writhed like snakes and flung his paw away.
[ Access denied · Owner only ]
The owner can't open it, nobody else can open it. Then who can open this book?!
It's okay. I don't regret it. That little one will sleep well tonight.
Yeoni smiled. Yet the tips of their hooves trembled a little. Their spring was right before their eyes, beyond their reach.
Yeoni. Don't open that book. Don't look for a way, either.
His voice was strangely low. Yeoni slowly turned to look at Yeongnyangi.
You know this book.
I don't know, either. It's the first time I've seen it.
Liar. Your fur stands up when you lie. It's standing up now.
Yeongnyangi did not answer. Instead, he lifted his left paw a little. As Yeoni's voice sharpened, the scorch marks on it darkened.
When the card smelled of rain, when we saw the empty shelf—you were the only one acting strange. What is it? What are you hiding?
I can't tell you now. I'm sorry.
Now? Then when? With you, it's always later!
Hey, hey. Both of you, calm down. Fight after a meal. An empty stomach makes your words harsher.
Stay out of it, Moka. This is between us.
Yeoni's right. This is my problem.
You're both saying the same thing. That's why you're fighting.
Yeongnyangi's paw twitched again. Yeoni didn't see. They had already turned back toward the book.
You two. Wait a moment. The air has changed.
The shadow beneath the pedestal swelled. Black fingers rose through every gap in the chains and clutched the book.
The vessel's first spring. That was mine from the beginning.
You again? Stop eating other people's books!
Not eating, child. Taking back.
Dozens of black hands lunged at once. Yeongnyangi sprang forward, slashing his claws, and fire sparked from Moka's ladle.
Yundal took off his glove. With a rush of wind, the hole in his palm sucked in handfuls of black hands.
Urgh... Today's menu is rather salty.
The hole spread about a finger joint toward his wrist. Still smiling, Yundal raised the hand again.
Mister, stop! The hole's getting bigger!
It's all right. If it's to protect your book, my lady, I'll put this much on your tab.
Then real rain began falling from the ceiling. Between the black hands, a black shadow slid down the streams of rain.
The tiger. It leaped onto the pedestal and pressed a paw onto the book. The black hands withdrew as though recognizing a master.
Retrieving it. I'll take this.
Retrieving? That's my name on the book. Does your ledger even include other people's springs?
You're late. But very well. Bring it.
No!
Yeoni leaped up and grabbed the other side of the book. Over the chains, the pig's hoof and the tiger's paw touched.
It lasted only an instant. The tiger's paw trembled. A raindrop fell onto the top of Yeoni's head.
Why... are you smiling in the rain?
I don't know. Rain just makes me happy. It always has.
The tiger's red eyes shook. But the next moment, the ring at its neck flashed and tightened.
The tiger jerked the book away. The chains slipped from Yeoni's hooves.
Rain is just rain. There's nothing to be happy about.
Why are you taking that book? Were you in that spring, too? Is that why you erased the borrower's name?
So many questions. Debtors aren't supposed to ask questions.
I don't owe you anything!
Yes. Let it end that way this time. That's better for you.
With the book in its mouth, the tiger bounded up the stairs. Three or four steps at a time, leaving wet tracks, it vanished toward the domed ceiling.
After it! This time, I'm tying a ribbon on that striped tail.
Yundal sank down with his back against the pedestal. He cradled his ungloved hand against his chest.
Go ahead. I'll sit for a moment and follow. It would be nice if Mr. Otter stayed beside me.
Why me, of all people?
Because you're the loudest. Beside a loud person, I don't get forgotten.
That's cheating, con artist. Fine. But you owe me a meal later.
We're going together.
Okay. But when this is over, tell me everything. Promise.
When it's over.
Cat. Don't lose the pig. If you do, I'll shave off all your fur.
Never thought I'd live to be threatened by an otter.
Yeoni never asked whether that answer was a promise. Side by side, the two ran up the wet stairs.
Beyond the top of the stairs, the rain grew louder. Under the domed ceiling, the entire breathing library was slowly getting soaked.
[ The First Spring · On loan · Borrower: ■■■ ]
The three black squares on the borrowing card blurred little by little in the rain, as though a three-syllable name were about to rise from beneath them.

episodes.title: A Name Is a Debt
episodes.tag: Episode 20 · A Name Is a Debt

beats.t: The spiral stairs rising toward the domed ceiling seemed endless. At every level, rainwater poured between the bookshelves like waterfalls.
Up there! The wet pawprints keep going up.
The stairs are slippery. Stay by the railing.
(Yeongnyangi's cradling his left paw again. He keeps doing it.)
Is your paw okay? You've been walking strangely ever since you fell in the water.
Cats always walk like this. With dignity.
Your dignity is limping.
Then a black current rolled down the stairs from above. Drifting books struck their ankles like fallen leaves.
More water? Does that tiger just turn it on like a faucet?!
The current swallowed three steps at once. Just as Yeoni's feet began lifting off the stairs, warmth stirred around their wrist.
The baby dragon poked out its head and opened wide. The pouring water swirled into its tiny mouth.
You drank more? I told you your belly was going to burst!
The baby dragon answered with a burp. It smelled of rain. Yeoni nearly laughed, then held it in.
It's a storehouse for water. It must not be full yet.
Okay. Unlimited refills today, then.
A dull thud sounded several steps above. A whole section of waterlogged staircase was collapsing.
The stairs are gone. At least five paces to the other side.
(Cats can jump, but I'm a pig. Pigs can't fly five paces.)
Yeoni looked beneath the collapsed stairs. Pale green vines still breathed in the gaps between the wet bookshelves.
Yeongnyangi. Go across first. I'll get there my way.
What way?
Pig-style trapeze.
When Yeoni stretched out a hoof, a vine sprang from a shelf and wound around it. Yeoni threw themself into open air.
The vine bent like a bow, then sprang back. A small pink body cut through the rain and tumbled onto the opposite stairs.
Successful landing! OIIINK! Five stars!
That was a tumble, not a landing.
Tumbling counts as landing. Pig rules.
Yeongnyangi bounded lightly across. As he landed, his left paw buckled for an instant. Yeoni saw, but said nothing.
A small door stood at the stairs' end. Strange light leaked through its cracks. Neither day nor night, but the light of a sun consumed by darkness.
Beyond it was the library roof. A sun hung in the middle of the sky, but half of it had been erased in black.
Is that the sun? Why is half of it missing?
It's been eaten. Remember the black hands appearing on each island? Their master is over there.
At the edge of the roof, the black tiger stood on a rain gutter. Chains dangled from the black book in its mouth, swaying in the wind.
Persistent. Weren't you taught to be quiet in libraries?
I'd rather not hear that from someone who ran off with another person's book.
It isn't someone else's book. It was in my ledger from the start.
Then show me. Your ledger. Why my name is in it.
The tiger did not answer. Instead, it raised a paw. The falling rain gathered at its tips.
All the rainwater on the roof rose at once and crashed toward Yeoni. The baby dragon opened its mouth, but this time there was too much.
Yeoni.
Yeongnyangi leaped in front of them. The torrent struck his navy cloak and pushed the small cat back a step.
Yeongnyangi, move! You can't get hit by water!
That's why I'm telling you to move. Because you can't be hit, either.
In the pause between currents, Yeoni lunged. A vine caught the edge of the tiger's cloak.
The cloak flew wide. The tiger twisted, but Yeoni refused to let go.
And Yeoni saw.
The cloak's lining was densely stitched with gold thread. Amid the gold were several characters sewn in black.
The letters wavered like reflections in water, unreadable. Beside them, a tiny drum-shaped knot and a gray feather were sewn together.
That feather. The one I lost on the crow's island.
And that drum knot. Captain Drum, right? That child's name?
Let go.
Answer, and I will. Why are you keeping his name? You said handing it over to the ledger was the end of it.
Because handing it over is the end. Once it's over, the scars on his wrists will never heal.
Then... you were protecting it?
Don't get the wrong idea. I'm only holding it. I can hand it over any time.
But you haven't yet.
The tiger's red eyes wavered. Rain dripped from its whiskers.
One more question. What's your name?
A name is a debt.
What?
When someone calls it, you owe them. I'm not owing anyone anything ever again.
Then I'll lend to you first. No interest.
I've heard that before. This collar is what it cost.
Something flowed from the sun's black half. Black hands reached out, long as cracks drawn across the sky.
What is taking so long? Bring the book. And the rest of that pig's fortune.
The golden ring at the tiger's neck glowed red-hot. It caught its breath and curled inward.
Hey, your neck. Are you okay?
Move, pig. Stay next to me now, and you'll get swept away, too.
Have you forgotten your debt? What you borrowed from me?
The ring tightened again. Staggering, the tiger dropped the book onto the roof.
The instant the book struck the roof, the chain's padlock split with a sharp crack. The two characters engraved on it sprang up as light.
壬午. Im-o. Yeoni, your Year Pillar.
The light of the two characters flew into Yeoni's chest. The familiar chart appeared before their eyes.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  7/8
They're in! Seven. Only one left now!
But Yeoni's smile soon faded. Something was wrong with the first character of the Year Pillar.
[ Year 壬 · Frozen ]
The character 壬 was trapped in black ice. The others glowed warmly, but that one alone did not breathe.
Why is it frozen? I got it, but it feels like I didn't.
Don't try to thaw it.
What?
It will hurt if it melts. You don't need to know what's inside it yet.
The tiger picked up the book in its mouth again. The lock was broken, but black chains still bound the book.
Wait! What's inside? You really were in that spring, weren't you?
The tiger did not look back. Its black body leaped into the rain, becoming rain itself and scattering.
The hands stretching from the sun's black half slowly withdrew, too. As though this was enough for today.
When they returned beneath the domed ceiling, the rain had stopped. Among the soaked books, Moka rolled embers along to dry the shelves.
Back, pig? Judging by your face, it got away again.
It did. But I got something. Halfway.
Halfway? My lady, may I see your chart?
Yeoni held out a hoof. As the chart appeared, Yundal rested his chin on his gloved hand.
壬午. Your Year Pillar. 壬, Im Water, is Direct Resource for you. Water that nurtures and shelters you.
Direct Resource. Like a mother?
Something like that. What Eul Wood born in summer needs most is rain. But that rain is frozen.
What happens when it's frozen?
Still, what has returned has returned. Frozen or not, it's sitting in your place.
So what's the problem with it being frozen? Does it turn into shaved ice?
It doesn't rain. Wood grows thirsty. And when Metal cuts Wood, there's no Water between them to offer support.
Yundal trailed off, glancing at Yeongnyangi. Shaking out and straightening his wet hat, Yeongnyangi looked away as though he hadn't noticed.
Then we just need to melt it.
The one who knows how just turned into rain and disappeared.
Stripes? It froze it and knows how to thaw it? A bigger con artist than you.
I only cheat at compatibility readings. I don't deal in ice.
Admitted to cheating. Everyone heard that, right?
Thank you for remembering me, Mr. Otter. I mean that.
It said it would hurt. If it melted.
Nobody answered. Only Moka's ember gave a little crack.
(The book with my name on it. Captain Drum inside the cloak. A name is a debt. The umbrella someone offered to share.)
(It feels like it all connects, but I can't see the thread yet.)
Yeoni looked up at the chart again. Seven slots were filled. The one remaining blank was the first character of the Hour Pillar.
[ Hour □ · Empty ]
Strange. This slot has been empty since I first met you. There's no trace of theft, unlike the others.
If it wasn't stolen, what is it?
It seems like someone's meant to sit there, but that someone hasn't sat down yet.
Then the empty slot glowed faintly. When Yeoni moved their hoof, the light moved with it. In the direction where it shone brightest stood Yeongnyangi.
Yeongnyangi. It gets brighter toward you.
You're seeing things. Ignore it.
Yeongnyangi stepped back. The glow weakened by that much. Yeoni stepped closer, and it brightened again.
I'm not imagining it.
At that moment, gold flashed deep in Yeongnyangi's eyes. Like sunlight catching a blade.
Yeoni. Let's leave it here for today.
Yeongnyangi turned and walked toward the wet stairs. The sound of his dragging left paw echoed for a long time through the empty library.
By morning, the library had fallen quiet as though it had never been wet. Dried books lay open in rows on every reading desk beneath the domed ceiling.
Book one hundred and twelve. Pig, know what I'm doing with fire right now? Drying books. Me, a chef.
Good work. Five stars. Ironing service added.
Pay me in food, not stars. Can't eat stars.
With each ember Moka rolled, the damp pages unfurled softly. Something like the scent of warm bread rose from them.
Lovely smell. It must be a book about someone's birthday morning.
You can tell that from how a book smells?
No. Just saying things. Sounds convincing, though.
See? A con artist starts scamming first thing in the morning.
And Mr. Otter starts remembering me first thing. Thank you.
Don't put it like that. I can't even get mad.
The baby dragon wriggled off Yeoni's wrist. Its belly was round and swollen, and tiny droplets flew out whenever it yawned.
Look at this one. Still digesting yesterday's flood.
If a dragon gets an upset stomach from drinking water, what kind of weather is that? Monsoon?
A storehouse that isn't full is good news. It means it can drink the next flood, too.
Hear that? You're our team's official water purifier.
Apparently pleased, the baby dragon curled its tail once around Yeoni's hoof and fell asleep again.
At the end of the desk, Yeoni opened their hoof. The eight-slot chart appeared. Seven spaces were filled, one of them frozen black.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  7/8
(Only one left. But where do I find this blank?)
Yundal, this last slot. The first character of the Hour Pillar. What kind of place is it?
Since your Day Master is Eul Wood, the character that can go there is fixed. Gyeong Metal—庚. The place of Influence.
Influence. The one after Expression, Wealth, and Resources?
Yes. The energy that governs and protects you. Rules, responsibility, things like name tags.
But it's strange. We found all the other characters on islands. There wasn't an Island of Influence.
No chart is without Influence. If you can't see it, it's hiding.
Yeoni remembered the first day. Fog over the river, and lights rising beyond it.
(Yeongnyangi said it then. The characters of your Four Pillars are scattered across four islands.)
Blue light, flickering firelight, golden light, and a light like old bookshelves. There had definitely been four.
There were four islands. Companions, Expression, Wealth, Resources. But there are five groups among the Ten Stars.
You've been studying, my lady. Care for a part-time job at my compatibility booth?
