That's not what we're talking about.
Where'd the fifth light go, then? Someone pocket it?
Gyeong Metal is a blade, iron. Hard, cold, straight. The most difficult counterpart for Eul Wood.
A difficult counterpart has to sit in my slot?
When a difficult counterpart becomes your partner, the bond is the strongest. Eul and Gyeong are drawn to each other.
(Cold, straight iron. Why does someone keep coming to mind?)
Then the reading room door opened. Yeongnyangi came in. His fur was half dry, and he hesitated very slightly with each step on his left paw.
Yeongnyangi, perfect timing. At the start, you said there were four islands. Where's the fifth?
It isn't here now.
Isn't here? But there are five groups?
Customer Support is closed.
Every time you say that, I'm deducting a star.
Yeongnyangi sat at the far end of the desk. Normally, he would have sat beside Yeoni. Yeoni glanced at that empty place.
(He's been like this since yesterday. Every time I move closer, he steps back.)
Mr. Cat, may I ask when your birthday is?
Why?
Habit. I ask everyone I meet. Especially those who stay beside our lady.
I don't know.
You don't know. Interesting in itself.
Con artist, you're testing the cat, aren't you? Even I can see that.
Yeoni rose and slowly walked between the desks, the chart floating over their hoof.
One experiment. Everyone stay still.
What now? Pig experiments usually end with me getting hurt.
Yeoni went to Moka. The blank stayed quiet. Then to Yundal. It trembled ever so slightly, then stilled again.
My hour is empty, too. Just two empty spaces saying hello.
Finally, Yeoni walked toward Yeongnyangi. One step, two. The blank grew brighter.
Directly before Yeongnyangi, it blazed white. Like sunlight striking cold iron.
It did this yesterday. It's doing it today. Still my imagination?
Light naturally goes toward brightness. It's because my fur is white.
I've never heard such a ridiculous excuse.
Yeoni. Step back.
Why? What's wrong with me getting close?
Instead of answering, Yeongnyangi pushed back his chair and stood. The blank's glow sharply dimmed, matching the distance he had put between them.
It's nothing. Just tired today.
Yeongnyangi left the reading room. The closing door sounded unusually loud.
Hey, what's with that cat lately? He was always obnoxious, but now his obnoxiousness looks sad.
I don't know. Whenever I ask, he says later.
Yundal watched the door for a long time. His gloved fingers tapped the desk twice.
My lady. In a woman's chart, Influence has another meaning.
What is it?
Ah, I'll tell you next time. If I say it now, I think you might bang your head on the desk.
Now I'm even more curious!
Me too. Tell us. Or I'll burn your glove.
Then it's even more of a secret.
All afternoon, Yeoni wandered the library searching for the fifth light. Moka grumbled along behind.
It's a library. If you don't know something, look it up. Let's try the catalog desk.
That chatty card cabinet from the first day? It's the one that told me to be quiet.
The catalog desk's drawers rattled open as soon as they saw the pair. One card flew out and stopped before Yeoni's nose.
[ Please state your search terms · Borrowing allowance: 0/1 ]
Flower Pig. Influence. Fifth light.
The writing on the card spread like ink, then gathered again. This time, the result was a single line.
[ No results · Location: Outside the library · Contact: Customer Support ]
Customer Support?
What's Customer Support? They have that here?
They do. From the very first day. Customer Support that accepts neither complaints nor worries.
Yeoni turned the card over. Its back was blank. No—one very faint pawprint marked it.
That's a cat paw. Look at the size. I know because he puts that paw on my skewers all the time.
(Four islands. The fifth light isn't an island. It's outside the library. Contact: Customer Support.)
Moka. Is there anything about Yeongnyangi you haven't told me?
Huh? No. Why ask me? I'm an otter. Otters don't know about secrets.
Your tail is wagging incredibly fast.
I'm drying my fur! It got wet drying the books!
Moka hurried off toward another shelf. Yeoni watched him go for a long time.
(Moka knows, too. Yundal looked like he knew. I'm the only one who doesn't.)
That night, everyone slept in a small room deep inside the library. Moka snored with his head on a book pillow.
(Can't sleep. I keep thinking about that blank.)
Tossing and turning, Yeoni looked toward the corner. The spot where Yeongnyangi always curled up to sleep was empty.
Yeongnyangi?
No answer. Yeoni pushed back the blanket and sat up. Between Moka's snores, they could hear their own heartbeat.
A few strands of white fur and a note lay in the empty spot. A pawprint served as a signature.
[ Back soon. Worries not accepted. · Customer Support ]
What kind of note is this? Why won't you accept worries?!
(Since when does our Customer Support close without a word like this?)
Yeoni stood, holding the note. The baby dragon on their wrist opened sleepy eyes, then turned toward the window.
Rain sounded outside. The sky was clear, but the smell of rain was there.
I know that smell.
(The smell from the drowned shelves, from above the chains. A wet cloak.)
Yeoni folded the note and clutched it tightly. Then they opened the window without a sound.
Hanging from the frame, Yeoni looked up. Two shadows stood at the top of the rounded roof.
One was a white cat in a hat. Even beneath the half-eaten sun, the hat's crescent shone gold.
The other was a black tiger. Rainwater dripped without cease from the hem of its soaked cloak.
Why are they together? Are they fighting?
The baby dragon bit down hard on Yeoni's hoof. Whether it meant don't go or hurry, Yeoni couldn't tell.
Okay. I'll be quiet. Hold your breath, too.
They were not fighting. They stood a little apart, facing the same direction. Like two who had known each other a long time.
The wind blew. Yeongnyangi's eyes flashed gold. A blade-like gleam cut across the roof and vanished.
(Yeongnyangi. Whose side are you on right now?)
Just as Yeoni was about to climb over the window frame, both shadows on the roof turned toward them at once.
Yeongnyangi slipped silently out of the sleeping room. Before closing the door, he looked back once. Yeoni slept with their mouth open, having kicked away the blanket.
Keep your blanket on. Catch a cold, and you'll blame Customer Support again.
He caught the blanket's edge with his paw and pulled it up to Yeoni's shoulders. Turning in their sleep, Yeoni hugged that paw like a pillow.
Let go. I'm not a pillow.
Yeoni did not let go. Yeongnyangi lay there for a long time, then very slowly freed his paw. He slid a book into its place.
Sorry. That book is Customer Support for today.
There was no answer. Instead, Yeoni mumbled one star in their sleep. Yeongnyangi smiled very faintly.
Climbing the stairs, he leaned a shoulder against the wall. His left paw refused to obey again.
He lifted it to look. Red rust spread over the scorch marks. Since his plunge into the water, it had grown one finger joint a day.
Scorched by fire, rusted by water. Iron needs quite a lot of care, too.
He covered the rust with his cloak. So Yeoni wouldn't see it tomorrow morning, either. Moka and Yundal had already noticed, but both could keep a secret.
No, the otter couldn't. That tail had probably told everything this afternoon.
The smell of rain drifted through the stairwell window. Whenever he caught it, something in Yeongnyangi's mind rattled open, then shut.
A bus stop in the rain. Water falling in strings from an old roof.
Someone's hand held an umbrella. A small hand. The umbrella tilted halfway toward the person beside it.
Beneath it, someone laughed. In the rain, like a fool, utterly happy.
Let's share. Someone said it in his memory. Yeongnyangi tried to catch the voice, but only rainwater filled his grasp.
He pressed his forehead to the cold wall. The memory always ended there. The hand holding the umbrella. Whose hand it was, who stood beside it.
If only I knew the name.
[ Contract, Article 1 · The guardian may not speak his own name · The moment the name is called, the contract ends ]
Golden letters appeared before his eyes, then vanished. Customer Support's rules. The rules he had personally signed when he first took the job.
I know. I've never forgotten.
He had forgotten what his name was. But he had not forgotten what he had agreed to gain by giving it up.
Just once more. This time, by your side until the end.
He looked at his reflection in the stairwell window. Navy hat, violet eyes spreading into gold, rusted paw. The face of a cat in a hat.
When I first opened my eyes with this face, you looked at me and asked if I was just a cat.
And gave him a star rating. One. Yeongnyangi still remembered that one star exactly, though he could not remember his own name.
The wind was strong on the roof. A half-eaten sun hung in the night sky. A sky that was neither day nor night.
The black tiger sat at the roof's edge, as though it had been waiting for him all along.
You're late, cat.
I smelled rain and came to look. Whose book are you here to steal this time?
I'm not here to work today. I have something to tell you.
No politeness for the pig, none for me. Who do you speak politely to?
Don't ask pointless questions.
The ledger's owner? That voice?
Shut up. That voice is listening even now.
The tiger glanced at the sky. The black half of the eaten sun writhed very slowly.
Its red eyes lowered to Yeongnyangi's left paw, finding the rust hidden beneath his cloak precisely.
That paw. Spreading a joint a day, isn't it?
How do you know?
It's all in the ledger. Every time you're hurt beside that child, the child's column grows heavier by a line.
Keep your paws off that column.
I'm not the one touching it. You are. The stronger that child's fire grows, the more you melt. And the longer you hold on, the smaller that child becomes.
Yeongnyangi said nothing. They both knew he had no answer.
Leave. Leave now, and that child can live with seven slots.
Seven slots make a vessel. You know that, too.
How do you know about that?
I can't read the ledger, but I can read the sky. Enough to know what that eaten sun wants.
Raindrops began falling between them. The sky was clear, but rain fell only where they stood.
And your rain. I think I've smelled it before.
You're imagining it.
An umbrella. A bus stop. An offer to share.
The tiger's tail struck the roof hard. Rainwater splashed upward.
Don't talk about that. You have no right to speak of that spring.
Then I was right.
We came from the same spring.
The tiger did not answer. Instead, it raised a paw and gripped the ring at its neck. Though the ring had done nothing.
Don't pretend to know when you can't remember. That's the cruelest thing of all.
I can't remember. That's why I'm asking.
I remember everything. Every last thing. That's why I live like this.
What happened that spring?
The person you said you'd protect disappeared. That's all.
Yeongnyangi's paw twitched. The rusted area suddenly burned. He had no memory, yet his body hurt before his mind could.
I see. That must be why I took this job this time.
It'll end the same way again. You'll be late again, and I'll be left alone again.
Don't ask. Why should I answer a cat who doesn't even know his name?
We're even, then. I don't know yours, either.
The wind blew. Deep in Yeongnyangi's eyes, gold flashed and vanished. A light that came without his knowing.
Those eyes just now.
Ignore it.
They were like that before the empty slot, too. Do you not know yourself, or are you pretending not to?
Customer Support does not answer personal questions.
Then a window opened below. Very carefully, but a little noisily, as a pig would.
The white cat and the black tiger turned at the same moment. A pink hoof hooked over the window frame.
Yeoni climbed over the window frame and onto the roof. The tiles were slippery. The roof was far too round for a pig's hooves to grip.
What are you two doing here? At night. In secret. In the rain.
Yeoni. Go inside. It's dangerous here.
You coming to a dangerous place alone is even more dangerous!
The tiger looked from one to the other. Then it let out a tiny breath, somewhere between a sneer and a sigh.
That's enough for today. Nothing to put in the ledger.
Wait. What did you just say to Yeongnyangi?
If you're curious, ask the cat. Why his eyes sometimes turn gold.
The tiger jumped from the roof's edge. There was no sound of falling. Only the rain grew louder once, then faded.
Then I'll ask. Why do your eyes turn gold?
Reflected moonlight.
That's half a sun, and there's no moon. Nothing to reflect.
Yeoni. Let's just go inside tonight. I'll tell you tomorrow.
With you, it's always tomorrow. Always later, always when it's over.
Yeoni opened a hoof. The chart appeared. Its last blank was already glowing faintly.
Then I'll check for myself.
Yeoni stepped closer. The blank brightened. Yeongnyangi stepped back.
Another step. And another. Yeongnyangi's hind paws reached the roof's edge. There was nowhere left to retreat.
Yeoni, stop.
No.
The instant Yeoni's hoof touched the fluffy fur on Yeongnyangi's chest, white light burst from the blank. A clear ringing, like metal being struck, echoed through the sky.
The light stood straight as a blade, then gathered into one character. Cold, hard, and straight.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour 庚辰 ]  8/8
It's full! All eight slots! Yeongnyangi, look!
[ Hour Stem 庚 · Borrowed slot · Owner unverified ]
Borrowed slot? Owner unverified? What does that mean?
The character 庚 shone, then flickered. It brightened when Yeongnyangi breathed in and dimmed when he breathed out. As though breathing with him.
Yeongnyangi. Is this you?
No.
It's breathing with you!
Coincidence.
As he said it, Yeongnyangi's fur briefly lost its luster. Its white tips faded to ash, then returned.
Your fur just now. The color drained out.
It's nighttime.
Do you know how many excuses you've made today? Moonlight, fur, night. What's next?
Weather.
Then the roof's small window burst open. Moka popped out holding an ember. Yundal climbed up behind him, yawning.
What?! Why's a bell ringing on the roof?! I thought there was a fire!
Ah, my lady. That slot. Finally filled, I see.
Yundal. This slot is breathing with Yeongnyangi.
Yundal looked between the chart and Yeongnyangi. Then he covered his mouth with his gloved hand, holding back a smile.
I see. So that's why you didn't know your birthday.
What does that mean? What does a birthday have to do with this slot?
I'll tell you tomorrow. If I tell you now, you might roll off the roof.
Con artist, you said that yesterday, too. Keep saying tomorrow, tomorrow, and you'll turn into a cat.
Yundal. Don't say anything this time.
The next morning, the four sat around a reading-room desk. It felt like a courtroom.
To be precise, three people and one animal. The baby dragon left Yeoni's wrist and coiled at the center of the desk like a judge.
Let's do this over breakfast. I grilled skewers. Trials need snacks.
Moka set down the plate. Yeoni and Yeongnyangi reached for the same skewer at the same time. Hoof and paw froze above it.
You have it.
No. You eat it.
No, I said you have it.
Why all the generosity over one skewer?! There are twelve! Twelve!
That skewer tells us everything about what happened on the roof last night.
Nothing happened! One slot lit up, that's all!
As Yeoni said it, their nose grew a shade deeper than pink. Yeongnyangi turned toward the window without even taking a skewer.
All right, Yundal. Finish what you were saying yesterday. You said Influence has another meaning in a woman's chart.
You really want to hear it now? Have you checked how hard the desk is?
Hurry up.
For an Eul Wood Day Master, Gyeong Metal is Direct Officer. The energy that helps you stand upright. And in a woman's chart, Direct Officer is...
Direct Officer is. Stop dragging it out. The meat's burning.
The husband star.
Yeoni's forehead hit the desk with a thud. A book Yundal had placed there in advance caught it.
That's why I told you to check how hard it was.
H-h-husband?
Ack. Cough. Wait. A skewer went down the wrong way.
A misunderstanding.
What else could it be?! Your breath is attached to the slot!
I'm Customer Support. Not a husband.
Who said I'd marry you?! I don't want to, either!
Neither do I.
Why don't you want to?!
Wow. Both saying they don't want to at once. Aren't they basically married already?
Mr. Otter's more accurate than I am, and I read compatibility for a living.
Yundal. Husband star doesn't mean an actual husband, right? Just the name of a star?
It's a star's name. A place in your chart that protects you, guides you, and makes you want to take responsibility.
It doesn't necessarily mean someone you'll marry. Just that there's someone who sits in that place.
(Someone who sits in that place. The cat who's stayed beside me since I first opened my eyes.)
Yeoni raised their head to look at Yeongnyangi. He stared only out the window. The tips of his ears were a little red.
(So cats' ears turn red, too.)
But enough joking. My lady, could you bring up that slot again?
Yeoni opened their hoof. 庚 still flickered. The farther Yeongnyangi moved toward the window, the fainter it grew.
A borrowed slot means this character wasn't originally yours. Mr. Cat is lending you his own.
Lending it? Then what happens to Yeongnyangi?
He becomes that much emptier. By the amount he lends.
So when the cat goes away, the slot goes dark. When he gets close, the cat empties out. What kind of messed-up contract is this?
The contract is a bit of a mess. None of your concern.
How could I not be concerned?! You're saying you're lending yourself to me.
I didn't lend it. You came closer, and it lit up.
Then let's check. My lady, could you bring out one vine?
Not understanding, Yeoni held out a hoof. A slender vine grew onto the desk, bending limply over its edge.
Now, Mr. Cat, please stand beside our lady.
No.
Say no, and I'll push you. With my tail.
With Moka shoving his back, Yeongnyangi reluctantly stood beside Yeoni. 庚 on the chart shone brightly.
At once, the drooping vine stood upright. Straight as a pillar, it stretched toward the ceiling. Its leaves were firm and gleaming.
What? I've never seen my vine this straight.
Eul Wood bends alone. With Gyeong Metal beside it, it stands straight. That's Direct Officer. The energy that helps you stand.
Yeoni looked from the vine to their side. Yeongnyangi was clenching his teeth. His left paw hovered just above the floor.
Yeongnyangi. Does it hurt?
No.
When Yeoni stepped away, the vine sagged again. Tension left Yeongnyangi's shoulders. He had been holding his breath.
Then I just need to stay away?
Yeongnyangi did not answer. His silence was the answer.
Then the circular skylight darkened. Though it was morning, the entire reading room rapidly sank into shadow as if the sun were setting.
What now? More rain?
No. Worse than rain.
Yundal clutched his gloved right hand to his chest. Inside the glove, something sounded like escaping air. The Void was inhaling on its own.
This hand has never been so hungry. I think I know what that thing up there wants to eat.
What does it want? Don't talk around it. My tail's standing on end because I'm scared.
The sky cracked beyond the glass. Starting at the half-eaten sun, a black fissure stretched across it.
Crack. The sound came not from the sky but from Yeoni's chart. A fine fracture marked a corner of 庚.
My slot cracked. Yeongnyangi, are you okay?
I'm fine.
Liar. Cat, your teeth are chattering. I can hear them from here.
Mr. Cat. Hiding it is hurting our lady more now.
As those words were spoken, Yeongnyangi hid his left paw behind his back. Yeoni saw the movement. This time, they did not pretend otherwise.
That paw. Show me.
Yeoni.
I said show me.
Yeongnyangi looked at Yeoni for a long time, then slowly started to hold out his paw. But before it fully emerged, the glass shook violently.
Found you.
The voice sounded from everywhere at once. Between the shelves, beyond the glass, inside the crack in Yeoni's chart.
The hidden fifth light. There you were, beside that child.
The fissure in the sky widened another handspan. Beyond it, something slowly opened its eyes.
Black hands poured from the fissure in the sky. The round skylight shattered, and hands fell into the reading room like rain.
Definitely worse than rain! Con artist, now would be a great time for a con!
Mr. Otter, take our lady's left. I'll eat the right.
Yundal removed his glove. The hole in his palm swirled and sucked in the three nearest black hands. Its rim widened by a fingernail's width.
Yundal, your hand! The hole's growing!
Right now, I'm more afraid of you getting smaller than it getting bigger.
Moka hurled an ember like a ball. One black hand recoiled from the burn. But the hands passed Yeoni by.
Huh? They're not coming for the pig.
Then who?
Yeoni stretched out a vine and caught the nearest hand. The instant it touched, the vine withered black. It wasn't holding the hand. It was being eaten.
They're eating my vine. Why are they so hungry?
They've been starving a long time. And today, they seem to have found something tastier than you, my lady.
The hands swarmed in only one direction. Toward the white cat by the window.
Yeoni, get down!
Yeongnyangi bristled all over. Golden blades rose from his paws and severed several black hands at once. But each cut hand split into two and lunged again.
Cat. You are a blade. A blade belongs in its sheath.
A black hand seized Yeongnyangi's rusted left paw. His knee buckled.
Let go. This isn't yours.
The hand did not release him. Black threads spread between its fingers and began winding tightly around his leg. The tips of his white fur turned gray.
Let go of his paw!
Something burst deep in Yeoni's chest. Fire like the noonday sun poured from their hoof. 丙 blazed red on the chart.
The flames burned the black hand. And did not stop. The fire that consumed the hand swept straight over the white paw in its grip.
Ghh.
The black hands scattered like screams. The sky's fissure slowly closed. Only the smells of burning and melting metal remained in the reading room.
Is it over? It's over, right? Pig, was that you? Hotter than the festival island's sun.
My lady, please turn down the fire. The books are sweating.
Yeoni looked at their own hooves. Embers still crackled at the tips. They hastily shook them out.
I've never done that much before. It was just... they grabbed Yeongnyangi's paw.
Then a low groan came from the window.
Yeongnyangi lay collapsed on the floor. The cloak covering his left paw had burned away, exposing everything he had hidden beneath.
Yeongnyangi.
Scorch marks spread from paw to shoulder. Red rust covered them. This was no wound from the last day or two.
How long has it been like this? This didn't happen today.
It's nothing.
Nothing spreads all the way to your shoulder?
Yeoni's hoof moved before an answer came. They drew out a thin vine and began wrapping his paw. As they wound it, the vine's tip touched the scorch marks and crumbled.
Stop. It won't help right now.
Stay still. I'll decide whether it helps.
My lady. Sit down. I'll explain.
You knew, too, Yundal?
Yes. Since the day Mr. Cat taught you the breathing exercise.
Moka, you too?
Since the festival island. The day you first shouted in the courtroom. Smoke came from the cat's paw.
When I asked him, he said he'd poison my skewers if I told the pig.
I never said that. I said I'd eat them all.
That's even crueler!
Since then? All those days, everyone but me?
Nobody answered. Moka lowered his tail, and Yundal put his gloved hand in his pocket. Their silence was the answer.
So I was the only one who didn't know. I was the only one happily going around making fire.
Your Month Stem is Byeong Fire. Hurting Officer. Fire that lets you say what you want and break free of constraints.
And Mr. Cat is Gyeong Metal, Direct Officer. The structure, the rules, the name tag.
When Hurting Officer meets Direct Officer, Direct Officer gets hurt. It's called Hurting Officer Meets Officer. The stronger your fire, the more Mr. Cat melts.
[ 丙 Hurting Officer → 庚 Direct Officer · Hurting Officer Meets Officer ]
丙 on the chart was still red-hot. Wherever its heat touched the corners of 庚, black scorch marks spread.
So. I did this? In the courtroom, at the noon concert, and now?
It isn't your fault. That's how the energies clash in this chart.
Then you should have told me that's how the chart works!
Why didn't you tell me?
Because you would put out your fire.
Of course I would! If my fire does this to you!
That's why I didn't say it. Without your fire, you aren't you. A festival that can't sing. Skewers with no taste. You saw them, too.
Then what about you? It's okay for you to melt?
That's why I'm by your side.
Don't say that. Saying things like that isn't cool at all.
Yeongnyangi fell silent. Yeoni rubbed their eyes with a hoof. Tears mixed with soot and smeared black.
With you, it's always later. You said you'd tell me when it was over. Is this when it's over? When the rust reaches your shoulder?
I'm sorry.
I'm not asking for an apology!
Then what do you want me to say?
I don't know! Just... just say it hurts when it hurts. Is that so hard?
The reading room went quiet. Moka stood frozen with the skewer plate, and Yundal's hand had stopped halfway through putting on his glove.
It hurts.
Huh?
It hurts. Every time you make fire. But if you can't make fire, that hurts more.
Yeoni could say nothing. Yeongnyangi slowly pushed himself up. His rusted paw dragged on the floor.
When I stay beside you, you become smaller. When you grow, I melt. That's our chart.
Then what are we supposed to do? One of us has to keep hurting?
No. One of us can step aside.
Yeongnyangi.
In that instant, words escaped Yeoni's mouth before thought could catch them. Like fire, with no time to stop them.
Then step aside! Don't stay next to me getting hurt! I'm not grateful for that at all!
Yeoni regretted it as soon as the words were out. But they had already fallen to the reading-room floor and rolled away.
Yes. That's right.
No, that's not...
Yeongnyangi turned away. His white tail vanished through the doorway. The door closed quietly. This time, there wasn't even a loud sound.
[ Year 壬午 · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  7/8
庚 went dark on the chart. The blank was empty again. The vine around Yeoni's hoof drooped limply to the floor.
I told him to move aside. He really left.
Hey. Pig.
What?
Stop crying and go catch him. That's who you are. Talk first, run after.
At Mr. Cat's pace, he'll be at the bottom of the stairs about now. He can't go fast on that rusted paw.
What do I say when I catch him? Stay beside me, and he'll melt again.
We'll solve that together later. A chart is a problem, not a verdict. I've yet to see a problem without a way to solve it.
First time I'm trusting the con artist. Hurry!
Yeoni wiped their tears with a sleeve. Then they kicked open the door and ran.
As they raced downstairs, scenes flashed through Yeoni's mind. The cat who only nodded even after receiving one star. The back that stood before them in the courtroom.
His figure going alone to the river after the noon concert. His left paw walking strangely after the water. Yeoni had seen it all, and pretended not to see any of it.
(I knew, too. It wasn't just that nobody told me. I didn't ask.)
Outside the library lay a river. An empty ferryboat rocked on the current of starlight.
Yeongnyangi! Yeongnyangi, I said it wrong! Come back!
The call fell into the river and drifted away. The boat rocked once. Yeoni rushed over and looked inside. Empty.
What cat actually moves aside because you tell him to? Usually, you don't listen to a thing I say.
A single white hair lay on the boat's floor. Yeoni wound it around a hoof. Still warm.
There was no reply. Dots of red rust marked the river stones. The pawprints led downstream, then ended in the fog.
The mist was thick. Yeoni raised a hoof. Just a little fire would show the way.
An ember formed at the tip. Yeoni stared at it for a long time, then clenched their hoof and put it out.
If I light this fire, you'll hurt again somewhere.
Without fire, Yeoni walked into the mist. Feeling out each rust mark, they followed. Their hooves kept slipping on the cold stones.
Each time they fell, they checked the white hair first. Each time, it had grown a little colder.
I'll take back that one star. Give you five. So please answer me.
Only the water answered beyond the mist. The pawprints ended there.
Over the broken trail, a black shadow slowly crawled. A shadow shaped like a human hand.
No.
The shadow slipped into the fog and vanished. Along with the smell of rust.

episodes.title: Because There Is No Water
episodes.tag: Episode 24 · Because There Is No Water

beats.t: At dawn, mist lay low along the river. A pink pig slept curled on a wet stone.
A white hair was wound around one hoof. Refastened who knew how many times through the night, the knot had three layers.
Found you. You really slept here?
Moka. Where's Yeongnyangi?
Not yet.
Yeoni nodded. They did not cry. Their face had cried all it could through the night, with nothing left to give.
My lady, let's go inside first. Sleep on cold stones, and Eul Wood takes damage from the roots up.
What would I do inside? If I stay here, I'll see him as soon as he comes back.
Go inside and eat. If the cat comes back and sees you like this, he'll get mad at me. I don't want that.
Moka took Yeoni's scruff in his teeth and dragged them. Even as they were pulled away, Yeoni kept looking back at the river.
Mist over the water scattered and gathered again. Between it, one black ripple passed silently. Nobody saw.
Unfamiliar objects stood on the long reading-room table. A kettle, a metal spoon, a plant pot, and a candle.
All right, class begins. Today's tuition is your birth date and time, my lady.
You already know it.
Some things you want to hear again even when you know them.
Con artist, is this really the time?
It is. There's no cheaper way to put a smile on our lady's face.
Yeoni did not smile. But they raised their head a little. As though that were enough, Yundal picked up the metal spoon.
This is Mr. Cat. Gyeong Metal. Hard, sharp, able to cut Wood.
Yundal tapped the small tree in the pot with the spoon's tip. One leaf fell.
Don't.
Yes. That's why Mr. Cat was always careful beside you. Metal controls Wood—金克木. Metal overcomes Wood.
Then we were wrong for each other from the start. Yeongnyangi and me.
No. This is where the real lesson begins.
Yundal lifted the kettle and poured water over the spoon. The water ran along it and soaked into the pot's soil.
Metal generates Water. Water nourishes Wood. With Water between them, Metal feeds Wood instead of cutting it.
[ 庚 Influence → 壬 Resource → 乙 Day Master · Officer and Resource in Mutual Generation ]
It's called Officer and Resource in Mutual Generation. Officer generates Resource, and Resource generates me. A way for Mr. Cat to become a well instead of a blade.
The little tree drank and spread its leaves slightly. Yeoni stared at those leaves for a long time.
Then... Yeongnyangi doesn't have to hurt?
As long as there's Water.
And the fire? You said the pig's fire melts the cat.
Water for that, too.
Yundal lightly cupped his palm above the candle. Its flame did not go out. It merely stopped wavering and shrank to a suitable size.
Resource guides Hurting Officer. Hurting Officer Balanced by Resource. Not putting out the fire, but giving it a path.
(I don't have to put it out. Even if I don't, Yeongnyangi won't get hurt.)
For the first time, light returned to Yeoni's eyes. Bracing against the table, they sprang up.
Water. All we need is water. Where is it? There's a whole river full!
Probably not that water.
Why?!
If it were that water, I'd have dunked the cat in the river already.
Mr. Otter is right. River water is just water. We need the Water in your chart.
Your Year Stem. Im Water, 壬. That's your Resource.
The three went down to the memory vault. Yeoni's chart floated at its center. Seven of its eight slots were lit.

The old door's grain changed into an image on a card. Stars engraved its border, and an open doorway appeared at its center. Below it, words rose instead of a number.
[ THE DOOR · Destiny code 8/8 confirmed · Return available ]
This. I know this. The card from the app at the beginning. I tapped it and came here.
The door home. Only someone with all eight characters can pass.
Then I can go? Home? To my room?
Yes. Your room. The one with the upturned umbrella.
Yeoni took a step toward the door, then stopped and looked back. Moka, Yundal, Luna, Luna's sister. And Neo.
We're all going together, right?
No one answered immediately. Yundal gently held his gloved hand before the door. The golden threads broke off in front of it.
[ Year □□ · Month □□ · Day □□ · Hour ■■ · 7/8 · Entry denied ]
As expected. Not me. I have no birth hour.
Your hour? The one Blue Rabbit ate?
Yes. According to this door, someone missing one of the eight characters isn't quite a complete person yet. A little hurtful.
Then we find it. Together. And afterward, we leave together.
You're willing to wait for me, my lady. Proof we're compatible.
No.
Yundal smiled. But the smile took a little longer to end.
I'm not going, either.
Moka?
I'm an otter from here. Someone has to guard the fire on the festival island. Bring a skewer-grilling otter to the human world, and you'll make the news.
But still.
Still what? One fewer person to hear my rap. That's the only thing I'll miss.
Don't cry, human. You're uglier than you were as a pig.
As he said it, Moka pressed his forehead once against the back of Yeoni's hand. Just as on the day he shared his breath.
Then Neo...
I'm going.
You are?
I'm a borrowed slot. If the slot goes, I follow. And Customer Support makes house calls.
How many stars for the house-call service?
Five. Didn't you say so at the river earlier?
You heard that?
Yeoni and Neo stood before the door. Luna pressed a bag of bread into Yeoni's arms. Her sister merely waved from the oven.
Come back, Sis. Human Sis or Pig Sis, I like both. Come back for sure.
I will. Next time, I'll bring bread. Paid for with money.
If it's not as good as ours, we won't accept it.
My lady. Once you're over there, things here may blur like a dream. But don't worry too much.
They won't blur. How could I forget bread this good?
Of course. You can't forget bread.
Yundal slipped his gloved hand into his pocket. He knew better than anyone what it felt like to be the one forgotten.
Yeoni grasped the handle. Not cold. Warm as fresh bread. The door opened, and a golden wind poured in.
Crossing the threshold, Yeoni thought they heard something behind them. Yundal murmuring very softly, a name other than his own. But the wind covered it.
The door closed. Those left in the bakery watched it for a while. It was an old storage door again.
And where nobody saw, a few raindrops seeped through its closed cracks. To the other side. As though following someone.
Far upstream from the bakery, where the current broke white against rocks, the black tiger crouched alone.
Twelve marks from black hands scarred its back. Wounds throbbed beneath the torn cloak. The tiger did not lick them. Licking them felt like admitting they hurt.
Instead, it felt inside its cloak. The paper-wrapped bread was still there. All the warmth had gone, leaving only its shape.
She said once it cooled, it was just bread.
It unfolded the note. Three crooked syllables spelled a name. The drumming child from the festival island. The child whose applause it had collected.
Are you still drumming? Even without applause?
The note did not answer. The tiger folded it again. Its fingertips were careful, different from the paw that closed the ledger.
It did not take out the bread. It checked another part of the cloak. The note with the drum boy's name. Bread beside it. Two things absent from the ledger now.
It opened the ledger. Yeoni's entry read No balance remaining. Yet beneath it, a faint line nobody had written was spreading.
[ Ledger · Eulhae Yeoni · Uncollected: 1 ]
Uncollected.
Money not received. Something still owed. The tiger scratched the line with a claw. It would not erase. It grew clearer instead.
What haven't I collected? I took everything. Even that child's tomorrows.
As it spoke, a touch returned. The child with nothing, pushing the ring with their forehead. The voice saying to say it hurt when it hurt.
What it had collected was fortune. Yet the ledger was recording that it had received something. Something it could not repay.
The ring on its right forepaw suddenly heated. Glowing red, the golden band tightened one notch, then another. Bone sounded under pressure.
Ghh.
A black fissure opened over the river. The gap into the other sky where it had been driven. From beyond, a voice flowed through the ring.
Tiger. That paw you wrapped around my vessel. Still attached, I see.
It is.
A pity. I should have taken it off.
The ring tightened again. The tiger did not scream. It drove its claws into the rock and held on. The rock cracked.
Why did you come to me? Do you remember?
To stop that child before they became a monster.
Yes. One day, that child will betray everyone. As they betrayed you. Who gave you the chance to prevent it?
You did.
Have you forgotten that kindness?
I haven't. Not for a day.
Yet today, you saved that child.
The tiger could not answer. Only the river sounded. It truly had no words. It did not know why it had done it.
Instead of an answer, a scene rose. Not one it had chosen. Whenever the ring tightened, this scene always spilled out.
A rainy bus stop. A wet bench. A hand tilting an umbrella halfway toward it. Rain always hid the face.
And then the next scene. That same hand pushing it away. A sense that something black and round had glimmered behind the hand's owner's eyes.
That feeling always broke off there. Black Moon's voice filled the gap. That child betrays. That child betrays.
One question. How much was that bread?
What?
I smell something inside your cloak. A smell absent from the ledger.
Without realizing, the tiger wrapped a paw around the cloak. That movement answered. Laughter came from beyond the fissure.
They called it free? Nothing is free. You know that best. That bread's price will be charged one day. In your blood.
I'll pay for the bread. Leave that bakery alone.
Oh? An order?
A request.
The ring tightened fiercely one last time. The tiger pitched forward, face plunging into the river. Cold water entered its nose.
I'll grant your request. In return, do your job.
The child has gone to the human world. That cat regained his human shell, too. Though not his name.
Go as well. With a human face. This time, finish it there.
My human face was lost long ago...
I'll return it. A loan. You know the interest.
Black fur streamed away like rain. Paws became hands, claws became nails. The ring did not vanish. It became a fine gold cord wound into the flesh of her right wrist.
The fissure closed. A woman with wet hair knelt on the riverbank. She still held the ledger.
She remained there a long time. Then searched her cloak, now a black coat. Inside its pocket, a note and a roll.
She took out the bread, removed the paper. Cold. She bit into it.
Cold bread. Yet it was sweet. It smelled of butter. A flavor no ledger could record spread slowly across her tongue.
Her shoulders trembled once. She did not cry. Only rainwater ran down her face.
She ate half, wrapped the other half again, and put it away. No one asked why. Even if someone had, she could not have answered.
A rainy night. A fluorescent light flickered in an old apartment corridor. Two homes at its end. Before one stood an umbrella holder with a torn corner.
A black umbrella was propped before the vacant home next door. Water dripped from its tip onto the floor.
The door opened, then closed. Only the smell of rain remained in the corridor.
The vacant apartment was empty. Dust covered the floor. Without turning on the light, the woman stood by the window. Water fell from her wet coat.
Sounds came through the thin wall. Something dropping onto the floor. Then a sleepy voice.
Neo, that's my sock. Don't throw it out. It's only a little hole.
The woman pressed a palm to the wall. The golden cord at her right wrist shone coldly. A low voice on the other side stopped short. As though someone had sensed her.
You two are noisy even here.
She withdrew her hand. Without removing her wet coat, she sat on the floor and leaned against the wall. Until the sounds beyond it faded.
The ledger lay open on her knees. One uncollected line glowed faintly in the dark. She looked at it for a long time, then shut the book.

episodes.title: The One Who Stays
episodes.tag: Episode 27 Side Story · The One Who Stays

beats.t: The night before the door opened. All the bakery lights were out, and only the oven breathed low.
Yundal sat alone on a chair before it. A yellow sheet and a brush rested on his knees. Three layers of bandages covered the hole that had spread to his wrist.
All right, dear customer. Last service of the day.
There was no customer. Yundal was used to talking to himself. Since people had begun forgetting him, half his conversations had always been with himself.
The brush passed over the paper. 乙亥. His lady's Day Pillar. Eight small stars around it. He left the last star empty.
A talisman is strongest when used only once. Try to use it twice, and greed gets into it.
He held the finished talisman to the firelight, then nodded in satisfaction.
Wayfinding Talisman. Once, it lights our lady's way back. No expiry date. No refunds.
What are you doing there?
Oh, Mr. Cat. Customer Support patrols at night, too.
I followed the smell. Ink.
Neo looked at the talisman in Yundal's hand. Then the bandage beneath it. A black stain seeped from its edge.
Is that for Yeoni?
Yes. I'll slip it into her bread bag tomorrow. Give it directly, and she'll thank me. Then I think I'll cry again.
You don't cry.
You don't know me at all, Mr. Cat. I cry easily. People just forget that I did.
Neo did not answer. Instead, he sat in the chair beside Yundal. For a while, they watched the oven fire together.
You knew you couldn't cross the door?
Yes. Since I first fell into this world. Without your birth hour, you can't return. I've reached that door twice in three years.
Both times...
Yes. Both times, the door failed to recognize me.
A log collapsed in the oven. Sparks flew. Yundal caught one in his bandaged hand. It vanished into the hole in his palm.
I'll stay beside Yeoni over there. You hold on here.
Of course. Holding on is the one thing I'm good at.
And... thank you. For today, at the river.
Wow. Mr. Cat said thank you. Write that on a talisman and sell it, and I'd make a fortune.
I take it back.
The following morning, the door opened. Golden wind filled the bakery storeroom.
As his lady crossed the threshold, Yundal murmured a name very softly. A name other than Yundal. Hoping the person crossing might take it along.
The wind covered it. His lady seemed to glance back. But the door was already closing.
Too much to hope for, then.
The door became an old storage door again. It ended more quickly than he'd expected. Yundal stood there a long time, then stroked the handle once. Still warm.
Around noon, Moka packed. His luggage amounted to a bundle of metal skewers.
Then I'm off. Festival island. Need to catch a boat before sunset.
Take care, Mr. Otter. Cut back on the rapping, too.
Not cutting back on rap. And don't mope alone, con artist. If you're going to mope, come do it on the festival island. I'll give you skewers.
Free?
On credit.
With that, Moka ran toward the dock. Not once did he turn. So Yundal could keep waving until the otter's tail vanished at the alley's end.
That night, Yundal unfolded a sheet at a table in the bakery corner. Not a talisman this time. Just white paper.
He dipped his brush in ink and wrote a name. Not Yundal. The name he had always written beneath his home address three years ago.
Before the ink dried, the letters' edges blurred. Stroke by stroke, they erased themselves, as though sinking into the paper. When the last vanished, the sheet was white again.
A little fast today.
He wrote again. It vanished again. The third time, he put down the brush and read the name aloud.
The name dispersed in the air the moment it became sound. Among bread smells and oven smoke. Reaching nobody's ears.
It's all right. I remember.
He didn't know whether it really was all right. But over three years, he had learned very well how to say it.
Mister, aren't you sleeping?
Ah, Miss Luna. You're awake?
Thirsty. Mister, what's your name? My sister said to ask in the morning. You're a first-time customer who keeps staying.
Yundal's face froze briefly. A first-time customer. Not words to hear from someone who had baked bread beside him yesterday.
Yundal. Leap month. A month that's there, yet isn't. So it's a name you don't have to feel bad about forgetting.
Mr. Yundal. I've memorized it! I'll tell Sis tomorrow.
Thank you. Then please ask me again tomorrow.
Yawning, Luna returned to her room. Yundal watched her for a long time. Tomorrow morning, that child would ask again. Mister, what's your name?
Yundal opened the bakery door and stepped into the alley. He looked up. The fissure where Black Moon had been driven away was closed. But not completely.
Starlight seeped through the sealed crack. Not this world's stars. Unfamiliar stars in twelve rows, one great unnamed star set in each.
Another sky.
The hole in his palm pulled toward that starlight on its own. As it always had since appearing. Toward Black Moon.
There you are. The master of the thing that ate my time.
Yundal adjusted his glove, firmly over the bandages.
Our lady will return if she uses the talisman. That's the kind of person she is. Someone who can't forget the taste of bread.
Then I'll go ahead and secure a place. Location matters for a compatibility booth.
Mr. Cat will get jealous again. That helps business, too.
The next morning, when Luna's sister opened the bakery, nobody sat at the corner table. One brush and one white sheet. Nothing was written on it.
Who left paper here?
Luna's sister folded it and put it in a drawer. She did not throw it away. She didn't know why, either.

episodes.title: The Room I Came Back To
episodes.tag: Episode 28 · The Room I Came Back To

beats.t: When Yeoni opened their eyes, a familiar stain marked the ceiling. Where rain leaked. Their room.
It was still dark outside. Rain tapped the window. Their body felt heavy, like someone waking from a long dream.
This... is my room? My actual room?
They raised a hand. No pink hoof. Five fingers. A little flour beneath the nails.
(Bakery flour. It wasn't a dream.)
The phone beside the pillow lit up. The date was only one night later. All the time spent circling five islands, one night.
[ Code Destiny · Destiny code 8/8 · Return complete ]
One night? Do you know how much bread I ate over there? All of that in one night?
Fabric brushed beside the bed. Neo sat in a chair. Silver hair and deep navy clothes. The same human form Yeoni had seen on the river.
...Neo? You're Neo, right?
Neo stretched stiff shoulders, as though he'd sat there all night. Then spoke in his usual businesslike tone.
“Customer Support. On your first morning after returning, are you experiencing any difficulties?”
You came back with me. You really came all the way here?
“Other people can see me here, too. So don't call me Customer Support outside. Awkward to explain.”
I was always a little weird. You're just making me weirder.
“Still the same form. Though that doesn't mean I have an ID. Quite a lot to explain.”
Yeoni carefully held Neo's wrist. His hand was warm. Beneath his left sleeve, the rust-colored wound from the river remained.
A human hand. Still feels amazing.
“You had hooves until yesterday, too. Let's not get too amazed at each other.”
So tell me if it hurts. Becoming human doesn't change the promise.
“I know. Hard to hide it when checking my hand is the first thing you do.”
Even as he spoke, Neo did not pull away. Instead, he briefly closed his fingers around Yeoni's.
As the sun rose, the room revealed itself. Piled assignments, a dried-out plant, and an umbrella shoved into a corner.
The umbrella was inside out, two ribs broken. Just as the wind had left it the night before Yeoni went to the other world.
(That day really was the worst. Umbrella flipped, bus missed, angry ratings posted.)
A card lay facedown beside the umbrella. Who knew how long it had been there. A small star pattern marked its back.
What's this card? Was it always in my home?
Yeoni tried turning it over. It slipped from their fingers. No matter how often they tried, it would not turn. As though the time had not yet come.
“That card is yours. It'll turn when you're ready. Leave it for now.”
Customer Support always saves the important things for later. One star deducted.
Instead of the card, Yeoni picked up the umbrella. They taped the broken ribs and slowly straightened the bent ones by hand. Not pulling. Pushing.
If it's flipped, fix it. Don't throw it away.
The umbrella opened. A little crooked, but it would keep out rain. Yeoni liked it.
A paper bag rested on the desk. The bread Luna had pressed into their arms at the door. Still warm.
Luna's bread. I really brought it back. Really.
One bite spread the scent of butter through the room. Yeoni remembered the words: fortune could be taken, appetite could not.
A folded sheet came from the bag's bottom. A brush-drawn crescent and unreadable characters.
(What's this? Not a receipt. Not Luna's sister's handwriting.)
“A talisman. I can smell it. Smells of a compatibility con artist.”
Yundal? When did he slip this in?
The paper would not unfold. Trying to force it made Yeoni's fingertips sting. They tucked it, still folded, inside their wallet.
I'll definitely ask him later. If there's a way back.
“The door's closed. No way back right now.” Neo looked outside. The hand on his knee slowly stiffened.
The trip to school was strangely smooth. The bus came on time, with a front seat empty.
A coin in the vending machine brought down two drinks. Even though Yeoni was late, the professor smiled and marked them present.
Weird. So weird. Nobody stepped on my foot today.
Outside the classroom, a classmate caught Yeoni. They thought the group-project materials were lost, but Yeoni's file alone had survived intact.
Only my file? Usually mine is the first one to vanish. That's practically a law of nature.
The classmate looked at Yeoni like a savior. Yeoni smiled awkwardly. Being the one praised was unfamiliar.
Guess I'm lucky today. Should I buy a lottery ticket?
The phone in their bag vibrated. One line appeared in the message preview. No sender.
“Customer Support. Lottery tickets are not recommended. That's not how you use fortune.”
(When did he send a message? And how does he know my phone password?)
Won't even let me dream. Another star deducted.
Yeoni's bad luck had always been diligent. Showed up to work every day without fail. Today, it was absent without notice.
(Because it's 8/8? Once the code is complete, does luck become normal, too?)
At lunch, Yeoni ate half a roll on a bench. They saved the rest. Somehow, it felt as though they would give it to someone.
Not dieting. Just wanted to save half. Respect for the bread, maybe.
Then a raindrop fell from the clear sky onto the back of Yeoni's hand. Cold. Looking up, they saw not a single cloud.
(The smell of rain.)
Yeoni knew it. A smell from somewhere before. By the river, and from a wet cloak.
Must be my imagination. It's summer. Summer has lots of smells.
But the drop on their hand did not dry for a long time.
Yeoni returned the remaining half-roll to the bag. They didn't know who it was for. Half simply felt like someone's share.
Learned that over there. Bread doubles when you share it. Luna's sister said so.
By evening, real rain fell. A fluorescent light flickered in the apartment corridor.
Moving boxes stood outside the home next door. It had been vacant a long time.
A black umbrella rested before its door. There since last night. Water still dripped from its tip.
(That umbrella was there last night, too. It moved in before the boxes.)
A mover set down the last box and asked for a signature. A woman in a black coat signed, her back turned.
Wet hair spilled over her collar. Tall. Her signing hand moved strangely slowly. Stroke by stroke, like writing in a ledger.
Hello, I'm next door. Moving in the rain must have been hard.
The woman's shoulders stiffened for an instant. She did not turn.
Yes. Thank you. Sorry for the noise.
A brief, polite voice. Its ending was cool. Like rainwater.
Then the door behind Yeoni opened. Neo came out and stopped beside them.
Neo's gaze fixed on the woman's right wrist. He half stepped in front of Yeoni. Lips about to offer a greeting shut tight.
Neo! What's wrong? She's our neighbor. Sorry, he's not usually like this.
It's all right. Your companion seems a little wary of me.
The woman never showed her face. Taking the black umbrella, she went inside.
The door closed. Only the smell of rain remained. Exactly the smell from the drop on Yeoni's hand that afternoon.
That night, Neo did not sleep. Sitting on the windowsill, he stared only at the wall.
(I've never seen him this guarded. Not even when he was a cat.)
Neo. Why don't you like her? You haven't even seen her face.
“I don't know. There's a smell. I've smelled it somewhere, but I can't remember.”
You can't remember? Customer Support?
“Things from there blur here. Yundal said it. They might fade like a dream.”
Yeoni pulled up the blanket. The words were frightening. Luna's smile, Moka's sharp tongue, the tiger's red eyes. Their edges were already blurring.
Yeoni opened the phone's notes and wrote whatever came to mind. Bread. Luna. Moka. Yundal. Black tiger.
Can't forget. Writing it down should keep it from blurring so much.
Their fingers faltered. Nothing came after tiger. The drumming child's name. They had definitely seen it, but the shapes were blurred as if by water.
I can't remember the child's name. I saw it inside that cloak.
“The tiger has it. Not knowing it doesn't make it disappear.”
(The tiger has it. Write that down, too.)
Yeoni added a line. Drum boy's name, inside tiger's cloak. Then a small question mark beside it.
“...Good habit. Five stars.” Neo's voice softened a little.
First time I've seen Customer Support rate the customer.
No sound came from beyond the wall. Someone lived there, yet there wasn't even a breath.
Then the phone screen flickered. A black dot spread in the app icon's corner. Like a moon covering the sun.
[ Checking connection · · · ]
When Yeoni looked again, the dot was gone. Only the rain continued. On the windowsill, Neo never took his eyes from the wall.

episodes.title: The Black Umbrella Next Door
episodes.tag: Episode 28 Side Story · The Black Umbrella Next Door

beats.t: Three clear days in a row. A high sky, and sun icons across the whole week's forecast.
Yet the woman next door came out with her black umbrella again.
(Umbrella again. Zero percent chance of rain today.)
They stood by the elevator. The woman held the folded umbrella's handle. Her tightly clenched hand was white.
Hello. You brought your umbrella again. I wondered if I'd read the forecast wrong.
It won't rain. I just carry it.
Oh, so like a parasol? To shade you from the sun.
Something like that. The sun stings a little.
The conversation ended there. The elevator numbers descended slowly. Silence grew heavier one floor at a time.
I'm Yeoni. Next door. May I ask your name?
My name... I'll tell you later.
Why? Is it a secret?
Giving someone my name feels like owing them. Giving something when there's nothing to receive is a little...
Behind Yeoni's ear, something tingled. It sounded like something heard before. But where would not come to mind.
(A name as a debt. Who says that? ...And why does it feel familiar?)
The elevator arrived. They entered side by side. Two figures reflected in its mirror. The woman did not look.
You've been here a few days, but I haven't heard a sound. Haven't you unpacked yet?
Not much to unpack. I won't be staying long.
Oh, just a short stay? A business trip or something?
Something like that. I'll leave when the job's finished. I don't know when that will be.
For the first time, the woman looked at Yeoni. Very briefly, as if checking something. Then back to the floor display.
(Why did she look at me like that? Like she was checking whether something had happened to me.)
When the doors opened on the first floor, the woman stepped out first, walking quickly. The black umbrella's tip tapped the floor.
In the playground before the building, a child fell and scraped a knee. The child bit their lip, trying not to cry.
Before Yeoni could run over, the woman stopped. Midstride. Abruptly.
She set down the umbrella and knelt. A bandage came from her coat pocket, as though prepared in advance.
If it hurts a lot, you can cry. Holding it in doesn't make it hurt less.
The child finally cried. The woman did not soothe them. She simply applied the bandage carefully and waited until the crying was done.
(Her voice is cold, but her hands are so careful.)
Her sleeve rode up as she placed the bandage. Something like a thin golden cord flashed at her right wrist. A bracelet, perhaps, but it seemed embedded in the skin.
Perhaps sensing Yeoni's gaze, she pulled down her sleeve. Then picked up her umbrella without a word.
The child must have been really frightened. I'm glad you helped.
Nothing to thank me for. I was just passing.
For someone just passing, she had stopped a long time. Yeoni watched her walk away.
The child's mother ran up and bowed. The woman was already too far away to accept it. As though gratitude were a heavy burden.
(She avoids being thanked. Like hearing thank you would bring disaster.)
The child tugged Yeoni's sleeve and asked the woman's name. Yeoni didn't know, either.
I don't know. I'll be sure to ask next time. Maybe she'll answer then.
At home, Neo waited in the entryway. When Yeoni rolled up a dry sleeve, he tilted his head briefly.
“You met that woman again? You smell of rain.”
It was clear today, dear customer. No possible smell of rain.
“That's what's strange. Someone who smells of rain on a clear day.”
(Right. It is strange. An umbrella in clear weather. Rain scent in clear weather.)
Yeoni sat on the sofa and opened their notes. The list from three days ago. Bread. Luna. Moka. Yundal. Black tiger.
But reading it did not clearly bring back their faces. What color was Moka's tail? Which hand wore Yundal's glove?
Neo. It's already blurring. I can't remember Moka's voice.
“Mine, too, little by little. The longer we're here, the farther away things over there seem.”
Then I'll write more. Faster than it disappears.
Yeoni added lines beneath the list. Moka, otter, bad at rap. Yundal, right-hand glove, compatibility scams. Black tiger, red eyes, a name is a debt.
At the last line, their fingers stopped. A name is a debt. The same shape as the words by the elevator today.
(Could it be? No. That tiger is over there. This is reality.)
“What are you thinking? You look serious.”
Nothing. Just that lots of people in the world have similar ways of speaking.
Yeoni underlined the last word. The phone beside them gave a brief chime. Over a captured image of the notes, a tiny umbrella icon blinked. An unfamiliar symbol.
Late that night, Yeoni went into the corridor with the recycling. The fluorescent light flickered again.
At the window at the corridor's end stood the woman next door. Beneath her open black umbrella. Indoors, on a night without rain.
...Not sleeping? What are you doing there?
The woman slowly turned. Her eyes were dark beneath the umbrella's shadow. But when the light flickered, red flashed in them.
(Red... no. The fluorescent light.)
Go inside. You'll catch a cold.
A cold? It isn't even raining.
You're right. It isn't.
(She's telling me not to get rained on. Even though there's no rain.)
You should go inside, too. The corridor's cold. Standing under an umbrella makes you look even colder.
I'm fine. I need to stand here before I can sleep.
A strange answer. But Yeoni asked no more. It felt as though another question might break her.
Yeoni took the saved half-roll from the bag they carried and quietly placed it on the windowsill.
A midnight snack. Leftover, so it's free. You don't have to eat it.
The woman did not fold her umbrella. Until Yeoni closed the door, she only looked outside. She did not touch the bread.
Only after closing the door did Yeoni realize. Water marks ran along the corridor floor, from the window to the neighbor's door. On a night without one drop of rain.
The next morning, the windowsill was empty. The bread bag hung neatly folded from Yeoni's door handle. No note inside.

episodes.title: The Price of a Safe Tomorrow
episodes.tag: Episode 28 Side Story · The Price of a Safe Tomorrow

beats.t: The good luck continued for a week. Yeoni began to feel a little afraid.
The scholarship paperwork passed on the first try. The sneakers they wanted were half price. Whenever they needed it, the elevator waited on the first floor.
(Bad luck not showing up for work makes me more anxious. What kind of person am I?)
“Good fortune makes you suspicious first.”
The other world taught me that. Nothing was free except the bread.
“Still thinking about the bread bag coming back folded?”
(Yes. Did she eat it? Just return the bag? Folded so neatly, it looked like a receipt.)
I think she's afraid to receive things. Because then she has to repay them.
“People like that have usually had a lot taken from them. Or taken a lot from others.”
Could be both.
The doorbell rang. The woman next door stood outside holding a box.
Your package came to my apartment by mistake. It's yours.
Oh, thank you. Would you like to come in? Have some tea?
I'm fine. I'll leave in a moment.
Yet she did not go. Standing in the doorway, she looked inside. At the taped umbrella in the corner.
You repaired the umbrella. Instead of throwing it away.
Yes. It flipped, but it looked like it could survive. A waste to throw it out.
Seated beside the sofa, Neo looked at her. His hand tightened on the armrest.
The day that umbrella flipped was the worst day of my life. Missed the bus, got soaked, gave an app one star.
A rating?
Yes. To the universe. And the universe actually replied. Hard to believe, I know.
The corner of her mouth moved very slightly. Too brief to call a smile. Gone at once.
I believe you. The universe replies. Always late, though.
Oh, that sounds like experience.
Just saying things. Never mind.
You've been lucky lately, haven't you?
How did you know?
Written on your face. But good luck doesn't last. You know that, right?
She took a business card from her coat pocket. Gold letters on black. Tomorrow Guarantee Consultation.
A short folded contract was attached. We hold and protect your tomorrows on your behalf. No misfortune will reach you.
Leave them in our care before bad luck returns. Then you won't lose anything.
(I've seen this on the island that sold time. Blue Rabbit's contract. Read the fine print first.)
Yeoni read to the end. At the bottom, in tiny letters: During custody, the user's important decisions must be discussed with the custodian beforehand.
What counts as important? It doesn't define the scope.
Everything. Every risky decision.
So in exchange for protection, I hand over my choices.
Better than choosing and getting hurt. You're someone who gets hurt making choices. A great deal.
There was strange certainty in her words. Like someone who had seen Yeoni hurt many times.
I'll choose whether to get hurt, too. Thank you, but no.
Why? Getting hurt is painful. You don't like pain. Nobody does.
I don't. But if I only take safe paths someone else chooses, that isn't my tomorrow.
The woman opened her mouth, then closed it. As though about to argue and losing the words.
Her fingers clutched the card's corner. The paper crumpled.
Leave a debt alone, and it grows.
The room fell quiet. Goosebumps rose along Yeoni's back. That tone. That sentence. Heard before the vault on the island that sold time.
...What did you just say?
Nothing. Just something adults say.
The woman reached to retrieve the card. Her sleeve slid up.
A scar circled her right wrist, as though something had squeezed it for a long time. A thin gold cord was embedded at its center.
(A ring mark. On the right. ...The right forepaw.)
Yeoni tried to catch the memory. Black fur, golden ring, the feel of pushing with their forehead. But it blurred like wet paper.
Then Neo rose beside the sofa. He started to grab the woman's outstretched wrist, then stopped. His fingertips brushed the gold beneath her sleeve.
Neo! Don't! She's a guest!
...It's all right. I'm not hurt.
She avoided Neo's eyes, pulled down her sleeve, and stepped back.
Excuse me. I'll leave the card. Knock if you change your mind.
The door closed. Yeoni picked up the fallen card. A contract on the front. And the back.
Handwriting covered the back. Thin and neat. Every stroke pressed carefully, like writing in a ledger.
[ Don't go to the bus stop on rainy days ]
(The bus stop? Why the bus stop?)
“Can't tell if that's a warning or a threat.” Neo braced against the chair's armrest, his knuckles tense.
Could be neither. Could be concern.
“Who shows concern by offering a contract first?”
(But why the bus stop? The one in our neighborhood is just an ordinary stop.)
Yeoni looked outside. The bus stop before the apartment stood quietly beneath a streetlight. Water dripping from its roof's edge looked strangely familiar.
For an instant, someone seemed to stand beneath it, an umbrella tilted halfway. One blink, and nobody was there.
Neo. Was someone at the stop just now?
“Nobody. But I smelled rain.”
People over there did that, too. Could only express worry through a price tag.
Yeoni set the card beside their notes and added one more line. Woman next door. Umbrella on clear days. Ring mark on right wrist. Leave a debt alone, and it grows.
Before sleeping, Yeoni pressed a palm to the wall. Cold. Very faintly, paper turned beyond it. One page, then another.
(A ledger. That tiger was always writing things, too. Who owed how much.)
The sound continued a long time, then stopped abruptly. Someone caught a breath, very quietly.
The weather app sent a notification. Tomorrow: showers from three in the afternoon.

episodes.title: A Promise at the Rainy Bus Stop
episodes.tag: Episode 28 Side Story · A Promise at the Rainy Bus Stop

beats.t: At three in the afternoon, the forecast proved accurate. The classroom windows suddenly darkened, and a downpour began.
(She said not to go to the stop. But I have to catch a bus to get home.)
Yeoni opened the taped umbrella. Its ribs stood crooked. But it opened.
Can't get home without the bus stop, Ms. Neighbor. Thanks for worrying, though.
Inside the wallet in their bag, the folded talisman grew faintly warm. Yeoni did not notice.
In the hallway, classmates cried that they had no umbrellas. The convenience store had already sold out.
This is all I've got. Two ribs held with tape. Anyone sharing has to accept getting half soaked.
Nobody raised a hand. Everyone laughed at the crooked umbrella. Yeoni laughed with them.
(Still a pretty good umbrella. Repaired things are all right.)
The bus stop roof sheltered a crowd. Rain hammered the asphalt white.
(Here I am. Nothing's happening. Scared myself for nothing.)
The display showed seven minutes until the bus. Yeoni shook out the umbrella and stepped beneath the roof.
Then the talisman in their wallet grew unmistakably hot. Yeoni opened the bag. The crescent on the folded paper glowed very faintly.
Why is Yundal's talisman... Is something here?
At the roof's edge, on the boundary of falling rain, stood someone in a black coat. But today, no umbrella.
Ms. Neighbor? What are you doing there?
Her hair was soaked. Water streamed from her coat's shoulders. The umbrella she carried every clear day was nowhere.
Where's your umbrella? You always carry it when it's sunny.
I gave it to the playground child earlier. They were alone in the rain.
The bandage kid? But what about you?
I can get wet. I'm used to it.
Yeoni did not think. Before thought, their hand moved. They tilted the umbrella halfway over the woman.
Let's share. We'll both get half wet, though.
At that moment, something overlapped in their mind. The same stop. The same rain. Their own hand tilting an umbrella. And someone whose face was erased.
(This... the scene in the library. The person then was...)
The face would not come. Only the face of the person beneath the umbrella was white and empty, as though rubbed out with an eraser.
The woman lifted her head and looked straight at Yeoni. Her eyes were red. Whether from rain, Yeoni could not tell.
...How much is this?
What? How much is what?
Sharing your umbrella. How much? What do I give you?
A strange question. Yet she truly waited for an answer. Like someone unable to receive anything without a price tag.
It's free. Why charge someone when it's raining?
Her shoulders collapsed. Her breath caught. She covered her mouth. Water flowed over the back of her hand.
Are you okay? Does something hurt?
I've heard those words before. A very long time ago. At the same bus stop.
From me?
No. Not you. It can't be you. You don't remember.
It was neither an answer nor a confession. Closer to speaking to herself.
It's okay not to remember. We're sharing now. This belongs to now.
She looked at Yeoni for a long time. Thin rain passed between them. One umbrella rib trembled in the wind.
Belongs to now. I didn't know there was such a thing. I thought everything had to be repaid.
Think about repayment later. Staying dry comes first. Well, half dry.
The bus pulled in with a spray of water. People lined up. Yeoni looked at the woman.
Come with me. Same apartment building.
Go ahead. I'll take the next one.
Then keep the umbrella. I can run after I get off.
Yeoni placed the taped handle in her hand. She could neither release it nor properly hold it.
The bus departed. The stop receded outside the window. Without opening the umbrella, the woman crouched, holding it to her chest. Her shoulders shook.
Yeoni reached the apartment completely soaked. Water pooled on the corridor floor. A package sat before the neighbor's door.
Today, the label faced up. Yeoni had not meant to look. It simply caught their eye.
[ Recipient · Seo Hanbi ]
(Seo Hanbi. Hanbi. ...Cold rain.)
Cold rain. Rain was in her name. Umbrellas on clear days, rain scent on clear days. Even her name was rain.
(Says a name is a debt, then leaves it written on packages like this.)
Yeoni almost laughed. But instead, their chest hurt. They remembered the shoulders collapsing at the stop.
Inside, Neo offered a towel. Instead of asking what had happened, he took the wet bag first.
“That woman again. Stronger smell this time. Rain and tears.”
Yes. She cried. I shared my umbrella, and she asked how much.
Neo said nothing for a while. His finger pressed the folded towel's edge.
“...I know someone who asks how much. Over there.”
I think I know, too. But don't tell me yet. I want to figure it out.
“Why solve it yourself? Faster if I tell you.”
If you tell me, it's your memory. I need to figure it out to believe it. She'll need that to believe it, too.
Instead of answering, Neo sat beside Yeoni. Their wet shoulders touched, but he did not move away. They stayed like that until Yeoni spoke first.
“...Still stubborn. That's a relief.”
At the same time, beyond the wall, an umbrella stood open to dry in the unlit room. Crooked ribs wrapped in tape.
Seo Hanbi sat beside it and opened the ledger. Yeoni's entry. Beneath the uncollected line, a new line spread.
[ Ledger · Eulhae Yeoni · Uncollected: 2 ]
She stared at the number for a long time. One more thing she could not repay.
The golden cord tightened at the wrist holding the pen. Pain burrowed into flesh. She made no sound.
Instead, she took a folded note from her coat's inner pocket and laid it on her palm. The drumming child's name. She folded it once more to keep it dry.

episodes.title: The First to Recognize Her
episodes.tag: Episode 28 Side Story · The First to Recognize Her

beats.t: The next morning, Yeoni opened their notes and read each line aloud.
One, black umbrella even on clear days. Two, rain smell in clear weather. Name: Seo Hanbi, cold rain.
Three, saying giving a name creates a debt. Four, saying a debt grows if left alone.
(Five, ring mark on right wrist. Six, habit of stopping before someone hurt.)
Yeoni pointed to the next line. Seven, Neo wary of her right wrist. Stepped in front of me the instant he saw her.
“Eight, asked the price when you shared an umbrella.”
I was about to write that. No spoilers from Customer Support.
Then Yeoni remembered. The Library of Resources. The chase between shelves. The name stitched inside the fluttering black cloak. The drumming child's name.
(That tiger stopped before a hurt child, too. Didn't know what to do when given bread.)
Seo Hanbi is that tiger. The black tiger.
“...Yes. I remember now, too. That smell. Upriver.”
But why is that tiger living next door? As a human?
“One of two reasons. To hunt you, or protect you.”
(She wrote not to go to the bus stop on the card. Would someone hunting me write that?)
Then I'll ask. She's next door.
“Dangerous. Over there, she hunted you. She still has claws here.”
I know. But I saw her cry at the stop. Hunters don't cry like that.
“...Your judgment of people has improved. Thanks to Customer Support's training.”
Thanks to Luna's sister's bread. I saw a lot of people while eating bread.
At the door, Yeoni's hands shook while tying their sneakers. Neo crouched beside them and held the loose knot.
“I'm coming. Don't stop me if I hiss.”
Yeoni stood before the neighbor's door, empty-handed. Maybe they should have brought bread.
Three knocks. After a long wait, the door opened a little. Seo Hanbi's eyes appeared through the chained gap.
What is it? It's early.
I've come for my umbrella. And to ask something.
The taped umbrella emerged through the gap. Yeoni did not take it. Instead, they called softly through the door.
Ms. Tiger?
The umbrella fell. Tap. The sound alone echoed through the corridor.
...Wrong apartment.
Do you still have the drumming child's name? In your coat's inner pocket?
Without knowing it, Seo Hanbi's hand went to her chest. Then stopped. Too late.
It's there. Thank goodness.
Color drained from her face. Beyond the chain, she steadied her breathing. The door did not close.
I can't remember that child's name. Things blurred after I came here. But you still have it.
I tried to throw it away. So many times. It would clear the ledger. But I couldn't.
How... Everything blurs here. You weren't supposed to know anything.
I wrote it down. Afraid I'd forget. Everything you let slip.
Then you know what I did to you. Who collected all your fortune.
I know. That's why I came to ask. Why move next door? To finish it, or to protect me?
Seo Hanbi couldn't answer. Beyond the chain, her lips opened and closed twice.
Both. Ordered to finish it. Wanted to protect you. Managed neither.
Is that why you stood with an umbrella every clear day? Guarding my door?
When rain comes, it comes. Where there's water. That's why I told you not to go to the stop on rainy days.
What comes?
Instead of an answer, Yeoni's phone lit up in their pocket. A pitch-black screen. A black circle at its center. A sun burning red only at the rim.
Black hands reached from the screen. One, two, twelve. They wrapped around Yeoni's wrists and ankles.
These... those hands from over there! But this is reality!
Too late, hound. I told you to finish it there. I'll collect in person.
No! That child isn't empty yet!
Then empty it. Open the door. With your own hands this time.
The hands dragged Yeoni toward the phone. The screen widened into a door. Unfamiliar stars swirled beyond.
Seo Hanbi tore off the chain. The door flew open. At her right wrist, the gold cord burned red.
The black coat became fur. Hands became paws, nails claws. A black tiger filled the corridor, standing before Yeoni.
Get your hands off that child.
One sweep severed three hands. They grew back. The tiger cut again. The golden ring on its right forepaw dug into flesh.
Disobeying again. Have you forgotten whose ring that is?
I haven't. That's why I'm repaying it myself this time.
The tiger covered Yeoni with its body. This time, the hands wrapped around the tiger instead.
Ms. Tiger! Let go. Let's hold on together!
Thank you for the umbrella. I'll put that in the ledger. As uncollected.
The hands dragged the tiger into the screen. The tip of its black tail brushed Yeoni's hand last. Like cold rainwater.
The corridor went quiet. The fluorescent light flickered once, then came back on.
On the floor remained a taped umbrella and one wet pawprint. A red pawprint.
I called her. I recognized her, and that's why...
Neo knelt before Yeoni. He offered his hand but waited until they took it. His gaze still faced the corridor's end.
“Not your fault. Because you recognized her first, she chose with her own hands. Perhaps for the first time.”
[ Another sky has opened · The Twelve Palaces ]
The app opened on the phone by itself. Like the day Yeoni first installed it, only one button appeared.
Nobody's making me press it this time. I'll press it myself.
Yeoni picked up the umbrella. Its taped handle was still warm from Seo Hanbi holding it for so long.
I have to return this. I'm going to bring her back. This time, she's not getting away for free.
Inside the wallet, Yundal's talisman began glowing warmly. Over the folded paper, a crescent slowly waxed.

episodes.title: This Time, I Press It
episodes.tag: Episode 29 · This Time, I Press It

beats.t: One button filled the phone screen. Like the day Yeoni first installed the app. That day, rain had fallen, Yeoni had been angry, and a finger had slipped.
No slipping this time. Read the terms first.
Sitting on the bed, Yeoni scrolled. The text went on endlessly. A habit learned on the island that sold time. Fine print first.
[ Another Sky · The Twelve Palaces · Entry requirement: Your birth date and time ]
(Birth date and time. The Four Pillars islands didn't ask for any of this. Just sucked me in.)
One more line lay below. This sky is built from your star chart. You know best where you stand.
I know best? I barely even know my zodiac sign.
Neo sat beside the open bag. Supplies gathered overnight piled on his knees.
“You don't need that. No room.” Yeoni pointed to the thick blanket. After a moment's thought, Neo folded it in half.
“Nights could be cold. Folded in half, it fits. I'll carry it.”
Customer Support's getting a free ride. Fine, come along.
Yeoni packed things one by one. The taped umbrella. Notebook. Charger. Two red bean buns from the convenience store.
(One for me. One for her. This time, I'll carry it until she takes it.)
The talisman in the wallet grew warm again. Yeoni took it out. The crescent on the paper had half filled.
Yundal's talisman. Still warm. Use it, and it takes us to him, right?
“He said one use. Toward the guide.”
Then we find our guide first. I'm tired of wandering alone.
Yeoni tapped the birth details fields. Their fingertips trembled a little. July 6, 2002. 8:30 a.m. Seoul.
(Mom always said being born at breakfast meant I'd be lucky with food.)
[ Eulhae Yeoni · Preparing natal chart · · · ]
A twelve-part board formed on the screen. Square compartments ringed an empty center, like a game board. Tiny star names glimmered in each.
What's this? Different from the Four Pillars. Twelve spaces instead of eight characters.
“Didn't it say another sky? Another sky is read with different characters.”
