More to study. My grades this semester are doomed.
Then a black spot spread in one of the twelve spaces, like a drop of ink. It slowly crept along the compartment's border.
Neo. Look. One space is turning black.
Neo set down the supplies and leaned toward the screen. His eyes hardened as he read.
“The smell of an eclipse. It's reached into that sky, too.”
She must be there, too. They dragged her into the phone.
“Probably.” Neo chose his words for a moment. “Scared? You can tell me.”
Yes. Terrified. But being scared and not going are different things.
Yeoni looked around the room. The ceiling stain. Where rain leaked. The star card on the desk. It still would not turn over.
(The first time, I was dragged away. For giving the universe one star. Not this time.)
Yeoni picked up the star card and tried lifting its corner with a nail. It did not budge. As though it were still too soon.
You're coming, too. You'll turn over someday.
They slipped it between notebook pages, then wrote in large letters on the first page.
[ Moka · Otter · Bad at rap / Yundal · Right-hand glove · Compatibility scams / Seo Hanbi · Umbrella · Uncollected: 2 / Neo · Was a cat · Human now · On my side ]
“Why write the last line?”
Even if you change again, I need to remember it's you. You've been on my side since you were a cat.
Instead of answering, Neo gently covered the back of Yeoni's hand. Gold briefly leaked between his fingers.
Okay. Rating first.
Now. I'll leave it in advance this time. I gave this app one star at first.
Yeoni opened the review field. Their finger hesitated a long time, then moved.
[ ★★★☆☆ · Being dragged away is the worst. But I made friends because of it. The other two stars after I get back. ]
“Three stars. Customer Support is moved.”
Don't be. I might deduct some when I return.
Yeoni retied their sneakers and shouldered the bag. Neo took the umbrella. Together, they stood before the door.
Ready. Customer Support, connect me.
“I'm not Customer Support.”
I know. But saying it that way makes it less scary.
The screen still held only one button. Round. With a short word on it.
[ YES ]
On that first day, the button had pulled Yeoni's finger toward it. Today, it pulled nothing. It simply waited. Leaving the choice to Yeoni.
(Nobody's forcing me to press. So this really is my choice.)
Seo Hanbi. I'm coming to get my umbrella back.
Yeoni pressed firmly with a thumb. The screen swelled white. The floor rippled like water, and the ceiling stain shone like a constellation.
Their body fell upward. Not down, up. The room shrank to a fingernail-sized square. The square became a star.
OIIINK! Wait, falling upward this time?!
“Still haven't broken the habit. Wasn't oink your pig sound?”
A habit! Habits stay even when bodies change!
Crossing the boundary, Neo's fingertips turned gold. Without thinking, Yeoni gripped his hand tightly. Their bodies did not change. Both stood in human form.
You can let go. Same this time.
I know. I'll just hold on a little longer.
Then hold tight so you don't slip.
Yes. I won't let go this time.
Their feet met ground. Stone, cold and smooth, with starlight shining up from beneath. As though another sky lay below.
Yeoni looked down at their hands. Not hooves. Five fingers. Nails. Even the watch mark at the wrist.
Human. Not a pig. I came as a human this time.
You already regained your form. What you've found once in that sky won't be lost in another.
Thank goodness. Human hands can hold an umbrella.
A vast palace stood before them. Too many roof layers to count. A star hung at every eave, swaying like a lantern.
Twelve gates punctuated the wall around it. Each had a plaque engraved with a star pattern instead of words.
[ Natal chart reading · Eulhae Yeoni · Life Palace: Yin (寅) · Main star: Lian Zhen ]
(Life Palace. Lian Zhen. I don't understand any of it.)
Neither do I. First time in this sky.
There are things you don't know, Neo?
I don't know everything. Just good at pretending.
That's an impressively honest confession.
Yeoni took the talisman from their wallet. The crescent was nearly full. The paper turned on their palm by itself, like a compass needle.
This way. Toward Yundal.
It pointed to the western of the twelve gates. Its plaque showed a horse-shaped star and a long road.
A gate of travel? Suits that con artist. Never settling anywhere.
A colonnade led toward the gate. Little star people passed between pillars, their bodies half made of light. Burdens on their backs, lanterns in their hands.
(Everyone's made of starlight. But their faces are like ours. Busy, tired.)
Yet some faces were gray, as though their light had drained away. They carried lanterns, but none were lit.
What's wrong with them? Like the gray stamps on the Island of Expression.
Eaten. Their light.
One gray-faced person stopped beside Yeoni. They looked at Yeoni—or at something beyond them.
“...The Career gate has closed. Black things come from there. Don't go.”
The Career gate? Where is that?
No answer. Carrying the lightless lantern, the star person vanished down the colonnade.
(Don't go. Why is everyone telling me not to go somewhere lately?)
There must be a reason they're warning us away. Let's find out.
Yes. That's the problem.
A sheet clung to a pillar. Wet. Even under a clear sky, water dripped from it.
Yeoni took it down. Thin, neat handwriting. Each stroke pressed carefully, like writing in a ledger.
[ Ledger · Eulhae Yeoni · Uncollected: 2 ]
Hers. Seo Hanbi passed through here.
The water smell is still strong. Not long ago.
Yeoni carefully folded the damp ledger page into the notebook, beside the star card.
I'll collect what's uncollected. So she can stop going around repaying it.
At the colonnade's end, the wind changed. Wet ash replaced the scent of stars. One side of the sky was black as spilled ink.
There. That sky looks rotten.
Step back. Not ordinary darkness.
Threads flowed from the black sky. Touching the ground, they split into fingers. The fingers scratched the stone as they crawled closer.
You came of your own accord, vessel. Nobody pushed you this time.
Yes. On my own feet. So I'll leave on my own feet, too.
Whether you leave is for this sky to decide. One of your twelve spaces is already mine.
Neo stepped forward. Golden blades from his fingertips cut three black fingers. Instead of sparks, black steam rose from the cuts.
...These hands eat Metal.
Neo, your hand! Your fingertips are black!
His right fingertips were stained as though dipped in ink. He shook his hand. The stains stayed.
Stings a little. I can still move it.
Don't say that. Every time you say that, you're not okay.
Hurting Officer rose to Yeoni's throat. They wanted to shout, to pour everything at that black sky. But they remembered Neo had been hurt every time.
(Hold it. Shout now, and Neo gets hurt again. Something besides shouting.)
Instead, Yeoni raised the talisman high. The crescent filled completely. The paper flared silver.
Silver swept the colonnade. The black fingers flinched and retreated. The talisman became ash, scattering from Yeoni's palm.
A human diviner's talisman. The Void borrows others' hands now. It won't stop me long.
The black sky slowly closed. The fingers on the ground unraveled like threads and vanished. Only wet ash remained in the air.
Silence returned. Only then did Yeoni realize they had held their breath. They let out a long sigh.
Used up the talisman. Guess the way to Yundal burned with it.
No. Look there.
Where the ash scattered, silver dust formed a line to the western gate. Like someone leaving breadcrumbs.
Not a con artist after all. Even laid out a path.
A con artist. A skilled one.
Still jealous.
Not jealousy. An objective assessment.
Yeoni looked at Neo's right hand. The stain had crept a little toward his wrist. He hid it behind his back.
Don't hide it. We agreed no hiding this time.
...I'll tell you if it spreads. I promise.
Before it spreads. That's the promise.
Neo nodded silently. Yeoni wanted to put that promise in the notebook, too.
A bell rang beyond the western gate. A very familiar voice rode the wind.
“Compatibility readings! Just your birth date and time, and I'll find your destined partner. Half price today only.”
...That voice.
Half price. It was already a scam at full price.
Suppressing a laugh, Yeoni ran toward the western gate. Silver dust shimmered beneath their feet. Behind them, a crow cawed above a distant gate marked Career.
Beyond the western gate lay a market. Starlight tents stood in rows, with tiny stars hanging from poles instead of lanterns.
At its center, customers crowded one particularly shabby tent. Crooked letters read: Compatibility · Naming · Wayfinding. Credit accepted.
Credit accepted. Definitely him.
Only one person would write that sign.
Inside, a man with a glove on his right hand read a young star woman's palm. Her face blushed with starlight.
Look at this line. A benefactor comes from the west. Very close, too. May I ask your birth date and time?
Just as she opened her mouth, Neo stood before the tent. A silver cloak swayed behind the shoulders blocking its entrance.
Customers from the west. These ones aren't taking a free consultation.
The gloved hand froze in midair. The man slowly looked up and met Yeoni's eyes.
Yundal. You said you'd secure a spot. You really did.
The smile left Yundal's face. Not even surprise. As though something had caught in his throat.
...You know my name?
Of course. Yundal. Right-hand glove. Compatibility scams.
Over there, everyone forgot after a day. Luna, her sister. Every morning, a first-time customer.
Yeoni took out the notebook and opened its first page before him. Their handwriting lay there. Yundal · Right-hand glove · Compatibility scams.
I wrote it down, afraid I'd forget. They said the air here erased memories, so I wrote faster than they disappeared.
Yundal stared at the line, tracing the letters with a gloved finger. At compatibility scams, his mouth lifted as though collapsing.
Of all things to survive, compatibility scams. That's a business loss.
It's true.
That makes it hurt more. You haven't changed, my lady.
She's already gone. Don't blame me for losing your customer.
The young star woman glanced between them and left. Without ever paying for her palm reading.
Mr. Cat hasn't changed, either. You're responsible for this month's sales.
Then a savory smell came from behind the tent. Charcoal, sizzling oil. Yeoni's stomach reacted first.
Pig. Followed your nose, didn't you? Still a pig's nose.
Moka?! Why are you here? You said festival island!
I went. Then this con artist chased me there by boat. Said a guide needed someone to cook.
True. Star people's food is light. Doesn't fill you up. Three days starving, and I started thinking about otter skewers.
So I came to collect his tab. Thirty skewers he owes.
You came to another sky to collect that?
Thirty skewers is serious money. Oh, right. Still not used to you being human. The bakery was so hectic, I didn't get a good look.
I'm human now. Not a pig.
Still a pig. A pig at heart. Same face when someone hands you a skewer.
Grumbling, Moka pushed one into Yeoni's hand. Starlight mushrooms and unknown fruit on a stick. Flavor. Warmth.
Delicious. Just like the first one on the Island of Expression.
...Obviously. My skewers taste good even when the sky changes.
With that, Moka whipped his head away. His tail swished fiercely behind him. Only the tail could hide nothing.
Otter. Good to see you.
Good, nothing. Neo, what's with your hand? It's black.
Everyone looked at Neo's right hand. The stain had passed his wrist. He pulled down his sleeve.
Cut a few black hands on the way. Must have rubbed off then.
More than that, I think. Let's discuss it over the chart.
Yundal cleared the tent's table. A twelve-part board was engraved on it, the same shape Yeoni had seen on the phone.
This sky's map. A natal chart. Each compartment is a palace. Each palace, a room of life.
(Eight characters in the Four Pillars. Twelve rooms here.)
A room for self, siblings, partner, children, money, body. For outside journeys, friends, work, home, inner peace, and parents.
Twelve rooms must be hard to clean.
That's why most people leave one or two messy.
Yundal pointed with a gloved finger to one space, marked 寅. The very star name Yeoni had seen on the phone shone there.
[ Life Palace: Yin (寅) · Lian Zhen · Bright ]
Your room, my lady. Its ruling star is Lian Zhen. Also called the Prison Star. A star that confines itself.
Confines? Am I trapped?
You're the one confining. A star holding fire, gripping it tightly for fear it will burn someone else.
Yeoni could not answer. Moments when Hurting Officer erupted came back. The courtroom. Neo's scorched hand. Since then, Yeoni had shut their mouth every time they wanted to shout.
(A star holding on. Right. Lately, I'm always holding it in.)
What does the pig hold? Always giving everything away.
Exactly why it's Lian Zhen. Gives freely when giving, grips tight when angry. Shining brightly, it becomes principle. In darkness, a prison.
It says bright now.
For now.
Yundal took out a small pouch and shook it. Four handfuls of colored dust fell onto the chart. Gold, red, blue. And black.
In this sky, four labels attach to stars. Your birth year determines them. You were born in an Im year, 壬.
Gold dust settled on a star in the Children room beside the Money room. Red on the great star in Money. Blue on a small star in the room of outside journeys.
[ Prosperity Transformation: Tian Liang · Authority Transformation: Zi Wei · Distinction Transformation: Zuo Fu · Obstruction Transformation: Wu Qu ]
Prosperity is blessing flowing in. Authority, the power to hold. Distinction, the light that makes a name. And Obstruction.
The black dust fell last. The Work room, marked 午, Wu. Two great stars stood side by side. It clung to one, then seeped into the chart.
The black one. Same space that spread on my phone.
Obstruction marks a blockage. Something you should have received but didn't. A place where regrets gather. Black Moon uses that name in this sky. Obstruction Transformation.
Even the name's gloomy.
It's attached to Wu Qu. A star of Metal.
The tent fell quiet. Yeoni slowly looked at Neo. He wasn't watching the chart. He watched one part of the sky beyond the tent.
Metal. You're Metal, too, Neo. Gyeong.
Coincidence.
Not many coincidences in this sky. And that space is the Career Palace. The room of work and one's name. As for who represents Officer in your chart...
Enough.
Neo's voice lowered. Yundal fell silent, his eyes fixed on Neo's sleeve.
(Officer. Influence. In the library, Yundal said Neo was my Influence. Then what the black thing is after...)
Yundal suggested visiting Yeoni's room first. A chart alone wasn't enough. You had to enter a room to know how it smelled.
The Yin gate stood on the palace's east side. Beyond it was a round room, mirrors covering every wall.
All me. Little me, middle-school me, last year's me.
Every reflected Yeoni gripped something. At seven, tears. At fifteen, an exam paper. Last year, an upturned umbrella.
All holding something. Could just let go.
Afraid it'll fly away if they do. Everyone's like that.
A red lantern floated at the center. Inside, a flame fluttered like a bird in an iron cage. Its edges were dark red.
“So it's you. The owner of my room.” A low, hoarse woman's voice came from the lantern.
Are you... Lian Zhen?
“Some call me that. Others call me Prison. You've learned to cage your fire.”
Yes. Someone gets hurt when I shout.
“Good. Fire that knows confinement doesn't burn others. But remember: fire only confined will rot.”
(Rotting fire. What does that mean?)
“Fire remains fire in hands that know when to use it. When that time comes, don't hesitate.”
How do I know when?
“Watch who gets hurt. When someone is hurt not by your fire, but by your silence.”
Then a mirror cracked. Black water seeped through, running down the frame to the floor.
Black again. Why, when this is my room?
The three directions. Your room at Yin, Work at Wu, Money at Xu. They form a triangle. Blacken one point, and the whole triangle tilts.
Plain words, con artist!
Fire next door fills our room with smoke, too.
Say that first.
Black water crawled toward the lantern. The flame curled inward. Layers of red light went dark, one after another.
“Child. The Wu room. My sibling star is crying there. The Metal star.”
Wu Qu?
“The black thing clings to that star and eats its Metal. Once it has eaten it all, it will seek something that resembles Metal.”
Yeoni turned. Neo stood before a mirror. In the reflection, the stain reached his elbow. In reality, it was still below the wrist.
Neo. Your hand in the mirror. It's blacker.
Mirrors sometimes show what comes next. Then it's still ahead.
Don't say still!
Hurting Officer's fire surged to Yeoni's throat. They clenched their teeth and swallowed it. At that moment, Neo's right hand twitched.
...Sorry. I shouldn't shout.
It's fine. That much only tickles.
Inside the lantern, Lian Zhen seemed about to speak, then stopped. That silence felt strangely heavy to Yeoni.
Outside, the palace square was unsettled. Gray-faced star people walked in a line toward somewhere, carrying unlit lanterns.
Where is everyone going?
Toward Wu. The Work room.
Yundal's gloved right hand pulled that way on its own. Something beneath it sucked in air. With his left hand, he gripped his right wrist tightly.
Urgh... Happens when Black Moon's close. The hole knows first.
Yundal, your hand.
I'm fine. Act hurt in front of customers, and sales drop.
That's my line.
Learned it from you, Mr. Cat.
Then a metallic voice rang from the colonnade's end, accompanied by a hammer striking a judgment bench.
“Judgment. All who enter this sky's Work room, all who sing, all who laugh: everything confiscated.”
Moka dropped his skewer. Metal clanged against stone. His whiskers trembled.
Moka? What's wrong?
...That voice. I know it. Since before it became a crow.
The market's star lamps went out one by one. The star people folded their tents and left. Only one charcoal fire remained in Yundal's tent.
Moka wasn't grilling. He simply held a metal skewer and watched the coals. His whiskers still trembled now and then.
Moka. That voice earlier. Who was it?
A kid used to sing on the festival island. Museong. Huge voice. Terrible at keeping time.
Couldn't sing?
Terrible. But he looked happy. Always closed his eyes onstage. Said looking at the audience made him nervous.
A spark jumped from the coals. Moka pressed it out with the skewer's tip. His grip tightened.
One year, at the sunrise concert, his voice cracked. First line. Really loudly.
And?
Everyone laughed. From the next day, he was gone. A few years later, the crow came. Saying anyone who sings gets mocked.
Moka stopped. His face held something more, swallowed back. Yeoni didn't ask. It was a face that would speak someday without being asked.
You said a boy's face showed beneath the crow mask on the Island of Expression. If that boy guards a gate here, there must be a reason.
Black Moon brought him, probably. Said it would collect his feathers. Even his remaining song.
That damned eclipse. Why keep taking other people's songs?
A low breath came from beyond the coals. Neo leaned against a tent pole with his eyes closed. His right arm was black to the elbow.
Neo. It's farther up than before.
Said I'd tell you when it spread. Telling you now. It spread.
How can you say it so calmly?!
Yundal reopened the chart on the table. The Wu space was blacker than before. Black energy stretched into its neighbor like thread.
Obstruction Transformation can't be erased. It's a label attached by your birth year. As long as you were born in an Im year, Obstruction attaching to Wu Qu is fixed.
Then there's no way?
Can't erase it doesn't mean no way. Obstruction resembles a debt. A stagnant place where something owed was never received. Black Moon uses that place like a straw.
(Debt. Uncollected. Just like the words she always used.)
To pull out the straw, we first need to see what's stuck inside that room. The Wu room. We have to enter the Career Palace.
I'll go.
No. That's where it eats Metal. You're the last person who should go.
That's why I have to. Wu Qu is a Metal star. I'm the one that door can respond to.
...True. The Career Palace door only responds to Metal. And Mr. Cat is the only Metal in your chart.
Tell me things like that beforehand!
I just did. Must have caught Mr. Cat's habits.
Yeoni bit their lip. They wanted to shout at the black space, at Neo enduring with that calm face, at the eclipse calling them a vessel.
(Hold it in. Shout, and Neo gets hurt. But only holding it in makes fire rot.)
Then together. You absolutely don't go alone. That's the condition.
Negotiating now, too.
Graduate of the island that sold time.
The way to the Wu gate lay at the palace's southern edge. The sky darkened as they went. Stars had gone out one by one, as though drowned in black water.
Gray-faced star people lined up. At the line's end stood a high judgment bench. Something in a black cloak sat atop it.
Next.
The person at the front offered a lantern. The figure struck its hammer. Light drew from the lantern like thread and streamed through the door behind the bench.
Confiscated. Crime: laughing.
Taking their light for laughing?
Shh. Behind the bench is the Career Palace. All the stolen light goes there. To Wu Qu.
The crow. The same black mask and cloak from the Island of Expression. But one feather at its chest was unusually black. Like charcoal. Like ink.
(That feather. Same color as the black thing clinging to Wu Qu on the chart.)
Look. Blackness runs from that feather into the door.
Moka was right. An ink-like thread streamed from the chest feather into the doorway. It pulsed as though alive.
That's the straw. The root of Obstruction Transformation. The crow holds Black Moon's straw planted in this sky.
Yundal proposed a plan. Disguise themselves as gray faces and join the line. He removed his glove and offered his right hand to Yeoni.
I'll draw in your light briefly. Your face will turn gray. I'll return it once we're through.
But that hurts your hand.
It does. I'll put it on your tab.
A black hole sat at the palm's center. The surrounding flesh cracked like a broken vessel. Wider than when Yeoni first saw it.
The hole inhaled. Warmth drained from Yeoni's cheeks. They knew without a mirror. Their face had turned ash gray.
...Urgh. Your light is hotter than I expected.
Me too. Hurry.
Mr. Otter's expression is already gray.
You con artist!
Moka disguised himself in gray, too. But Neo's Metal could not be concealed. He would hide behind a pillar beside the line and wait for the door to open.
(Gray face. So this is what the people on the Island of Expression felt. Nothing seems like it would taste good.)
The line shortened. The bench drew near. Yeoni's turn. They offered empty hands instead of a lantern.
Your lantern.
Don't have one. Never did.
No light, nothing to confiscate. Pass.
Yeoni passed the bench. Next, Moka. He lowered his gray face. But...
His tail tapped the floor. Tap, tap. A rhythm. Unconsciously. The beat he always hummed by the charcoal.
...That rhythm just now.
No rhythm. My tail just does that.
Lies. Confiscated.
The hammer rose. At that moment, the door behind the bench rattled. A metallic sound came through the crack. It was trying to open on its own, toward the pillar's shadow.
The door reacted to Mr. Cat's Metal! Now!
Neo ran from the shadows, vaulted over the bench, and touched the door. As it opened, Yeoni, Moka, and Yundal rushed after him.
Intruders! Metal! Metal has entered!
The Career Palace resembled an iron temple. Walls and pillars, all metal. But rusted. Black rust. Ash-gray lanterns lay piled like mountains on the floor.
Two great stars floated at the center. One shone heavily in earthy light. The other gleamed like metal, its whole body bound in black thread.
Tian Fu and Wu Qu. The storehouse star and the Metal general. Both are normally incredibly bright.
Wu Qu is tied up. Those threads came from the crow's feather.
The bound star groaned, a low cry edged with metal. Neo caught his breath. The same sound came from inside his body.
“...A child of Metal. Don't come. These threads eat Metal.”
I knew when I came. Do I cut them?
“Cut them, and they grow again. Uproot them. Their root is planted in the chest of the child on that judgment bench.”
With fingertip blades, Neo severed five threads. The cut ends twisted like snakes and sprang at his arm.
Neo!
Black threads climbed his wrist, past the elbow, to shoulder and neck. Ash gray spread to the ends of his silver hair.
Ghh...!
Mr. Cat, stop! The more Metal cuts, the more Obstruction moves into Metal!
Yundal extended his right hand. The hole began drawing in threads. Several vanished inside. By that same amount, cracks along the hole's rim spread toward his wrist.
Yundal, stop! Your hand is splitting!
Fine. Still only the wrist.
What's wrong with all of you?! Why do you all only say you're fine?!
Yeoni's voice struck the iron walls and rang. Hurting Officer's fire flared. And Yeoni saw Neo flinch.
...Sorry. Shouted again.
No. That didn't even tickle.
A lie. More gray had spread over Neo's neck. Instead of speaking, Yeoni clenched their fists. Nails dug into palms.
(Speak, and he hurts. Hold it in, and everyone hurts alone. What am I supposed to do?)
The door slammed behind them. Wings beat. The figure from the judgment bench had entered.
Metal walks in of its own accord. Saves me the trouble of a trial.
Judgment. This Metal is bound to Obstruction. At noon in three days, it will be erased from this sky.
By what right?! Who are you to erase someone else's name?!
A name invites ridicule. Erase it, and nobody laughs. That is mercy.
The crow raised its hammer. But its hand shook. Whenever the black feather pulsed, its shoulders flinched.
(It hurts. That feather's eating the crow, too.)
Then Moka stepped forward. The gray had left his face. Not because Yundal returned his light. Moka had shaken it off himself.
Hey.
Otter. Confiscated for the crime of rhythm.
You know that rhythm, too. The one we practiced behind the sunrise stage.
Moka's tail tapped the floor. Tap, tap, tap. A pause, then tap.
The hammer fell from the crow's hand. Its impact on the iron floor echoed for a long time.
...How do you know that rhythm?
Museong. It's you.

episodes.title: The Owner of the Black Feather
episodes.tag: Episode 32 · The Owner of the Black Feather

beats.t: The iron-walled room fell silent. Only the black threads binding Wu Qu stirred, pulsing like a heartbeat.
I know no one named Museong. I am the keeper of the Career gate.
Liar. You scrape the floor with your right big toe before you answer. You did it every time you went onstage.
The crow's claw stopped dead against the floor. It had been just about to scrape the iron.
(It really was about to. Moka remembered even that.)
The otter's memories are subject to confiscation. The crime of laughter, the crime of rhythm, and the crime of remembering.
Then take them all. But take off your mask first.
The black feather in the crow's chest gave a violent throb. The crow clutched its chest. Its wingtips shivered.
The feather is resisting. Hearing his name seems to shake its roots.
Keep calling his name, Mr. Otter. Not loudly. Just clearly.
Museong.
A hairline crack crossed the mask, running from forehead to chin.
Museong. The day after the sunrise concert, I went to your house. I couldn't knock.
The mask split and fell. It struck the iron floor in two pieces. The cloak's collar slid down.
Underneath was a boy's face. About Yeoni's age, perhaps a little younger. Dark hollows lay beneath his eyes. He looked as though he hadn't slept in a long time.
...I know you didn't knock. I saw you through the window. You stood there for ages, then left.
You should have come out.
I thought you might laugh again if I did.
Moka's tail slumped to the floor. The tail that always kept time made no sound.
Years earlier, on the Island of Expression. The dawn stage at the Sunrise Festival. Before the sun had stopped at noon, when the far edge of the sea was just turning red.
A boy stood onstage with his eyes closed. The audience was packed. He always sang with his eyes closed because looking at the crowd made him nervous.
Rise, sun. Today's first song is for you.
The drum sounded. The boy took a deep breath. And on the very first line, his voice cracked. Like a rooster crowing. Loud enough to carry to the farthest edge of the dawn sea.
Laughter burst from the front row. One person laughed, then the next. It spread backward like a wave.
A small otter sat in the middle of the front row, holding a skewer among his friends. He was laughing too.
The boy opened his eyes. For the first time since stepping onto the stage, he looked at the audience. Laughing faces. And among them, a familiar otter's face.
The boy sang to the final line, his voice still cracked. Then he never went onstage again.
...I laughed too. Right in the front.
Moka.
All my friends were laughing. Wouldn't it have been weird if I didn't? So I laughed. One second. No, maybe two.
Three seconds.
Right. Three. You counted.
Moka set down his skewer. The metal skewer he never let out of his hand. Then he looked straight at the boy.
I'm sorry. For those three seconds. I've wanted to make up for them ever since. I didn't know how, so all I did was grill skewers.
(The tune Moka always hummed over the coals. It was this boy's song.)
Museong's lips trembled. He tried to say something. But the feather in his chest moved first. The black threads jerked tight.
Ghh...!
A low, cold voice seeped from the feather. It wasn't the boy's voice.
An apology for three seconds, to repay years of silence? Otter, your price is wrong.
Black Moon!
Ask the boy what I promised when I gave him the feather.
The night of the sunrise concert. A seaside hill at the edge of the island. The boy sat alone, his throat hoarse.
I wish I'd never sung at all.
Something settled through the sound of the waves. A single black feather. Though there was no wind, it landed precisely on the boy's knees.
I will make sure your voice never cracks again.
...Really?
Simply remove every voice that could crack. Yours, and everyone else's. If no one sings, no one can mock you.
The boy pushed the feather into his chest. Warmth spread instead of pain. He felt as though no one would recognize him anymore. His hunched shoulders relaxed.
That night, the boy's voice entered the feather. From the following day, the island's songs began disappearing one by one.
First, a market seller's bargaining song. Then a hum at the washing place. Then the children's skipping songs. Every vanished song went to the same place: the black feather in the boy's chest.
The more songs the feather ate, the larger it grew. Black feathers sprouted on the boy's arms. Wings emerged from his back. One morning, a crow stood in his mirror.
Well done. Now there is no one left to mock you. No one sings anymore.
...Then why is it so quiet? So quiet it hurts my ears?
That is peace.
Museong stopped there and lowered his head. No one spoke. Only the sound of rust falling from the iron walls remained.
That's why you banned singing on the Island of Expression. The feather wanted it, not you.
No. I wanted it too. At first, I really liked it. An island where nobody laughed. I made that.
But laughter wasn't the only thing that disappeared. The applause went too. Because no one sang.
The hands of the people who laughed probably clapped too. Can you cut out only the memories that hurt?
(His own arm is like that, and he's still worrying about the boy first.)
The cat mister is right. By the time I realized it, the feather had already put down roots in my throat.
He called you mister.
...This is not the moment.
Museong sank to his knees. Threads from the feather coiled around his neck. Every breath made a metallic sound.
I understand now. That feather is his throat. His breath, his voice—everything is inside it.
Then if we pull it out...
His breath comes out with it. He dies. Drawing it into my Void would have the same result.
But if we leave it, Wu Qu will be erased. At noon in three days.
That means you'll be erased too!
Neo didn't answer. The gray spreading to his neck rippled with each breath. A metallic rasp mingled with the end of every inhalation.
Pull it out.
What?
Pull it out. Your cat will live. Wu Qu will too. All the confiscated light will return.
I ended on that hill years ago anyway. The feather is only breathing for me now.
Don't talk nonsense!
Otter. You just apologized. That's enough. It really is.
Yeoni looked at Neo, then Museong. Their breathing made the same sound. Metal. The sound of something strangling them.
(Throw one away to save the other. Black Moon's favorite arithmetic.)
Yeoni. Don't worry about me. You make the decision.
(A decision. Lian Zhen said fire rots if you only cage it. That my silence can hurt people.)
Yeoni had been holding their fire back all this time. Shouting hurt Neo. But while they held it in, everyone was lining up to pay the price alone.
I'm not pulling it out.
Then the cat will...
The cat won't be erased. Neither will Wu Qu. And you won't die. All three.
Such greed, vessel. The scales do not tip that way.
Fire rose in Yeoni's chest. This time it didn't explode. It was small and steady, no larger than a lantern flame.
Then I won't use your scales. They always tip toward you.
Yeoni looked at Neo. He hadn't flinched. The gray hadn't spread any farther either. Their eyes met for a moment. There might be another way.
...It doesn't hurt.
(Because I spoke instead of shouting? Because I lit it instead of making it explode?)
We neither pull it out nor erase anything. That leaves one option.
We change it. The Obstruction.
Obstruction Transformation into Prosperity Transformation. Turn a blocked place into one that flows. It works in theory. Though no one has tried it.
'In theory' is the scariest phrase there is.
True. Every compatibility reading works in theory too.
(They said Obstruction was like a debt. A place that stagnates because it never received what it was owed.)
What Museong never received. I think I know what it is.
Everyone looked at Yeoni, even Museong. Yeoni gently nudged Moka's back.
Applause. What he didn't get onstage that day.
...I don't need applause. That couldn't possibly remove the feather.
No, it makes sense. If Obstruction marks something unreceived, receiving it could release the blockage. But it has to be real. Pity applause doesn't enter the ledger.
Real applause. How do we do that?
You always hummed over the coals. I'm the only one who's heard that song all the way through. It was pretty good.
You heard it? Since when?
The first day. Your rapping was awful, but that song was good.
Moka looked at Museong for a long time. Then he tapped the floor once with his tail. Tap.
At that moment, the entire room shook. Rust rained from the iron walls. A bell rang beyond the ceiling. Once. Twice.
Three days is too long. Noon is now.
He's moved the time forward! Wu Qu is starting to be erased!
Lines of light went out one by one in the bound star. Neo fell to his knees. The bell rang a third time. When the twelfth bell rang, it would be noon.

episodes.title: Returning the Swallowed Songs
episodes.tag: Episode 32 Side Story · Returning the Swallowed Songs

beats.t: The fourth bell rang. Another line of Wu Qu's light went dark. Eight tolls remained until the twelfth.
You know I can't sing.
I know. You can't rap either.
Why bring that up now?!
Because everyone here already knows what you're bad at. That's why it's okay.
The fifth bell rang. Neo dropped to one knee and braced a hand on the floor. The gray had reached beneath his chin.
Hurry. I can't promise the rhythm, but I can add a low note.
I know twelve compatibility songs. All their lyrics are weird.
...What are you doing? Stop. It's ridiculous.
(It is. That's the idea. This time, the laughter won't be aimed at you.)
Yeoni cleared their throat. Even at karaoke, they were always on tambourine duty. But today there was no tambourine. Only their voice.
Ridiculous is fine. This time we'll be the ridiculous ones. You just listen.
Moka drew a breath. His tail tapped the floor. Tap, tap, tap. A pause, then tap.
Then came the first line. Moka's voice cracked. Like a rooster crowing. Very loudly.
Yeoni burst out laughing. But they sang along through their laughter. They didn't know the words, so they followed the tune. They got that wrong too.
Ha ha. You're both a semitone flat.
Yundal joined in, laughing. He added strange lyrics: if the Four Pillars matched, everything matched; if they didn't, it was half price.
Neo sustained a low note. The Metal energy in his voice resonated through the iron walls. He was half a beat late.
It was a mess. They sounded like four people singing four different songs. But the tail's rhythm never faltered. Tap, tap, tap. A pause, then tap.
Everyone's laughing. While they're singing.
(Yes. We're laughing now. Without laughing at anyone.)
Something spilled from Museong's eyes. He almost closed them, as he had onstage. Then he didn't. He watched the smiling faces until the end.
The sixth bell drowned in the song. No one heard it.
The song ended. Or rather, everyone stopped because they were out of breath. Moka leaned on his knees, panting.
Yeoni clapped. Moka and Yundal followed. Neo brought his trembling palms together too. His slightly delayed claps found their way into the rhythm.
The applause passed beyond the stage and gathered beneath it. The kneeling boy lifted his head toward the sound.
This is for that day. Late, huh? Years late. Sorry.
...But I didn't sing.
You did. You sang every last line that day. With your cracked voice. This applause is for the person who sang to the end.
The black feather in Museong's chest trembled. Its color changed from the tip downward: ink black to gray, gray to warm gold.
Prosperity Transformation. It really worked. Obstruction has turned to Prosperity.
The black threads stretching from the feather turned gold too. They no longer constricted Wu Qu. Instead, they poured light into the star.
The bound star breathed. Iron gray turned silver again. Black rust peeled from the walls like scales.
“...Thank you. What was blocked now flows. Metal was always a vessel for what flows.”
The gray receded from Neo's neck, past his shoulder and elbow, below his wrist. Only a coin-sized black stain remained on his fingertips.
I'll carry what's left. It isn't a debt to pass on to Wu Qu.
There you go again. You're telling me everything later.
I promised.
The gray lanterns piled in the corner lit one by one. Their light streamed through the door to their rightful owners.
The seventh bell rang. But the sound had changed. It spread clear and bright instead of clanging against metal. This bell wasn't counting down to noon. It announced an open door.
(Noon never came. The time Black Moon dragged forward has come loose.)
Yeoni crouched beside Neo and touched the remaining black stain. It was cold, like a piece of metal.
Earlier. When I spoke. Did it really not hurt?
It didn't. Your fire takes a different shape when you speak than when you shout.
(The shape of fire. Fire that explodes, and fire you light.)
Today, you lit it. So everyone sang beside that fire.
...Say things like that when your hand has healed.
Neo patted Yeoni's shoulder lightly. Once again, he was half a beat late.
In the corridor back to the market, Yundal slowed down. He held his gloved right hand against his chest.
Yundal. Your hand.
I swallowed rather a lot of thread earlier. The hole has spread past my wrist.
A black crack crept above his wrist from the edge of the glove, like a fine line of ink.
I'm fine. With Wu Qu freed, your chart should be clearer too, my lady. I've protected my business capital.
There it is again. Nobody's allowed to say they're fine anymore. From now on, saying it costs a fine.
How much?
Ten skewers. Pay Moka.
The market's star lamps glowed again. Color returned to the gray cheeks of the star people. Someone hummed while bargaining.
A little star child came running from the end of the corridor. At the sight of Museong, the child hesitated, then offered a palm-sized lantern. The very lantern confiscated at the judgment stand.
For me? But I'm the one who took it.
Instead of answering, the child pressed the lantern into Museong's hand and ran off. A few steps later, the child turned and stuck out a tongue.
Was that forgiveness or teasing?
Both. That's how we do it on the island.
Ever since the feather turned gold, my wings won't grow. I'm just a person.
Come to the island. They're bringing back the sunrise stage this year. I'll squeeze you in beside my grill.
What if my voice cracks again?
Then we'll laugh again. And clap again. That's what a stage is.
Museong laughed. His voice was hoarse, but it was unmistakably laughter.
There's one thing I should tell you. The voice that gave me the feather used to say something a lot. That there's a vessel in the Wealth room.
A vessel.
The Xu room. No star person who went in ever came back. And I heard chains dragging in there. Every time it rained.
(Chains. Rain. ...Seo Hanbi.)
The next morning, in the corridor at the edge of the market, Museong tucked a golden feather behind Moka's ear. Moka left it there.
See you at the sunrise stage. I'll sing with my eyes open this time.
You'll still get the notes wrong.
Yeah. So sit in the front row. Laugh louder than anyone.
Museong descended the cloud steps beneath the corridor. A few steps down, he turned and waved broadly. His voice was still hoarse.
That looks good behind your ear.
Shut up. I put it there because of the wind.
There isn't any wind.
There will be later. I'm ready in advance.
By that logic, you should carry an open umbrella before it rains.
Whoa, Neo made a joke. That was a joke, right?
Just an observation.
You're becoming quite talkative, Mr. Cat. An excellent sign for compatibility.
Enough about compatibility.
Yundal unfolded the natal chart. The Wu sector had cleared. But fine diagonal lines crossed the Xu sector like rain.
Xu. The Wealth Palace. The room of wealth. It's a little special in your chart, my lady. Your Body Palace is here.
Body Palace?
If the Life Palace is the face you're born with, the Body Palace is the room your body occupies. Your body lives in the room of wealth.
My body's a wallet?
Metaphorically. A place to hold what you receive. And a place to let it flow onward.
(A place to hold things. Museong said there was a vessel in the Wealth room.)
Yeoni glanced at their palm without thinking. Nothing was there. Yet a slender trail of rainwater seemed to pass between its lines.
Reaching the Xu gate at the palace's northwestern edge meant crossing a cloud valley. Rain began the moment they arrived at the valley.
This rain. It smells different.
(I know. It's the smell from the hallway on clear days.)
A sheet of paper clung to a wet rock. Yeoni peeled it off. Half the writing remained, blurred by rain.
[ Ledger · Eulhae Yeoni · Outstanding: 2 ]
A ledger page. Seo Hanbi's.
A few steps farther, another sheet. Then another. The pages lay scattered along the path, as though someone had dropped them deliberately.
She left a trail. While being dragged away.
Dragged away?
The same entry on every page. Outstanding: two. She tore out only your entries.
(There must have been so many others. Why mine?)
She's showing the way. Perhaps she wants us to find her. Or perhaps it's a warning to stay away.
I don't care which. We're following the pages.
Yeoni picked up the wet sheets one by one and slipped them into their notebook. The paper was cold. Rainwater soaked their fingertips.
As though in answer, a sound rose from below: chains scraping rock. Something heavy being dragged.
A black shape appeared in the mist below the valley. A huge beast with a striped back. Black chains wrapped its neck and forelegs.
...The tiger.
Hands gripped the ends of the chains. Dozens of black hands. They were dragging the tiger deeper into the mist.
Water pooled in every pawprint. A ledger page dropped onto each pool.
Seo Hanbi!
The tiger turned its head. Its red eyes found Yeoni through the mist. It moved its mouth without making a sound.
Don't come.
The hands jerked the chains. The tiger vanished into the mist. Only the rattling chains echoed for a long time.
Yeoni tried to leap into the valley, but Neo blocked the way. They grabbed his collar. He didn't retreat, but neither did he seize their wrist.
Move! They're dragging her away!
We can't see beneath the mist. If you fall too, I can't save you. Let's find another way.
She saved me. At the bus stop. In the hallway. I haven't repaid her even once.
Fire entered Yeoni's voice. Neo clenched his teeth. It hurt, but he didn't move away. He held his ground until Yeoni caught their breath.
I'll give you the chance to repay her. But we need to know the way. Those hands came from the Xu room.
Mr. Cat is right. The room with the vessel. Once we're there, we'll learn why she's being dragged away.
Beyond the Xu gate stood a vast hall. Rain poured through an opening in its rounded roof. Shallow pools covered the floor like mirrors.
An empty throne stood on a dais at the back. A violet star floated above it, shedding cool, clear light.
Zi Wei. Sovereign of the stars. In your chart, it holds Authority Transformation: the power to decide.
Beside the throne stood a small star that seemed to hold a seal. In a corner, a mass of mist crouched, swelling occasionally as though breathing.
The star with the seal is Tian Xiang. The mist in the corner is Tuo Luo, the star that drags things along. It delays things and holds you back.
(The star that drags. So the chains were coming from here.)
“You've come, child of Eul. I have waited long. Though there is nowhere for you to sit.”
Star, a tiger was dragged away earlier. Do you know where she went?
“I do. But first there is something you must see. At your feet.”
In the middle of the pool beneath the dais stood a huge vessel. Earth-colored and as tall as a person. Its interior was deep and dark.
Rain fell into it, but it never filled. Every drop vanished, as though it had no bottom.
“This is you. The vines of Eul Wood hold even the breath of others. That is why Black Moon calls you a vessel.”
What do you mean, hold?
“Black Moon has no body. Even after devouring the sky, it has nowhere to dwell. So it seeks something to contain it. An empty vessel, yet one that can hold anything.”
The darkness inside the vessel swirled. Scenes appeared within it: Yeoni sharing bread. Holding an umbrella over someone. Giving their last coin to a child.
(Things I gave away. But why are they all inside the vessel?)
“You are a giver. Giving is good. But Black Moon used that. It had your fortune collected from you. Giving emptied you; collection emptied you further.”
Had it collected? By whom?
The star didn't answer. Instead, a ledger page rose from the bottom of the vessel. A ledger densely filled with collected fortune. A familiar signature stood at the end. A name like rain.
The tiger collected your fortune on Black Moon's orders. That was what emptied you. Though she must have thought she was preventing it.
Preventing it? She took all my luck, and I spent the whole spring tripping and slipping.
Yes. That's true. The harm is still harm. But who gave her that ledger is also part of the truth.
(Every day I fell. Every day my umbrella blew inside out. She was writing another line in her ledger.)
Then Seo Hanbi was, from the start...
“Deceived. She took up the ledger to protect you, and that ledger emptied you. She still does not understand the calculation.”
Only rain could be heard. Yeoni laid a hand on the vessel's rim. It was cold. And utterly empty.
Then what should I do? Stop giving? To anyone, ever again?
“No. A vessel must be empty to hold something. Emptiness is not a sin.”
“The vessel decides what it holds. Not Black Moon.”
The violet star above the throne blinked once. A single ray fell into the vessel. A small character etched itself into the bottom: 權, Authority.
(The power to decide. The Authority Transformation in my chart. I decide whether to hold something.)
Did you hear? You decide.
Yes. I heard.
(I suppose I decide whether to forgive Seo Hanbi too. But I can't decide that yet.)
Star. I have to bring her back. I've got a mountain of questions for her. I'll decide whether to forgive her after that.
“That, too, is for the vessel to decide.”
My lady, you sounded very grown-up just now.
I am a grown-up. Twenty-three.
Then a sound came from the natal chart in Yundal's hands. The sound of glass cracking. The panel of eight characters floated up by itself.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: Gyeong-Chen ]
In the Hour sector, the character Gyeong flickered on and off like someone breathing unevenly.
Gyeong. Mr. Cat's place is wavering.
“A borrowed place cannot endure forever. That cat sits in your chart on borrowed terms. The day of repayment approaches.”
Repayment? Neo. What does that mean?
Just as Neo opened his mouth, his right hand turned transparent. The black stain faded with it. Rain passed straight through his palm.
...I'm still fine.
I told you nobody's allowed to say that! That's a fine! Ten skewers!
I'll pay. Later.
Tell me now, not later. What did you borrow, and when do you have to repay it?
Neo opened his mouth, then closed it. Color slowly returned to his hand. Yeoni didn't look away from it.
Outside the hall, the sky was moving. Twelve doors rotated slowly, the whole palace turning like a giant clock.
Hey, the sky's spinning. I'm getting motion sickness.
The palaces are becoming houses. Twelve palaces into twelve houses. The next sky is opening.
“Child of Eul. In the next sky, the stars have twelve houses. There, they call it by another name.”
It?
In the middle of the sky, a black circle appeared in the space between stars. It had the shape of a moon. But it gave no light. It swallowed light.
“The dark moon. That is what they call Black Moon there.”
Beneath the dark moon, chains sounded again, much farther away this time. Yeoni took out their notebook and added a final line: Seo Hanbi. Dragged away. Must find her.

episodes.title: The Sky of Twelve Houses
episodes.tag: Episode 34 · The Sky of Twelve Houses

beats.t: The ground beneath them rocked. Yeoni opened their eyes to a wooden deck. Beyond it, stars flowed like a river.
It was a ship. Instead of sails, great brass rings rotated in overlapping layers. Constellations were engraved on every ring.
What happened to the palace? We were just in a palace.
The palace folded itself into a ship. When the sky changes, so does the transport.
A ship? I can't handle ships. You think everyone from an island can?
Don't people from islands usually sail?
That's what makes it so unfair. Urgh.
Moka ran to the railing and tried to empty his stomach into the starry sea. Nothing came out, which only made him more miserable.
Neo sat at the bow, silver hair scattering in the wind. He had tucked his right hand inside his left sleeve.
Neo. Let me see your hand.
Both my feet are still attached. You mean my hand, right?
It went transparent earlier. I saw.
It's white now. If you want to see it, I'll show you later.
(Later. Always later. I'm writing that down.)
Yeoni opened their notebook. Seo Hanbi. Dragged away. Must find her. Above that, they added: Neo's hand. Must see it later.
A round table stood in the middle of the deck. A circle glowed beneath its glass top, divided into twelve slices.
This is the natal chart of this sky. In astrology, it's called a birth chart.
Looks like a pizza.
Exactly. A twelve-slice pizza. Each slice is called a house. Twelve rooms of life.
Yundal touched the circle's leftmost edge with a gloved finger. The light was brightest there.
This is the threshold of the first house. The Ascendant. The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment you were born.
Why does that matter?
Because it's the first face people see when they meet you. Like a front entrance.
A constellation rose above the threshold: a creature with pointed ears and a curled tail. The stars gathered into a little cat.
A cat... Just like Yeongnyangi.
Your Ascendant is Leo, but the stars have settled into a cat's shape. Mr. Cat is standing at your front entrance, my lady.
Neo adjusted his coat collar. He said nothing. Only the rims of his ears reddened.
And right beside it, Venus. The star of love, pressed right up against the entrance.
You may skip that commentary.
Why? This is my favorite part.
That means stop pitching compatibility readings.
They're arguing again.
Don't make me watch an argument while I'm seasick.
Yeoni looked around the circle. At the very top, in the tenth house, lay a silver dot.
The Moon. Right at the top. A placement where people easily see your feelings.
That's a bit embarrassing.
Sounds right. Everything's on your face. When you're mad, your cheeks go red first.
It's a Taurus Moon, so you dislike instability. Mealtimes, where you sleep, the same familiar people.
(The same familiar people. Is that why change scared me?)
Yundal's finger slid toward the lower part of the circle, just above the eastern threshold. The twelfth house. Only there was the glass cloudy underneath.
This is the twelfth house. The hidden room. A place for endings, burdens carried in secret, and things shut away.
Two red dots overlapped beneath the cloudy glass, flickering like flames.
Mars and Jupiter are together here. The power to fight and the power to expand, side by side in the hidden room.
So, hidden strength?
Hidden strength. Or perhaps someone hidden away.
Then a faint sound came from beneath the glass. Chains scraping the floor.
Did you hear that?
I heard it. Chains.
(Seo Hanbi. You're there.)
Before the meeting, Yeoni went to the bow. Neo leaned against the railing, gazing at the starry sea. Moka's groans drifted from a distance.
They say there's a big cat at the entrance. In my chart.
I heard.
I can tell you like that. Your ears are red.
The wind is cold. That's why I'm flushed.
The wind was blowing from the other side. Yeoni chose not to mention it and sat beside Neo.
Neo. When you first saw me, did you see my front entrance too? My first impression, I mean.
I did. You were angry, holding an umbrella that had blown inside out.
The worst.
You kept holding that inside-out umbrella until the end. That's the first image I remember.
Yeoni hugged their knees, brushing against Neo's shoulder. It was warm. Only his right hand stayed hidden inside his sleeve.
(Still won't show me his paw. But I'll leave it there for today.)
The ship suddenly listed. The brass rings screamed to a halt. One side of the sky was being erased.
A black circle passed between the constellations. Starlight vanished wherever it went, as though scooped out with a spoon.
The dark moon. Astrologers call that lightless lunar point Lilith. In this sky, that's Black Moon's name.
How many names does that thing have?
As many as the skies it has eaten.
Then it can't still be hungry. How many skies has it eaten?
It doesn't eat because it's hungry. It eats because it's empty. The kind that never fills, no matter how much it swallows.
(Never fills. A bottomless vessel. But they said that was me.)
Without realizing it, Yeoni pressed a hand against their stomach. It felt cold inside, as though something there was holding its breath.
The black circle stopped directly above the birth chart. The glass cracked. A star was plucked from the seventh house.
The seventh house. The place of partners. It's eating a companion.
Neo reached for the railing and stumbled. His right hand had turned transparent again, this time above the wrist.
Neo!
Stand back. It's after me. Not you.
A voice seeped from the black circle. Low and gentle. Colder for its gentleness.
Vessel. Your tiger is in the twelfth house.
Come and fetch her. If you do not, the chains will shorten, one by one.
She's not my tiger. But I'm coming.
Yes. That is always how you come. Carrying an umbrella.
The black circle sank beneath the starry sea. Smoke rose from the empty place in the seventh house. Part of the sky remained missing.
The ship began moving again, slowly and on a tilt. The four gathered around the table.
Let's plan. The twelfth-house door opens only with its chart owner's time. The time of birth, down to the minute.
Eight thirty. Mom said it was just after her morning drama ended.
How do you know that?
I hear it every birthday. Including the drama's ending.
Good. You can enter, my lady. Mr. Cat can too, since he occupies your chart.
What about me?
You can follow them, Moka. The door doesn't bar guests. However...
Yundal stopped. He laid his gloved right hand on the table. From the edge of the glove, a black crack crept toward his elbow.
I can't. I'm a passenger without an hour.
You can't cross the doorway because you don't have a birth hour?
In this sky, time is the key. Anyone without one is erased at the door. Little by little.
Yundal's shadow faded across the table. Yeoni rubbed their eyes. It was still faint.
Then we find it. Your birth hour.
Blue Rabbit ran off with it. Who knows where in this enormous sky?
At that instant, a cheerful bell rang alongside the ship. Ding-dong. The bell of a shop door opening.
A cloud-shaped airship pulled up close beside them. Rabbit-ear sails fluttered. A sparkling advertisement hung along its side.
Dear customers! Blue Rabbit Finance has opened a branch in this sky too!
It's that rabbit. You haven't gone under yet?
Gone under? A new sky means a new interest rate! Today's special: starlight loans!
An hourglass hung around Blue Rabbit's neck. Its sand was pale pink, the color of the sky at dawn.
My Hour of the Rabbit.
Oh, our Hour of the Rabbit customer! You haven't been erased yet. How impressive!
Put that hourglass down.
No, thank you! This is the most expensive thing in this sky. You need an hour to open doors!
Blue Rabbit waved a forepaw. The airship slid away into the star clouds, its ear-shaped sails twitching tauntingly.
After him. Right now. We're not losing him this time.
My lady. Promise me one thing. When we catch that rabbit, you must be the one to find my hour.
Me?
I can't really remember when I was born anymore.
Yundal smiled as he spoke. The edges of his smiling face blurred little by little into the starlight. Yeoni studied it for a long time, determined not to forget.
Before Yundal had finished, Moka hauled on a rigging rope. The brass rings started turning again. The ship lunged forward.
Seasickness can wait. Those rabbit ears are going on a skewer today.
Moka, you said you couldn't handle ships!
I can't. That's why I'm ending this fast!
The starry sea struck the hull in silver spray. Ahead, rabbit-ear sails appeared and vanished between clouds.
My lady. Be ready to hear my story. To find my hour, we have to walk backward.
Backward?
It's called birth-time rectification. We trace the events of a life one by one and rewind to the moment of birth.
Yeoni opened their notebook again. At the top of a fresh page, they wrote: Yundal. Time of birth. Find it backward.
The ship raced through star clouds. Far ahead, rabbit-ear sails bobbed just beyond reach.
All right. Walking backward. Yundal, start with the most recent event.
Recent? When I offered you a compatibility reading and Neo nearly grabbed me by the collar?
Not that. Something big. A day that cracked your life open.
Something big. There's the day I got the app. Three years ago, on the first day of the rainy season.
Yeoni wrote: App. Three years ago. First day of the rainy season. While they wrote, Yundal tilted his head.
Oh. What did I just say?
App. Three years ago. First day of the rainy season.
Ah, right. Thanks to your notes, my life will survive better in your notebook than in me.
His laugh sounded strangely thin. Yeoni turned the page and pressed their pen down hard.
How exactly does this birth-time rectification work?
For each event, we work out which houses the stars were passing through that day. With the right birth time, everything fits. With the wrong one, it doesn't.
Like trying keys in a lock one by one.
Exactly. And my first impression. That's the biggest key. Remember the front entrance?
First impression? Easy. Con artist.
Correct. That's what everyone says the moment they see me.
The circle beneath the glass spun. The eastern threshold flickered. Daytime hours vanished, leaving only night and dawn.
Next. Were you ever badly hurt as a child?
Hurt? Hmm. I think so.
Yundal's voice trailed off. His gloved fingers groped at the air, as though he couldn't get hold of a memory.
How strange. It's my story, but it feels like someone else's.
A low voice came from the bow. Neo spoke without turning from the starry sea.
Eleven years old. You fell from a ferry and broke your left arm. Your grandmother carried you on her back and ran ten li.
...How do you know that?
You told me on the Island of Wealth. The day you asked my birthday for the third time.
You remember all that?
When you take that much interest, how could I forget what you say?
Wow. Is that love or obsession?
Guard duty.
Yundal said nothing for a long time. Then he lowered his head. His shoulders shook once. It was impossible to tell whether he was laughing or crying.
Everyone forgets me, and of all people, Mr. Cat remembered.
I've never been good at forgetting. You'll have to find another customer support desk for complaints.
I've tried complaining to the universe. It doesn't take them.
Yeoni wrote: Eleven. Ferry. Left arm. Grandmother. Beside it, in smaller letters: Remembered by Neo.
There's one more thing. You said you were born before the rooster crowed. Your grandmother always told that story.
The circle under the glass spun again. One star slotted into the age-eleven event. Another into the first day of the rainy season. The eastern threshold narrowed.
The two hours just before dawn. Within the Hour of the Rabbit. I already knew that much. The problem is the minutes.
We need the minutes too?
That's what Blue Rabbit's contract said. The hourglass returns only if I personally state the time down to the minute. A clause added because no one was supposed to manage it.
The rabbit-ear airship was directly ahead. Moka wound a rigging rope around his paw and pulled alongside. The two ships collided with a crash.
Oh my! Unauthorized boarding means ten times the late fees!
I'll collect those fees in rabbit ears.
Paper swarmed over the airship's deck like a blizzard. Loan contracts. The signature field on each one gaped like a mouth.
Just sign for an instant starlight payout! Interest payable in memories!
The contracts tangled into a net. One sheet slapped onto Yeoni's wrist. The signature field began trying to write their name by itself.
My hand's moving on its own!
Give me your hand, my lady.
Yundal removed his glove. A black hole lay in the center of his palm. Ink streamed from the contracts into it.
The papers went blank. The signature fields closed. But the hole in Yundal's palm had widened by another handspan.
You said it grows when you use it!
The fine is ten skewers, right? Put it on Moka's tab.
Don't put it on my tab!
Moka pulled out a bundle of skewers and planted them in his charcoal tin. Acrid smoke covered the deck. Blue Rabbit sneezed.
Achoo! That's chili smoke! You're obstructing my business!
Island specialty. Makes you cry, right? That's the flavor.
The four ran through the smoke into a golden corridor inside the airship. Vault doors lined the walls. Blue Rabbit stood before the last one.
A dead end! But it won't help. Our Hour of the Rabbit customer can't state the minutes.
Article Seven. The customer, in person, in their own words, must state their birth time down to the minute. No substitutes!
He's right. I truly don't know anymore.
The edges of Yundal's face blurred again. The golden corridor's light passed him by, as though unwilling to illuminate someone who wasn't there.
(He doesn't know. No. We have all the pieces. We only have to fit them together.)
Yeoni flipped through the notebook. First day of the rainy season. Eleven, left arm. Before the rooster crowed. And first impression: con artist.
Yundal. Your grandmother said before the rooster crowed. What time did the roosters crow in your village?
What?
It's different in every village. My grandmother's rooster crowed at five thirty. So reliably she used it instead of a clock.
My grandmother too. She put the rice on when the rooster crowed. When it was cooked, the six o'clock news started.
How long did the rice take?
In an iron pot? About thirty minutes. She said I arrived before that. She laughed because I cried before the rooster did.
The stars interlocked above Yeoni's notebook instead of the glass. The rainy-season star, the age-eleven star, the before-the-rooster star. They all fit at a single point.
Then just before five thirty. Around five twenty.
The age-eleven position fits that time too. I counted.
How adorable, playing detectives! But he still has to say it himself. And he can't remember.
Yeoni held the notebook out to Yundal. Every word on that page was his story. He studied the paper for a long time.
You don't have to remember. You can read it. This is yours, Yundal. I only wrote it down.
I'm reading my own life, written by someone else.
Not just someone else. A companion.
Yundal drew a breath and read. First day of the rainy season. Ferry. Left arm. Grandmother. Rooster. His voice shook at the final line.
Five twenty in the morning. The child who cried before the rooster. That's me.
The hourglass around Blue Rabbit's neck cracked. Pale pink sand poured out. It never touched the floor, streaming through the air into Yundal's palm.
No! That's the most valuable thing I have!
The edges of Yundal's face sharpened. At last, the golden corridor's light shone on him. Moka silently gave him a thumbs-up.
Your face is clear, my lady. Or am I the one who's clear?
Both.
Then the entire airship lurched. Darkness filled the windows. The dark moon hung directly overhead.
Black hands descended from the sky, their fingers long. They passed Yeoni and reached straight for Blue Rabbit.
A hand that has lost the Hour of the Rabbit is useless. You called yourself the weakest. How honest.
C-Chairman! I still have three branches! And performance reports!
Collect him.
A black hand seized Blue Rabbit's vest. Glittering business cards crumbled between its fingers. His feet lifted from the floor.
Wait. Let go!
Yeoni moved before they could think. They grabbed Blue Rabbit's forepaw and pulled. Moka seized Yeoni around the waist.
Are you crazy? He's a loan shark!
I know! I still don't want him eaten!
Neo cut through the air with his transparent hand. Two black fingers snapped off. The vest stayed in the enemy's grasp; Blue Rabbit tumbled to the floor.
Without his vest, Blue Rabbit was smaller than expected. Just an ordinary rabbit with one folded ear.
...Dear customer. I'll make this one interest-free. Just this once.
Is that how you say thank you?
The weakest always survives longest! Closing-down sale in the next sky!
Blue Rabbit jumped into a lifeboat. A paper sign reading CLOSING DOWN fluttered at its stern. He vanished into the star clouds in an instant.
Back on their ship, Yundal sank onto the deck and opened his right hand. Pale pink sand glittered in the lines of his palm.
But the hole at its center remained. It hadn't shrunk at all. The sand circled its rim, resisting being drawn inside.
We found your hour. Why won't it close?
The hour was stolen. The hole, I dug myself. Even when the thief is gone, the hole remains.
That hole will close with me. Never before me.
The dark moon slowly receded. Silence settled over the deck. Yundal pulled his glove back on, carefully, one finger at a time.
Then I'll have to follow your journey to the very end, my lady.
Don't say that with a smile. That's a fine.
I didn't say I was fine.
Dawn spread across the skyship's deck. Beneath the star clouds, a pale golden path had opened where none had been before.
Is that a road? There's a road in the sky.
A road visible only to someone who's recovered their hour. A road home.
Then are you going?
Instead of answering, Yundal raised his gloved hand. The center of the glove sagged inward.
If I go, this hand goes with me. And the people there keep forgetting me. A home where my mother meets her son for the first time, for the third time.
Then you're not going?
I'll decide after breakfast. Hungry people make expensive decisions.
That's true. As a chef, I approve.
Moka lit a small brazier on one side of the deck. He cooked porridge with dew gathered from the star clouds. It smelled simple and warm.
Oink. I mean, that smells good.
You just said oink.
I didn't.
You did. I have recorded it.
Could I get a copy of that record? For blackmail.
When did you two become such friends?!
Smiling, Yundal drew a folded sheet from his clothes. His own Four Pillars chart. New characters sat neatly in the Hour column that had been empty for so long.
It's strange seeing all eight characters filled in. Like wearing someone else's clothes, and like finally wearing clothes that fit.
So what does it say? Your fate.
Wonderful luck with women in my later years. My lady, Moka, would you happen to know your birth—
I'll tip the porridge over.
I'm joking. What it actually says is: someone who lights other people's paths and finds his own late.
That's exactly right at the moment.
Isn't it? I finally believe the saying that fortune-tellers are worst at reading their own fortunes.
You ask for everyone else's birthdays easily enough.
That's business. This is a consultation. No consultation fee.
The four sat around the brazier. Yundal cradled his bowl in both hands. Yeoni watched his hands, then took out their notebook.
Yundal. That's not your real name, is it?
Caught me. How long have you known?
Article Seven. It said you had to state your birth time yourself, but it never asked your name. Blue Rabbit already had your name.
My lady, you should have become an auditor.
Yundal means an extra month inserted into the calendar. A place outside the usual twelve months.
That's right. A month that exists and doesn't. No ancestral rites, no birthdays counted.
Perfect for someone people forget, so I chose it myself. My naming skills are the real thing too.
A brief silence followed his laugh. Charcoal cracked in the brazier. Yeoni put down their pen.
Tell me your real name someday. I'll write it down.
Even written down, it'll be forgotten. The paper will remain, but whoever reads it will wonder: whose name is this?
Then I'll keep reading it. Every time I wonder.
...You really are stubborn.
Always has been. If something tastes bad, they'll say so to the bitter end.
The sky suddenly darkened. Three black hands crawled onto the golden path, chains wrapped around every finger.
The road home lies upon my palm. Try walking it.
You came to block the road? That's low!
No. It didn't come to block the road. It came to watch me. To see whether I go.
Yundal stood and removed his glove. This time he didn't hesitate. A black vortex poured from the hole in his palm.
The three black hands were dragged toward the hole, nails scraping the deck. One, two, three. Each disappeared into it.
The hole has grown. The more of mine you eat, the more you resemble me.
Then I'll eat plenty. Leave you hungry.
Yundal dropped to his knees. Sweat beaded on his forehead. The rim of the hole had spread another finger's length toward his wrist.
Why did you use it again? You said it grows!
I've decided, my lady. I'm not going.
This hole closes only when Black Moon dies. So the quickest way is to stay beside the person heading toward Black Moon.
Then you're staying because of us.
No, because of me. Does putting it that way make you feel less guilty?
After Yeoni and Moka fell asleep in the cabin, Neo called Yundal to the bow. This time, he didn't hide his transparent hand.
One favor.
Mr. Cat asking me? The sun will rise in the west tomorrow.
If I disappear, stay beside them.
Yundal stopped smiling. Below Neo's wrist was empty space. Starlight passed straight through his hand.
Since when?
Since we reached the sky of twelve houses. No, a little before that.
Does my lady know?
They wrote it in their notebook. Neo's hand. Must see it later. I can't leave this until then.
No.
...What did you say?
Our compatibility is wrong. My lady and I. I've checked. Keep your own place, Mr. Cat.
This isn't the time for jokes.
I'm not joking. A guardian whose first thought is to disappear is dangerous. That thought opens a real door.
Neo lowered his head. The edge of his cloak stirred in the wind. Only after a long silence did he speak.
Then just this. If they forget me, remember me. I'm sorry to ask even that of you, when you've always been the forgotten one.
That, I'll accept. A contract between people who are forgotten.
After Neo returned to the cabin, Yundal remained at the bow. A faint moon hung at the edge of the sky, as though leaving a place open for him.
Grandmother. I found my hour. They say I cried before the rooster.
No one answered. Yundal laid his gloved hand over his chest. The hole in his palm seemed to swallow his heartbeat bit by bit.
Not my name yet. I'll find that at the end. My lady says they'll write it down.
A small light shone through the cabin window beneath the deck. Half asleep, Yeoni hugged their notebook.
In the morning, the skyship reached the twelfth house. A door floated among the clouds, old chains wound around its frame.
My lady. Your birth time.
July 6, 2002. Eight thirty in the morning. Mom remembered because her morning drama had just finished.
The number display above the door clicked around. Eight thirty. The chains loosened and fell. The door swung inward.
Inside stretched an endless room of looms. Threads descended from the ceiling and continued beneath the floor. Tiny scenes formed along every thread.
What's this now? A knitting factory?
The twelfth house is the room of endings and hidden things. Here hang the endings of lives other than this one.
Yeoni touched a nearby thread. A scene flashed up: a rainy bus stop. One umbrella. Two pairs of wet sneakers.
Is that me?
Let go. Right now.
At the urgency in Neo's voice, Yeoni released the thread. The scene vanished. Only a rain-soaked chill remained on their fingertips.
(Why is Neo so frightened? Like someone who knows that bus stop.)
Yundal walked slowly between the threads. Near the ceiling, a red star and a blue star floated side by side. Their descending threads twisted into one thick cord.
The two stars in your twelfth house. Mars, the fighting star. Jupiter, the giving star.
Fighting and giving in the same room?
That's why this house is difficult. Hidden enemies are here, and hidden help too. You have to go all the way to the end to know which is which.
Decide before the end and you're usually wrong.
Moka furtively touched another thread. A scene appeared: an unfamiliar kitchen, a steaming pot, someone's laughter. He snatched his paw away.
Didn't see anything. Really. No cooking scenes or anything.
I didn't say a word.
...Guess I cooked in another life too. Never ends.
Deep in the room came the sound of dragging chains, mixed with wet footsteps. Something heavy was being dragged downward.
That way. The chains.
Look at the floor. All the threads go down. Beneath the twelfth house is another sky.
A sky inhabited by twenty-seven moons. The chains are being dragged there.
Then is that the sound we've been following?
No one answered. Instead, the smell of rainwater rose between gaps in the floor. A smell that didn't belong aboard a skyship on a clear day.
Yeoni pressed their stomach. It felt empty inside, like a vessel waiting to be filled.
Follow, vessel. The spring you lost lies below.
I decide my own spring.
The voice didn't answer. Instead, every thread in the floor pulled taut. Something below was tugging on them.
If we go down, can we come back?
Everyone who went down came back. As far as I know. Admittedly, I don't know much.
I'll lead. Yeoni, stay behind me.
No. Beside you.
Neo looked at Yeoni for a moment, then stepped aside. Light from the threads leaked through his transparent fingers.
Yeoni jotted in their notebook: Twelfth house. Below. Chains. Smell of rain. Then they drew a line and added one more thing: Go down together.

episodes.title: The Soaked Ledger
episodes.tag: Episode 36 Side Story · The Soaked Ledger

beats.t: In the lowest chamber of the twelfth house, where the loom threads ended, a black tiger lay prone. A chain dangled from the golden ring around its neck.
Every so often, the chain pulled. Each time, the tiger slid another handspan downward. Its claws scored long marks in the floor.
A little longer. Just hold on a little longer.
Even the tiger didn't know whom it was speaking to. Beneath its forepaws lay a ledger, its cover drenched.
The ledger opened by itself. An unfamiliar page lay among familiar entries. The handwriting was unmistakably its own. Only when it had written it was missing from memory.
When did I write this?
The first line held a date. Spring. The numbers had blurred beyond reading. Beneath them, one line: Bus stop. Rain. Half an umbrella.
A bus stop. That child offered an umbrella at a bus stop last time too. Near our apartments, on that rainy day.
The tiger shook its head. The same scene overlapped twice: one from this life, one it didn't remember. They looked exactly alike.
The ledger doesn't lie. That was the only thing I was proud of.
As it read, the rain grew louder. The ledger became a window. Beyond it stood an old bus stop.
A girl in a school uniform stood drenched, water dripping from her hair. Beside her, another girl tilted half an umbrella over her.
It's her.
The girl with the umbrella smiled. Let's share. Half each. She didn't care that her own shoulder was getting wet.
The drenched girl couldn't speak. In all her memory, that was the only day someone had offered her something without wanting anything back.
I know her. I can't remember her name. But I know her.
The bus arrived, and they boarded together. The girl with the umbrella took a packet of gummies from her bag and handed over half. Without counting. Without thinking.
The drenched girl held the gummies for a long time without eating them. They were too precious. She didn't know how to repay what she'd received.
I tried to repay her. The next day, I bought an umbrella and brought it. She only laughed. Said she already had one.
A tiny doodle marked the ledger's corner: two clumsy umbrellas. Beside them were the erased remains of Received and To Repay.
The ledger turned. Seasons passed. The two girls waited for the bus together every day. The umbrella was always half each.
The drenched girl began working part-time. A convenience store, dawn leaflet rounds, a restaurant on weekends. She saved the money in an envelope. On the front she wrote: Go to the sea together.
The sea. Yes, we said we'd go to the sea. She'd never seen it before.
The envelope grew thicker. Whenever the girl with the umbrella heard about it, she clapped. I'll save too. Half each.
Half each. She always said that. The umbrella, the gummies, the sea. She set aside my share before counting her own.
The tiger read those words aloud. Its throat tightened afterward, as though these weren't words in a ledger but words it had heard from someone long ago.
Why would someone like that act that way, just that one day?
The rain intensified as though answering. Water spilled over the bus-stop roof. The tiger was afraid to turn the page. Still, it pushed the paper with a paw.
Then the final page. The same bus stop. The same girl holding an umbrella. But she wasn't smiling. She didn't offer the umbrella.
She snatched something from the drenched girl's hand: the envelope holding money saved for so long. Then she turned away.
