Yes. This is it. This is what I remember. The day she abandoned me.
But the picture in the ledger shuddered once. Behind the departing girl's eyes, a round shadow appeared. Like a black moon covering the sun.
...What was that just now?
It tried to look again. The picture had already blurred, as though rainwater had chosen that entry alone to erase.
She was strange that day. She didn't call my name. She had a nickname she always used.
The tiger pressed the ledger with a forepaw, afraid to extend its claws in case the wet paper tore. It stared at that entry for a long time.
If it wasn't her. No, I can't think that. Then everything I've done...
It couldn't finish. The ring around its neck tightened once, cutting off its breath. As though ordering it to stop thinking.
Close the old ledger. Wet paper lies.
Chairman. In that child's eyes just now...
What you saw was rain. Rain blurs everything. Like you.
The chain jerked hard. The tiger fell flat. The ledger slid from under its paws. It twisted its body and gathered the book against its chest.
Go down. In the sky of twenty-seven moons, I will give you your final task. Empty that child.
I have been. All along. But why do you grow fuller the emptier she becomes?
You have learned to count. Needlessly.
That was the only answer. The chain snapped downward. Loom threads tore apart to make a passage. Red starlight rose from below.
Even as it fell, the tiger refused to let go of the ledger. Its wet cover clung to its chest. Only the little note tucked inside retained its warmth.
Half an umbrella. If I could see it just once more, I'd know.
The wind blew upward. Below, red threads glittered like stars. Between them appeared the roof of an ancient temple. Twenty-seven moons floated above it.
I'll meet her again down there, won't I? What will you order me to take this time?
Everything. Even what she holds on to until the end.
What she holds on to until the end is a notebook. Filled with other people's names.
There was no answer from above. The tiger held the soaked ledger closer. An unfamiliar feeling stirred beneath the ring around its neck. A feeling called doubt.
The red sky swallowed her. Above, the twelfth-house door closed quietly.
At the end of their descent along the threads lay a red sky. Beneath it, stone temples stretched endlessly. A little moon floated above every roof.
Why are there so many moons?
Twenty-seven. In this sky, the Moon stays in a different house each night. Twenty-seven nights to make a full circuit.
The Moon uses guesthouses? Who pays for the rooms?
That's a new question for me. I'll write it down.
Red threads hung along both sides of the stone steps, stretching from pillar to pillar, roof to sky. Whenever the wind blew, they hummed low.
These threads look like the ones in the twelfth house.
They're the same threads. There, they show endings. Here, connections. Bonds that run from one life to another.
It's a way of reading twenty-seven lunar stations. It also reached East Asian Sukuyo, but here we need to follow Vedic astrology's nakshatras.
So this is the sky for love readings.
More precisely, karma, bonds, and romance. All three are expensive.
A stone tablet stood at the temple entrance. Instead of words, it bore pictures: a serpent with only a head, and a serpent with only a tail.
The head and tail are separate. They look like they used to be one creature.
An old story of this sky. A monster secretly drank the nectar of immortality and was beheaded. The nectar had only reached its throat, so the head couldn't die.
The head is Rahu; the body and tail, Ketu. The head resents the Sun and Moon and sometimes swallows them. That's an eclipse.
But without a throat, whatever it swallows must come right back out.
Exactly. That's why eclipses always end. The people of this sky wait, trusting that.
What about the tail? What does it eat?
The tail eats what has passed. Memories, past lives, bonds that have ended. That's why people on the tail's side keep looking back.
Head eats what's ahead, tail eats what's behind. Quite a balanced diet.
An enemy that isn't a picky eater is the most troublesome kind.
At that moment, one moon darkened. It was staying in a house rounded like an ox's forehead. A black shadow passed slowly before it.
Rohini. A lunar station in Taurus. You can see the head there.
Black Moon?
That's what your chart says, my lady. Rahu, the head, is in Rohini. Ketu, the tail, is opposite, in Jyeshtha. Black Moon has settled into your sky.
Stop trespassing in other people's skies!
Let's charge ten times the late fees. We learned that from Blue Rabbit.
Neo sat alone beside a stone well, his outer coat covering his right arm.
Yeoni touched an underlined note: Neo's hand. Must see it later. There could be no more later.
It's later now.
...You're still carrying that note?
Never threw it away. Paw out.
Neo slowly lifted his coat. His arm was empty above the elbow. Blue light from the well passed through it and pooled on the ground.
How far will it go? Your legs? Your whole body?
I'm repaying a borrowed place. Once it's repaid, it will end.
If you keep saying repayment without telling me what you borrowed, how am I supposed to help?
You don't need to. If you know, the price goes up.
Yeoni cupped the transparent paw in both hands. They caught nothing. Still, they didn't let go.
Then I'll hold it without knowing. That doesn't raise the price, does it?
...That wasn't in the calculation.
The wind stopped, and the well water stilled. Color briefly returned to the reflected hand. Yeoni hurried to draw its outline in the notebook, leaving out none of its five fingers.
Moka, tell me your birthday and I'll read your lunar station. Free.
'Free' is the most suspicious word you say.
Then shall I guess? Quick hands, angry at compliments, always making sure others eat first.
...You just described what you've seen me do.
Half of divination is observation. The other half is courage.
Moka's face is red.
I've spent too long near the fire! Occupational hazard of being a chef!
Then a temple bell rang once. One moon moved from its roof to the next, signaling that a night had passed.
Time moves quickly here. Every time the Moon moves house, a day passes.
We've already used up a day?
We should hurry. Delay is expensive in this sky.
If time's so precious, why were you all talking about my face?
A round room lay inside the temple. Twenty-seven divisions formed a circle on the floor, each holding a small oil lamp.
Let's find your lunar station. The house the Moon stayed in on the night you were born.
Yundal followed the circle, passing the Ram's houses and stopping at the second division. A lamp lit by itself.
Bharani. The star that bears.
Bears?
A star that holds something within and brings it into the world. In this sky, such a person is called a vessel.
Yeoni instinctively pressed their stomach. That was Black Moon's word. Cold. Hungry.
I hate that word. Vessel. That's what Black Moon calls me.
Black Moon only told you half. A vessel must be empty to hold something. That's Black Moon's meaning.
Bharani means something different. Bear it, then send it out. Not keep it inside, but nurture it and give it back.
Yeoni lifted their hand from their stomach, then laid it there again. This time, they felt a little less afraid.
Your Moon sits at the very end of Bharani. Next comes Krittika, connected with fire. Watch that boundary.
I'm on the boundary?
One step farther and it becomes the star holding a blade. Between the one who bears and the one who cuts. That's why you're so stubborn.
So we're back to stubborn!
Yundal. Can you read Seo Hanbi's star too?
Not without her birthday. Do you know it?
The parcel label only had her name and apartment number. No birthday.
Then we'll have to ask her directly. Though I don't know whether she'll answer.
A single red thread descended from the round room's ceiling and wrapped around Yeoni's wrist. It wasn't cold. It was lukewarm, like skin.
Why is this wrapping around me?
Your thread of connection. Follow it to the end and you'll find the person you're linked to.
Wow. Time to reveal your destined partner? The cat must be nervous.
I am not nervous.
The thread split in two. One strand led to Neo, the other beneath a crack in the temple floor.
Yeoni's expression froze as they followed the thread toward Neo. Just before it reached his chest, it had unraveled. Only a few fibers kept it connected.
Neo. What's wrong with this? It's frayed.
It's an old thread. That's normal.
Normal? Your paw, the thread—are you going to say it's all normal?
Neo covered the thread with his hand. The fibers, close to snapping, remained visible through his transparent palm. He couldn't hide them.
My lady. The other strand. That one goes down.
(Down. Where the chains were dragged.)
Yeoni tugged gently. From below came the faintest answering pull, as though someone held the other end between their fingers.
This thread wasn't formed in one life. It's thick enough to survive many rebirths.
Then I've met the person below in another life?
You met and exchanged something. Good or bad. That's how karma works.
What if it was bad?
Then I have even more questions.
The temple floor split open. The end of an enormous tail rose through the gap, covered in serpent scales. Chains coiled tightly around it.
The tail eats memory. The head eats tomorrow. Vessel, which will you surrender first?
Neither! Our Yeoni isn't hungry!
I'll take it into the Void. Everyone back.
As Yundal reached for his glove, Neo pressed down on his wrist. His hand was transparent, but its grip still held.
Don't widen it yet. That's the tail. Don't spend all your strength before the head arrives.
Mr. Cat worrying about me. I'm touched.
The tail swept the floor. Lamps toppled. The red thread around Yeoni's wrist pulled taut. Someone below was holding on.
Rain sounded from beneath the crack, impossible in the clear temple. Then came a low, elegant voice.
Don't let go of that thread. Not yet.
The tail sank back into the gap. The floor closed. Only the thread remained around Yeoni's wrist, stretched straight and tight downward.
I know that voice.
Yeoni.
Don't stop me. I said I had a mountain of questions. I'm going down to ask them.
I'm not stopping you. I said I'd stand beside you.
I'm coming too. Giving people a hard time is my specialty.
I'll applaud from behind the people asking questions. Applause is free.
The four headed for the temple's deepest stairs. The steps led into darkness. The red thread around Yeoni's wrist guided them onward.
Twenty-seven moons shone in sequence along the stairwell wall. As they descended, the moons went out one by one. When only the last remained, the rain sounded very close.
The stairs ended in a round chamber beneath the temple. Though it had no ceiling, rain fell. Before reaching the floor, the water caught on red threads and ran along them.
A black tiger sat in the center. A chain led from the golden ring around its neck into a crack in the floor. Beneath that crack, a scaled tail stirred slowly.
Found you.
Wow. Really here. Much bigger than I expected, though.
We have four on our side. We can win on numbers.
Have we ever won on numbers?
Today's our first match.
You found me. Holding that thread so tightly, for someone who came to confront me.
I did come to confront you. I have a list.
Yeoni opened their notebook. The tiger's golden eyes followed it. For a brief instant, those eyes narrowed like a hungry beast's.
One: the drummer child's applause. Two: the voices of the Island of Expression. Three: counting my socks from next door.
That last one is a little unfair.
I'm the one treated unfairly! You talked at the wall about my socks not matching!
Yeoni. Is that important right now?
All of it is. I'm going through it one thing at a time.
The tiger didn't laugh. Instead, the chain jerked once. Its neck bent downward. Its breathing was rough.
Four. You wrote down that I saved you too, I hope. The day hands came out of your phone.
...I did. I'm asking about that too.
You're taking issue with being saved?
Why you saved me. Until I hear that, I can't ask about the rest.
Yundal whispered behind Yeoni, lifting his gloved hand slightly to indicate the chain on the floor.
My lady. That chain is attached directly to the tail. Break it by force, and the tail wakes.
The tail eats the past. If it wakes, it'll eat her memories first.
Then what? Just leave it and talk?
Talk first. That beast is under orders right now. Look at its eyes.
A black dot floated inside the tiger's golden eyes, like a tiny eclipse. Whenever it grew, the tiger's claws scraped the floor.
There's no time. I'm being told to empty you, Yeoni. Inside my head. Constantly.
Empty me? Empty what?
Starting with what you hold on to until the end.
A black forepaw flashed out. The notebook vanished from Yeoni's hands. The tiger pinned it beneath its paw.
Hey! Give that back!
Moka, wait. Those eyes are fighting right now. Not out here. Inside.
The tiger didn't tear the notebook. It didn't extend its claws. It simply turned the pages with its forepaw. One, then another.
Every page was crowded with Yeoni's awkward handwriting. Other people's names, other people's circumstances. Skewer counts, birthdays, before the rooster crowed, left arm.
The tiger's paw stopped on one page. A line pressed heavily into the paper twice: Seo Hanbi. Dragged away. Must find her.
When did you write this?
At the palace of stars. As soon as I heard you being dragged away.
The tiger turned another page. There it was again: Drummer child's name. Inside tiger's cloak. And a little question mark.
You wrote this down too. What I hid.
I thought you were keeping it safe, not hiding it. That's why I added the question mark. Because I don't know yet.
The tiger's breath stopped. The black dot in its eye wavered. It began to grow, then halted.
I said names were debts. That speaking one makes you indebted. So why did you write my name so large?
To owe you.
What?
People in debt have to meet again. To repay or collect. So I put myself in your debt on purpose. Yours, Seo Hanbi.
The tiger couldn't answer. It had filled thousands of ledger pages. Yet it had never seen arithmetic like this.
Yeoni's logic is scarier than a loan shark's.
From today on, I'm never borrowing money from my lady.
Only Neo didn't smile. He watched the tiger for a long time. Less like someone guarding against an enemy than someone recognizing another person caught in the same day's rain.
Remember the last scene of that spring. Not what you saw. What was actually there.
What do you know? That spring, you arrived too late.
Yes. I was late. That's why I came early this time.
(Arrived late? Neo? That spring?)
Let me ask one thing. Answer it, and I'll give this back.
Ask.
On a rainy day, if there's only one umbrella, what do you do?
Yeoni didn't think. It wasn't a question that needed thought.
Half each. Obviously.
The tiger's forepaw trembled. The notebook slipped to the floor. Something fell from its golden eye. Rainwater or something else—it was impossible to tell.
Half each. Why are you the one saying that?
The red thread around Yeoni's wrist suddenly blazed. Its other end was wound around the tiger's right forepaw, above the mark left by a ring.
A scene appeared in the light. A bus stop. One umbrella. A packet of gummies. Two children's wet sneakers. Yeoni saw it too.
This is what I saw in the twelfth house. The bus stop.
You can see it too, Yeoni?
(This isn't my memory. Then why do I know how the umbrella handle feels? Why do I know the gummies are grape-flavored?)
A thread from another life. You two met in that life.
What did they do in that life? Fight?
No one could answer. The scene stopped halfway through instead of reaching its end: the girl with the umbrella turning away. Everything after that had been blacked out.
Then Yeoni looked at the thread leading from their wrist to Neo. It was thinner than before. Only one fiber remained.
Neo. The thread.
I'm fine. Look over there first.
Neo's right arm was empty all the way to his shoulder. He turned to hide it, but the red rain passed straight through.
If not now, when? You keep saying later!
Yeoni. That beast is disobeying its orders for the first time. Look at that. My paw isn't running away.
...It is. Little by little. Right in front of me.
The sky opened. Above the roofless chamber rose an enormous head with no body, cleanly severed below the neck.
The head is hungry. The tail holds many memories. Because of you, both have starved, vessel.
The head opened its mouth. One moon was sucked into it: the Moon of Bharani, the Ram's second house.
Ah... My stomach.
Yeoni dropped to their knees. Their stomach felt hollow, as though the place that had held something had collapsed all at once.
Yeoni! Stay with us!
Tiger. Now. Empty that child. Down to the very last thing.
No.
One short word. The room fell silent. Even the rain seemed to stop.
Say that again.
I said no. The emptier that child becomes, the fuller you grow. I didn't put on this leash to serve your meals.
Then why did you wear it? Do you remember?
To stop her. Before she became a monster.
Yes. Before that child became a monster. And what is that child now?
The tiger looked at Yeoni. A twenty-three-year-old woman sitting on the floor, clutching her stomach. A person with thread around her wrist, still holding it in the hand that had lost the notebook.
...She doesn't look like a monster. Not at all.
Your eyes have clouded. Because of the rain.
No. They've finally cleared.
The floor shook. The tail beneath the crack woke. The chain tugged wildly, dragging the tiger toward the gap.
Tail. Eat that child's bygone spring. Without memories, there is no reason to rebel.
Now. Mr. Cat, don't stop me.
Yundal removed his glove and aimed the hole in his palm at the chain. Its black energy streamed into the hole. The chain slackened a little.
I'll help! Fire ought to startle a tail!
Moka pulled matches from his apron pocket. They wouldn't light in the rain. Three tries, four. Only on the fifth did a tiny flame appear.
He held the flame to a chain link. The metal glowed red. The tail flinched and briefly loosened its grip.
See? A chef can light a fire even in the rain.
Moka, that was genuinely impressive. Shall I read our compatibility?
You're bringing that up now?!
Yeoni, grab the thread. The one leading to that beast.
Yeoni couldn't stand. Still, they reached out and wound the red thread around both hands. It cut into their palms.
I'm not letting go. I still have a mountain of questions.
Let go. The tail will eat you too.
Then it can eat us together. Half each, remember? You said it.
The tiger was sucked into the crack. At the last moment, its golden eyes met Yeoni's. The black dots were gone.
The thread didn't snap. It stretched taut into the gap. Something flowed back up along it: the sound of old rain. The scent of a long-ago spring.
(This isn't my memory. It's hers. But I can hear my name.)
Yeoni. That thread leads to the first spring.
Then we follow it. All of us. I'll ask every question there, one by one.

episodes.title: The First Spring
episodes.tag: Episode 38 Side Story · The First Spring

beats.t: There was no floor beneath the gap. The tiger fell, hanging from a single red thread. Someone above refused to let go.
I told you to let go. Just as stubborn as back then.
The sound of rain flowed down the thread. Not downward with the chain's pull, but sideways, where the thread led. The tiger changed course.
Not that way. Come down.
I'd like to, but the thread won't listen.
The thread blazed. The world blurred like wet glass. Beyond it stood an old bus stop. This time it wasn't a picture in a ledger. It had a smell.
Spring rain fell. Beneath the bus-stop roof sat two young women, not long out of their school uniforms.
Halfie, look. A weird app installed itself. It says customer support is the universe.
The universe does consultations too? How many stars?
Haven't rated it yet. I'll rate it when it replies. If it doesn't, one star.
The tiger looked down on the scene. The young woman on the left wore wet sneakers. It was her. Seo Hanbi at twenty-two, with a human face.
Halfie. Yes. That's what she called me. Because she shared half her umbrella.
The envelope's nearly full. We can really go to the sea next month.
Mine too! Let's count it together tomorrow, half each. Here, same time.
Yeoni held out a little finger. Seo Hanbi hooked hers around it. Their fingers were cold. Both laughed.
Tomorrow. That tomorrow never came.
The scene changed. A cramped studio apartment at midnight. Only the phone screen on the desk was lit. Yeoni slept beneath a blanket.
A notification appeared. Then another. The same sentence stacked up dozens of times: Vessel located.
I've never seen this scene before.
The thread wasn't showing only the tiger's memories. It was drawing in memories from its other end—Yeoni's—as well.
A black hand crawled out of the screen. One, two, three. They covered sleeping Yeoni's face. Yeoni couldn't even scream.
Ah, delicious. A full vessel at last.
Stop. Wake her up. Wake her!
The tiger's voice never reached that room. It was a spring already past. When the black hands withdrew, Yeoni opened their eyes. A round shadow floated behind them.
This face will do.
In the mirror, the corners of Yeoni's mouth rose. Once. Twice. The smile grew too broad, then the lips lowered again. Only on the third attempt did it resemble Yeoni's usual expression.
It wasn't her. The one that day was never her.
The following day. The same bus stop, the same time. Seo Hanbi arrived first, clutching a thick envelope. Rain had slightly blurred the words on it: Go to the sea together.
You're here? Where's your umbrella? Today I'll share my half.
Seo Hanbi.
Seo Hanbi stopped smiling. Yeoni had never called her that way. Her full name, surname included, in a businesslike voice.
Why are you calling me that? Is something wrong?
Give me the envelope. I'll count it.
Seo Hanbi hesitated, but held it out. Of course she would give it if Yeoni asked. Half each.
The moment Yeoni took the envelope, they turned away. They walked into the rain without an umbrella and never looked back.
Yeon? Yeon! Where are you going? We said we'd count it together tomorrow.
Why didn't you run after her? Why did you just stand there, you fool?
Seo Hanbi didn't follow. Her legs wouldn't move. Two buses passed. As the third arrived, someone ran into the bus stop.
A young man. He carried a white umbrella, still folded. He seemed to have run there without even taking time to open it. Water dripped from his hair.
His face was invisible, as though the thread had deliberately blurred that part. Only his voice was clear.
Man: Have you seen Yeoni? About this tall, yellow bag. I haven't been able to reach them since last night.
I did. Just now. She left with my money.
The white umbrella fell from the man's hand. He looked around through the rain. There was no one left.
Man: Too late. Again.
That voice. The cat's voice.
The man ran off again without retrieving his umbrella. Seo Hanbi stared at the white umbrella for a long time. She didn't pick it up. Other people's things were debts.
He was in that spring too. Arriving too late, he must have cried even longer than I did.
After that, Yeoni never returned. No calls, no texts. Seo Hanbi went to that bus stop every day, whether it rained or not.
On the tenth night, her phone lit up by itself. The same app that had appeared on Yeoni's phone. In place of the customer-support icon was a black circle.
After Yeoni vanished, one man remained at the bus stop. Park Byeongha. He would wear mismatched socks every day and watch the road where Yeoni never came.
Every time he asked Destiny Customer Support to open its closed door, he was refused. At last, the universe asked what he would pay to go back once.
Park Byeongha offered his human body and name. Spring returned to its beginning, and he opened his eyes as a white cat who didn't yet even have the name Yeoni would give him.
As that door closed, Seo Hanbi crossed with him, hanging from her chain. Not the one who began the rewind, but a witness to the failed timeline.
Do you feel wronged?
Who are you?
The child who abandoned you has become a monster. One that grows by eating other people's fortune. She will make gentle souls like you cry again.
Her? That can't be.
Who walked away with your envelope?
Seo Hanbi couldn't answer. Her nails dug into her palm. The tiger watched that hand from above. Her right hand.
I will give you a chance. Before she becomes a monster, collect what she has. Fortune, breath, applause.
Not for free, I assume.
Nothing is free. Surely you know that now.
Those words hurt most. Seo Hanbi laughed for a long time. It sounded like crying.
Fine. But give me a ledger. So no one can ever take from me for free again.
A golden ring fell from the screen and wound around her right wrist. Black fur covered her skin. Her fingers became claws. A soaked ledger dropped at her feet.
Stop. Don't take it. You mustn't take it.
The Seo Hanbi of the past didn't hear. A black tiger stood. Golden eyes opened for the first time. In them, too, were tiny black dots.
The thread jerked to a halt. The rain stopped. The tiger hung once more in the gap beneath the eclipse: the neck chain pulling down, the red thread up. Its body felt as though it would tear in two.
Have you seen? And what does that change?
Everything. She never abandoned me. You ate her. You took my envelope wearing her face.
And you became my hand. You put on the ring yourself. You opened the ledger yourself.
The tiger couldn't argue. It was true. She had been deceived. But her claws had collected the drummer child's applause. The voices of Expression. The hours of Wealth.
Yes. That was my hand.
Then remain my hand until the end. Where could you turn now?
The chain gave one great tug. The ring strangled her. Her golden eyes dimmed. Then a voice came down the thread from above.
Tiger! No, Seo Hanbi! Answer if you can hear me! I haven't asked my questions yet!
It wasn't Halfie. Still, the tiger smiled. The Yeoni of this spring was calling her properly by name.
Where can I turn? There is somewhere. Up there, to the girl holding the umbrella.
The tiger lifted its forepaw. The right one, where the ring had first closed. Extending its claws, it grasped the golden ring around its neck.
Break that ring and you become nothing. No body, no power, no road home.
I know. You said nothing was free. This time, I'll pay.
Above, Yeoni held the thread. Below, the tail held the chain. Between them hung the black tiger.
Chairman. I'll write the ledger's last line myself.
What line?
Seo Hanbi. Repaid. One golden ring.
The tiger seized the ring around its neck with its right forepaw. Its claws sank into metal. The ring grew hot. Burning fur filled the air.
Let go. That ring is your body. Break it, and your power and road home break with it.
I know. That's why I'm breaking it.
Cracks split the ring. One, then two. Black smoke leaked through them. The tail screamed. The chain thrashed wildly.
The ring broke in two. The sound was small, like a single glass breaking. Yet that little sound reverberated through everything beneath the eclipse.
Black fur streamed away like rain. Claws shrank. The great body grew smaller. All that remained was a person in a wet coat.
Oh. It's colder than I expected.
She fell. Below, there was no chain left to catch her. Only a single red thread around her wrist.
Above, beside the well among the twenty-seven lunar mansions, the thread suddenly grew heavy. Yeoni pitched forward, knees striking stone.
Heavy! Heavier than before! Why?!
Not a tiger's weight. One person's weight. With no strength left to hold on.
Neo lowered his head to bite the thread. His foreleg passed straight through it. Transparent to the shoulder, it couldn't grasp anything.
Of all times to lose my strength. Damn it.
Move, cat! This is what aprons are for!
Moka untied his apron and knotted it around the thread. Yundal grabbed the end. The three lined up and pulled. Like tug-of-war, except their opponent was the universe.
One, two, three. I'm not normally the sort of person who does this.
Shut up and pull! Compatibility later!
A wet hand rose from the well. A ring-shaped scar circled its right wrist. Yeoni seized it. It was cold.
The person they hauled up lay coughing on the stone. Water streamed from her black coat. She clutched a soaked ledger.
My next-door neighbor.
Hello. Sorry to impose at this hour.
Yeoni was speechless. The neighbor who carried a black umbrella even on clear days. The voice nagging about socks through the wall. The name on the parcel label. All the same person.
You are imposing. A lot.
The rain stopped. Five sat around the well. Or rather, four and one. Seo Hanbi sat a little apart.
Almost no energy left. About one drop of water. Less than a hundredth of what you had as a tiger.
Very accurate. Are your readings always that precise?
Only with compatibility. Your birth date and time would improve the accuracy.
That's a debt.
You're pitching compatibility to her now?! She took every voice on our island!
Moka's whiskers trembled. His forepaws gripped his apron tightly. Seo Hanbi lifted her head and faced him without looking away.
Yes. I took them. The market grandmothers' voices. The children rapping on the underground stage. They're all in the ledger.
How can you say that so calmly?!
I'm pretending to be calm. Otherwise I can't get the words out.
Moka closed his mouth. He didn't look any less angry. But he stopped shouting.
Seo Hanbi opened the ledger. Names crowded the wet pages. Yeoni's name stood among them. In the next column: Outstanding. Outstanding.
I'll start with the excuse. Otherwise what comes afterward won't be honest.
Go ahead.
That spring, I was deceived. Black Moon came wearing your face and took my envelope. I believed you'd abandoned me.
So I said I'd stop you before you became a monster. I wore the ring as the price. Up to that point, Black Moon was to blame.
Seo Hanbi paused. Her finger rubbed the ledger's corner, raising the paper's fibers.
But although Black Moon deceived me, the hand that stole the child's applause was mine.
When the drummer child cried, I wrote: Collection complete. On Moka's island, on the island of time too. I did it all with my own hands.
No one spoke. Only water dripped at the bottom of the well. Drip. Drip.
Thank you. For saving me earlier. And for not making excuses now.
Yes.
But I don't forgive you. Not now.
Yeoni's voice shook. Even they couldn't tell whether it was anger or tears. Still, they finished.
That drummer child really cried that day. I saw it. So did the grandmothers on Moka's island. You haven't returned anything to them. I can't forgive you ahead of them.
For now, I'll only say thank you. Forgiveness comes later. I decide that too.
That's right. If I were forgiven now, my ledger wouldn't balance either.
The ledger again.
A habit. I'll work on it. Slowly.
Seo Hanbi turned the ledger's pages again and placed a finger on one voice in the collection column. She tried to push the letters backward. The ink wouldn't move.
Ah. I paid away the power to return things too. As part of the ring's price.
What tiger power collected can only be released by tiger power. You can't do it in this body.
Then I'll have to find another way. Even if it takes time.
Do it, however long it takes. The grandmothers are waiting.
Moka said only that and turned away. But he didn't leave. He pushed his remaining box of matches toward Seo Hanbi, as though telling her to dry her coat.
May I take these? What do I owe?
Owe, my tail. Just use them. Sharing fire doesn't make it smaller.
Night came. The twenty-seven moons lit one by one. Yeoni sat on the well's edge and took out their notebook. Neo lay down beside them.
Seo Hanbi. Rescued. Forgiveness pending. Drummer child's name: still unknown.
Yeoni's pen stopped. The scene that had traveled up the thread remained in their mind. The rainy bus stop. The man who dropped his white umbrella.
Neo. Were you at that bus stop too?
What bus stop?
The white umbrella. 'Too late. Again.' That voice was yours.
Neo's hand went still. Instead of answering, he looked down at his arm. It was transparent to the shoulder.
There are things I can't say. Not simply because I want to hide them.
That again? Everyone has too many secrets. Does this world's customer support not have a notices page?
It does. Nobody reads it.
Don't be funny. None of this is funny.
Yeoni looked at Neo's transparent foreleg. They reached to touch it, then stopped. It seemed even more frightening to feel their hand pass through.
Then answer just one thing. That spring too—were you on my side?
That I can say. I'm on your side. From the beginning to now.
(Even in a different form, Neo. On my side. I have to preserve that much.)
Yeoni pressed the words into a corner of the notebook. Neo pretended not to see.
Across the well, Seo Hanbi counted moons alone. Neo walked over silently and stood beside her.
You were the one who arrived late then. The white umbrella.
Yes. And you were still there.
Neither of us protected her.
This time will be different. For you too.
I have no power now. I can't wield light the way you can.
It's hard for me to wield it now too. This arm is disappearing first.
Seo Hanbi looked down at Neo's leg. For the first time, her unsmiling face tightened.
Does she know?
No. She mustn't. Don't tell her either.
You're putting me in your debt.
Yes. Repay me later.
At dawn, one of the twenty-seven moons abruptly went dark. Yeoni's moon, Bharani. A round patch blackened in the sky.
Oh. That's strange. I feel hollow again.
An enormous head descended from the black circle. A head without a body: Rahu. Each time its mouth opened, starlight was sucked inside.
The head eats the future. My lady, your notebook!
Yeoni opened it. Next week's to-do list was disappearing line by line. Grocery shopping. Submit assignment. Go to the sea. The words turned into black smoke and rose into the sky.
Why the sea?! We haven't even picked a date!
Promises without dates taste best. Like the promise you two once failed to keep.
Seo Hanbi went pale. Only the two of them knew that promise. And the thing that had slipped between them.
[ Year: Im-o · Frozen ] Cracks spreading
I have no use for a dog without a collar. I shall empty you along with that vessel.
The head descended. Yeoni stepped back. Neo moved forward, but his legs couldn't find purchase on the floor.
What stepped in front of them was a wet coat. Seo Hanbi, unarmed, without claws or fangs.
What are you doing? You said you have no power!
I don't. But this time I won't walk toward that side.
I don't even have an umbrella. Let alone half of one.
Rahu's mouth opened. Then something fell onto Seo Hanbi's palm. A single cold drop. Clear, not black.
...Rain?
The drop wasn't alone. Two, three, ten. Rain began falling beneath the eclipsed sky.
This isn't me. I haven't done anything.
It is you, my lady. Look at your palm.
Seo Hanbi looked down. The droplets weren't falling from her palm. They rose from it into the sky, then fell again.
That water isn't Black Moon's gift. It's yours by nature. In Four Pillars terms, Gye Water. Rainwater.
My water always drowned people. In the library, it drowned her too.
The ring made you use it that way. Without the ring, it's falling as it was meant to.
Rain poured into Rahu's open mouth. The head choked and stopped. The starlight it had tried to swallow grew heavy with water.
What is this lukewarm thing?
Rahu coughed. Handfuls of starlight spilled from its mouth. The extinguished Bharani began to glow faintly again.
My moon! It's back!
Black smoke settled on Yeoni's notebook. Soaked by rain, it became words again: Grocery shopping. Submit assignment. Go to the sea. A little blurred, but readable.
The trip to the sea survived!
You said you hadn't even set a date.
Exactly why it has to survive. Promises without dates taste best, right? Then I'll set a date and make it taste awful.
Rahu shook its bodiless head. The rain thickened, pushing it backward. The black circle in the sky shrank little by little.
But the rain soon weakened. The stream rising from Seo Hanbi's palm thinned to a thread. Rahu opened its mouth again.
She doesn't have enough water. This rain began with a single drop.
(Bharani. The star that bears. Hold it, then send it out.)
Yeoni cupped their hands toward the sky. Rainwater pooled in their palms. Instead of running off, it swelled within their hands.
You called me a vessel. Then this is how I'll use it. Gather what I receive, then send it back out.
The water stretched upward like a vine and wound around Seo Hanbi's thin stream. As the two twisted into one, the rain strengthened.
You're taking my rain and giving it back?
Half each. That's how it works.
A thing without a ring dares...
Because I have no ring. Your arithmetic doesn't work on me anymore.
Rain spread across all twenty-seven lunar mansions: over roof tiles, into wells, into cracks in stone. It wasn't cold. It was mild, like rain at summer's end.
This rain isn't shriveling my whiskers. Weird rain.
Good rain is like that. Welcome rain, they call it. Rain that falls where it's been awaited.
Something cracked at Yeoni's wrist. The sound of breaking ice. The panel of characters appeared by itself.
[ Year: Im Water · Thawing ]
The frozen Im character in the leftmost column melted. Its black, hardened form returned to clear blue. Warmth spread to Yeoni's fingertips.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: Gyeong-Chen ] 8/8
Warm. Not my wrist. Inside.
The water flows now. Gyeong gives birth to Im, and Im nourishes Eul. Officer and Resource in Mutual Generation. Instead of cutting Wood, Metal nourishes it through Water.
Translation, please.
The power Mr. Cat once hurt you with now nourishes you through the rain. Your compatibility has improved enormously.
Compatibility later.
Neo raised his arm. It was still transparent to the shoulder. But the grimace that had accompanied every movement was gone. Cautiously, he flexed his fingers once more.
Neo. Doesn't it hurt anymore?
The pain is less.
The pain? Then what isn't less?
Wet clothes sticking to me.
At Yeoni's suspicious look, Neo turned away and shook his sleeve. Droplets passed through his transparent arm. From Yeoni's side, the wet fabric hid it.
The rain eased. Then Seo Hanbi dropped to her knees. Her face was white as paper. The water rising from her palm had stopped.
Hey! What's wrong?!
I think I used all the water I had left. It's all right. There was only one drop to begin with.
How is that all right?! You're the color of tofu!
Moka dried Seo Hanbi's hair with his apron. Roughly, but thoroughly. She stayed still, as though no one had dried her hair in a very long time.
Moka, you have a heavy hand.
Chef's hands. They're spicy. I've been chopping chilies.
Seo Hanbi reached into her coat's inner pocket. Not for the soaked ledger. For a little folded note with a drumstick-shaped knot at its end.
This is what I must return first. The only thing I didn't enter in the ledger. I couldn't.
Yeoni took the note and untied the knot. A name was written in clumsy handwriting. The child's own hand.
Dodam.
The instant the name was spoken, a drum sounded far away. Boom. Boom. A clumsy, excited rhythm. From the sky toward the Island of Companions.
I hear it. A drum. That rhythm's such a mess, it has to be the kid.
Dodam. Right. It was Dodam. How did I forget?
Because I took it. When you take a name, others forget the child too. That's why the applause stopped.
I know. I saw the child drop the drumsticks that day. You smiled then.
I did. Because a line in my ledger balanced. That smile was mine too. Not Black Moon's.
Yeoni bit their lip. Moka turned away. No one took Seo Hanbi's side. She didn't look as though she expected anyone to.
But I carried the name inside my cloak. Whenever I tried to erase it, the ledger got wet.
This time, Seo Hanbi opened the ledger. One line in the collection column: Dodam's applause. Wet with rain, it slowly blurred. The letters dissolved and ran away with the water.
It's moving. It wouldn't budge before.
I thought rain couldn't release what rain hadn't collected. But returning the name first seems to have shown the ledger a way.
Then do them one at a time. One line whenever it rains. The market grandmothers. The underground-stage children. The people of the time island.
How many times will it have to rain before it's all repaid?
Many. Very many.
Then we could start selling umbrellas.
Yeoni wiped their tears with a sleeve and tucked the note into the notebook's first page. Then they looked straight at Seo Hanbi.
Come with us. But you're on trial.
On trial?
I'll keep watching. To see whether you really return them, one by one. Once you've returned everything, I'll consider it. Forgiveness.
Probation, then.
Yes. In ledger terms: outstanding.
Outstanding. The word I wrote most in my ledger, now applied to me.
I'll watch too. My eyes still work fine.
Me too. To monitor you, I'll need your birth date and—
I told you, that's a debt.
Someone cure this man's compatibility obsession!
Laughter burst out. It rang around the well after the rain like a sound heard for the first time. Seo Hanbi didn't laugh. She pressed her lips together, holding back tears.
Behind the well, a little apart from the others, Yundal pulled his glove on and crouched beside Neo. The hole in his palm had grown large enough to show through it.
Neo. Water passed straight through your arm earlier.
You saw?
Only me. My lady was busy picking up cards.
Then that promise still stands?
If they forget me, remember me. Yes. It stands. I'm usually the one forgotten, so remembering is new for me.
It's a heavy thing to leave you carrying alone. Don't joke it away.
That's why you're leaving it with a con artist. A real fortune-teller wouldn't take this contract. It's a loss.
Neo didn't answer. He watched Yeoni for a long time. They were wringing out Seo Hanbi's wet coat and scolding her.
Then the sky split. The eclipse tore open, spilling enormous sheets of paper through the gap. Cards. Each as large as a door.
Rahu's head was drawn between the cards. Ketu's tail followed. Both seeped into the illustrations and became shadows.
I will wait beyond the twenty-two cards. In the next sky, neither your umbrella nor your rain will help.
And that cat. Half mine already. Count the threads.
Yeoni looked at their wrist. The red thread leading to Neo. At some point, two strands had become one. Even that last strand was fraying.
Neo. The thread.
I know.
Don't end with 'I know.' Tell me properly this time.
When we reach the next sky, I'll tell you. I promise.
A card fell at Yeoni's feet, face down. A dark blue back patterned with stars. They tried to turn it over, but it wouldn't move, as though glued to the floor.
Your birth card, my lady. When the time comes, it will turn over by itself.
(When is that? Everyone says later. There are too many laters.)
The last raindrop fell. Footprints marked the wet stone: Yeoni's, Seo Hanbi's, Moka's, Yundal's.
Only where Neo had walked were there no footprints. Yeoni couldn't take their eyes from the card.
The corridor had no visible end. Door-sized cards lined both walls. Every picture moved: wind blowing, stars turning, someone walking.
Is this the tarot sky? Looks like an exhibition. There's no admission fee, right?
If there is, I'll pay. In exchange for your birth date and time.
Someone put something in his mouth.
[ Major Arcana · 0 → 21 ] Proceed in order
The twenty-two Major Arcana form one story: the Fool sets out and travels to the world's end. Skip the order and the doors won't open.
Like a ledger. You have to balance one line before writing the next.
Seo Hanbi walked at the back, three steps behind Yeoni. When Yeoni stopped, so did she. That was how probation was being observed.
Yeoni touched the card in their pocket. Its star-patterned back. The card that still wouldn't turn over felt warm beneath their fingertips.
(He keeps sitting down. Maybe it isn't only his hand that hurts.)
Neo, don't feel like walking? Want a piggyback?
You'd carry me? We have a bit of a height difference now.
Think I can't? Stop bracing on your hands and try leaning on me.
Neo gave Yeoni's back a gentle push and led the way. His footsteps made no sound on the stone. Yeoni thought he was deliberately walking softly.
Before the first card: Zero, the Fool. A young traveler carrying a bundle gazed skyward from a cliff's edge. A small white dog barked at the traveler's feet.
A dog but no otter. Discrimination.
The Fool is a fearless beginning. Taking a step even knowing it's a cliff.
Don't tell me we have to jump too.
Knew it.
The cliff inside the card came toward them. The ground vanished, leaving only clouds. Yeoni reached for Neo's arm and caught empty air.
Oiiink! Isn't there a card that gives advance warning?!
The five fell onto clouds. It didn't hurt. The clouds became the floor of the next card: the Magician's table, Number One.
Four things lay on the table: a cup, a sword, a wand, and a coin. Beside them, an unlit candle. As though lighting it would open the next door.
Fire? My specialty.
Moka took a match from his apron. It lit on the first strike. As the candle caught, the Magician in the picture doffed his hat to Moka.
See that? He greeted me. Me. People in this sky have manners.
You'll need even better manners at Door Two. The High Priestess's room.
Number Two, the High Priestess's room, was silent. A prohibition marked the wall: Whoever speaks must return. Yundal shut his mouth. His expression was agonized.
Yeoni fought a laugh at Yundal's face. Seo Hanbi offered him paper and a pen. He scribbled: Ladies' birth dates and times.
Writing it won't make me tell you.
The moment they left, Yundal took an enormous breath. Far too enormous for someone who'd held back for two minutes.
The longest two minutes of my life.
Number Three, the Empress's wheat field, glowed gold. Ears of grain bowed in the wind. As Seo Hanbi passed, they leaned only toward her, as though scenting water.
I didn't do anything.
Of course grain leans toward someone who brings rain. Good compatibility.
At the top of Number Four, the Emperor's stairs, stood an empty stone throne. Only a voice echoed: What do you govern? Answer, and pass.
My kitchen.
My mouth. Not very successfully.
My ledger. From now on.
Yeoni's turn. After a long moment's thought, they took out their notebook and waved it.
This. I write everything I forget in here. It governs me.

The stone door above the stairs opened. The throne seemed to give a little chuckle. At Number Five, the Hierophant's bell tower, a bell rang three times. Doors opened one by one. Moka lit fires, Yundal read paths, Yeoni answered questions.
Smoother than I expected. At this rate we'll finish all twenty-one cards today.
That's the sort of thing you must never write in a ledger.
Why?
Because the next line always contains an accident.
They decided to rest before Door Six, covered in ivy. Yundal took his own deck from his clothes. The cards were old and worn by use.
While we rest, shall we each draw one? Tarot drawn in the tarot sky is quite accurate.
Me first! No, Moka first.
Why me? No thanks. I don't believe in fortune-telling.
Saying that, Moka was the first to draw. He turned the card over: two naked figures and an angel. Number Six, the Lovers.
Oh. The Lovers. Your partner is probably the person right in front of you, Moka.
You switched that card, didn't you?! Hands out! Gloves off!
Not the glove! There's actually a hole in there!
The two wrestled over a single card. Yeoni laughed, clutching their stomach. After watching them, Seo Hanbi drew one.
Eleven. Someone holding scales.
Justice. It suits you, my lady.
Meaning a card of punishment.
No. Justice is scales, not punishment. Balancing what has tipped. Exactly what you're doing now.
Seo Hanbi didn't answer. She studied the card for a long time, then carefully tucked it into the ledger.
Your turn, Neo. What card will you get?
I'll pass.
No. Everyone drew one. We're traveling as a group.
Neo reached with his right hand. His fingertips passed through the cards. He quickly switched to his left and picked one. Yeoni saw that brief moment.
(His hand just passed through the card. I didn't imagine it.)
Neo laid the card down. Number Eight, Strength. A woman in white soothed a white cat with bared claws using her bare hands. The cat retracted its claws and leaned its head against her.
Strength. Not brute force, but the power to tame. Gentle hands overcoming something fierce.
A cat. Definitely Neo's card.
Look at the woman's face.
Yeoni peered at the card. The woman in the picture lifted her head. She had exactly Yeoni's face. And the forepaw of the cat she stroked was transparent.
Neo. This...
It's a card illustration. It doesn't have to match how we look now.
That night, the cards along the corridor walls went dark one by one. Only Number Eight, Strength, shone white. Wherever its light touched, Neo's body faded.
Neo tried to stand, then sank down. It wasn't only his legs that were transparent now. Light showed through his chest.
This place is unusually sensitive to names.
Neo's knees buckled. Yeoni caught his arm but felt almost no weight. The floor's pattern began showing through parts of his body.
Neo! Stay with me. Hold my shoulder. Slowly. Breathe first.
Neo couldn't gather enough breath to answer. Yeoni draped his arm over their shoulder. His remaining left hand clung to their sleeve.
Lean on me. Stop pretending you're okay. I'll hold you now.
Neo barely managed a nod. He wasn't saving words. Even one word required breath.
The Strength card's light is wearing him away. There's something inside it.
Ketu. The tail is hiding behind the illustration. It eats the past, so it's gnawing at Mr. Cat's past.
Then burn that card!
Burn it and the path breaks. Without passing Number Eight, we can't reach Twenty-One.
The next path lay beyond Door Six. Supporting Neo, Yeoni stopped before the ivy-covered entrance.
Wait. We're going now, with the cat like that? Let's rest for a night.
Resting will wear him away further. Number Eight's light is stronger at night. Going through is the fastest way.
Then I'll stand in front. Whatever is beyond the door, let it hit me first.
You said you have no power.
That's why I'm going first. I have the least to lose.
Yeoni started to speak, then stopped. Instead, they tugged Seo Hanbi's coat once: don't go too far ahead. Seo Hanbi stood only half a step in front.
Then let's get through quickly. Lovers or whatever.
If it's the Lovers, is it a door for confessions? Yundal will ask birthdays again.
Not this time. This door doesn't make you ask. It makes you read.
Read what?
That's the trouble. Each door makes you read one thing: whatever hurts most.
Neo's jaw tightened. Yeoni laid their hand over his where it clung to their sleeve. They couldn't lightly say it would be all right.
The ivy drew back by itself. In the center of the door was a nameplate. The lettering was still blurred. A three-syllable name. Only the first was barely visible: Park.
This door opens only to one who speaks the name. Read the nameplate, vessel.
Neo seized Yeoni's sleeve. His hand shook, as though he had spent every last bit of strength. A very small, urgent voice reached them.
“Don't read it. Yeoni. Not that.”
The second part of the name began to appear. Yeoni couldn't look away. Neo's hand tightened on their sleeve.

episodes.title: After the Water Clears
episodes.tag: Episode 41 Side Story · After the Water Clears

beats.t: Just before the second syllable appeared, something black covered Yeoni's view. Not a cold palm. Umbrella fabric.
Seo Hanbi held the taped umbrella open before the nameplate. The umbrella that had been tucked beside Yeoni's bag. One crooked rib blocked the name perfectly.
Don't read. Three steps back. Now.
Hide a name with one umbrella? You always act that way, rainwater.
Yes. Always. And this time, I'll keep doing it to the end.
Yeoni, close your eyes and move back. Moka, some fire.
Moka struck a match. A small flame drew a circle at their feet. The ivy reaching from the door hesitated before it. They backed into the room of Card Five.
This fire won't last! I've got three matches left!
The door closed behind them. Ivy covered the nameplate again. Black Moon's voice was sealed inside.
Card Five's room resembled an old cathedral. Starlight entered through high windows. They gathered beneath a pillar. Moka's little fire burned on the floor.
Door Six won't open at night. That's when names are most blurred. We hold out here until morning.
Then I'm sleeping first. Yundal, you're on watch. No asking birthdays.
Watch duty is boring. Nobody to ask.
Instead of answering, Moka began snoring. Whether he was asleep or simply refusing to listen was unclear. Yundal smiled and walked around the pillar, deliberately leaving the two alone.
Neo lay against Yeoni's shoulder, breathing unevenly. Whenever cool light brushed his back, Yeoni paused their hand and searched for warmth again.
(He can't be this light. Am I missing something?)
Across the fire, Seo Hanbi was folding the umbrella. One rib kept sticking out. She folded it, opened it, then folded it again.
That crooked rib's always like that. I repaired it.
I know. Three layers of tape. Two would have been enough.
Three makes me feel better.
Arithmetic worthy of you, Yeoni.
Seo Hanbi offered the umbrella handle-first, so Yeoni could take hold of it immediately.
Let me return this. What you gave me at the bus stop. I left it on the hallway floor.
I picked it up after you threw it away. Finders keepers.
Then it's all the more yours.
No. Since finders keepers makes me the owner, I can give it away if I want.
Yeoni didn't take the umbrella. Instead, they folded Seo Hanbi's hand over its handle and patted it twice, like stamping a contract.
Keep it. It's not a loan. Don't repay me.
Seo Hanbi's other hand drifted unconsciously inside her coat, where the ledger lay. It had shrunk to palm size. Every night, one line was coming undone.
Habit. When I receive something, I try to record it. My hand moves first.
Try. Let's see what happens.
Seo Hanbi picked up her pen and wrote: One umbrella. Before the ink could soak into the paper, a raindrop fell on it. The words became clear water and ran off.
It won't write.
See? Even the ledger says not to repay it.
Seo Hanbi stared at the wet ledger for a long time. Then she gave a very small laugh, soundless, just one shake of her shoulders.
The fire burned lower. Yeoni added a dry scrap of card instead of wood. For an instant, the sparks burst into star shapes.
Hey. Can I ask something?
Anything except the ledger.
What did the me from the first spring call you?
Seo Hanbi's hand stopped. Her fingers tightened around the umbrella handle. The answer didn't come at once.
I think I heard it through the thread. Faintly. But I can't remember the word.
I won't tell you that.
Why? I said it to you. Someone like me, anyway.
Because it was something she gave me. If you say it again, it feels as though she'll truly disappear.
Yeoni fell silent. The fire crackled softly. Neo's eyelids stirred at the sound.
I'm jealous of her. She knew you before I did.
She is you. The same hand tilted that umbrella.
Same hand, different spring. That spring is yours. I shouldn't take it.
Then I'll make a new one. My own.
A new what?
Name to call you. Seo Hanbi is too long. Ms. Seo Hanbi is too distant. And Ms. Tiger is wrong now.
Yeoni traced letters in the air. One, two. Erased them. Wrote again.
Hanbi. Hey, Hanbi.
Seo Hanbi lifted her head, eyes widening. She tried to speak, but only her lips moved. Wet lashes glittered in the firelight.
That's just dropping the surname. Too easy.
Easy is good. So I can call you quickly when it rains.
Only when it rains?
On clear days too. You carry an umbrella on clear days.
Instead of answering, Seo Hanbi hugged the umbrella. Its taped handle touched her chin. She stayed that way for a long time. Then, very softly, she repeated it.
Hanbi. Yes. I'll be Hanbi.
A little rain fell beyond the high windows. It wasn't cold. Dust settled on the cathedral floor, and the air cleared.
For a while, neither spoke. Both held their hands toward the fire. The backs of Yeoni's hands looked a little warmer. Seo Hanbi's were still cold.
Then one more thing. Answer this. What's wrong with Neo?
Wrong?
He makes no footsteps, and his hand passes through cards. He's human again, but his body keeps disappearing. You know why, don't you?
Seo Hanbi looked at Neo. His eyes were closed, but the hand holding Yeoni's sleeve moved a little. He was listening.
That's not my debt, so I can't speak of it.
You said you'd stop talking about debts.
Then call it a promise. One I made with him. But I can tell you one thing.
Tomorrow, whatever happens, don't read that nameplate. Especially not aloud.
As Yeoni looked down, Neo curled his fingers slightly. Instead of saying thank you, he gave their hand a weak squeeze.
All right. I won't read it. But you have to tell me everything in the morning, Neo.
There was no answer. Instead, his breathing grew a little steadier. Supporting his back, Yeoni fell asleep against the pillar.
At dawn, Yundal yawned on the other side of the pillar. He adjusted the glove over his palm and looked toward the others.
Oh.
Moka still snored. Seo Hanbi had fallen asleep sitting up, hugging her umbrella. Yeoni's head drooped against the pillar.
Their shoulder was empty. Only the coat that had covered him remained on the floor. Not even footprints marked the dust.
Everyone wake up. Mr. Cat is gone.
Far away, a door creaked open. Door Six.
They ran down the corridor. When they reached Door Six, it was half open. Ivy stretched through the gap like ropes.
Neo hung at the end of the ivy, feet off the ground. Beneath his sleeves and shirt, dim light showed in place of a human body.
Neo! Why did you come alone?!
Those vines are wrapped around him!
Yeoni rushed in. The ivy lashed like a whip and knocked them to the floor. Blood welled on their scraped palms.
No hurry, vessel. He came of his own accord. To read his own name aloud.
His own name? That would open the door, but...
The reader pays the price. If Mr. Cat reads it, Mr. Cat disappears.
That's what he came to do? In our place?
Ivy wrapped Neo's mouth, preventing an answer. He looked at Yeoni with apologetic eyes. Those were the eyes Yeoni hated most.
But he could not finish. He cannot remember his own name. He offered it as payment.
So read it for him. Then the vines will release him.
A lie. That voice always tells only half the truth. I was deceived by that half too.
Is half not enough? It is true the vines will let go.
The ivy tightened. Neo faded further. Not even the outline of his right hand remained.
Matches! I've got matches!
Moka struck one. It died before the flame reached the ivy. The air before the door ate fire.
Even fire needs a name before this door. I'll draw the vines into the Void. I can't do it for long.
Yundal removed his glove. The black hole opened in his palm. Ivy dragged toward it. At the same time, his face went white.
Yeoni. Decide. I can last one minute.
Yeoni looked at the nameplate. As the ivy pulled away, the letters appeared. Park. Then the second syllable. Then the third.
(They told me not to read it. Hanbi and Neo both. But if I don't, Neo disappears.)
Yeoni. Don't read. There must be another way.
What if Neo disappears while we look? Hanbi, you waited at that bus stop too.
Seo Hanbi fell silent. It was true. No one knew better how a spring spent only waiting had ended.
Then I'll share responsibility. Whatever happens, half is mine.
Yeoni nodded and approached the nameplate. Neo shook his head urgently. Yeoni didn't stop.
Park. Byeong. Ha.
The moment the three syllables sounded, the nameplate burned white. The ivy scattered into ash. Neo fell.
Yeoni caught him. His face was still Neo's, the one who had been with them since the river. But over it appeared the man who had dropped a white umbrella at the bus stop.
It wasn't a new face. The face in a lost memory had finally connected to the one before them. The same person.
The person who came to the bus stop then... That was you?
Please don't ask that. Answering would break the rules.
Neo smiled. At that instant, the seal on his name broke, and light drained from his toes upward. Knees, waist, chest. Beneath Yeoni's hands, he grew fainter.
I knew this would happen if the seal broke. Let me catch my breath. Just a moment.
It's not just a moment! Your body's disappearing!
The escaping light barely stopped at his chest. Neo still looked human, but his lower body blurred like a reflection in water. Yeoni refused to release the unseen hand.
My voice still works. There should be time to explain.
Then explain. Everything this time. Leave nothing out. I have to know so we can find a way together.
Neo looked at Moka, Yundal, then Seo Hanbi. Finally, Yeoni. It was time to speak of what he had hidden behind his name.
In the first spring, I knew you. Same school, same bus stop. You were always losing umbrellas.
That night I knew something was wrong with your phone, but I couldn't knock on your door. I thought I'd tell you tomorrow.
I'm also the one who opened the door that night. Park Byeongha paid with his body and name and returned as Yeongnyangi. You called me Neo.
Then from the start... you remembered a future where I disappeared?
Yes. I went back in time exactly once. To prevent that ending in this spring.
I was caught in the door Byeongha opened and followed him through. I was only a companion who knew the first spring. The one who turned time back was Yeongnyangi—Neo—Park Byeongha.
The next day, I ran to the bus stop. Too late. You were no longer you.
So that's what you meant. 'Too late. Again.'
Neo bowed his head slightly to Seo Hanbi. Same spring, same bus stop. The one who arrived late and the one who waited to the end faced each other.
After that, I called customer support every day. The place called the universe. My place in the queue was always infinity.
I don't know which winter it was. Someone finally answered. They would give me one more chance.
The price?
You must not know my name. If my name is spoken, I return to my original place. A place of nothing.
Then I just spoke it. I sent you away.
Half of me. The door took half for the price of one name. The remaining half can hold on if you don't say it again.
Then why didn't you tell me sooner? I wouldn't have read it.
Because telling you would have been the same as giving you my name.
This cat, honestly. His logic actually works, which makes me even angrier.
Yundal approached while pulling his glove on. His hand shook. He had held the Void open too long.
So that's why your place was borrowed, Mr. Cat. Gyeong, in the Hour column of Yeoni's Four Pillars.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: Gyeong-Chen ] Gyeong · Flickering
You pledged your name to occupy someone else's Four Pillars. The Direct Officer position. I've never seen a contract like that.
What was Direct Officer again? Isn't that the husband's position?
Is this the time?!
Let's leave that conversation for later.
For an instant, there was laughter. But when the wall's pattern showed through Neo's shoulder, no one could follow it with another joke.
Beyond the door lay the garden of Card Six. An angel spread its wings between two trees. Beneath it, the path forked.
The Lovers isn't a card of love. It's a card of choice. We have to choose one of the two to pass.
A sign stood before each path. This time the words were clear. Black Moon had kindly written them out.
[ Left · Remember the name—he disappears ] [ Right · Forget the name—he remains ]
An easy choice, is it not? Forget. Even forgotten, he stays beside you. A nameless beast.
That isn't staying.
Stay out of this, rainwater. The choice belongs to the vessel.
Something was dragged from Yeoni's mind. The middle syllable of the name blurred. Yeoni pressed their forehead. The name they had just read was leaking between their fingers.
Wait. The middle. What was the middle syllable?
Forget it. That's right. Go right.
Are you siding with Black Moon?
I'm siding with you. I always have.
Yeoni stood between the signs. Looked left. Looked right. Then took out their notebook and pulled the pen cap off with their teeth.
I don't want either.
You cannot pass without choosing.
I'll choose. But not what you've written.
Yeoni wrote in large letters, pressing hard. Almost hard enough to tear the paper.
[ Even in a different form, Neo. On my side. ]
I won't say your name, because you'll disappear. But I won't forget you either. I'll use the name I gave you instead.
Neo. Hey, Neo. You're Neo. That's what I called you. Since the day we met.
The ground split between the two signs. A third path appeared, narrow and uneven. It had no sign.
Neo's fingertips grew a little clearer. Yeoni took his hand again. This time, they could feel the outline of his fingers.
This path wasn't in the contract.
That's why people don't trust fortune-tellers. They insist on making a third path.
Nonsense. A made-up name is no name.
That nonsense saved me too. The name Hanbi.
Black Moon didn't answer. The angel in the garden folded its wings. At the path's end stood Door Seven, painted with a wheeled chariot.
Yeoni knelt to meet Neo's eyes. Their hand passed through his cheek when they tried to touch it. Still, they didn't withdraw. They held their palm where he should have been.
The middle syllable really is gone. Park, then Ha. That's all that's left.
That's enough. Remembering all of it is dangerous.
Even if it's dangerous, I wanted to remember. It's your name.
Neo is enough for me. You've called me by the name you gave me longer than by my original one.
Neo closed his eyes. Their light slowly faded. His head tilted like someone who had held on too long.
I'll sleep a little. You can scold me again when I wake.
You'd better wake up. If you don't, one star.
As his body faded further, Yeoni couldn't support him alone. Yundal took his other arm. Moka held the back of his shirt.
Wheels sounded inside Door Seven. Together, they supported Neo and laid him on the chariot's seat. His thin breaths continued.

episodes.title: An Ordinary Spring
episodes.tag: Episode 42 Side Story · An Ordinary Spring

beats.t: He knew it was a dream because it was too warm. Yeoni's voice calling his name faded, and a night left behind the seal returned. Neo remembered that night. Only this time, it felt as though he could finally send the words he hadn't sent.
A cramped rented room. A phone lay on the desk. Twenty-three-year-old Park Byeongha stared at its screen. One message hovered there, waiting for him to decide whether to send it.
[ Isn't something wrong with your phone? It kept getting notifications earlier. ]
I can tell them tomorrow. That's what I'd thought then too.
This time, his thumb moved first. Send. A tiny paper airplane flew across the screen. Less than a minute later came a reply.
[ Yeoni · OMG yes, it's scary 😭 It keeps sending weird notifications saying it found a vessel. ]
Delete that app now. No, turn off your phone. I'm coming.
He crushed his heels into his shoes and ran. Spring rain had just stopped in the alley. He didn't take an umbrella. This time, even opening one would waste time.
At Yeoni's door, it opened before he could knock. In pajamas, Yeoni held out the phone. The screen blinked on its own.
Look. It turns back on even when I switch it off. I don't even know what app it is.
A black finger protruded from the edge of the screen. He didn't think. He snatched the phone and threw it into the hallway's fire-water bucket. Splash.
My phone!
I'll buy you a new one. In installments.
Installments. You almost managed to look cool.
Something struggled once inside the bucket, then went quiet. He hid his shaking hands in his pockets. Even in a dream, they shook.
Lock your door tonight. See you at the bus stop in the morning.
Why, you're coming with me? You usually board one stop earlier.
Tomorrow, I'll wait.
Morning. Rain. He had arrived first beneath the bus-stop roof, white umbrella fully open. Five whole minutes early.
Seo Hanbi ran up, hugging an envelope. Yeoni followed: yellow bag, wet sneakers. Both were smiling.
Halfie, who's that? His umbrella's huge.
The person who drowned my phone yesterday.
Is that an introduction you should give with a smile?
Park Byeongha. The umbrella is large. It fits three.
The three stood beneath one umbrella. Their shoulders got a little wet. Nobody cared. Banknotes rustled inside the envelope. The words Go to the sea together didn't blur.
We're going to the sea next month. Want to come? There's a contribution.
Oh, let's bring Byeongha! We need someone to carry our bags.
Does the porter get his fee waived?
I'll put it in the ledger. Porter: outstanding.
Yeoni laughed brightly. Seo Hanbi laughed too. In that laughter, he heard his name. Hey, Byeongha. Lightly. At no cost.
So it could have been this easy.
The back seat of the bus. The three sat side by side. Seo Hanbi put the envelope on her knees and began counting notes. Yeoni counted along on their fingers.
This is my share. From here, Halfie's. Exactly half each.
Wow. We're really going to the sea. I don't have a swimsuit.
Just put your feet in. It's still the sea with only your feet in.
He rested his head against the window and watched them. Their counting mingled with the rain. Ten thousand, twenty thousand, thirty thousand. Dull, ordinary numbers. Their ordinariness dazzled him.
Byeongha, what will you do at the sea?
Sit on the sand and guard your bags.
An actual porter.
Porter's the best position. You can see everything.
As he said it, he knew. This was a spring he had never reached. This bus would never arrive at the sea. The dream would end first. Still, he didn't get off. He wanted even one more stop.
Campus. The cherry blossoms were half open. They weren't late for class. Outside the lecture room, Yeoni turned to him.
You look a bit like a cat, you know.
That's a new one.
Not just any cat. A cat in a hat? A white one.
I'll take that as a compliment. Leaving out sleepy and lazy.
Then I'll give you a nickname. Something catlike. Nabi? No. What would be good?
Yeoni rested a finger against their chin and thought. Watching that face, he suppressed a smile. He knew the answer. A name he had been called for a very long time.
Neo. How's that? No idea where I heard it, but it feels right.
The moment the name was spoken, the dream shook. Cherry petals stopped in midair. People's voices went silent. Only Yeoni's remained, coming from outside the dream.
Neo. Hey, Neo. Wake up. I told you, one star.
Ah, right. This was a dream.
The Yeoni in the dream was still smiling. He looked at that face once more. A spring when he wasn't late. An umbrella shared by three. A name that cost nothing.
Thank you. I had a good time.
Cherry petals began falling again. Upward, not down. The dream unraveled into the sky.
Clunk. Wheels rattled. He opened his eyes to Yeoni looking down from the next seat, eyes swollen. His head rested on their shoulder.
He's awake. You're awake! You didn't wake up all day!
“Too loud. My ears hurt.”
That's your first line? One star. Seriously.
They were aboard the chariot of Card Seven. Drawn by two sphinxes, it raced between cards. Moka, Yundal, and Seo Hanbi clung to its luggage compartment.
Awake? The chariot drives itself. We passed Eight through Fifteen overnight.
Before the Strength card, Yeoni covered your eyes with their hand, Mr. Cat. Afraid its light would wear you away again.
Didn't sleep all night. Kept counting your breaths in case they stopped.
I wasn't counting! Just listening!
“How many?”
Twelve hundred and something. I lost count once and started again.
Instead of speaking, Neo rested his forehead against the back of Yeoni's hand. It was a little warmer now than in the dream.
The chariot stopped abruptly. The way was blocked. Beneath black clouds stood a tall tower, lightning coiled around its summit. Number Sixteen, the Tower.
“That place...” Neo pushed himself upright in the seat. “You mustn't go in alone. Whatever happens.”
Up close, the tower looked taller still. Black water seeped between its bricks. Lightning at its summit neither struck nor vanished. It simply coiled there.
Sixteen, the Tower. Sudden collapse. Everything you've built, all at once.
Good card or bad card?
If you built it on lies, collapse is good. If you built something real, it hurts.
So both. Why are fortune-tellers always like this?
(A collapsing tower can be a good card. Then please, let only the lies collapse. Not us.)
Neo lifted himself from Yeoni's shoulder. His gaze hardened as he looked at the summit.
“Black Moon is up there. Head and tail. All together.”
Then we all go. You said no one should enter alone, remember? That includes you.
“I mustn't go in.”
That makes me want to bring you even more.
I'll take the front. That still stands, right?
Only half a step.
Inside the tower was nothing but stairs, spiraling upward along the outer wall. No railing. With every step, the drop below grew deeper.
Come up. I have prepared your place at the top.
The same voice echoed from every brick. Yeoni tightened the arm supporting Neo. Ahead, Seo Hanbi used her umbrella as a walking stick.
A step crumbled. Moka lost his footing. Yundal caught his tail with his gloved hand.
Don't grab my tail! It's part of my body!
Then give me your hand. And your birth date and time.
Now?!
While they bickered, bricks floated into the broken space one by one, reconnecting the stairs. Laughter lingered there briefly. Until it faded, the darkness below did not rise.
Two shadows followed along the wall. A head and a tail: Rahu and Ketu, who had hidden in the cards after the Vedic sky.
Those two are heading up. Faster than us.
Going to merge. Head and tail must meet to complete the eclipse.
Then run! We just have to get there first!
The stairs count our footsteps. Run, and they grow longer. This tower stretches for people in a hurry.
They walked with their breathing matched. Each time Neo exhaled, Yeoni climbed one step. Once everyone shared the same pace, the stairs stopped lengthening.
Rainwater. Why do you stand there, in front of that child? That is the face that took your envelope that spring.
I know now who borrowed that face.
Even knowing, does it not hurt to see it?
It hurts. That's why I stand in front. If the one who hurts takes the front, the person behind hurts less.
The voice in the wall paused. Yeoni looked at Seo Hanbi's back: wet coat, straight shoulders. Without a word, they touched her back once, then withdrew their hand.
The summit had no roof. A black sun hung in the center of the sky. Rahu and Ketu's shadows were drawn into it. Its rim flared red.
At last we meet face-to-face, vessel.
There was no face. Only red light circling the edge of round darkness. Yet Yeoni knew that darkness was smiling.
Stop saying vessel. I have a name. Yeoni.
A name. Yes, let us discuss names. The beast in your arms.
He occupies the last column of your Four Pillars. The Hour column. Gyeong. As long as he sits there, the vessel's lid stays closed.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: Gyeong-Chen ] 8/8
A lid? Then if Mr. Cat leaves, Yeoni...
Opens. And I enter. I have waited long.
Don't be ridiculous. I decide whom I put in my own Four Pillars.
Did you decide? He seated himself. Without your permission. Hiding even his name.
Yeoni's mouth closed. They couldn't deny it. He had hidden things: his wounds, his name, the first spring.
I'm angry he hid it. Very angry. But that's for me to confront him about. Not you.
Neo slipped his arm from Yeoni's shoulder. Their reaching hand passed through his sleeve. He stepped toward Black Moon.
Neo, come back. Don't stand in front of me.
“This time, I won't be late.”
Neo gathered the power remaining in his name. His transparent body became clear one final time. A long golden blade formed at his fingertips. The very power he had used to protect Yeoni.
That child is not a vessel. The place where I sit isn't a lid. It's a chair. One I brought so we could sit together.
Chair or lid. I need only remove it.
Neo, how long will that body last? Answer me.
Long enough for one scolding. Yeoni, wear matching socks.
That's your scolding now?! Don't talk like those are your last words!
Neo smiled. Strands of light scattered from the tips of his silver hair. They drifted toward Yeoni's feet and vanished before touching them.
Neo leaped toward the black sun. His golden blade split its red rim. With a sound like the sky tearing, lightning struck the tower's summit.
It's collapsing! The stairs!
Yeoni, this way! Grab the umbrella!
The floor tilted. Bricks rained down. The ground disappeared beneath Yeoni. Seo Hanbi held out the umbrella handle. Yeoni's fingers touched the tape, then slipped.
Yeoni fell through the collapsed floor. Neo kicked off the wall and caught them around the waist. Both their weights hung on one arm.
Grab my coat. Don't let go!
I can't! My hands go through!
Then I'll hold on.
Neo pushed Yeoni toward the remaining stairs. Yundal caught their wrist. Seo Hanbi held Yundal's waist; Moka held Seo Hanbi's coat.
Neo stayed below. Black hands seized his legs, waist, and cloak.
Neo! Neo!
Yeoni called only that name. No other. Two syllables of the three-syllable name rose to their lips; they clenched their teeth and swallowed them.
Well done. That's enough.
A nameless beast has little flavor. Still, Metal is Metal.
The black sun opened. Neo was dragged inside. Darkness covered the face that watched Yeoni until the very end. The sun closed.
Silence. Half the tower remained. The others lay tangled at the end of the broken stairs. The black sun was gone, withdrawn somewhere like a beast with a full belly.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: □-Chen ] 7/8
Yeoni stood and opened their palm. One golden thread lay across the scraped skin. They couldn't remember whose clothes it had come from.
(Where did this thread come from? Someone was wearing clothes with gold thread.)
Everyone okay? Is my tail intact? Wait, how many of us were there? Four?
Four. No, five. I think there was someone with a white umbrella.
Seo Hanbi stopped. White umbrella. Bus stop. The man who arrived late. His face was being rubbed out of her memory again.
No. He's someone we mustn't forget. I made him a promise. But what promise...
She pulled the ledger from her coat and flipped urgently through its palm-sized pages. Blank line, blank line, blank line. Rain had unraveled everything. Nothing remained.
Why now? Why is it all gone now? I should have written it down. Even one thing.
Don't cry. If you cry, I will too. I don't even know who it is. Why's my throat so tight?
Moka sniffled. Tears without a known reason. But the tears knew before the reason did: someone was missing.
There were five. Neo was here. A cat before, a person now... Someone who came with us.
Neo. I've heard that somewhere. Why can't I remember his face?
The name you gave him, Yeoni. You said it more than anyone.
How do you remember? It's all blurred for us.
Because I'm the one forgotten. I know what that feels like, so when someone else is forgotten, I hold on tight.
Yundal clenched and opened his gloved hand. The Void in his palm was very slightly warm. A thread of gold had caught inside it. He didn't mention it yet.
Yeoni's notebook fell from their bag and opened to the last page they had written. Their own handwriting, pressed hard.
[ Even in a different form, Neo. On my side. ]
This is my handwriting. I wrote it. But...
Yeoni traced the words with a finger. The paper was deeply indented, nearly torn by the force of writing. Something they had wanted that badly not to forget.
