Why can't I remember? I pressed so hard. It says on my side. Who was on my side?
Yeoni. Trust those words. Memories can be erased, but your hand can't lie.
Who... was Neo?
Morning never came beneath the tower. The sky had stopped at gray.
They sat in a circle among fallen bricks. No one suggested getting up first.
Yeoni looked down at their feet. A white sock on the left, a gray one on the right. Mismatched.
(Wear matching socks. Who said that? Not Mom. Mom doesn't say things like that.)
Strange. The voice of that scolding remained in their ears.
Low, sounding put-upon, with a little laughter mixed in. No face came with it.
Looking at your socks?
Yes. I think someone told me to wear matching ones.
Mr. Cat. He hated your mismatched socks more than anyone.
Mr. Cat. Is he Neo? In my note?
Yes. A cat at first, then human. We kept calling him Mr. Cat out of habit.
Yeoni opened their notebook again. They no longer knew how many times.
The same words remained plainly on the page. Even in a different form, Neo. On my side.
I've been thinking too. That cat... I think he lit a fire with my matches once. Or did I light it for him?
All I have left is a white umbrella. A rainy bus stop, a folded white umbrella. The voice saying, Too late.
The three offered one fragment each. The fragments didn't fit.
Cat, silver hair, umbrella, socks. The words remained, but they wouldn't join into one face.
Different appearances, all the same person? Why can't I recognize any of them?
Yes. The same person as a cat and as a human. The sock lectures stayed the same too.
Yeoni couldn't laugh. It felt as though everyone knew someone only they didn't.
No. Everyone half knew someone they didn't know at all.
I must be a terrible person. I wrote that he's on my side, and I don't know his face.
Yeoni took out their phone. Even in the world of destiny, its screen lit up.
An app icon: a little star set above a moonlit door. The same as the night it first appeared.
Yeoni tapped customer support. They hadn't known it could make calls. But there was a button: Call.
[ Customer Support: Universe ] [ Agents: None · Queue Position: ∞ ]
Same as ever. Definitely the app I gave one star.
The ringing went on and on. No one answered. Yeoni didn't hang up. Holding it to their ear made them feel strangely less alone.
(Someone must have called like this every day too. An unanswered phone. Trying to find someone.)
The infinity symbol in the queue flickered briefly. It nearly became a number, then returned to infinity.
Yeoni didn't see. Too tired to look at the screen, they had closed their eyes.
[ Queue Position: ∞ ] ...9,999... ∞
Their pocket warmed. Not the phone. Beside it, a card they had carried for a long time.
Dark blue, with stars patterned on the back. Yeoni's birth card.
This one. It never would turn over.
The card stirred on its own, very slowly in their palm. The stars turned downward, and the picture faced up.
[ Birth Card · 17 · The Star ]
A waterside beneath the night sky. A woman knelt, pouring from two pitchers.
One into water, one onto land. Above her, one great star and seven small ones.
The Star. The card after the Tower. The one that rises after everything has fallen.
I know this card. It was in my room. The day my umbrella blew inside out, this picture was on the floor.
The night they first opened destiny's door returned to mind. The bus card they'd given one star, the inside-out umbrella, cards scattered on the floor.
Among them, the Star. That memory remained unerased.
The card poured out light. The gray sky split, and night descended.
Water rose among the fallen bricks, clear and ankle deep. Stars reflected in it.
Where are we? Inside the card?
Inside your card, Yeoni. Usually only its owner can enter a birth card. Perhaps being together lets us come in together.
The woman from the card wasn't by the water. Only two pitchers stood there: one empty, one full.
Two pitchers. One pours into the water, one onto the land.
The Star gives back what it receives. What was received to the water; what can be shared to the earth.
Seo Hanbi lifted the full pitcher. Heavy. Rain sounded inside it, the sound that matched her name.
This is my rain. The rain I released from the ledger. It all gathered here.
Yeoni. Give me your hand. The scrape from the tower.
It's nothing.
Then it should heal even faster.
Seo Hanbi tilted the pitcher. Fine rain fell onto Yeoni's palm.
It wasn't cold. The scrape closed very slowly. Not even a scab remained.
Carrying the pitcher, Seo Hanbi went around the group. Moka's singed whiskers. Yundal's trembling palm.
Wherever the rain touched, wounds vanished one by one.
The place where I used the Void doesn't hurt. That's never happened before.
My whiskers grew back. Hanbi, if you could do this, why not sooner?
Before, I only knew how to collect.
The water in the pitcher diminished a little. Faint ledger-ink stains on the back of Seo Hanbi's hand washed away with it.
She looked at them for a long time without speaking.
The final raindrop fell onto Yeoni's left hand.
The hand they had kept clenched since the tower. Something glittered between their fingers.
A golden thread unraveled from Neo's coat. When rain touched it, the light trapped inside came alive.
Then it seeped into Yeoni's palm. It hadn't vanished. It had entered.
Hot. My chest. No, inside my chest.
Wait. Let me look at your Four Pillars again.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: □-Chen ] 7/8 · Faint Metal within the Day's Eul
There's Metal inside your Day Master. Inside Eul. That means a combination is holding.
Combination? Compatibility again?
Actual compatibility this time. Eul and Gyeong are drawn toward each other. Even after Gyeong left its column, Eul held on to a piece.
Yundal removed his glove. A golden ray was caught inside the Void in his palm too.
Light that had broken away as Neo was swallowed at the tower. Yundal's Void had held that single strand.
I had one too. I couldn't find the moment to tell you. You were crying so much.
Then Black Moon didn't eat all of him. Pieces remain. One with me, one with Yundal.
And you're Bharani, Yeoni. We saw it in the Vedic sky. The star that bears. A vessel contains. Bearing protects.
Black Moon called you a vessel. If Mr. Cat is already inside that vessel, there's no room for Black Moon.
Yeoni laid a hand on their chest. There was a warm spot. They didn't know who he was, but they knew that place existed.
I don't remember. But this handwriting is mine. This hand is mine too. If I won't trust what I wrote, who will?
Yeoni opened a fresh page and pulled the pen cap off with their teeth. They wrote down each fragment the others offered.
[ Neo · Cat, then human · Silver hair · Lots of scolding · Socks · Umbrella · Once arrived late · On my side ]
Do we really need 'lots of scolding'?
The most reliable information we have. Everyone remembers it.
Add one more. Extremely jealous of me.
Needs verification. Someone told me to believe only half of what Yundal says.
Mr. Cat said that too.
Everyone laughed. The first laughter since coming down from the tower. It spread over the star pool, making its reflected stars tremble.
At the bottom of the page, Yeoni added one more line. This time, no one dictated it. It was their own sentence.
[ Going to find him. Even without remembering. Trust my handwriting. ]
That line is a far better ledger than mine.
I won't be someone who only gets rescued again. I'll follow my own handwriting and choose our ending myself.
It's a note, not a ledger. A note with nothing to repay.
The last of the pitcher's water fell into the star pool. The reflected stars began shifting, one by one.
They formed a path toward Card Eighteen.
Next is the Moon. Eighteen. A card of deception. Not everything you see is real.
A card Black Moon would like.
If it's a card of lies, I can burn it all. I've still got two matches.
Save those two carefully, Moka. The Sun is the very next card.
Sun? That's my department. Just wait, Moon.
Suddenly you're looking impressive, Moka. One more star for you.
As Yeoni stood, they looked into the pool. Their face reflected back: swollen eyes, hair a mess.
But the Yeoni in the water was smiling. Yeoni wasn't. The reflected mouth lifted once, then twice.
As though practicing how to smile. Only on the third attempt did it resemble Yeoni's smile.
Hanbi. Look. My face...
Seo Hanbi looked into the pool and went white.
She had seen that smile before. In the first spring, at the rainy bus stop.

episodes.title: The Moon and the Sun
episodes.tag: Episode 45 · The Moon and the Sun

beats.t: Card Eighteen, the Moon. Two moons hung in the sky. One shone coldly. The other was black as its shadow.
A tower stood on either side of the path. Far away, a dog and wolf cried in turn. There was no way to tell which was the dog.
The Moon has one rule. Don't trust what you see.
Then what do we trust? Walk with our eyes shut?
Trust each other. Hold hands, call names, and check that someone answers.
Yeoni touched the notebook in their pocket. Its paper corner brushed their fingertips. That alone was a little reassuring.
(I don't know the face of the person on my side. But I know the handwriting. That's enough.)
Every puddle reflected a moon. Every puddle reflected Yeoni. Even when Yeoni stopped, the Yeoni in the water stopped half a beat late.
That's been copying me. But a little late each time.
Don't look. Step over the puddles, not in them.
Then mist descended. Ankles to knees, knees to shoulders. In an instant.
Hey, hands! Hold hands!
Yeoni reached out. Something brushed their fingertips, then slipped away. Everyone's voices receded into the mist.
Seo Hanbi stood with the umbrella open. Its taped ribs pushed back a little mist. Only Yundal remained beside her.
Moka and Yeoni went the other way. From the sound of it.
Didn't you say this was a card where we can't trust sounds?
True. So believe only half of what I'm saying too.
Footsteps approached through the mist. First a yellow bag appeared. Then Yeoni's face.
Hanbi! Found you. Yundal too.
Seo Hanbi began stepping forward, then stopped. Yeoni's sneakers were dry. After all those puddles.
Where's Moka?
We got separated over there. More importantly, Hanbi. I've been thinking.
Wasn't it your fault Neo got eaten?
The mist went quiet. Neither dog nor wolf cried.
Yeoni.
It was you in the first spring too. You opened the door. This time, you stood in front, and Neo got eaten.
Yeoni, that's...
Stay out of this, Yundal. This is between us.
Seo Hanbi's umbrella tip trembled. Her lips moved to answer, but no sound emerged. Those were the words she wrote in her ledger every night.
Yes. That's why I'm trying to repay...
Then give me the umbrella first. It was mine to begin with.
Rain began falling through the moonlight. Then more footsteps ran through the mist. Splash, splash. Straight through the puddles.
A second Yeoni appeared, soaked from head to sneakers. Their knees bore signs of a fall. Moka followed, panting.
What is that?! Why are there two Yeonis?!
Ah. Can't even half believe this.
Wet Yeoni looked at dry Yeoni. Dry Yeoni looked back. Their faces were identical, down to the swelling beneath their eyes.
What are you? What are you doing with my face?
I was about to ask you. Hanbi, that's the fake. Remember the thing smiling in the puddle?
Seo Hanbi looked between them. Dry Yeoni's smile was familiar. So familiar she couldn't breathe.
Let's verify. Yeoni's birth date and time.
July 6, 2002. Eight thirty. Eulhae Day Pillar.
Right. That's me. But that thing knows too!
Both correct. Black Moon eats Four Pillars charts. Numbers won't distinguish them.
Then my turn. Yeoni, how many stars did you first give me?
Two. Because the flavor was a crime.
Two! Seriously, it knows that too?
Both right again. This is driving me crazy.
The rain thickened. Wet Yeoni's teeth chattered. Dry Yeoni stood in the rain without getting wet. No one was calm enough to point it out.
The same face either way, rainwater. You couldn't choose in the first spring either.
Seo Hanbi raised her head. That voice. The one from behind the bus-stop bench, the one that first gave her the ledger.
I couldn't then. I can now.
Seo Hanbi closed the umbrella. Rain poured directly onto her head. Cold water soaked into her coat.
Dry Yeoni reached toward the umbrella in her hand.
Good. Give it here. It's mine.
Wet Yeoni moved too. Teeth chattering, staggering toward Seo Hanbi. Then they raised their bag to cover her head, leaving their own in the rain.
Idiot, why close the umbrella? You'll catch a cold.
Rain parted around the yellow bag. A small roof formed above Seo Hanbi. Clumsy, crooked, only half a roof.
The real Yeoni offers an umbrella first. Never asks to take one.
And if there's no umbrella, even a bag.
Seo Hanbi turned toward dry Yeoni. The folded umbrella's tip aimed at its chest.
Take off that face. It's not a face you get to own.
Dry Yeoni's smiling face cracked. Black light seeped through. The corners of its mouth split to its ears.
A pity. I meant to use it for longer this time.
The face fell away in pieces. Beneath it was nothing. One black circle devoured moonlight: the dark one of the two moons.
But it doesn't matter. Inside the Moon card, I can become anything. Your mother, your friends, even that cat.
Faces appeared in the mist: Yeoni, Seo Hanbi, Moka. Behind them stood someone with silver hair and dark blue clothes.
Neo.
The name escaped first. Yeoni couldn't recall who he was, but at the sight of the silver coat hem, their fingertips trembled.
Yeoni, that's a fake. The real one's clothes weren't that intact. His cuffs were frayed from hiding his injured arm.
Why tell me that now? It makes me want to see him more.
Enough. Everyone move. Fire for lies.
Moka struck his matches. Both remaining matches at once. Flame swelled between his fingers, then surged into the sky.
The sun rose. Card Nineteen, the Sun. Mist burned away in an instant. Faces hidden in moonlight curled like paper and vanished.
When they opened their eyes, they stood on a familiar stage beneath a noon sun. The world inside the Sun card resembled Moka's island.
Our island. The stage from the day the sun returned.
Moka, you really were the sun. Raising it with two matches.
Meaning I've used both. I'm empty-handed now. You're responsible.
Shall I put it in the ledger? Two matches, outstanding.
You said that ledger won't write anymore!
Instead of answering, Seo Hanbi shook out her wet hair and offered Yeoni a hand. Yeoni took it. Both were still drenched.
Hanbi. Thank you for what you said. But even I got confused. I thought that thing might be me.
I was confused too. The smiling faces were identical.
Then how did you choose?
The wet one. You're always the wet one, Yeoni.
A door stood open behind the Sun card's stage. A trumpet sounded beyond it. Card Twenty, Judgement.
Each time the angel in the sky blew its trumpet, a name rose from the ground. Names Black Moon had eaten. But they sank again. No one was there to call them.
Judgement calls. Someone has to call a name for it to rise.
Then I'll call them.
You have to know the owner. You only know a few names, Yeoni. I don't even know my own.
Yundal clenched his gloved hand. Black showed through the palm. The Void had grown a little.
Your hand. It's bigger than before.
I swallowed some mist today. I'm fine. It still fits in the glove.
The next door was Twenty-One, the World. A figure danced within a round laurel wreath. The card where the Fool's journey ended.
If that's the end, do we go to Black Moon now?
Normally it ends at Twenty-One. With the Fool as Zero, that's twenty-two cards. But look.
Beneath the laurel wreath, a narrow gap stood between the cards. Wide enough for one more card. Wind leaked through it.
[ 23 · THE DOOR ]
Letters appeared above the gap, then vanished. Yeoni had seen them before. In their room on the first night, before all this began.
That door. I know that door. It was in my room.
The gap widened, revealing a wooden door. Its handle was worn; the place for a nameplate was blank. No name at all.
An empty nameplate this time. Nothing to read.
That's scarier, kid.
Yundal stood before the door and removed his glove. The black circle in his palm tilted toward it, like water flowing downhill.
Beyond this, it smells like my palm. The smell of emptiness.
The Void. Black Moon's home. And probably where Mr. Cat is.
Then open it.
Very decisive. Once we enter, all five skies collapse into it. Are you ready?
I wrote it in my note. Going, even without remembering.
Yeoni gripped the handle. Cold. Then came a sound from the other side. Very faint, but unmistakable.
“Your socks. Wear matching ones.”
Yeoni's hand froze on the handle. They didn't know whose voice it was. But the tears came first. They looked down at their feet. Mismatched socks.

episodes.title: The Eclipse of Every Sky
episodes.tag: Episode 46 · The Eclipse of Every Sky

beats.t: Beyond the door was no floor. Black panels formed only where they stepped, vanishing when they lifted a foot.
There was no up or down. Far away floated a single black sun. It swallowed light instead of giving it.
The Void. A place that admits anything because it's empty. I never imagined the inside of my palm looked like this.
Thinking we're inside someone else's palm feels really weird.
Don't step on the palm lines. If my love line breaks, you're responsible, Moka.
No one laughed. Any laughter was sucked toward the black sun the moment it emerged.
It eats sound too?
Everything. That's why we can't stay long.
Yeoni took the notebook from their pocket. The first line had faded a little. They traced over it with a finger.
[ Neo · Cat, then human · Silver hair · Lots of scolding · Socks · On my side ]
We heard his voice through the door. Telling me to match my socks. He's somewhere here.
Then finding him comes first. Fighting comes afterward.
We'll probably end up fighting while we look. We always do.
The ground shook. Things fell between the black panels. Huge things. Fragments the size of buildings.
The star palace of twelve palaces fell upside down. Its rooftop stars went dark one by one.
The observatory skyship slid down with torn sails. The sky of twelve houses crumpled like a folded map.
The bell of the twenty-seven lunar mansions rang once. Then the entire temple tilted toward the black sun.
Cards from the corridor scattered like a blizzard. Finally, five islands from the sea tumbled down, small as toys.
That's our island! The Island of Expression!
All five skies are collapsing here. Black Moon left the door open and waited for us to enter.
It's destroying everything because we came in?
Not destroying. Eating. Once it's eaten everything, only one sky will remain here. That one.
Yundal pointed at the black sun. Fallen fragments orbited it, disappearing one by one.
Eyes appeared in the black sun. Not one. One for each fallen sky. Five in all.
Welcome. I have waited, vessel.
Names rose around the sun. Names Yeoni had heard along the way: black Obstruction Transformation. The dark moon Lilith. Rahu's head and Ketu's tail. The collapsing Tower.
The same thing all along. Wearing a different name in each sky.
The more names, the better. Each meal added one.
Hundreds of black hands stretched from beneath the sun. A person's name tag hung from every finger.
Give those names back. Not one belongs to you.
Rainwater, always demanding the return of others' things. Yet you never once protected your own.
Seo Hanbi tightened her grip on the umbrella. She didn't answer. Instead, she stepped forward, in front of Yeoni.
Before fighting, let us trade. I am fair. I taught the ledger-keeper that myself.
A black hand lowered before Moka. A little stage opened on its palm: the noon stage with the sun overhead, packed with an audience.
Ember. I will return every song on your island. The applause too. In exchange, withdraw.
We got our songs back by singing them ourselves. Not from you.
Moka knocked the stage away with the back of his paw. It scattered into ash.
And applause isn't borrowed. It's received. If you don't know the difference, don't perform.
Fortune-teller. Don't you want to go home? I will return your hour. The Hour of the Rabbit. And your name.
A clock appeared on the palm. Its hands trembled near five twenty. Yundal couldn't take his eyes from them.
Is that real?
Yundal.
Yundal reached out. Just before his fingertips touched the clock, he stopped. His gloved fingers trembled in midair.
Even if it's real, I won't take it. If I do, I go home. But Yeoni stays here.
And I found my own hour through birth-time rectification. No reason to receive it from you.
A black hand moved before Seo Hanbi. A rainy bus stop rested on its palm. The bus stop of the first spring. An envelope lay on the bench.
Rainwater. I will let you return. To that day, that bus stop. This time I won't interfere. The girl, the envelope, the sea—all yours.
Seo Hanbi stopped breathing. The rain sounded too real. She could read the envelope: Go to the sea together.
Back to that spring.
Hanbi.
Yeoni said only her name. Neither stopping nor holding her. Letting her choose.
If I return to that spring, the umbrella this spring's Yeoni gave me disappears. The one with three layers of tape.
I'm not going. I'll repay what I owe in this spring.
Seo Hanbi covered the bus stop with her hand, quietly, as though setting down something held for a long time. The little bus stop dissolved into rainwater.
Every one of you, so dull. Then I will ask the vessel directly.
The last hand opened before Yeoni. Neo lay curled on its palm, eyes closed, body cloudy as glass. It was impossible to tell whether he breathed.
What you have forgotten. You cannot even remember its name, can you? Empty yourself and I'll return it. Become my vessel, and it can remain inside you too. Forever.
Yeoni looked at that face. No name, no memory came. Only their palm grew hot.
Gold seeped from Yeoni's left hand, where the thread from beneath the tower had entered. The light stretched toward the black hand, then gathered in their palm again.
Ah.
What is this? Why is my hand hot?
For the first time, Black Moon's voice wavered. All five eyes turned toward Yeoni's palm.
So there it was. The piece I couldn't finish eating.
Hundreds of black hands lunged at once. At Yeoni. More precisely, at their left hand.
Yeoni, back!
Seo Hanbi opened the umbrella. Rain poured beneath it, standing as a wall that blocked the hands. Whenever a finger touched the rain, a name tag fell away.
Don't need matches. My fire comes from my mouth!
Moka drew a great breath and shouted. Rap. Rhythm and lyrics both a mess. Still, sparks flew from his voice. Several hands scorched and recoiled.
I'll eat them. Move a little.
Yundal removed his glove and held out his palm. Hands streamed into it. His face went white. The circle of the Void spread to his wrist.
Stop! It's growing!
That's what this hand is for.
But the hands were endless. The rain wall thinned. Moka's voice cracked. Yundal's knees buckled.
Why resist? Surrender one vessel and it all ends.
Yeoni held their golden left hand against their chest. If they gave up even this, the road back to that person would vanish. They didn't know why, but they knew that.
Yundal. This light. What is it?
Gyeong. Mr. Cat's Metal. A piece remained inside your vessel.
Your Four Pillars have all five energies by nature. Wood, Fire, Earth, Water, and that Metal.
Yundal indicated Seo Hanbi, Moka, himself, then Yeoni.
And we happen to have all five here. Fire, Earth, Water, Wood. Metal in your hand.
If we gather the five energies...
An eclipse forms when Sun and Moon overlap. If the five energies make one circuit, that overlap comes undone. Probably.
Why so many probablys?!
At that instant, the rain wall tore. A black hand slipped through and seized not Yeoni, but Seo Hanbi's wrist. Her right wrist, at the ring scar.
Then I shall eat Water first. Remove one of five, and nothing turns.
Seo Hanbi was dragged toward the black sun. The umbrella fell from her hand. Its taped handle rolled over the black panels.
Hanbi!
Yeoni didn't think. They picked up the rolling umbrella and ran. Their golden left hand gripped the umbrella; their right caught Seo Hanbi's other hand.
Let go! You'll be dragged in too!
No. You chose me earlier. This time, I choose.
The two were dragged together. Moka grabbed Yeoni's bag strap; Yundal grabbed Moka's waist. The four hung in a line as the black sun drew closer.
What kind of tug-of-war is this?! Our side's too weak!
Tug-of-war ends with one pull all at once. Not yet.
Then gold flared once more from Yeoni's left hand. Along the umbrella handle, along Seo Hanbi's wrist. At its touch, the black fingers flinched and loosened a little.
Give me that light. It was mine to begin with.
Don't be ridiculous. It's written in my note. On my side. The person on my side isn't yours.
The four were dragged in a line. The black sun drew close enough to fill the sky. Wind blew from its rim, without heat.
Yeoni, let go. Please.
No. The harder it pulls, the tighter I'll hold.
But the harder they pulled, the farther they were dragged. The black hand was eating Yeoni's strength too. Their pull became its power.
Yeoni, that won't work! It eats the force of pulling!
Then what? Let go?
Then a very old phrase returned. Yeoni couldn't remember who had said it. On the island, before the first ring.
(Don't pull. Push.)
Yeoni relaxed the hand pulling Seo Hanbi. Instead, they placed their left palm against her wrist, between the black fingers and the scar. The palm leaking gold.
Hanbi, take this. Don't repay it.
Gold pushed from Yeoni's palm into Seo Hanbi's wrist. The moment it touched the black fingers, they split cleanly, as though cut by a blade.
Ghh.
Seo Hanbi's wrist came free. The four tumbled onto a black panel. The umbrella rolled until Moka's foot stopped it.
Alive. Are we alive? How many fingers does everyone have? Count them.
Ten. Still ten for me too. One's a little black.
The black sun retreated briefly, like a beast withdrawing an injured hand. They used the opening to gather on the widest panel.
Yeoni opened their left hand. The gold was fainter than before, no more than a small ember.
It's smaller. By the amount I pushed into Hanbi.
Because of me, the piece is this small.
No. I chose. And it worked. You're here now.
Seo Hanbi held her right wrist instead of answering. The scar was warm, a temperature she had never felt there before. Moisture beaded where Metal had passed.
Wait. Seo Hanbi, let me see that wrist.
Yundal examined it. A droplet above the scar glittered with gold. He gave a short laugh.
That's it. What you just did, Yeoni—that's the answer.
Meaning? Simple words. I'm on fire duty, not thinking duty.
The five elements generate one another. Wood makes Fire, Fire makes Earth, Earth makes Metal, Metal makes Water, and Water returns to nourish Wood.
[ Wood → Fire → Earth → Metal → Water → Wood ]
Your Metal just entered Seo Hanbi and became Water. Metal generates Water. Mr. Cat's energy gave birth to rain.
My rain came from Mr. Cat.
That's the natural order. You're a summer tree, Yeoni, so your chart needs Water. That Water comes from Metal. Mr. Cat was always the one who brought rain.
(Is that why the cat always carried an umbrella? When he was human.)
Yeoni startled at their own thought. An umbrella when human? They had no memory of seeing that. Yet the note said it: Umbrella when human.
So make a circuit. Five of us holding hands, each pushing energy to the next. Not pulling.
Then the order matters. Who stands beside whom?
Like a compatibility reading. This one is free.
Yundal drew a circle on the black panel with his finger and assigned a person to each of five positions.
Yeoni is Wood. A vine, so first. Moka is Fire, on Yeoni's right.
Wood feeds me, right? Yeoni, raise me well. Expensively.
I'm Earth. After Fire. The Void is Earth, empty ground that can hold anything.
Then since I'm Water...
Seo Hanbi comes after Metal, to Yeoni's left. The problem is Metal's place.
The fifth place stood empty, between Yundal and Seo Hanbi. No one occupied it.
The cat's place.
Yes. That's why I brought this.
Yundal removed his glove. A golden thread hung at the Void's rim: the light he had caught when Neo disappeared at the tower.
The only useful thing this hand has eaten. Good thing I didn't throw it away.
You've kept it all this time?
I couldn't just throw away a clue that might bring someone else's husband back.
He's not my husband! Yet!
Yet?
Yeoni blushed. They had no idea why they'd said yet. Seo Hanbi laughed softly. This time, not just a shoulder shake, but a sound.
After the circle was drawn, no one spoke for a moment. Far away, the black sun caught its breath.
Yundal. That clock earlier. Did you really not regret leaving it?
Of course I did. Five twenty. Seeing the hands there took my breath away.
But if I received it from Black Moon, I'd spend my life as someone who borrowed time from it. I didn't want that.
Borrowed things grow. I know that well.
If the ledger expert says so, it must be true.
What will you do when you get home, Yundal?
Call my mother. See whether she remembers my voice. If not, I'll introduce myself again.
Yundal smiled, but his gloved hand was clenched. Yeoni rested a hand briefly over that fist, then lifted it.
She'll remember. We remember you. Your mother will too.
What are you plotting?
The black sun approached again. This time not its hands, but the sun itself descended. All five eyes fixed on Yeoni.
Now. Hold hands!
Five formed a circle: Yeoni, Moka, Yundal, the golden thread in the empty place, Seo Hanbi. Yundal set the thread afloat, and it stretched taut in midair.
Moka, take it!
Yeoni drew a deep breath and pushed it into Moka's hand. Vines spread across the back of their hand. Fire bloomed in Moka's palm, far larger than a match flame.
Whoa, what's this? Feels like I've got firewood!
Moka pushed the fire toward Yundal. As it touched his palm, the rim of the black circle hardened like fired clay.
Hot. But for the first time, my hand doesn't feel empty.
Yundal added Earth's energy to the golden thread. One strand split into many, tracing shoulders and hands in the empty place.
Neo's shape stood there briefly. Only a faceless golden outline. It turned toward Seo Hanbi and breathed out.
Received. Yeoni, my turn to give.
Rain poured from Seo Hanbi's umbrella. Not cold rain. It fell onto Yeoni's head, shoulders, left palm. Beneath it, the faded gold brightened again.
It went around. A full circuit!
A circle. Break it in one place, and it ends.
A black hand slipped behind Yundal. The Void suddenly gaped wide. Earth's energy began leaking from his hand.
Ah. This is a little...
You don't touch someone standing beside me!
Moka gripped Yundal's hand tighter. Fire wrapped the Earth as though firing it again. Yundal's palm hardened once more.
The five energies began circling. One turn, two. Faster each time. A bright five-pointed star formed on the black panel.
Stop. That is not something a vessel can do.
I told you, I'm not a vessel. I'm Lee Yeoni. A university student. I write star reviews and I'm bad at matching socks.
The star flew into the center of the black sun, where Sun and Moon overlapped. Cracks split the overlapping rims. Ancient light leaked through.
It's splitting! Splitting open!
Something's shining inside. Something tiny.
White. Something white.
The overlap is coming apart. But it won't hold long. It's closing again.
The split was barely wide enough for one person. Deep inside, something white flickered faintly, no larger than a firefly.
Yeoni looked at that light. Still no name came. But their feet moved toward the gap first.
You can't go alone. That's a mouth waiting to eat the vessel.
I know. But only a vessel can go in there, right? If I'm a vessel, that can be useful too.
Once you enter, I'll hold the entrance with the Void. Not for long. One song at most.
Then I'll sing. Come out before it ends. No encore.
Seo Hanbi placed the umbrella in Yeoni's hand. The handle with three layers of tape.
Take it. It's a loan. You must come back to repay it.
You just used your ledger voice.
Just this once.
Umbrella in hand, Yeoni jumped through the gap. Behind them, Moka's dreadful rap began. It grew fainter.
As they fell, sounds went out one by one. Rap, rain, their own breath. Only the umbrella handle in their hand was warm.
(When scared, notes. Going to find him. Even without remembering. Trust my handwriting.)
Inside was deep and still. Neo lay on his side on the floor. His glass-transparent body moved slowly. He opened his eyes.
“Who are you?”
I'm not quite sure either. But I came to find you. That's what my note says.
Neo couldn't get up. Propped on one arm, he looked up at Yeoni. His lower body rippled like a reflection in water.
Nothing surrounded them. Only fragments of swallowed things drifted like dust: a birthday-cake candle, a graduation photograph, a name tag.
“A note. Strange one, aren't you? You came all this way trusting one note.”
Yes. It's my handwriting.
“I don't know you. I'm sorry.”
Pain stabbed Yeoni's chest. They couldn't remember him either, yet hearing that he didn't know them felt like abandonment.
That's okay. I don't know you either. We're even.
“Even?” Neo gave a short laugh. “I've heard that way of talking somewhere.”
(Somewhere. I hope it was from me.)
Yeoni sat beside Neo and laid the umbrella across their knees. His gaze rested on its taped handle.
“That umbrella. Three layers.”
How do you know?
“I don't. I just noticed. Two would have been enough.”
Three makes me feel better.
Neo's eyebrows shifted slightly. Yeoni didn't miss that tiny response.
My note says you scold a lot.
“Slander.”
See? Already talking plenty. Silver hair matches too. Cat, then human... I must have seen that myself.
“What's this about socks?”
No idea. But apparently you talked about them all the time. Yundal said so.
“Who is Yundal?”
Someone you were very jealous of. I almost added that to the note too.
Neo tilted his head. Somehow the gesture was familiar. Yeoni tried to smile and choked up instead.
How touching. But time is short, vessel.
The surrounding darkness became a voice. Every time its sound touched Neo, his outline faded.
You want him back? There is one way. Speak his true name. It is written on the floor.
Three syllables appeared beneath Neo. The space between the first and last was blank.
[ Park □ Ha ]
The middle's missing.
You know it. On the tip of your tongue, isn't it? Say it and every memory returns. Every day you shared with him.
It really was on the tip of their tongue. The shape of that syllable. All they had to do was say it. Everything lost beneath the tower seemed ready to return at once.
Let me show you what you lost.
Scenes flashed over the darkness. A cat on a rainy night. A hat-wearing cat on an island, dark blue cloak streaming. A large hand tilting an umbrella. Only the face remained hidden.
Show me his face. Just his face.
Speak the name and you'll see. A simple trade.
“Don't say it.”
Neo raised his head. For the first time, strength returned to his eyes.
“I don't know you, but don't say that name. I don't know why. I only know you mustn't.”
If I do, you disappear.
Neo couldn't answer. Yeoni stared at the blank space on the floor.
I wrote this down too.
Yeoni opened the notebook. Wet paper had blurred in places, but it was still readable.
[ Neo · Cat, then human · Silver hair · Lots of scolding · Socks · Umbrella · Once arrived late · On my side ]
There's no Park-whatever anywhere here. This is the only name I wrote.
That isn't a name. It's a nickname you invented.
Right. I invented it. So it's mine. You can't eat it.
Yeoni laid a hand on Neo's forehead. The gold renewed by rain spread slowly from their palm.
Neo.
Nothing happened. Once more.
Neo. Wake up. I told you, one star.
Neo's eyes opened wide. White light filled his blurred fingertips. The joints of his fingers became clear one by one.
“I believe I said I wouldn't get up until I received five stars.”
You never said that.
“I did. In a dream. Under cherry blossoms.”
Light spread along his arms, shoulders, chest. The darkness erasing him withdrew. A pulse beat beneath Yeoni's palm.
The hand they had first held on the ship. The face always beside them. No stranger was returning. Their shared time was finding its place.
Sorry I'm late. Again.
Late again. Definitely one star.
One is enough. Better than zero.
The cat of the first night. Breath supported on the island. The first hand held on the ship. Even the last scolding as they were pushed up from the tower. Scattered memories linked together.
Socks. You told me to wear matching socks. What kind of last words are those, idiot?
Everything else was too long. I wanted to leave you at least that.
The middle syllable returned too. Yeoni knew it. They rolled it silently inside their mouth. Made no sound.
I know your name. I remember everything. But I won't say it. You're Neo. The name I gave you.
Do you remember what I hid now?
Yes. That you'd disappear if your name was spoken. Why decide that alone? You should have asked me.
Because you'd have said no.
Of course I'd say no! That's why you should have asked!
Yeoni hit his chest with a fist. Not very hard. The second fist simply stayed there.
Decide something like that alone again and you get negative stars.
I don't believe negative ratings exist.
They do now.
The light subsided. Neo stood in human form, clear to his toes. Only after taking his hand did Yeoni lift their head.
What have you done? That name has no value. No power.
A powerless name requires no payment. Even the universe probably didn't know that.
Yeoni's left hand heated again. Not only the palm this time. Inside their chest, where the empty column of their chart had been.
Yeoni! Can you hear? Now! Eul and Gyeong, if you two unite!
Yundal's voice came from beyond the gap. Moka's rap continued, voice cracking, rhythm faltering.
Yeoni's Eul and Neo's Gyeong drew together. Like a vine winding around a metal pillar. Metal supporting the vine instead of cutting it.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: Gyeong-Chen · 8/8 ]
Full. All eight spaces. The space that was empty since the app first appeared.
The Eul–Gyeong union. Wood and Metal unite into Metal. A blade, not a vessel.
No. It must be empty. A vessel must be empty.
But I'm full. With nothing borrowed from anyone. All my own.
If the vessel fills, where am I to go? Where am I...
At last, Black Moon's voice grew small. Like a hungry child's. For a fleeting moment, Yeoni felt pity in that sound.
You decide. In your own place, not someone else's vessel. But it won't be here.
Neo stepped in front of Yeoni. Silver hair and gold-embroidered clothes stood clear in the darkness. This time, using light didn't wear his body away.
Let's go. Everyone's waiting. If Moka's rap gets any longer, that'll be the greater danger.
The black sun collapsed from within. The moment the vessel filled, Black Moon lost its support. Yeoni and Neo were flung through the split.
They tumbled onto a black panel. Moka's rap stopped dead on its last line. Yundal withdrew his hand and sank down.
Out. Both of you. No encore needed.
I said one song, and you sang three. Moka, you really are fire.
Mr. Cat.
Seo Hanbi.
They faced each other. Neo, freed from a cat's body; Seo Hanbi, freed from a tiger's. People who had crossed the same spring to reach this place.
Thank you. For staying beside this one.
Repaying me? Then I'll accept. This once.
What did you two do in there, anyway? Why's Yeoni's face red?
Nothing! I just called his name!
Just a name, and the Hour Pillar filled? With compatibility that strong, I should retire.
Yundal. Remove that hand. From Yeoni's shoulder.
Ah, that jealousy. You're truly back.
There was no time to celebrate. The black sun screamed. Its five eyes burst one by one. It shrank: fist-sized, then seed-sized.
This isn't over. If there are no skies to eat, I can eat what lies beneath them.
The black seed pierced a panel and fell. They had thought only darkness lay below. But where it fell, an enormous root appeared.
That's... the root of every sky. The World Tree.
If it eats that, not just five skies but every sky ends. Reality too.
Then we follow. All together.
I'll take the front too this time. A whole step, not half.
My voice is gone. You lot make the noise this time. Especially the cat.
Yundal silently put his glove back on. The black circle spread to his wrist and showed beyond it. No one mentioned it.
Neo offered his back. Yeoni hesitated, then wrapped their arms around his shoulders. This time, their hands didn't pass through. They held his back a little tighter.
They descended along the root for a long time. Where darkness ended stood one tree, larger than all five skies combined.
Small papers hung from its branches instead of leaves. Each bore eight spaces: someone's birth year, month, day, and hour.
The World Tree. The tree holding every Four Pillars chart. A legend among fortune-tellers. It really exists.
Every paper is a person?
Yes. Yours, mine, Yeoni's mother's—somewhere up there.
(Mom's too. Somewhere there.)
Don't look for it. Once you see it, you'll want to touch it. These papers hold other people's time.
I won't. It's enough to know it's there.
Yeoni looked up. Paper leaves rustled whenever the wind blew. Billions of birthdays whispering at once.
But another sound mingled with the rustling. Something gnawing.
A black hole had opened in the middle of the trunk. Seed-sized Black Moon was burrowing inside. Growth rings around the hole blackened one by one.
It's eating the rings. Each line is a year of someone's life.
Several paper leaves fluttered from above. Their writing vanished before they reached the ground.
What happens to those people when their papers are erased?
In reality, someone loses a year. A birthday slips from memory, or a name grows faint. Like what happened to me.
The roots are drying. I'll water them.
Seo Hanbi held the umbrella upside down. Rain gathered in it, then overflowed, soaking along the roots. Withered rootlets lifted one by one.
I should do something too. Burn that thing out?
No! This is a tree! Set it on fire and the world becomes firewood!
Fire's the only thing I know!
Warmth, not fire. You did it on our island. When the sun rose.
Moka closed his mouth, then pressed both paws to the trunk. Warmth spread instead of flame. Frost melted from the bark. Sleeping birds among the leaves woke.
So that's how. Warming without burning.
Moka, that was rather impressive.
Don't praise me. It's awkward. You were easier when you wrote ledgers.
Seo Hanbi laughed aloud. Droplets at the umbrella's tip trembled with her laughter.
I'll widen the hole and pull it out.
Neo raised a hand. A golden blade formed at his fingertips, then stopped just before touching the tree.
Why stop?
My power cuts Wood. To get it out, I'd have to split this trunk too.
Neo's hand trembled. Yeoni remembered matching breaths with him on the island. His voice saying he could hurt them.
Then don't cut. Support it. Like you supported me.
Neo withdrew the blade and braced the trunk with both hands. Gold wrapped the tree like a prop. The splitting growth rings stopped.
This won't get it out. But I can keep the tree from falling.
That's right. That's always been your part. Supporting.
Support it. Hold on. In the end, I am still inside.
A black hand reached from the trunk. Not hundreds this time. Just one, thick and enormous. It crawled upward along the grain.
This tree is my final body. To remove me, you must kill it. To save it, you must leave me.
Coward! Hiding in someone else's home and threatening us!
That is how I live. Entering empty places. Your vessel has filled, so this is all I have left.
Yeoni turned those words over. Living in empty places. A place that admits anything because it is empty.
(Empty. An empty place. Where did I hear that?)
Yeoni turned. Yundal was already removing his glove.
You know it too. Emptiness is hungry. I was only hungry from the beginning.
I know you're hungry. But you can't eat other people's birthdays. Those belong to them.
Then what should I eat? I have no birthday.
Yeoni couldn't answer. The question lingered strangely in their ears. Something without a birthday. Something no one called by name.
Yeoni. I thought what you just thought too.
No. I didn't think it. I really didn't.
Emptiness eats emptiness. My palm is the hole Black Moon first made. It opened when Blue Rabbit ate my hour. It belonged to that thing originally.
So I'm giving it back. To its owner. Very tightly.
If you swallow it, you'll...
I know. We don't know how large the Void will grow. I might be emptied with it.
That isn't repayment. It's simply disappearing.
I'll do it. I used to be on Black Moon's side. The one who owes a debt should do it.
Your hands are Water, Seo Hanbi. Water can't fill a hole like this. It just flows in. This has to be my hand.
Never thought I'd hear that from you. You've grown, our ledger expert.
Smiling, Yundal pressed his bare palm against the black hole in the trunk. The dark circle spreading to his wrist met it.
A sucking sound rose, like a very long, deep breath. The black hand tore free of the trunk and was drawn into Yundal's palm.
Let go. This is my hole. I made it.
Exactly. You made it. You should fill it.
Yundal's face went white. The black circle spread beyond his wrist to his elbow. His outline began fading.
Uh, that person. Who was he? His name...
Moka stopped mid-sentence. His lips moved, but no name came out. He looked shocked at himself.
Yundal!
Yeoni shouted. The name hung in the air. At its sound, Yundal's outline sharpened a little.
That's an alias. A month that exists and doesn't. It doesn't stick well.
Alias or not, it's the name we called you! Neo came back with a nickname!
Yundal. Yundal.
Yundal! You can ask my birthday! I'll tell you everything!
Each time his name was called, another layer of Yundal's outline returned. Four voices held him to the ground.
Yundal. I'm not done telling you to take your hand off Yeoni's shoulder. Come back.
Ah, that makes me want to return. To be envied.
The last strand was swallowed. The black circle on Yundal's palm contracted. Smaller, smaller. Finally, one dot.
Then even the dot vanished. What remained was an ordinary palm. Lines, calluses, a slight tremble.
Black Moon's voice was gone. The last thing left was a tiny sigh. No one could tell whether it was a sigh of fullness or hunger.
(Goodbye. Next time, be born somewhere you have a birthday.)
It closed. The Void. Emptiness ate emptiness, and filled.
Yundal clenched and opened his hand again and again, as though the feeling of closing it were new.
The trunk's hole healed too. Blackened growth rings returned to brown. Fallen paper leaves rode the wind back to their branches.
Yundal. I remember your name. Why couldn't I before? Sorry.
It's fine. I don't know my own name either.
At that moment, a small light rose above Yundal's wrist. A clock hand. Five twenty. It stopped precisely there.
[ Hour of the Rabbit · 05:20 · Returned ]
My hour. My real hour. Five twenty in the morning. Just before sunrise.
Yundal said nothing for a long time. Then he rubbed his eyes with the back of his hand. No one teased him.
Your name too? Your real name?
Secret. We're not home yet. I'll tell you at my front door.
Smooth to the very end.
You too, Mr. Cat. Your voice trembled when you called my name.
It did not.
It did. I heard. One more star.
The treetop opened. From the tip of its highest branch, a card descended slowly. A blank card with no illustration.
Only a number appeared at the top: 23. The name field was empty. No picture, no words.
The twenty-third card. A destiny no one has written yet.
If it's empty, won't someone come to eat it again?
That's why someone must write it. This time a writer, not a devourer.
Then Yeoni's phone rang in their pocket. It hadn't rung once since they entered this world.
[ Customer Support: Universe · 1 waiting to connect ]
One waiting. Not 9,999.
Answer. This time, they'll pick up.
Yeoni paused their thumb over the call button. Everyone watched: Moka, Yundal, Seo Hanbi, Neo. Not one missing.
Ready to write my review. A five-star one.

episodes.title: A Name to Read, a Destiny to Write
episodes.tag: Episode 50 · A Name to Read, a Destiny to Write

beats.t: The phone rang twice. Instead of a third ring came a click. Every leaf of the World Tree rustled at once, then stopped.
Thank you for waiting. Destiny Customer Support. This is the universe.
The voice came from everywhere: tree, earth, Yeoni's phone. Excessively polite.
You know how long I waited? The queue was infinite!
Yes, valued customer. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. We are currently experiencing high inquiry volumes across the universe.
The universe was the agent? The agent was the universe?
Both, apparently.
We've reviewed your case. Destiny-code damage: eighty-seven percent. Cause: Black Moon. Resolution: Black Moon eliminated. Four Pillars restored to eight of eight.
You knew everything?
Everything is recorded, valued customer. Processing was merely delayed.
Late is always the problem.
Neo grumbled under his breath. Yeoni almost laughed. At this particular moment, he had the least right to say that.
May I ask something? Does that record include everything I did?
Yes, valued customer. Without exception. The applause you erased and the name you returned are on the same page.
Seo Hanbi lowered her head without making excuses. Only her fingers tightened on the umbrella handle.
Then the money I earned from compatibility readings must be there too.
Yes. Three refund requests have been filed.
People complain to the universe? Who filed them?
One final procedure remains: completing Card Twenty-Three. An empty destiny invites something else in.
The blank card descended before Yeoni, along with a pen. The very ballpoint clipped to their notebook.
I write it? Write what? What if I misspell something?
One line. The line you write becomes this door's rule. Please choose carefully.
Yeoni. One line can be anything. Truly anything.
Yeoni took the pen. Too many wishes crowded their mind: their mother's year, Yundal's name, Seo Hanbi's first spring. And Neo.
For your information, upon completing their mission, guardians return to their original place, leaving their memories of this world behind. This is policy.
The hand holding the pen stopped. Yeoni looked at Neo. He didn't look surprised.
You knew?
From the beginning. When I return, I'm Park-whatever. Someone who doesn't know you.
Stop saying Park-whatever. It's irritating.
Their surroundings became the card corridor. Countless cards floated like stars, like the sky viewed from the World Tree's crown. It was quiet, as though only the two remained.
Then I can write that line. Neo returns with his memories. Like that.
You could.
But if I do...
Yeoni couldn't finish. They looked up. Paper leaves fallen from the World Tree still scattered the ground, their names erased.
I can't return those people's names. Dodam's. Museong's. Yundal's real name.
I know.
Why do you always know everything? So irritating.
Neo rested his forehead against Yeoni's shoulder. Warm breath touched them. The ends of his silver hair tickled their cheek.
You've already given me a name. That's enough. Write what you want.
That's the most unfair thing to say.
I know.
Yeoni buried their face in his shoulder. He smelled of rain mixed with sunlight. A scent that had been beside them before his appearance changed.
If I find you again, don't pretend you don't know me.
I won't be pretending. I truly won't know.
Then I'll make you know me. Even if I have to bombard you with bad ratings.
A little frightening.
Yeoni wiped their tears with the back of their hand and set the pen to the card. The writing was crooked. They didn't correct it.
[ 23 · THE DOOR · Every swallowed name returns to its owner. The door opens from inside too. ]
As the final word was written, the card shone. An illustration formed: one door. A half-open wooden door, with an umbrella leaning beside it.
Received. A fine line, valued customer. Especially the latter part.
I just wrote that part. It's only fair for a door to open from inside too.
Indeed. We had overlooked that clause. This door will now open from both sides.
Neo lifted his head, then pressed his lips together, as though he had caught the hidden meaning first.
The World Tree's leaves rose together. Writing refilled every erased paper. Names scattered on the wind, seeking their owners.
A drum sounded far away. Small hands playing a clumsy rhythm. Yeoni knew it, a rhythm heard on the Island of Expression.
Dodam. Dodam must have found their name.
Then singing. Not a crow's broken voice, but a boy's voice, clear and slightly trembling.
Museong. He's singing. No one's laughing at him. Though he's a little off-key.
Yundal looked at his palm. A name rode the wind and settled on its lines. He stared at it for a long time.
Ah.
What does it say?
Secret, remember? I said I'd tell you at my front door.
We're at a door! There's a door right there!
Yundal looked at the half-open wooden door and smiled as though conceding.
Saebyeok. Kang Saebyeok. Mom named me Dawn because I was born at five twenty in the morning.
Saebyeok. Much better than Yundal.
I'll still use Yundal for compatibility readings. Better for business.
Seo Hanbi lifted the inside of her cloak. The place where names had been sewn was empty. Only a few loose threads remained.
All gone. No names left for me to carry.
Do you miss them?
No. I feel light. It's been so long since I felt this light that it's a little strange.
Farewells began before the door. Nobody wanted to speak first. Finally, Moka folded his arms and stepped forward.
I'm staying here. Have to teach the island to sing again. Rap included.
Perhaps leave out the rap.
Rap is the point! Change that rating. Five stars this time.
Five stars. Because the flavor is a crime.
Don't delete the app. I'll message you. Seriously.
Yundal—no, Kang Saebyeok—offered his hand. Yeoni took it. A hand without a glove. Warm.
If we meet in reality, don't pretend you don't know me. I'm tired of being forgotten.
I'll pretend if you ask my birthday.
Occupational hazard. Incurable.
You've held that hand too long.
We're saying goodbye. Allow that much, Mr. Cat.
I gave you three seconds. They're up.
Seo Hanbi stood beside Yeoni, holding the umbrella with three layers of tape. She too would return through the same door. As names returned to their owners, the name Seo Hanbi returned to reality.
I have work to do over there. Much to repay. Without a ledger.
Finally, Neo remained. Sitting side by side before the door, the two gazed at it silently for a while.
Before the open door, the twenty-third card split into two lights. One showed a cherry-blossom riverbank, the other a moonlit World Tree.
The card you wrote does not command only a return. You may now choose where to make your life.
Whichever we choose, our memories remain? No condition that makes us lose someone again?
Memories and bonds are preserved through both doors. One is not a wrong answer, nor is the other an escape.
I'll follow your choice. If a guardian chooses even your ending for you, that isn't protection.
I'll return to reality and repair what I damaged. But your home is yours to choose, Yeoni.
Wherever you live, I'm sending you my rap. They say the twenty-third door doesn't block news.
Yeoni looked slowly at both doors. This time, it wasn't about surviving a structure someone else had arranged. It was choosing their own next spring.
[ The Twenty-Third Card · I choose the world I will live in ]

options.label: Stay in the world of fortune

beats.t: A week passed. Yeoni's search history filled with names beginning with Park. Park Minsu, Park Junho, Park Seonghun. None right.
Searching only Parks will never end. Better find another clue.
The notebook's last page had gained more lines. Park-whatever. Possibly white hair. Obsessed with socks. Sensitive about star ratings.
That's all my clues? If I were a detective, I'd be fired.
Still, the bad luck had truly stopped. Toast fell butter-side up; buses arrived on time. Yeoni felt a little wistful about it.
Good luck is nice. But there's no one to tease.
Yeoni left a cushion in the empty place at the foot of the bed. Every morning they looked at it, and every morning felt a little foolish.
A thud came from outside the door, followed by something spilling. Yeoni slipped on their slippers and opened up.
Potting soil scattered the hallway. Seo Hanbi knelt in the middle, a new plant pot in each hand.
Oh. Was that loud? I'm sorry.
What's all this?
The lady in 302's pots. I broke them that day. With my tiger tail.
Yeoni remembered. The night black hands reached from the phone. A black tiger racing across the hallway. The place its tail had swept.
You remembered that?
I wrote everything down. Not in a ledger. Just a notebook.
Neat handwriting lined the notebook she offered. Some entries ended in a small circle. Others were unchecked.
[ Two plant pots, 302 ○ · Hallway window ○ · Twelve convenience-store umbrellas · Security-office chair · And Yeoni ]
What's the last line? I'm not an object.
I don't know when I'll be able to circle that one. It's the biggest line.
Yeoni couldn't find words. Seo Hanbi began scooping soil with her hands. Beneath her nails, black dirt gathered, at odds with her elegant politeness.
I'll help. Let me get a broom.
No, this is mine to...
Insisting on cleaning the dirt alone is stubbornness. Repayment and stubbornness are different.
They swept in silence. The door to 302 opened. The elderly woman saw the new pots and widened her eyes.
I'm the one who broke them. I'm sorry.
She looked at Seo Hanbi for a long time, then pressed one pot back into her hands.
She says keep one. Your room looks like it has no greenery.
I shouldn't accept.
Practice receiving too. Like the bread.
Seo Hanbi held the pot in both hands. She looked as lost as she had before bread offered at no price. Then she gave a small bow.
Thank you. I'll take good care of it. Truly, this time.
How will you repay twelve convenience-store umbrellas? Tiger tail again?
Claws that time. So I've arranged to work there. Night shifts. I asked them to deduct the umbrellas from my wages.
The owner agreed?
He called me strange. But he took me on. There are more people willing to accept strange people than I expected.
After saying it, Seo Hanbi looked slightly surprised, as though amazed those words had come from her own mouth.
That afternoon, a new tent stood outside the campus gate. Its handwritten sign read: Compatibility readings. First session free. Birth time unknown? I'll work it out.
This man. Honestly.
Customer, birth date and time first. Oh, Yeoni. Free customers aren't my favorite.
It says first session free.
Yours isn't the first. I read you fifty times over there.
Kang Saebyeok. The man called Yundal in the world of destiny. He no longer wore gloves. His palm held ordinary lines.
Do people remember you now?
Yesterday a regular called my name. 'Saebyeok.' I almost cried on the spot.
I called Mom too. Her first words were, 'Have you eaten?' After three years.
What did you say?
Lied and said yes. Family tradition.
Yeoni laughed and sat in a tent chair. Yundal—no, Saebyeok—opened his perpetual calendar without asking.
How's Hanbi? Doing well?
Sweeping soil in the hallway. Carrying a notebook.
Atonement her way. A notebook instead of a ledger. A good upgrade.
Aren't you bored without Mr. Cat? You fought every day.
Honestly, a little. Without anyone getting jealous, reading your palm isn't as fun.
You're looking for a Park, I hear. Among four million of them.
How do you know?
You walk around holding your phone with your search history visible. Half of divination is observation.
Saebyeok pointed to Yeoni's chart: Year Im-o, Month Byeong-o, Day Eulhae, Hour Gyeong-Chen. All eight spaces filled.
Gyeong has returned. The severed connection is restored. It could be a clue to finding him.
Stop using that expression.
Looking at this week's yearly influence: an eastern waterside. Before the blossoms fall. Where a helpful person stands.
Eastern waterside means the river. Do you know how many kilometers of riverbank Seoul has?
Find the rest with your legs. A reading gives direction. The rest is footwork.
Yeoni stopped as they stood. Dark clouds gathered outside the tent. Saebyeok glanced at the sky.
And rain this evening. Take an umbrella. An extra one too.
Six in the evening. A sudden shower poured down. Yeoni opened their yellow umbrella and ran beneath the bus-stop roof. The umbrella with three layers of tape.
Someone stood at the roof's edge without an umbrella, one shoulder half wet. Seo Hanbi.
Hanbi. Your umbrella?
I don't have one. The black umbrella vanished with the ring. It was never mine.
Rain drummed on the roof. The bus didn't come. They stood side by side, watching traffic lights spread across puddles.
It was here. Where you shared your umbrella with me in the first spring. This bus stop.
I don't remember.
I know. That made me glad. Because you didn't know that spring, I could begin repaying you from the start.
Yeoni tilted the umbrella halfway over Seo Hanbi's wet shoulder. Their own left shoulder soaked in the rain.
Don't. If you do, I...
I know. You said I did this then too.
Seo Hanbi's face crumpled. Not into the collapse of madness. More like someone who had held on for a long time finally sitting down.
Yeoni. I have no right to ask forgiveness.
Black Moon deceived me, but the hand that collected your fortune was mine. I shouldn't accept this umbrella with that hand.
I know. That's why I want to decide.
Yeoni adjusted their grip on the umbrella. Rain ran in lines from its edge.
You've repaid the pots. The window too. The twelve umbrellas aren't done. Keep repaying those.
Yes.
But separately from that, I forgive you now. I've decided.
Seo Hanbi looked at Yeoni like someone who didn't understand, then someone who did. She took one long breath.
Can you decide so easily?
It wasn't easy at all. I thought about it all week. Between searching for Parks.
Between?
The Park search is the main event. Sorry.
Seo Hanbi laughed aloud with a wet face. It was the first time Yeoni heard her laugh aloud then.
The rain thinned. Sunset leaked between the clouds. Wet asphalt glittered orange.
May I ask one thing? We made a promise that spring.
The sea?
You remember?
No. You told me. The day you returned the umbrella, after the water cleared.
You remembered that?
I wrote it in my notebook. Right above Park-whatever.
Yeoni swiped through the phone calendar. After cherry blossoms, before the rainy season. One square was empty.
Second Saturday in May. Let's go to the sea. I'll make gimbap.
Then I'll buy umbrellas. Two. With my own money this time.
[ App notification · Moka: Going to the sea? Without me? Prepare for bad reviews. ]
How did he know?
I think the universe tattled.
The bus came. Seo Hanbi boarded first. Folding the umbrella, Yeoni saw something across the street.
The road toward the river. Beneath a cherry tree still holding blossoms, a man's back as he folded a white umbrella. A strand of hair caught the light and looked white.
Oh.
The man sneezed. Seeing a stray cat pass his feet, he stepped back, like someone allergic to cat fur.
The bus doors closed. Yeoni pressed a palm to the window. The man walked east, toward the river.
Yeoni? What's wrong? Someone you know?
No idea. A stranger. But that sneeze...
Yeoni couldn't finish. They pulled out the notebook and hurriedly wrote beneath the last line: White umbrella. Cat allergy. Toward the river.
Eastern waterside. Before the blossoms fall.

episodes.title: A Promise by the Cherry-Blossom River
episodes.tag: Episode 52 · A Promise by the Cherry-Blossom River

beats.t: Monday. The moment classes ended, Yeoni took their bicycle to the riverbank. Eastern waterside. Before the blossoms fall. Those were all the clues.
Tuesday, three bridges. Wednesday, five. No white umbrella anywhere. Only cherry blossoms falling faster each day.
Once all the flowers fall, that's it? Are readings that cruel?
[ App notification · Kang Saebyeok: Thursday. Last day before the blossoms fall. Your daily fortune looks good. Reading fee later. ]
Why charge me? Do you know how many kilometers that eastern waterside covers? Pay for my calves first.
Even so, Yeoni pedaled. Today they'd deliberately worn mismatched socks. Yellow on the left, stripes on the right.
A test. If it's really him, he won't let this pass.
Putting on those socks that morning, Yeoni had laughed alone. The world's strangest investigation method.
[ App notification · Moka: Found him? If not, I'll cheer you on with rap. Yo yo, Mr. Park, where you at? ]
That's interference, not encouragement.
Wind blew from the river. A handful of petals fell from a cherry tree on the embankment. Yeoni started counting them, then stopped. Counting made them more anxious.
What if it really ends when the flowers fall? With him still not knowing me?
Yeoni gripped the handlebars. The center of their palm felt slightly warm. Where the Metal fragment had stayed.
Four in the afternoon. The seventh bridge. Yeoni collapsed onto a riverside bench. Their calves felt ready to burst. The bicycle fell beside them.
One star. Universe Customer Support, one star. No, half a star.
Yeoni opened their notebook. Possibly white hair. Obsessed with socks. Sensitive about ratings. White umbrella. Cat allergy. Toward the river.
I've written so much. Still can't picture his face.
As they closed the notebook, a petal settled between the pages. Yeoni left it there instead of brushing it away.
Then a sneeze came from the far end of the bench. Yeoni turned.
A white umbrella leaned against the bench. Beside it sat a man with a book open on his knees. A stray cat crouched at his feet.
Ah, sorry. I'm allergic to cats.
Then why not shoo it away?
It sat here first. This is its spot.
One strand of the man's hair was white, as though naturally so rather than dyed. His eyes were reserved, his voice low.
Yeoni held their breath. Their heart pounded up to their ears. No certainty. Plenty of people had white hair.
Your bicycle fell over.
Oh. Yes. I know. Deliberately.
Never met someone who knocks it over deliberately.
The man looked back at his book, then stopped. His gaze caught at Yeoni's ankles, between the yellow sock and the striped one.
Excuse me. Your socks don't match.
Yeoni couldn't answer. They bit their lip. Their eyes burned. Looking alarmed, the man closed his book.
Oh, sorry. What a strange thing to say. I don't know why I said it. To someone I've just met.
It's okay. I used to hear it every day.
Every day? From whom?
Someone who scolded a lot. I thought he was an ordinary cat at first. He wasn't. Later, he became human.
The man tilted his head. An unbelievable story, yet he didn't laugh it off. At that expression, Yeoni laughed through tears.
Where is he now?
He went home. Very far away. Barely said goodbye.
He's made you wait a long time.
Right? Completely irresponsible. His last words were about socks.
That was a bit much. Strangely, I feel guilty.
Without noticing, he rubbed his temple like someone developing a headache. Yeoni didn't miss the gesture.
Somehow, they began walking together. He righted the bicycle, Yeoni thanked him, and they were going the same way. That was all.
The cherry-tree path stretched along the river. Petals blew onto their shoulders. The last petals.
May I tell you something strange? I keep having the same dream lately.
What dream?
Walking this path with someone carrying a yellow umbrella. Sometimes there's a pig. With pink flowers.
A pig?
Thought it meant lottery luck, so I bought tickets three times. All lost.
It's not a lottery dream. Really.
Then what is it? Do you interpret dreams?
Apparently pigs mean you'll meet someone who helps you. I just made that up.
The man looked as though he didn't know why they were laughing. Yeoni couldn't stop. A petal caught in his white strand of hair.
Excuse me. What's your name?
Park Byeongha. Yours?
Park Byeongha. Yeoni rolled the name silently in their mind. The name first read at the Lovers card. The name that would make him disappear.
That rule belonged to the other world. Yeoni had written on Card Twenty-Three themselves: The door opens from inside too.
Still. That name was given by someone else.
Yeoni shook their head. There was another name to call. One they'd given him. One tied to a one-star rating.
I'm Yeoni. And may I ask a favor?
What is it?
I'm going to say a strange name now. You don't have to answer. Just listen.
Neo.
The wind stopped. Falling petals seemed to pause briefly in midair. Park Byeongha stopped walking.
Ah.
He pressed his forehead as though in pain and closed his eyes. Something raced beneath his eyelids.
A rainy bus stop. An inside-out umbrella. A cat's place at the foot of a bed. The sun of the Island of Expression. A dragon egg in a vault. Drowned bookshelves. White light inside the Void.
And Yeoni, first taking his human hand on the boat above the river. The warmth against his shoulder then.
Yeoni.
Yes. It's me. Mismatched socks.
Decided on the rating? You said you'd tell me when you did.
His manner of speaking had changed. Blunt, a little cheeky, strangely gentle at the end. The voice Yeoni knew.
Five stars. Almost took one off for being late, but I didn't. The review will be long, though.
Generous.
Yeoni gripped his shirt and cried. Byeongha hesitated briefly, then wrapped his arms around their back. This time, no part of him faded.
My hands don't show through now. Holding you like this... is okay, right?
My head. Just my head. You know how to pat it.
And Yeoni. Why are your socks mismatched again?
A test. You passed.
The stray cat following at their feet meowed. Park Byeongha sneezed. Yeoni laughed aloud.
The allergy survived. Couldn't they have fixed that when I returned? I'll have to call customer support myself.
Let's file a complaint. Only one person in the queue. Should connect quickly.
Do you really remember everything? Being Park-whatever and being Neo, both?
Both. Byeongha, going to work and paying rent. Neo, beside you. Even the hand you took on the boat.
Strangely, none of it gets mixed up. Maybe because both are me.
Then what should I call you? Byeongha? Neo?
The name you gave me. Yeongnyangi. Byeongha around other people. If you call me Yeongnyangi at work, explanations get long.
I wasn't planning to visit your office. Now I am.
Byeongha laughed. A slightly awkward smile with one corner rising first. Yeoni felt they would never forget it now.
The sun tilted over the river. Petals drifted slowly on the water. They stood side by side against the riverside railing.
I walked this path in a dream. In an ordinary spring. With you.
What did we do in the dream? Don't tell me we fought.
Nothing. Just walked. That was the best part. We fought after I woke.
Then promise. Every spring, we walk here. Before the blossoms fall. Doing nothing.
Promises are made to be kept. If it rains, you carry the umbrella. The yellow one.
[ App notification · Seo Hanbi: Sea trip, second Saturday in May. One more person is welcome. No one who sheds fur. ]
Haven't shed fur in ages. Still bringing that up?
You still sneeze.
Yeoni replied: Adding one. Human. No fur. Sock inspector.
[ App notification · Kang Saebyeok: You found him. My daily forecast was right, so the fee is due. Also, his birth time, please. ]
Why is he still asking birth times?
He wants to read our compatibility. Yours and mine.
The Eul–Gyeong union is enough for us. We came all this way together.
Still curious, though. What score we'd get.
If it's not a hundred, give that fortune-teller one star.
Smiling, Yeoni pocketed the phone and took Park Byeongha's hand. A human hand was larger than expected, and a little colder.
Your hand's cold. Because you're Gyeong Metal?
Your hand's warm. Because you're Eul Wood.
Hand in hand, they walked along the river. The stray cat followed at a distance. Park Byeongha sneezed again. The last petal drifted downriver.
Spring, three years later. Yeoni woke ten minutes before the alarm. The radio reported that cherry blossoms had begun opening outside.
A photograph clung to the refrigerator door. The seaside. Two umbrellas. A lunch box of split-open gimbap. Four people, all caught with their eyes closed.
Not one decent shot. Giving him the selfie stick was a mistake.
A cushion still rested at the foot of the bed. Habit now. Today, a white dress hung beside it.
It's really today. Not a dream, right?
[ App notification · Park Byeongha: Awake? Match your socks. Today, seriously. ]
First text on our wedding morning is socks? What about 'I love you'?
Yeoni wrote a reply, deleted it, and wrote again. Matched. Photo attached. Two matching white socks.
[ Park Byeongha: Passed. ]
He really hasn't changed.
Yeoni took the old notebook from a drawer. The sentence on its last page remained: Even in a different form, Neo. On my side.
Below it, they wrote today's date and added one line: Now my husband. Then slipped the notebook into the dress bag's inner pocket.
The doorbell rang. Before Yeoni could open it, elegant, polite speech reached them. Cool at the endings, yet strangely warm.
Bride, I've brought your makeup artist. And umbrellas. Rain is forecast this afternoon.
Rain? On my wedding day?
Don't worry. April rain passes quickly. And rainy weddings mean a happy marriage. Saebyeok said so.
We agreed to believe only half of what Saebyeok says.
The problem is that half is usually right.
Seo Hanbi now managed the convenience store. The woman who had worked nights to repay umbrellas had taken over when the owner retired. The world accepted strange people better than expected.
Her notebook still stayed in her bag. Every line had a circle. Except the very last.
[ And Yeoni ]
Still leaving that line unchecked?
Yes. I thought I'd circle it today. A wedding gift.
Don't. Leave it open forever. Come as a friend, not to repay me.
Seo Hanbi looked at the notebook for a long time, then put her pen back. Instead of a circle, she had drawn a tiny umbrella at the line's end.
Then this. A mark of sharing, not repayment.
After makeup, Seo Hanbi fastened the dress buttons one by one with careful fingers. In the mirror, she briefly lowered her eyes.
The Yeoni of the first spring wanted a dress like this too. We talked about it at the bus stop.
What did that spring's me say?
That you hoped it would rain on your wedding day. An excuse to share an umbrella.
That spring's me was very me.
I can't repay that Yeoni. So I'll be twice as good to this spring's Yeoni.
Forget twice as good. Just catch the bouquet today. I'll aim at you.
The venue was the riverside park behind the university. Kang Saebyeok stood in a suit before the front row, an emcee script in his hand and a perpetual calendar in his pocket.
One check before the bride enters. I haven't received today's auspicious-date selection fee.
Deduct it from your wedding gift.
Then I have to give a larger gift. Strange arithmetic.
Saebyeok now ran a small consultation office instead of a campus tent. The sign still read: Birth time unknown? I'll work it out.
Behind him sat a small middle-aged woman. She waved when she met Yeoni's eyes. Saebyeok reddened to the tips of his ears.
My mother. She came along. Wanted to see the people who call her son's name.
Ma'am! Do you know Saebyeok scams people with compatibility readings?
That was a secret!
Laughing, the woman called her son. Saebyeok. Instead of answering, he opened his script. Upside down.
And a congratulatory message has arrived. From very far away.
[ App notification · Moka: I'm rapping the wedding song. Dodam on drums, Museong on chorus. No refusals. I'm a five-star performer. ]
Can't refuse this one.
Whether the rap plays in this world, I don't know. The universe will handle it.
A drum really sounded from the phone speaker. Clumsy and joyous. Above it came a boy's clear voice, then rap drowning that voice out.
Still off-key.
That's the charm. Nobody's mocking him.
A short aisle beneath cherry trees. At its end stood Park Byeongha. The white strand of hair remained. His tie was slightly crooked.
Yeoni walked alone, without taking their father's arm. They had insisted. This path, at least, they wanted to walk on their own feet.
Late.
Three minutes. Nothing compared with how long you waited.
True.
Laughter rose from the guests. Yeoni straightened Byeongha's tie. He stood still like a tamed cat.
Yeoni. In the first spring, we never made it this far.
I know. That's why I walked here this time. By myself.
Yes. On your own feet. I didn't drag you here.
Yeoni understood. A vine winds around Metal to climb, but Metal doesn't pull the vine upward. They simply support one another.
Now the vows. Groom first.
I'm not good with words, so I'll keep it short. But I'll keep it for a long time.
I'll match your socks. If you go out in mismatched ones, I won't get angry. Might scold a little.
That's a vow?
And I'll never hide my name while staying beside you again. From beginning to end, as Park Byeongha. As Neo.
The guests fell silent. Seo Hanbi took out a handkerchief. Saebyeok lowered his head, pretending to read his script.
My turn.
When it rains, I'll carry the yellow umbrella. Half for you, half for me. No complaints about wet shoulders.
I'll rate you again every year. Stars may come off. Stay alert.
Already nervous.
They joined hands. The center of Yeoni's palm warmed. Byeongha's hand was a little cold, then quickly matched its temperature. Eul and Gyeong. Vine and Metal.
Then rain truly began. Fine spring rain. Guests murmured. Seo Hanbi drew umbrellas from her bag: one yellow, one black.
See? Bought with my own money this time.
Yeoni opened the yellow umbrella and tilted half toward Byeongha. Their own shoulder grew wet. Silently, he pushed the shaft back toward Yeoni.
I said half is mine.
Half of your half is mine. Vow amended.
At that moment, Yeoni's phone rang. Not an unknown number. The screen showed a name they hadn't been able to delete in three years.
[ Incoming · Customer Support: Universe ]
Now? During the wedding?
Answer. After all that waiting, another delay might hurt its feelings.
Congratulations, valued customer. Destiny Customer Support, the universe speaking. We're calling with your resolution notice and a satisfaction survey.
Right now? After not calling once in three years?
Yes. Today is when the outcome becomes final. Case received: spring when you were twenty-three. Case completed: today.
If you were satisfied with the process, please leave a star rating. Your valued review will greatly help our next customer.

Yeoni looked at the guests. Seo Hanbi blowing her nose into a handkerchief. Saebyeok hiding behind his script. Moka still rapping through the phone. Byeongha beneath the umbrella, one shoulder half wet.
At first, even half a star felt too generous.
Their thumb moved over the stars. One, two, three, four. Then five.
[ ★★★★★ · Review: Almost took one off for being late, but didn't. Worst wait time. Friendly agent. Satisfied with the result. Would not buy again. Once was enough. ]
Thank you for your valued review. Have an ordinary spring.
The call ended. The rain stopped. Sunlight poured between the clouds. Wet cherry petals fell, glittering.
Was that the universe? The universe calls weddings?
Should have put it on the guest list. Though it probably wouldn't give a wedding gift.
It would charge a consultation fee. Three years' worth.
What did you write?
Secret. I said I'd rate you again every year. I'll show you next year.
A white cat passed their feet. Park Byeongha sneezed. The guests laughed. Yeoni laughed too.
The bouquet left Yeoni's hand and landed precisely in Seo Hanbi's arms. Startled, she dropped her umbrella. Saebyeok applauded. No one lent the applause, and no one collected it.
