Am I allowed to accept this?
You absolutely accept that. Don't repay it.
Ordinary. A truly ordinary spring.
That's enough. Next spring too. And the spring after.
[ Destiny restored · A Spring in Reality ]

episodes.title: The One Who Stays
episodes.tag: Episode 51S · The Spring We Chose to Stay

beats.t: Yeoni's finger touched the moonlit World Tree card. The entire square drew a light breath, and the cherry-blossom view through the open door quietly receded.
[ Choice complete · Stay in the world of fortune ]
I'll stay here. Not to run away. I want to live what comes next with the people I protected, in the world I changed.
Then I'll stay too. This time, not because of guardian regulations. I choose as Park Byeongha.
The light unraveling Neo's body stopped. A white cat's tail overlapped him like a mirage, then the heartbeat of the human Park Byeongha grew clear again.
Yeoni, I'll return. There are debts to face and people to apologize to there.
Go and live, not just repay. Put off living until everything's repaid, and that's another ledger.
Yes. This time, I'll write a line of my own life every day. I'll remember that returning isn't only settling accounts.
Yeoni opened the yellow umbrella and placed it in Seo Hanbi's hand. Its shaft, wrapped in three layers of tape, was warm between two worlds.
Wait. Take this to reality. The first line of my new song. No copyright yet, so listen all you want.
The twenty-third door connects rather than closes. You can send news once a month.
Then I can write Mom too. Not as a daughter who vanished, but one who built a home in another world.
Let's write the first letter together. Can't have you impulsively giving a star rating first.
Why are you proofreading my letter? Besides, Mom already knows my rating habit.
Seo Hanbi laughed, a laugh unseen in the first spring. Umbrella in hand, she stood before reality's cherry-blossom door.
See you in the next rain. I'll tilt the umbrella then.
After the door closed, one yellow ray remained in the air. Not a severed path, but a promise open like a door.
All right. Goodbyes done. Everyone staying, eat first. Save the world then starve, and we'll lose all dignity.
Moka spun his pan. Vegetables and flames bounced to the beat. Smiling, Yeoni set plates on the table.
Your Four Pillars have found a place in this world now too. Fortune didn't choose an address. A person did.
Here too, I'll have to get up in the morning, work, argue, apologize. That's why I stayed. Life goes on here.
You understand well. I'll wake you at seven tomorrow. Staying in the world of fortune doesn't abolish lateness.
Considering undoing my choice.
Everyone laughed. Moonlight fell through the World Tree's leaves. Beneath it, Yeoni called this place home for the first time.
The square after the farewell was quiet but not empty. The remaining companions' breaths and footsteps steadily filled every space where emptiness might enter.
Yeoni told themselves they hadn't abandoned reality, only redefined the distance between two worlds. The more they explained it, the clearer their heart became.
I'll miss things even in the life I chose. But missing them doesn't mean I chose wrong. Both feelings can coexist.
Yes. Choosing doesn't mean hating one thing in order to love another. The place you left is part of your life too.
Following the grain of the World Tree's roots, Byeongha showed them a small homesite. A waterway in view, the teahouse's moonlight within reach, the ladle a little less audible.
Sounds like you're calling my ladle noise. Expect a giant cookware set as your wedding gift.
We haven't discussed marriage! We're only looking at a homesite!
I have, in my mind. I'll say it aloud after the house is built.
The tips of Yeoni's ears reddened. Even in a flower-pig body, their expression couldn't hide. Moka lowered his microphone and smiled like an otter who'd found material for lifelong teasing.
As night deepened, news arrived from the islands they had crossed together. The eclipse had retreated. Stopped festivals resumed. Forgotten names found their owners one by one.
You already have work to do here, Yeoni. After rescue ends, recovery remains.
I can't do that alone. We'll do it together. Being the main character doesn't mean I plan to carry the whole world.
At day's end, Yeoni leaned against a World Tree root. No finished home, no settled job, no complete plan. But the earth beneath their feet was solid.
Byeongha sat beside them. They stayed silent for a long time. Enduring the same night without disappearing was their newest promise.
Let's try living here from tomorrow. Good days and bad, making them all part of my choice.
Yeoni placed a little chair before the door through which Seo Hanbi had left. When a letter arrived next month, they would sit there and read every word.
Staying didn't mean closing a door. Instead of imagining somewhere to return, Yeoni finally began writing what to do here tomorrow.
Tomorrow I'll clean the teahouse windows. The next day, visit the Island of Companions and mend broken mirrors. After that, we'll choose then.
A practical enough plan. Except I'll clean the windows. When you do it, you only add patterns.
Yeoni argued as usual. Byeongha stubbornly held his ground as usual. To both, that little disagreement felt more miraculous than a miracle.
The first spring had no tomorrow. In the second, everything had been hidden to protect tomorrow. Now they prepared for it openly, together.
Yeongnyangi, I won't forget that you came to save me. But from now on, surviving is something we'll do together.
Understood. Rescue ends after one act. Life keeps asking for each other's hands.
[ The Twenty-Third Door · Preparing the first letter · Tomorrow ]

episodes.title: Letters Through an Open Door
episodes.tag: Episode 52S · Letters Through an Open Door

beats.t: On their first morning in the world of fortune, Yeoni switched off all three alarms and fell asleep again in a little room among the World Tree's roots.
Get up. What happens to your dignity if the person who chose this world is late on their very first day?
Doesn't the person who saved the world get a pass on wake-up calls?
No. There is an apple for breakfast, though. Get up now and I'll make you tea.
Yeoni's eyes flew open. The little kettle smelled of lotus blossoms, and Moka's saucepan beat drifted in through the window.
Tap, tap, tapping, wake the morning air. Fry the five elements, fill it with flair!
The whole rapping-otter-chef concept finally makes perfect sense.
From that day on, Yeoni took charge of a small consultation table at the Destiny Teahouse. It was a place to help people find their own sentences, rather than hand them answers.
Your heart seems to be running ahead, while the other person's pace is a little slower. Instead of pressing for reassurance, what if you leave room for a breath?
The wind fairy having the consultation stopped crying and nodded. Yeoni poured another cup of tea.
You left room for choices without making pronouncements. That was a good consultation.
Of course. I chose my own destiny. I can't go closing off somebody else's ending.
That evening, the golden line of the twenty-third door opened. Beyond it appeared Yeoni's studio apartment in reality and Seo Hanbi's yellow umbrella.
Yeoni, can you hear me? I'll read you the letter your mother sent.
The letter's first line was brief. Wherever you are, are you eating properly? At the second line, the ink had lingered a long time.
It hurts that you're gone, but you say you chose where to live, so I'm going to try to trust you. Take good care of your heart there, too.
I'll write back to Mom. I'll tell her I'm still oversleeping, working, and sharing meals with good people here.
And write that I take care of your socks.
Leave that out. You'll make it sound like I can't even put socks on without you.
I can hear both of you perfectly. Byeongha, no more hiding your name.
Park Byeongha. Neo. Yeongnyangi. Every name Yeoni calls me is mine. I'm not letting go of a single one now.
When the letter ended, the golden line did not close. It became a little star. Yeoni hung it by the teahouse window.
Send them some otter rap, too. Let's see if people in reality know a decent beat.
As long as this door exists, the two worlds aren't cut off. But the place where you make your life is here now, Yeoni.
Yes. I didn't stay because I couldn't go back. I chose a life here, with a door through which I can send news.
That night, Yeoni and Byeongha walked among the World Tree's roots. Lights glowed in the small houses beneath them, and far away the river of the moon shimmered.
Yeoni. Let's build a house, too. Not too far from the teahouse, and a little farther from Moka's morning beat.
All right. Big windows. Space for two umbrellas. And no sock inspection checklist on the fridge.
Byeongha smiled. Yeoni took his hand. Cool metal and warm wood walked at the same pace.

The first month at the teahouse passed very slowly. Every day, Yeoni organized the consultation notes and revised the words for the next person, making them a little easier to understand than yesterday.
Yeoni's consultations were not prophecies. They were closer to showing the flow of the five elements and shedding light together on the paths a person could choose within it.
Having a lot of Water energy doesn't always make someone gentle. When there's too much, your feelings may have trouble finding somewhere to flow. Today, let's make one small vessel for them.
At the back of the teahouse, Byeongha repaired and rehung a broken door handle and an old wind-chime mirror. With every nail he drove, Yeoni promised another star in his review.
Fixing one door handle is harder than being a customer service agent. Still, this is about building a home that will stay, not memories to erase.
At dinner, Moka's cooking always occupied the center of the table. It tasted different every day, was usually good, and occasionally left everyone drinking nothing but water.
You can't back up a failed dish, either. So you remember today's flavor and stir-fry tomorrow to a different beat.
Don't justify bad food by comparing cooking to destiny.
Yet Yeoni did not dislike what he had said. They were all already learning how to use an irreversible day as an ingredient for the next, instead of throwing it away.
When the second letter arrived from reality, Seo Hanbi's handwriting was neater than in the first. She wrote that she was learning a new job in a school counseling office.
I used to think even an apology was a debt. Now I'm learning that the person you become after apologizing matters more.
Hanbi, that was a good choice. But don't start trying to bear everything alone. Open the door and talk when things get hard.
Yeoni decided that they might rescue someone, but would not take on all that person's burdens. Making a place to carry them together offered comfort that lasted longer.
You've learned how to respect someone's choices. Then respect mine, too.
What is it? If you've secretly made another dangerous plan on your own, it doesn't count.
Let's prepare to get married. Sign the papers, make our promises in front of everyone, and turn this house into an address that belongs to us both.
Yeoni covered their mouth. Their eyes widened in surprise, and then a color like the purple ribbon spread across both cheeks.
Was that a proposal? Who starts a proposal with paperwork and an address?
Apparently, I do. And if you'd like, I can do it again.
Do it again. But the answer will be the same. Let's live together, Park Byeongha. Neo. Yeongnyangi.
The words were almost too characteristically Byeongha to be called a proposal, but Yeoni understood: he would never abandon his name or his address again.
Before writing their wedding vows, they wrote down the expressions each wore when frightened. Love was less an ability to read minds than a habit of asking and waiting.
If you don't understand my expression, ask instead of guessing. Even in a world of divination, I'll speak for my own heart.
That is the hardest promise, and the most necessary. I'll keep it.
[ A Moonlit Homesite · A New Promise Between Two People ]

episodes.title: A Wedding Beneath the Moonlit World Tree
episodes.tag: Another Final Episode · Spring in the World of Fortune

ending.label: Spring in the World of Fortune

beats.t: Three years later, spring in the world of fortune began on a night when the moon waxed full twice. Silver lotuses bloomed at every tip of the World Tree.
Two yellow umbrellas stood side by side at Yeoni's door. One had three layers of tape; the other bore a golden tag.
My socks match, right? Check properly today.
Pale purple on the left, pale purple on the right. Pass. You're more thorough today than when you saved the world.
It's our wedding. One black sock sneaks in and we've got an incident.
Yeoni secured a white veil behind the lotus. Today's flower-pig form was a choice to remember the body that began the journey, not a remnant of a curse.
One song before the bride comes in. Two moons, one team in love. A brand-new rhythm over time returned!
When Moka raised the microphone, the fairies flew while tapping the rhythm with their feet. For this one day, even the saucepan and ladle waited quietly beside the stage.
By the moon's angle, there is still a little time before the ceremony, but today the moment you choose is the right time.
Kang Saebyeok, no asking for birth dates today. Start a compatibility consultation at the wedding and I'll dock your star rating.
The golden line of the twenty-third door opened beside the guests' seats. Beyond it lay the cherry-blossom riverbank in reality.
I can see you perfectly. I brought an umbrella. This time, I'll tilt it toward you first.
Yeoni's mother stood beside Seo Hanbi. The edge of the letter in her hands trembled, but she was smiling.
Mom, I'm living well. This is my home. But that doesn't change the fact that I'm your daughter.
Beyond the door, their mother nodded. Her voice did not carry, but the shape of her words was clear. As long as you're happy.
Yeoni. You chose this moment, too. You can cry or laugh. Just don't let go of my hand.
You're the one who mustn't let go. You turned back time alone once. From now on, we write it together.
Byeongha took Yeoni's hand. It was the hand he had been unable to reach in the first spring and had had to hide in the second. Today he held it where everyone could see.
As Park Byeongha, as Neo, as Yeongnyangi, I love you. Whatever my name, I will stay beside you without hiding.
The me who was a flower pig, the me who was human, and the me of tomorrow all want to live with you. Let's not close our ending today.
The World Tree's lotuses bloomed all at once. Red threads, golden letters, and tiny fragments of the Milky Way fell over the pair.
Time for the wedding rap! Destiny isn't a verdict; it's lyrics you two rewrite every day!
The five elements are flowing without tilting to one side. But balance isn't something finished once today. Keep adjusting it together.
That's our specialty. Arguing, talking, and taking each other's hands again.
Don't leave out using star ratings as a threat.
Laughter erupted among the guests. No one offered borrowed applause, and no one took that applause away.
After the wedding, Yeoni and Byeongha spread out a place to sit beneath the World Tree's roots. Far away, a single cherry blossom fell beside the river in reality.
Yeoni, Byeongha. I'll write again next month. I'll take good care of the spring on this side, too.
We'll live our spring well here, too. Let's keep exchanging news.
Even when the twenty-third door closed into a little star, Yeoni felt no sadness. It was a door that would open again next month.
Are you happy?
Yes. It isn't ordinary, but it's the spring I chose. So to me, it's ordinary enough.
Byeongha rested his forehead against Yeoni's. Between their hands, the moonlight turned a warm gold.
During the three months of wedding preparations, Yeoni wrote many times in a notebook that marriage was not an ending. Their promise was a way to live each day, not a final result.
Byeongha no longer spoke of having returned through time as though it were a heroic tale. The time he had endured alone was evidence of love, but not a method to repeat.
Whatever happens, I'll speak first. I won't disappear alone again under the excuse of protecting you.
And I'll tell you when I'm hurting. I won't bear it alone just to reassure you.
Instead of grand prophecies, their wedding vows filled with small promises. Don't skip meals. Don't hold the umbrella alone. If memories grow hazy, start by reading the notes together.
Add coming to my show once a month. Essential cultural enrichment for a married couple.
That's a ticket subscription, not a vow.
The day before the wedding, Yeoni opened the twenty-third door and gazed a long time at the riverbank in reality. Not to regret the path untaken, but to make sure spring had come there, too.
Seo Hanbi held a yellow umbrella with a student who was afraid of the bus stop at night. She gave no answers. She simply stood beside the student until the bus came.
Hanbi is living her own spring, too. From a witness to the first spring to someone who waits for another person's spring.
Yeoni closed the door and went home. Byeongha was sorting socks in the entryway, and one pair was still mismatched.
These are yours. I put them in my drawer because you made them go missing first.
A sock trial even on the day before our wedding. That's so us.
Before leaving for the ceremony, they checked the teahouse lights one by one. It was a small task they repeated daily, yet such things had protected them longer than the world's great events.

Beneath the World Tree, there were seats for everyone they had met on the journey. For those who had lost their memories, those whose names had been stolen, and those who had not chosen forgiveness but were preparing what came next together.
Today's marriage isn't an event assigned by fortune. It's the result of choosing differently each time and still returning to walk in the same direction.
That's why I like it. Not because it was decided for us, but because we're choosing each other again today.
Standing in the moonlit place, Yeoni heard the World Tree's heartbeat. The sound that had frightened them on first falling into this world was now as comforting as the clock at home.
Byeongha held out his hand to her. It was no longer a hand reaching from the future to turn back the past. It was a hand taking the next step together from the present.
Let's go. Into our next spring.
